Archive \file{gowers\_degree\_stratification.zip} (arrival \texttt{26908b3b6}), manuscript \file{gowers\_degree\_stratification.tex} (2,071 lines, 30 pages), pin \texttt{43306653a} (its \file{SOURCE\_LEDGER.json}, shipped as \file{data/22-degree-filtrations-SOURCE\_LEDGER.json}). Printed below: the abstract and Section~1; Sections~2--5 are in Part~II (with sources~25 and~27, Section~\ref{gsr:en:sec:degeneracy}), Sections~6--10 form a chapter of Part~III (Section~\ref{gsr:cc:sec:colourings}), Sections~11--12 are in Part~V. Its `question' environment (``Research question'') is set in this report's `Research question' style; three of its statements, unlabelled as delivered, carry labels added at the write.}
\begin{partabstract}{22}
We develop two degree-sensitive refinements connected with Gowers' proof of
Szemer\'edi's theorem. First, we stratify the exceptional certificates in
Section~15 by the Boolean degree left after removing parity. A degree-$t$
certificate has success probability at most $p^{-t-1}$ for $t\ge2$.
For degree one we count exactly the certificate classes satisfying the
necessary balance constraints. Their number is a polynomial in the cube
dimension $k$ of degree $2d$, rather than an exponential in $2^k$.
For $d=2$ it is
$30k^4+204k^3+111k^2+114k$.
This yields a fully explicit finite replacement for the exceptional-set
estimate, with degree-sensitive sufficient field-size conditions for its
absorption step. We also settle the first-order degeneracy count for the
previously excluded two-cube case: its optimal coefficient is $k^2+3k$.

Second, for any prescribed equality pattern on a finite set of field
parameters, we determine the exact minimum number of successful directions
at a prescribed center among polynomial colorings of given degrees.
The answer is $q^{\max(n-B,0)}$, where $B$ is a maximum-weight column-basis
sum of an explicit evaluation matrix. This removes the earlier degree
restriction for symmetric progressions and gives a monochromatic analogue.
Norm forms attain the pointwise bound. We prove that a complete low-degree
norm construction cannot be extended by adding an arbitrary independent
summand; in the four-term case we give an exact count in terms of third
differences of that summand. Quantitative constant-line counts explain a
further obstruction in the characteristic-divisible norm layers.
All principal statements have proofs; exact finite verification and
integration notes accompany the source. No improved global Szemer\'edi
bound or resolution of the global quintic avoidance problem is asserted.
\end{partabstract}

The useful question behind this report is whether the degree actually
present in an auxiliary object can replace the worst possible degree
implicit in a large counting argument. We answer this in two settings.
In Gowers' exceptional-arrangement argument, degree controls the number of
independent restrictions imposed by a certificate. In polynomial coloring,
degree controls the number of variables that can be constrained by the
evaluation equations. Both arguments become substantially more precise
when they retain a filtration by degree.

Our direct source is Section~15 of Gowers' 2001 paper
\cite{gowers}, as transcribed and studied in the Ramsey part of
ProveIt \cite{repo22}. We use repository snapshot \texttt{43306653afaa};
the full revision identifier appears in the references and source ledger.
The earlier project reports \cite{prior22degeneracy,prior22extremal} already
determined the first-order coefficient for $d\ge2$ arrangements and the
low-degree symmetric-coloring threshold. Those results are prerequisites
and comparison points, not claimed again as new discoveries. The necessary
arguments are reproduced here so that this article can be read alone.

\begin{writenote}[6 October 2026; sources 21--27]

On the heading ``The direct Section~15 improvement'': the improvement is in the finite bound at moderate $p$; at Lemma~15.5 the thresholds of Section~\ref{gsr:en:22:sec:d4} gain nothing over source~18's Corollary~\ref{gsr:en:18:deg:cor-selection} at leading order (note after Corollary~\ref{gsr:en:22:cor:sharpscale}).
\end{writenote}

\subsection{The direct Section 15 improvement}

A $d$-arrangement consists of $2d$ parallel $k$-cubes. Its parameter
space has dimension
\[
 D=(2d+1)k+2d-1.
\]
Gowers' Lemma~15.4 bounds the number of degenerate arrangements by
$k3^{2d2^k}p^{D-1}$. The preceding project analysis replaced its leading
coefficient by $k+C_d$, where
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:22:eq:Cd-intro}
 C_d=\frac12\left(T_{2d}-2\binom{2d}{d}+1\right),
 \qquad
 T_{2d}=\sum_{a=0}^{d}\binom{2d}{2a}\binom{2a}{a}.
\end{equation}
It still bounded all nonparity certificates together by a very large
multiple of $p^{-2}$.

The new estimate distinguishes their degrees. The degree-one contribution
has coefficient $\Bal_{k,d}$, given by a constant-term formula in
Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:22:thm:balanced-count}. For each fixed $d$ it is a polynomial in
$k$ of degree $2d$. Certificates of higher degrees are assigned progressively
smaller probabilities. The resulting finite bound is
Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:22:thm:filtration-bound}. Its proof includes the necessary
summation by parts; subtracting two unrelated cumulative upper bounds
would not be a valid way to bound an individual degree stratum.

The case $d=1$ has different geometry. We identify all its divisorial
exceptions and prove
\[
 \delta_{k,1}(p)=\frac{k^2+3k}{p}+O_k(p^{-2}),
\]
with an explicit finite remainder. This answers a specific question left
open by the preceding report, including the exact formula
$\delta_{1,1}(p)=4/p-3/p^2$.

\subsection{Exact pointwise polynomial questions}

Let $\Pi$ prescribe which colors on a finite parameter set must agree.
Given a polynomial coloring $Q:\F_q^n\to\F_q^r$, write $S_z(Q)$ for
the directions $h$ realizing that pattern from the base point $z$;
the zero direction is included. We prove an exact formula
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:22:eq:pattern-intro}
 \min_Q |S_z(Q)|=q^{\max\{n-B,0\}}.
\end{equation}
The integer $B$ is computed by descending Gaussian elimination on a small
matrix of parameter powers. This is an exact extremal answer at every
\emph{prescribed} center: the minimizing polynomial is allowed to depend
on that center. It is generally a different question to minimize the sum
over all centers using one polynomial.

For symmetric $\ell=2m$ term progressions and degree caps $D_a$, put
$s_a=\lceil D_a/2\rceil$ and $t_a=\min(m,s_a)$. The answer uses
\[
 B_{\rm sym}=\sum_a t_a(2s_a-t_a).
\]
For monochromatic $\ell$-term progressions it uses
\[
 B_{\rm mono}=\sum_a \frac{r_a(2D_a-r_a+1)}2,
 \qquad r_a=\min(D_a,\ell-1).
\]
Both statements hold for arbitrarily large degree caps in characteristic
$p>\ell$; a bound on the field size alone would be insufficient.

For symmetric four-term progressions, the scalar quintic and sextic
pointwise budget is exactly eight. We exhibit the sharp example
$N_3+N_5$ at the origin. Thus a universal prescribed-center theorem
cannot lower eight to seven. We also prove concrete obstructions to two
natural ways of promoting such local examples to globally avoiding
colorings.

\begin{partabstract}{23}
We establish precise local refinements and sharpness results for three
parts of Gowers's proof of Szemer\'edi's theorem.  First, simultaneous
linear-phase partitions with cell lengths in a finite set $\mathcal S$
are controlled by the numerical-semigroup conductor $C(\mathcal S)$.
A torus-packing upper bound and a mixed-radix lower construction give
asymptotically matching constants when the permitted lengths are close.
In particular, the eventual universal threshold for cell lengths
$L,L+1$ is $L^{q+2}/\prod_i\varepsilon_i\,(1+o(1))$.
This proves the necessity of the extra tiling cost left open in an
earlier project report, even when different cells may use different
steps.  We also compute an exact exceptional-set profile for the
obstructions and a sharp almost-partition threshold.

Second, for real centered functions on groups of exponent five, we prove
the sharp cube-counting expansion
\[
 \|\delta+f\|_{U^3}^8
 \le\delta^8+6\sqrt2\,\delta^4u^4
 +\frac{2^{3/4}}3\delta^2u^6+O(u^8),
 \qquad u=\|f\|_{U^3}\ll\delta,
\]
with an absolute, dimension-independent error constant.  An exact
five-point model and indicator approximations attain the secondary
coefficient; a rigidity theorem determines the necessary harmonic
phase alignment.  Third, a localization to width at least $m/3$ lets
common slice refinements extend to full product boxes without further
width loss.  Paired interpolation and retained observations give an
explicit conditional replacement for the geometric part of Lemma~16.10.

Every principal new statement is proved in the article.  Exact finite
certificates accompany the proofs.  We distinguish these local results
from the remaining global parameter comparison and from Lean
formalization; no new general bound for Szemer\'edi's theorem is claimed.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small
\noindent Source revision: \snapshottwentythree.\\
Status: research draft with complete written proofs and reproducible finite checks.
\end{quote}
\label{gsr:fm:23:sec:introduction}

Gowers's 2001 proof develops several interacting quantitative mechanisms:
uniformity norms control configuration counts; phase approximation turns
algebraic structure into useful progressions; and repeated structural
refinements make fibre information compatible across coordinates
\cite{gowers}.  These mechanisms contain local questions whose answers
can be sharpened independently of the full density-increment iteration.
The present article concentrates on three such questions and proves
explicit results for each.

The reference repository already contains extensive earlier refinements,
and several changes to its transcription address the difference between
the printed paper and statements suitable for formalization
\cite{repo23source,repo23research,repo23status}.  We treat those results as
prior project work.  In particular, the previously obtained upper
exponent for prescribed linear-phase cell lengths is reproduced with
attribution; the new contribution is a matching obstruction, a sharp
leading constant, and the extension to arbitrary admissible length sets.
Similarly, the leading centered three-cube coefficient was known in the
project; here the order-five secondary coefficient is determined.

\subsection{Three principal conclusions}

\paragraph{Exact lengths have an unavoidable arithmetic cost.}
Let $T_{\mathcal S}(\boldsymbol\varepsilon)$ be the eventual universal
interval threshold for a partition into progressions of lengths in
$\mathcal S$, on which $q$ affine phases have arc diameters at most
$\varepsilon_i$.  If $L=\min\mathcal S\ge2$, $H=\max\mathcal S$,
$\gcd(\mathcal S)=1$ and $C=C(\mathcal S)$, then
\begin{equation}
 C\prod_i\left(\left\lceil\frac{L-1}{\varepsilon_i}\right\rceil-1\right)
 \le T_{\mathcal S}(\boldsymbol\varepsilon)
 \le C\left(\left\lceil\frac{(H-1)^q}{\prod_i\varepsilon_i}\right\rceil-1\right).
 \label{gsr:fm:23:eq:intro-threshold}
\end{equation}
For $\mathcal S=\{L,L+1\}$ this yields
$T\sim L^{q+2}/\prod_i\varepsilon_i$, uniformly in the tolerances for
fixed $q$ as $L\to\infty$.  This answers the prescribed-length
sharpness question posed in \cite[Question~11.1]{prior23linear}.
The lower example allows cell-dependent steps and persists for phases
coming from a prime cyclic ambient group.

\paragraph{Order five selects a different secondary coefficient.}
For $G=\F_5^n$, $\E f=0$, and $u=\|f\|_{U^3}\ll\delta$, the sharp
first two nonconstant terms of the weighted cube supremum are
\[
 6\sqrt2\,\delta^4u^4
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \frac{2^{3/4}}3\,\delta^2u^6.
\]
The proof retains the positive cost of the doubled dominant frequency
and controls the incomplete cubes by the fourth-power Fourier tail.
This turns the previous order estimate into a sharp coefficient with
an $O(u^8)$ remainder.  It also forces the dominant Fourier phase
$\theta$ to satisfy $\cos(5\theta)\to0$ in any family attaining the
secondary term.

\paragraph{A common base refinement can keep its full width.}
For a proper prime-field box $T\times J$ of width at least $m$, a
preliminary partition of $T$ into short index boxes leaves width at
least $m/3$.  Any subsequent common-step base refinement of width $W>1$
extends to a true partition of its product with $J$ into boxes of width
at least $W$.  This uses full residue chains on the final axis.
Combined with common slice covers and affine interpolation, it gives
complete geometric and sampling conclusions under explicit inputs.
The final Section~16 comparison of control functions remains a separate
problem.

\subsection{Scope of the mathematical and computational claims}

The article proves finite theorems and local asymptotics, including two
answers to questions explicitly posed in the preceding project reports.
We do not assert historical priority for all of the combined formulations.
Dirichlet approximation, numerical-semigroup conductors, cube
Cauchy--Schwarz, and two-point affine interpolation are established
ingredients.  The new arguments and the precise comparison with the
earlier reports are identified where they occur.

These results do not constitute a new best general bound for
$r_k(N)$, the largest size of a subset of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with no
nonconstant $k$-term arithmetic progression.  For context, Leng, Sah,
and Sawhney proved the stronger general estimate
$r_k(N)\ll N\exp(- (\log\log N)^{c_k})$ for $k\ge5$ in their 2024
paper \cite{lssbounds}.  Our local results are not compared against that
bound as if they were an alternative global theorem.

The repository snapshot is \snapshottwentythree, retrieved on 6 October 2026.
Its status record explicitly separates completed formal components
from unresolved statements and control-function comparisons
\cite{repo23status}.  We inspected the relevant source and proof
interfaces but did not compile a new Lean development.  The accompanying
Python programs check finite arithmetic and polynomial identities;
the proofs in the article establish the quantified mathematical claims.

\subsection{Reading guide}

Sections~\ref{gsr:dt:23:sec:phase-model}--\ref{gsr:dt:23:sec:partial} form a self-contained
treatment of the phase-partition problem, including exact witnesses and
algorithms.  Section~\ref{gsr:cc:23:five:section} is independent of the partition
argument and proves the characteristic-five cube result.
Section~\ref{gsr:en:23:glue:sec} supplies the geometric gluing theorem and its
conditional Section~16 specialization.  The final sections give a
verification record, integration recommendations, and further research
questions.

For reference, on a finite abelian group we use normalized averages and
the Gowers norm convention
\[
 \|f\|_{U^s}^{2^s}
 =\E_{x,h_1,\ldots,h_s}
 \prod_{v\in\{0,1\}^s}\mathcal C^{|v|}f(x+v\cdot h),
\]
where $\mathcal C$ is complex conjugation.  Fourier coefficients are
$\widehat f(\xi)=\E_xf(x)\overline{\xi(x)}$.  Fourier sums have no
normalizing factor.  For real functions the conjugations in the
physical-space cube product are immaterial.  The cube
Cauchy--Schwarz inequality used below is Gowers's Lemma~3.8
\cite{gowers}; in normalized form it bounds a mixed cube average by the
product of the $U^s$ norms of its $2^s$ vertex functions.

\begin{partabstract}{24}
We develop explicit, self-contained refinements of the structural reductions
in Section~7 of Gowers's \emph{A new proof of Szemer\'edi's theorem}.
First, a cubic supporting-line argument replaces the five-sample
intersection lemma by a three-sample theorem: the retained fraction
$\delta^5/\sqrt2$ becomes $7\delta^3/(3\sqrt6)$, with the same
$90\%$ good-pair conclusion and the same intersection threshold.
We determine the sharp constant in the corresponding scalar moment
relaxation and identify exactly why its two-sample analogue fails.
Second, retaining the actual edge mass of the popular-difference graph
through a one-sample argument yields an elementary energy-to-structure
bound with a linear retained fraction and relative doubling
$2^{17}\kappa^{-6}$.
Third, an injective vertical-fibre argument replaces the loss
$8kC^{4k}$ in the Freiman-restriction lemma by $kC^{2k+1}$.
The two structural improvements combine to replace the order-eight
restriction bound $2^{-1882}\gamma^{1164}|B_0|$ by
$2^{-295}\gamma^{103}|B_0|$.
We also prove weighted and higher-arity selection statements, a
finite-field-vector codomain extension, profile-dependent certificates,
and an optimized threshold formula.
The article separates these local improvements from stronger published
Balog--Szemer\'edi--Gowers results and from global quantitative
Szemer\'edi bounds. It includes complete proofs, a repository-specific
formalization plan, exact finite regression tests, and further research
questions. No new global record or literature-priority claim is made.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small

\label{gsr:fm:24:sec:scope}

The question addressed here is not whether the entire 2001 proof should
be replaced by contemporary higher-order Fourier analysis. It is more
specific: which losses in its elementary structural machinery can be
removed while retaining transparent statements, explicit constants, and
a short dependency chain suitable for formalization?
The answer developed below concerns Gowers's Lemma~7.4,
Proposition~7.3, Lemma~7.5, and Corollary~7.6~\cite{gowers}.
The corresponding statement and proof modules in the supplied
repository were also inspected~\cite{repo24}.

\subsection{The compiled improvement}

For a function $\phi:B_0\to H$ between subsets of abelian groups, a
\emph{respected additive quadruple} is an ordered tuple
$(a,b,c,d)\in B_0^4$ for which
\[
 a+b=c+d,\qquad \phi(a)+\phi(b)=\phi(c)+\phi(d).
\]
Repeated entries are allowed. A Freiman homomorphism of order $k$
preserves every equality between two sums of $k$ domain elements,
again with repetitions allowed.

\begin{theorem}[Explicit order-$k$ restriction]\label{gsr:fm:24:thm:headline}
Let $G$ be an abelian group, $p$ a prime, $B_0\subset G$ a nonempty
finite set of size $m$, and $\phi:B_0\to\F_p$ a function.
Suppose that at least $\gamma m^3$ additive quadruples are respected,
where $\gamma>0$. For every integer $k\ge1$, there is a subset
$B\subseteq B_0$ on which $\phi$ is a Freiman homomorphism of order $k$
and
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:24:eq:headline-general}
 |B|\ge \frac{2^{-(34k+20)}}{k}\,\gamma^{12k+7}m.
\end{equation}
In particular, for $k=8$,
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:24:eq:headline-eight}
 \boxed{\quad |B|\ge 2^{-295}\gamma^{103}|B_0|.\quad}
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\begin{writenote}[6 October 2026; sources 21--27]
\emph{Weaker than source~10 by $2^{10k+6}$} (checked at the write). Source~10's Corollary~\ref{gsr:en:10:cor:improved-order-eight} gives, under the same hypotheses, $|B|\ge2^{-(24k+14)}\gamma^{12k+7}m/k$; the ratio to the bound here is $2^{(34k+20)-(24k+14)}=2^{10k+6}$, which is $2^{86}$ at $k=8$ ($2^{-209}\gamma^{103}$ against $2^{-295}\gamma^{103}$). Both come from a Proposition~7.3-type step followed by a fibre extraction with $Q_k\le C^{2k+1}$; source~10's energy step has the better constants. Like source~10's, this bound implies the conclusion of the formal \file{corollary_7_6} (\file{Sections06\_07.lean}, line~197) where the hypotheses agree, since $\gamma\le1$ gives $2^{-295}\gamma^{103}\ge2^{-1882}\gamma^{1164}$; not formalized.
\end{writenote}

The hypotheses imply $\gamma\le1$: a graph with $m$ points has additive
energy at most $m^3$. The theorem therefore improves the source's lower
bound throughout its meaningful parameter range. Its proof is completed
in Section~\ref{gsr:en:24:sec:compiler}; no asymptotic qualification such as
``$p$ sufficiently large'' is needed.

\subsection{What is classical, what is derived, and what is not claimed}

Dependent random choice, popular-difference graphs, path counting, and
Pl\"unnecke--Ruzsa growth inequalities are established tools
\cite{gowers,foxsudakov,petridis}. Our contribution here is an explicit
reorganization and sharpening of these particular interfaces, including
the scalar certificates and the vertical-fibre bookkeeping. The proofs
establish the stated inequalities independently of any assertion that
their individual formulations have not appeared elsewhere.

Stronger published Balog--Szemer\'edi--Gowers theorems already exist.
For example, Reiher and Schoen obtain a subset of size
$(1-\varepsilon)\kappa^{1/2}|A|$ with relative difference-set bound
$C_\varepsilon\kappa^{-4}$~\cite{reiherschoen}. We explicitly import
that theorem in Section~\ref{gsr:en:24:subsec:modern} to derive a further
restriction estimate, with its dependence on the imported theorem
visible. Thus the elementary energy bound here is not advertised as a
new extremal record.

Nor is a local improvement automatically a new quantitative Szemer\'edi
bound. As a published modern benchmark, Leng, Sah, and Sawhney prove,
for every fixed $\ell\ge5$, a bound of the form
\[
 r_\ell(N)\ll N\exp\bigl(- (\log\log N)^{c_\ell}\bigr)
 \qquad(c_\ell>0)
\]
by substantially different machinery~\cite{lssbounds}.
We do not re-run Gowers's Sections~8--18 with the constants below, and
we make no claim about the best currently available global estimate.
The sharpness result proved here concerns a precisely defined scalar
relaxation, not an unrestricted graph or additive-combinatorial
extremal problem.

\section[{Source 25: Scope, main theorem, and relation to the source}]{Source 25. Scope, main theorem, and relation to the source}\label{gsr:fm:25:sec:d1}
\srcnote{25}{Section 1}
\partsource{\textbf{Added in the fifth write, 6~October 2026. Delivered title block.} ``The Codimension-One Degeneracies of Gowers Arrangements / An asymptotically sharp replacement for Lemma 15.4 and explicit random-selection thresholds / Research manuscript prepared for Vladimir Reshetnikov / Mathematical development and computational checks with ChatGPT / 6 October 2026''; \emph{the PDF author field reads ``Research prepared with ChatGPT for Vladimir Reshetnikov''}. Archive \file{gowers\_arrangement\_degeneracy.zip} (arrival \texttt{d7c4aa399}), manuscript \file{arrangement\_degeneracy.tex} (1,207 lines, 17 pages), pin \texttt{568d1802e} (its \file{SOURCE\_AUDIT.md}, shipped as \file{25-codimension-one-SOURCE\_AUDIT.md}). Printed below: the abstract and Section~1; Sections~2--8 are in Part~II (Section~\ref{gsr:en:sec:degeneracy}), Sections~9--11 in Part~V. Its macro \texttt{\textbackslash card} (an absolute value, not this report's operator) is renamed \texttt{\textbackslash cardtwentyfive}; its `question' environment (``Question'', numbered on its own counter there) is set in this report's `Question' style, numbered within its section (its Questions~1--8 keep their indices).}
\begin{partabstract}{25}
We study the full ternary-moment degeneracy condition in Section 15 of
Gowers's proof of Szemer\'edi's theorem.  For a $d$-arrangement of $k$-cubes,
put $D=(2d+1)k+2d-1$ and $n=2d\,2^k$.  Over a finite field of cardinality
$q$ and characteristic greater than $2d$, with $k\ge1$ and $d\ge2$, we prove
that the number of degenerate labelled arrangements is
\[
 (k+H_d)q^{D-1}+O_{k,d}(q^{D-2}),\qquad
 H_d=\frac{T_{2d}-2\binom{2d}{d}+1}{2},
\]
where $T_m$ is the central trinomial coefficient.  All constants in the
error term are explicit.  In particular, $H_8=2\,585\,444$.  The coefficient
$k+H_d$ is exact: the codimension-one components are precisely the zero
sidelength hyperplanes and a projective family of balanced ternary
cross-section hyperplanes.  Outside those hyperplanes, every remaining
witness has codimension at least two.  The key step is a minimal-Walsh-layer linearization, followed
by use of the moment equations involving the last coordinate that the
original counting argument does not need to retain.  A sharp single-witness
probability, a genuine second-order obstruction, and a small-characteristic
counterexample accompany the classification.  We also prove a finite-field,
arbitrary-$d$ random-selection theorem with exact Riesz-product parameters
and a better explicit ambient-size requirement.  The package includes
reproducible exact finite checks and a ProveIt integration plan.  These are
local refinements, not a claimed improvement of the final quantitative
Szemer\'edi theorem; no proof-assistant verification or literature-priority
claim is made.
\end{partabstract}
\label{gsr:fm:25:sec:main}

Gowers's Lemma 15.4 bounds exceptional arrangements before the random
selection in Lemma 15.5.  In the original notation, its estimate is
\begin{equation}
 \cardtwentyfive{\Dg_{k,d}(\F_N)}\le k\,3^{2d2^k}
 N^{(2d+1)k+2d-2}.
 \label{gsr:fm:25:eq:gowers}
\end{equation}
The proof chooses one nonconstant multilinear moment for each ternary
coefficient pattern, uses a polynomial fibre bound, and then takes a
union bound \cite[pp.~562--565]{gowers}.  The resulting constant treats
all witnesses as though they defined hypersurfaces.  This is the point
we sharpen.

The full definition of degeneracy uses \emph{every} coordinate monomial,
including monomials that contain the last, cross-section coordinate.
Gowers remarks after Lemma 15.4 that his argument could use fewer such
monomials.  For the present purpose, retaining them is decisive: they
usually give a second independent equation.

The ProveIt interface inspected here is
\texttt{Sections14\_15.lean} at commit \sha.  It defines degeneracy by a
ternary coefficient function which is not a \emph{modular} multiple of the
distinguished parity coefficient, and requires all arrangement moments
to vanish \cite{repo25lean}.  Our definition agrees with that interface,
after an invertible change from Boolean to centred sign coordinates.
The existing research README was also inspected to separate this project
from its density-transfer, phase-partition, energy, cube-counting and
floor-pattern developments \cite{repo25research}.

\subsection{Parameters}
Throughout the main results,
\begin{equation}
 k\ge1,\quad d\ge2,\quad q=\cardtwentyfive{\F_q},\quad
 p=\operatorname{char}\F_q>2d,
 \qquad n=2d\,2^k,\quad D=(2d+1)k+2d-1.
 \label{gsr:fm:25:eq:parameters}
\end{equation}
Define
\begin{align}
 T_m&=[z^0](z^{-1}+1+z)^m
     =\sum_{j=0}^{\lfloor m/2\rfloor}\binom mj\binom{m-j}{j},
 \label{gsr:fm:25:eq:trinomial}\\
 H_d&=\frac{T_{2d}-2\binom{2d}{d}+1}{2},
 &L_{k,d}&=k+H_d,
 &U_{k,d}&=\frac{3^{2d2^k}-3^{2d}}{2}.
 \label{gsr:fm:25:eq:constants}
\end{align}
The arrangement count is a count of labelled parameter tuples, including
repeated vertices when these occur.  There are exactly $q^D$ such tuples
satisfying the cross-section relation.

\begin{theorem}[Explicit sharp first-order count]
\label{gsr:fm:25:thm:main}
Under \eqref{gsr:fm:25:eq:parameters}, the number $Z_{k,d}(q)$ of degenerate
arrangements satisfies
\begin{equation}
 L_{k,d}q^{D-1}-\binom{L_{k,d}}2q^{D-2}
 \ \le\ Z_{k,d}(q)\ \le\
 L_{k,d}q^{D-1}+U_{k,d}q^{D-2}.
 \label{gsr:fm:25:eq:mainbounds}
\end{equation}
Consequently, for fixed $k,d$,
\begin{equation}
 \lim_{\substack{q\to\infty\\ \operatorname{char}\F_q>2d}}
 \frac{Z_{k,d}(q)}{q^{D-1}}=k+H_d.
 \label{gsr:fm:25:eq:limit}
\end{equation}
Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero or greater than
$2d$, the codimension-one irreducible components of the same degeneracy
locus are exactly $k+H_d$ explicitly described hyperplanes.
\end{theorem}

\begin{writenote}[6 October 2026; sources 21--27]
\emph{Against the formal statement} (checked at the write). \file{lemma_15_4} (\file{Sections14\_15.lean}, line~402) bounds the count by $k3^nq^{D-1}$, $n=2d2^k$, for prime $q$. Here $L_{k,d}+U_{k,d}/q\le k3^n$ for $d\ge2$, $q\ge5$: $H_d\le(3^{2d}+1)/2\le(3^{n/2}+1)/2$ because $n\ge4d$, and $U_{k,d}/q<3^n/10$, so $L_{k,d}+U_{k,d}/q<k+(3^{n/2}+1)/2+3^n/10\le k3^n$ (already for $k=1$, since $0.9\cdot3^n-1\ge(3^{n/2}+1)/2$ for $n\ge8$). So the theorem implies the formal bound for $d\ge2$ and primes $q>2d$, as source~18's does; not formalized. Its predicate is the formal one (note in Section~\ref{gsr:fz:25:sec:d9}).
\end{writenote}

The proof occupies Sections~\ref{gsr:en:25:sec:walsh}--\ref{gsr:en:25:sec:global}.
The leading constant cannot be reduced.  For the $8$-arrangements actually
used by Gowers, \eqref{gsr:fm:25:eq:mainbounds} gives
\begin{equation}
 Z_{k,8}(q)\le
 (k+2\,585\,444)q^{17k+14}
 +\frac{3^{2^{k+4}}-3^{16}}2\,q^{17k+13}.
 \label{gsr:fm:25:eq:d8}
\end{equation}
Thus the enormous ternary-pattern count has moved from the leading
$q^{-1}$ term to a $q^{-2}$ error term.  This does not eliminate the
large error constant, and it is not a dimension-uniform asymptotic.

\subsection{What is, and is not, established}
The main contributions developed here are the minimal-layer rank bound,
the separation of parity and non-parity degeneracies, the exact projective
hyperplane count, and their combination into \eqref{gsr:fm:25:eq:mainbounds}.
Section~\ref{gsr:en:25:sec:selection} gives a self-contained quantitative application
to the selection step.  The hypotheses $d\ge2$ and $p>2d$ are substantive;
we show what fails without them.

The proofs are conventional mathematical proofs, supplemented by finite
exact computations.  They have not been independently refereed or
formalized in Lean.  A targeted source search does not establish priority
for the classification in the broader literature.  In particular, the
standard finite-field viewpoint on hyperplane arrangements is classical
\cite{athanasiadis}; it is not presented here as a new method.  Nor do we
claim to have propagated these local savings through Sections 16--18 to
obtain a new bound for progression-free sets.

\section[{Source 26: The question and the scope}]{Source 26. The question and the scope}\label{gsr:fm:26:sec:d1}
\srcnote{26}{Section 1}
\partsource{\textbf{Added in the fifth write, 6~October 2026. Delivered title block.} ``Threshold free affine density increments on cyclic groups / Report275 / Research report prepared for Vladimir / 6 October 2026''; the PDF author field reads ``Research report prepared for Vladimir''. Archive \file{Report275\_Threshold\_Free\_Affine\_Density\_Increments.zip} (arrival \texttt{7e827c6f3}), manuscript \file{article.tex} (494 lines, 12 pages), pin \texttt{c94998a5d} (its \file{SOURCES.md}, shipped as \file{26-threshold-free-affine-SOURCES.md}). Printed below: the abstract and Section~1; Sections~2--4 and Appendix~A form a chapter of Part~I (Section~\ref{gsr:dt:sec:cor58}), Sections~5--6 are in Part~V.}
\begin{partabstract}{26}
A family of local affine correlations on disjoint modular progressions covering a set yields a density increment with no scale threshold. We keep the exact balanced mass of the cover. If its shortest progression has length $r$, the set has density $\delta$, the normalized balanced mass is $\mu$, and the summed correlation is at least $\alpha N$, then a proper progression has density at least $\delta+\alpha/3$ and length at least
\[
 \min\left\{\left(\frac{r(1-\delta)}{128\mu}\right)^{1/3},(N/8)^{1/3}\right\}.
\]
A complementary, parent-contained progression has the same density increment and length at least $\sqrt{\alpha r/(24\pi\mu)}$, over every cyclic modulus. For every cyclic modulus and $M$ pairwise two-comparable parents, the resulting guarantees are $(N/M)^{1/3}/8$ and $\sqrt{\alpha(N/M)/(96\pi(1-\delta))}$. This strengthens the full degree-one specialization of a specified repository version of Corollary 5.8. The proofs combine a subgroup-coset moment bound, removal of nonproper directions, and phase-flat residue partitions. A separate appendix records a common-step integer-box almost-cover, with its exact scope. The companion checks bounded identities and regressions; no formal verification, global Ramsey bound, or literature-priority claim is made.
\end{partabstract}

The local density-increment step is a useful place to separate an actual quantitative improvement from a change of hypotheses. The target here is the degree-one part of the repository predicate \texttt{corollary\_5\_8} at the source pin specified in Section~\ref{gsr:fz:26:sec:source}. Its displayed premises do not include a lower-scale assumption. A phase-partition argument alone can demand a minimum parent length that is not supplied by those premises. We avoid this issue by using a second-moment increment when the requested correlation gain is small, and phase refinement when it is large.

The principal results below are self-contained written theorems over cyclic groups. Their strongest form uses the actual balanced mass on the cover and does not require comparable parent lengths. Comparability enters only to express the answer through $N/M$. All progressions in the main body are modular and injectively parameterized. Integer representatives are treated separately in Appendix~\ref{gsr:dt:26:app:boxes}.

The cube-root scale, Dirichlet phase partitioning, and progression moments have classical precedents. Section~\ref{gsr:fz:26:sec:source} gives a narrow source comparison. The claims concern the explicit local interfaces proved here; they do not close the general-degree catalogue statement, change the repository's formal status, or improve a final Szemer\'edi or Ramsey bound.

\section[{Source 27: The target and the main conclusions}]{Source 27. The target and the main conclusions}\label{gsr:fm:27:sec:d1}\label{gsr:fm:27:sec:overview}
\srcnote{27}{Section 1}
\partsource{\textbf{Added in the fifth write, 6~October 2026. Delivered title page.} ``Combinatorics / Ramsey theory / Sharp Degeneracy Bounds for Gowers Arrangements / Hyperplane obstructions, second-order structure, and an exact finite-field count / An AI-assisted research draft prepared for Vladimir Reshetnikov and the ProveIt repository / 6 October 2026''; the PDF author field reads ``AI-assisted research draft prepared for Vladimir Reshetnikov''. Archive \file{gowers\_arrangement\_degeneracy (2).zip} (arrival \texttt{6078f6e16}), manuscript \file{article.tex} (1,824 lines, 28 pages); no commit pin: its \file{SOURCE\_AUDIT.md} (shipped as \file{27-degeneracy-second-order-SOURCE\_AUDIT.md}) and its bibliography record blob identifiers only. Printed below: the abstract, the status statement of its title page and Section~1; Sections~2--11 are in Part~II (Section~\ref{gsr:en:sec:degeneracy}), Sections~12--14 and Appendix~A in Part~V. Its \texttt{cleveref} references are written out as its own \texttt{\textbackslash crefname} settings print them (capitalized names, equations as a number in parentheses); its `question' environment (``Research question'', on the shared counter) is set in this report's `Research question' style.}
\begin{partabstract}{27}
Gowers's Lemma 15.4 bounds the proportion of degenerate labelled
$d$-arrangements by $k3^{2d2^k}/q$. We isolate the actual hyperplane
obstructions and prove a sharp first-order asymptotic over every finite-field
characteristic. In sufficiently large characteristic its coefficient is
$k+L_d$, where
\[
 L_d=\frac{\Tc_{2d}-2\binom{2d}{d}+1}{2}
\]
and $\Tc_r$ is the central trinomial coefficient. Outside these hyperplanes,
we classify $S_{k,d}=k(2^{2d}-1)+k(k-1)$ coefficient directions contributing
at order $q^{-2}$, and bound all remaining directions by a cubic remainder.
This replaces a single exponential union bound by separate linear,
square-root, and cube-root field-size requirements.

For $d=2$ the first two asymptotic coefficients are determined explicitly.
For $k=1,d=2$, a finite rational incidence certificate gives the exact
proportion, in every characteristic at least $11$,
\[
 \frac5q+\frac8{q^2}+\frac{40}{q^3}
 -\frac{367}{q^4}+\frac{563}{q^5}-\frac{248}{q^6}.
\]
The general theorems have conventional proofs. The last specialization also
uses a completely specified finite enumeration, reproduced by the accompanying
code and checked independently through subset sums of moment columns.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small
\noindent\textbf{Status and scope.} Unrefereed research draft; no proof-assistant
verification or independent mathematical review is claimed. Priority for the
refinements has not been established. These are local strengthenings of an
exceptional-arrangement lemma, not a claimed new global bound for
Szemer\'edi's theorem. The all-squarefree-moments definition of degeneracy is
essential.
\end{quote}

Gowers's proof of Szemer\'edi's theorem uses higher-dimensional arrangements
and a random selection step that favors arrangements respected by a partial
map. Lemma 15.4 controls the exceptional arrangements on which the expected
selection behavior can fail \cite[\S15, pp.~562--565]{gowers}. This article
studies that exceptional set itself. The aim is to replace a coarse count of
possible coefficient arrays by a structural classification of their zero
sets.

The relevant conventions are fixed in Section~\ref{gsr:en:27:sec:setup}. In particular,
arrangements are \emph{labelled parameter tuples}, not unlabelled geometric
sets; repeated vertices are allowed. Write
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:27:eq:dimensions}
 n=2d,\qquad m=n2^k,\qquad D=(n+1)k+n-1.
\end{equation}
There are exactly $q^D$ arrangements in the full ambient space. Let
$\Delta_{k,d}(q)$ be the fraction that are degenerate. Unless explicitly stated
otherwise, $k\ge1$ and $d\ge2$.

The printed bound in Lemma 15.4 is
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:27:eq:gowers}
 \Delta_{k,d}(q)\le \frac{k3^m}{q}
\end{equation}
in its prime-field setting \cite[p.~563]{gowers}. It is obtained by charging
roughly $k/q$ to each ternary coefficient array. Most arrays do not define a
hypersurface of bad arrangements. That observation is the source of the
improvement.

\subsection{Clean large-characteristic statements}

Define the central trinomial coefficient and three explicit constants by
\begin{align}
 \Tc_r&=[z^0](z^{-1}+1+z)^r
       =\sum_{j=0}^{\lfloor r/2\rfloor}\binom r{2j}\binom{2j}{j},\label{gsr:fm:27:eq:trinomial}\\
 L_d&=\frac{\Tc_n-2\binom n{n/2}+1}{2},\label{gsr:fm:27:eq:Llarge}\\
 R_{k,d}&=\frac{\Tc_m-2\binom m{m/2}-3^n+2^{n+1}}{2},\label{gsr:fm:27:eq:Rlarge}\\
 S_{k,d}&=k(2^n-1)+k(k-1).\label{gsr:fm:27:eq:S}
\end{align}
The integrality and the meaning of these quantities will be proved, rather
than assumed. $L_d$ counts cross-section hyperplanes; $R_{k,d}$ counts
non-parity coefficient directions; $S_{k,d}$ counts a distinguished
second-order subfamily.

\begin{theorem}[Sharp first order and a cubic remainder]\label{gsr:fm:27:thm:main}
Let $\F_q$ have characteristic $p>m=2d2^k$. Put $A=k+L_d$. Then
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:27:eq:mainbounds}
 \frac A q-\frac{\binom A2}{q^2}
 \ \le\ \Delta_{k,d}(q)
 \ \le\ \frac A q+\frac{S_{k,d}}{q^2}
                    +\frac{R_{k,d}-S_{k,d}}{q^3}.
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:27:eq:firstasy}
 \Delta_{k,d}(q)=\frac{k+L_d}{q}+O_{k,d}(q^{-2}).
\end{equation}
The coefficient $k+L_d$ is sharp.
\end{theorem}

\begin{writenote}[6 October 2026; sources 21--27]
\emph{Against the formal statement} (checked at the write). \file{lemma_15_4} (\file{Sections14\_15.lean}, line~402) gives $\Delta_{k,d}(N)\le k3^m/N$ for primes $N$, $m=2d2^k$. For $p>m$ the upper bound here is at most $(k+L_d)/q+S_{k,d}/q^2+R_{k,d}/q^3$ with $L_d\le(3^{m/2}+1)/2$, $S_{k,d}<k(2^{m/2}+k)$ and $R_{k,d}<(3^m+2^{m/2+1})/2$; since $q>m\ge8$ these give less than $k3^m/q$. So the theorem implies the formal bound for $d\ge2$ and primes $p>m$, as source~18's does for $p>2d$; not formalized.
\end{writenote}

The displayed lower bound may be negative for small $q$; it can always be
replaced by its maximum with $0$. Likewise any upper bound can be capped at
$1$. The theorem is useful as a stratified estimate, not merely as a
fixed-parameter asymptotic. The $q^{-1}$ coefficient no longer grows
exponentially in $2^k$.

\begin{corollary}[An explicit exceptional-set budget]\label{gsr:fm:27:cor:budget}
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{gsr:fm:27:thm:main}, let $0<\eps\le1$. It is sufficient
for $\Delta_{k,d}(q)\le\eps$ that
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:27:eq:threshold}
 q\ge\max\left\{
 \frac{3(k+L_d)}{\eps},\quad
 \sqrt{\frac{3S_{k,d}}{\eps}},\quad
 \sqrt[3]{\frac{3(R_{k,d}-S_{k,d})}{\eps}}
 \right\}.
\end{equation}
The characteristic hypothesis is separate from this size requirement.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
Each of the three nonnegative summands in the upper bound in
\eqref{gsr:fm:27:eq:mainbounds} is at most $\eps/3$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Two pairs of cross sections]\label{gsr:fm:27:thm:d2main}
For $d=2$, $k\ge1$, and characteristic $p>4\cdot2^k$,
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:27:eq:d2asy}
 \Delta_{k,2}(q)=\frac{k+4}{q}
       +\frac{k^2+21k-6}{2q^2}+O_k(q^{-3}).
\end{equation}
For $k=1,d=2$ the following exact formula holds over every finite field of
characteristic at least $11$:
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:27:eq:exactmain}
 \Delta_{1,2}(q)=\frac5q+\frac8{q^2}+\frac{40}{q^3}
              -\frac{367}{q^4}+\frac{563}{q^5}-\frac{248}{q^6}.
\end{equation}
The exact formula uses the finite incidence certificate in
Section~\ref{gsr:en:27:sec:exact}; the asymptotic formula does not.
\end{theorem}

\begin{writenote}[6 October 2026; sources 21--27]
\emph{Answers source~18's first question for $d=2$} (item~\ref{gsr:fz:q:II:degeneracy}; also source~22's first and source~25's first question). Checked at the write: Corollary~\ref{gsr:en:27:cor:general2} with $L_2=4$, $S_{k,2}=15k+k(k-1)=k^2+14k$ and $b_{2,2,p}=3$ (Proposition~\ref{gsr:en:27:prop:g2}) gives $S_{k,2}-\binom k2-4k-3=(k^2+21k-6)/2$, that is $8,20,33,47$ for $k=1,\ldots,4$; at $k=1$ this is the $8/q^2$ of the exact formula. The intake confirmed the exact formula by an independent exhaustive count at $q=11,13,17,19,23$ (a different normalization and a meet-in-the-middle count of all ternary relations), and found it fails at $q=5,7$, as the source says. A Monte Carlo at $k=2$ ($q=53$ and~$101$) found the core part near $S_{2,2}/q^2=32/q^2$ and the rest shrinking like $q^{-3}$; that is evidence for the case $k=2$, not a proof. The asymptotic needs characteristic $p>4\cdot2^k$ as stated; its proof needs only $p>2k+2$ (the remark in Section~\ref{gsr:en:27:sec:d6}).
\end{writenote}

\subsection{What is proved, and what is not}

The principal contributions are the classification of the first-order
obstructions, the exact second-order coefficient-direction count, the
cubic-remainder bound, and the exact eight-vertex specialization. The
all-characteristic extension in Section~\ref{gsr:en:27:sec:allchar} is not a formal consequence
of the original odd-prime Walsh argument: it uses Boolean coefficient
extraction, which is valid in characteristic two as well.

The argument does not change the definition of an arrangement, claim a new
inverse theorem, or rerun the whole proof of Szemer\'edi's theorem. In
particular, reducing one exceptional-set threshold does not by itself prove a
better final density bound. The proposed questions in Section~\ref{gsr:fz:27:sec:questions}
separate further local problems from that global bookkeeping task.

The repository source inspected for compatibility is
\gitpath{Combinatorics/Ramsey/Lean/GowersSzemeredi/Sections14_15.lean}
\cite{repo27}. It defines the moments, modular-multiple exclusion, and
Lemma 15.4 proposition used here. A proposition-valued statement in that file
is not evidence that the new theorems in this article have been formalized.
A precise integration map appears in Section~\ref{gsr:fz:27:sec:formal}.

Its sentence in Section~\ref{gsr:fz:27:sec:formal} that the research directory ``already contains numerous local refinements'' and that this article ``focuses on the degeneracy count rather than reproducing'' them overlooks sources~18 and~22. New in this report: the first order in every characteristic (Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:27:thm:allchar}), the core-direction classification with a cubic remainder (Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:27:thm:resolved}), the second coefficient for $d=2$ (Theorem~\ref{gsr:fm:27:thm:d2main}), which answers source~18's first question for $d=2$, the reduction of general $d$ to the statistic $b_{2,d,p}$ (Corollary~\ref{gsr:en:27:cor:general2}), and the exact eight-vertex count. Its endpoint $k=d=1$ (Proposition~\ref{gsr:en:27:prop:d1}) is source~22's Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:22:thm:twocube} at $k=1$.
\end{writenote}

\srcnote{28}{Section 1}

Delivered title page.} ``ProveIt research report / Logarithmic Selection, Local Freiman Models, and Higher Uniformity / Refinements of Gowers's Szemer\'edi framework / Prepared for Vladimir Reshetnikov / Mathematical development and computational checks with ChatGPT / 6 October 2026''; \emph{the PDF author field reads ``Research report prepared with ChatGPT for Vladimir Reshetnikov''}. \begin{partabstract}{28}
We refine two local questions arising from W.\ T.\ Gowers's proof of
Szemer\'edi's theorem and the accompanying ProveIt research collection.
The main result replaces the component selection in Section~10 by
random windows in the logarithms of the fibre size and the anchored
additive-energy weight. Boundary losses are measured with those same
weights. This retains the correlation between useful mass and exceptional
mass throughout the selection argument. We then normalize the anchored
agreement directly, choose modal directional differences, and use coupled
paths to obtain an exact Freiman model.

For a domain of density \(\alpha\) and an order-eight relation defect at
most \(2^{-21}\), the resulting theorem retains at least
\(\alpha(\log2)^2/[20\log(32/\alpha)\log(32/\alpha^2)]\) of the original
points. Its spectrum has size at most
\(2^{34}(1+\alpha)/[(\log2)\alpha^3]\), and its Bohr radius is at least
\((\log2)^2\alpha^5/[3\cdot2^{69}\pi(1+\alpha)^2]\).
The source group may be any finite abelian group and the target any
abelian group. All frequencies come from the original domain.
The local difference map preserves every order-seven relation.
Earlier repository work supplies the conceptual precedents for coupled
paths, dense Freiman extension, and Bohr regularization; these ingredients
are reproved here, and their provenance is separated from the new selection
and parameter chain.

Independently, we examine the open higher-dimensional analogue of the
repository's sharp odd-order \(U^3/U^2\) inequality. An exact two-harmonic
polynomial proves that adding a small negative third harmonic decreases
the \(U^4/U^2\) ratio of a cosine. A rational parameter gives
\(c_4^{\mathrm{odd}}>0.55872939\), improving the single-cosine lower
benchmark \(0.51813359\). We also prove
\(c_d^{\mathrm{odd}}\le\sqrt{160/323}=0.70381534\ldots\) for every
\(d\ge4\), and extend the failure of single-cosine local
extremality to every \(d\ge4\). The sharp constants remain open.
We provide reproducible finite checks, integration interfaces, and
further research questions.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small
\noindent\textbf{Principal conclusions.}
An order-eight approximate homomorphism on a finite abelian domain admits
an exact local model determined by the Fourier coefficients of the
original domain. The guaranteed retained fraction is
\[
 \frac{\alpha(\log 2)^2}
 {20\log(32/\alpha)\log(32/\alpha^2)},
\]
the number of defining frequencies is \(O(\alpha^{-3})\), and the
guaranteed Bohr radius is \(\Omega(\alpha^5)\).
The allowed proportion of failed order-eight relations is \(2^{-21}\).

\smallskip
Exact norm calculations give a new interval for the odd-order
\(U^4/U^2\) comparison constant and prove that a single cosine is
not locally extremal at any order \(d\ge4\) when the character
order is sufficiently large.

\smallskip
\noindent Repository comparison pinned to \pintwentyeight.
Complete proofs, exact finite certificates, and a proposed research agenda.
Research draft; no new Lean verification or global Szemer\'edi bound is asserted.
\end{quote}

The task is to strengthen actual steps of Gowers's argument while retaining
the information needed by later steps. Section~10 is a particularly useful
target: the set of frequencies in its conclusion must be extracted from
the original domain, not from an arbitrarily selected structured subset.
Gowers's Theorem~10.13 is designed to preserve exactly that information
\cite{gowers}. The theorem below has the same purpose, with different
explicit controls.

\subsection{The main local-model theorem}

Let \(G\) be a finite abelian group, of cardinality \(N\). A
\emph{finite domain over \(G\)} consists of a nonempty finite set \(X\)
and a map \(r:X\to G\). Put \(X_s=r^{-1}(s)\).
An order-\(k\) approximate homomorphism \(\phi:X\to H\), where \(H\) is
abelian, respects a prescribed proportion of the ordered \(2k\)-tuples
whose two base sums agree. Exact definitions appear in
section~\ref{gsr:en:28:sec:conventions}. Fourier coefficients in the next theorem are
unnormalized.

\begin{theorem}[A spectrum-defined exact local model]\label{gsr:fm:28:thm:main}
Let \(G\) be finite abelian, let \(H\) be abelian, and suppose
\[
 0<\alpha\le1,\qquad M>0,\qquad |X_s|\le M,\qquad |X|=\alpha MN.
\]
Suppose \(\phi:X\to H\) respects at least a fraction \(1-2^{-21}\) of
the order-eight relations of the domain. Define
\begin{align}
 p(\alpha)&=\frac{(\log2)^2}
 {\log(32/\alpha)\log(32/\alpha^2)},\label{gsr:fm:28:eq:p-main}\\
 \lambda(\alpha)&=2^{-17}\alpha^2
       \sqrt{\frac{\log2}{1+\alpha}},\label{gsr:fm:28:eq:lambda-main}\\
 g(s)&=|X_s|,\qquad
 \Gamma=\{\chi\in\widehat G:|\widehat g(\chi)|
                        \ge\lambda(\alpha)MN\},\\
 R_\alpha&=\frac{2^{34}(1+\alpha)}{(\log2)\alpha^3},\label{gsr:fm:28:eq:rank-main}\\
 \zeta_\alpha&=\frac{(\log2)^2\alpha^5}
                  {3\cdot2^{69}\pi(1+\alpha)^2}.\label{gsr:fm:28:eq:zeta-main}
\end{align}
Then \(|\Gamma|\le\min\{N,R_\alpha\}\).
There are \(Y\subseteq X\) and a Freiman homomorphism
\[
 \Psi:C\longrightarrow H,\qquad C=\Bhr(\Gamma,\zeta_\alpha),
\]
such that
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:28:eq:mass-main}
 |Y|\ge \frac{\alpha p(\alpha)}{20}|X|,\qquad \Psi(0)=0,
\end{equation}
and, whenever \(y,z\in Y\) and \(r(y)-r(z)\in C\),
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:28:eq:model-main}
 \phi(y)-\phi(z)=\Psi(r(y)-r(z)).
\end{equation}
In fact \(\Psi\) can be taken to preserve every order-seven relation
in \(C\), with the same parameters.
\end{theorem}

The set \(Y\) can depend on \(\phi\), while \(\Gamma\) depends only on
the fibre-count function \(g\). This distinction matters in the
multilinear stages of the source argument.
No assumption of prime order is needed in theorem~\ref{gsr:fm:28:thm:main}; primality
enters only if one wants to write a local additive map in cyclic
coordinates as multiplication by a scalar.

\subsection{What is improved relative to the inspected sources}

transcription, the formal development, a compiled collection of five
earlier reports, and supporting files for later reports. We additionally
retrieved and read the historical manuscripts of source~07
\cite{repo28seven} and source~12 \cite{repo28twelve}. Their earlier ideas are important
inputs to the present development.

available internally in the earlier formal argument. We do not claim it
as a new result. Likewise, polynomial Bohr radii, the full-fourth-moment
smoothing estimate, and coupled-path rigidity were already developed in
sources~12 and~07. The new work is the logarithmic component lemma,
the energy-weighted boundary estimate, their connection to a directly
normalized anchor law, and the complete resulting theorem.
The historical printed and corrected statements have different constants
and density qualifications; the comparison in table~\ref{gsr:fm:28:tab:comparison}
uses the corrected repository statement and the explicit sparse branch
of source~12, not the unrepaired printed density claim.

\subsection{A second result: the higher-norm extremizer changes}

For real centered functions on odd-order groups, the earlier collection
proves
\[
 \|f\|_{U^3}^8\ge2\|f\|_{U^2}^8,
\]
with equality for one conjugate pair of Fourier frequencies
\cite{repo28four}. It asks for the sharp comparison at higher orders.
It is therefore natural to test the same proposed extremizer at \(U^4\).
This test fails.

If a character \(\chi\) has order greater than \(24\), put
\[
 f_b=\chi+\chi^{-1}+b(\chi^3+\chi^{-3}),\qquad b\in\R.
\]
The exact calculation in the second part of the article gives
\[
 \left.\frac{d}{db}
 \frac{\|f_b\|_{U^4}^{16}}{\|f_b\|_{U^2}^{16}}\right|_{b=0}=54>0.
\]
Consequently a sufficiently small \emph{negative} third harmonic improves
on the cosine. We prove an analogous nonstationarity statement for every
\(d\ge4\), with an explicit sufficient character-order condition.
This rules out a natural extrapolation; it does not determine the true
optimal constants.

\subsection{Status and reading guide}

The mathematical claims are supported by complete arguments below.
Some finite polynomial coefficients additionally have short, exact,
reproducible enumerations. The manuscript has received independent
derivation and adversarial checking within this work, but has not been
peer reviewed or verified in Lean. The package records the checks rather
than treating computation as a substitute for proof.

There is no claim of priority over the full literature. Modern inverse
theorems, such as the quasipolynomial work of Leng, Sah, and Sawhney
\cite{lssinverse}, address a broader quantitative theory. Our explicit local
model is intended for the particular information-preserving interface
in this repository. Improving that interface does not by itself close
the later Section~13, Section~16, and Section~18 obligations.

\begin{partabstract}{29}
We prove three families of local refinements connected to Gowers's proof
of Szemer\'edi's theorem and to the existing ProveIt research reports.
First, a positive Fourier-moment argument gives
\(\|f\|_{U^d}^{2^d}\ge
2^{-m}\binom{2m}{m}\|f\|_{U^2}^{2^d}\), where
\(m=2^{d-2}\), for real functions whose Fourier transform vanishes on
the characters of order at most two. For centered functions on odd-order
groups this improves the previously used monotonicity bound for every
\(d\ge4\); in dimension four the coefficient improves from \(4\) to
\(35/8\). We give the full torsion-dependent moment polynomial,
moment-level equality and stability, and bounds on the unresolved sharp
higher-norm constants.

Second, we prove an explicit joint stability theorem at the absolute
endpoint of the derivative-spectrum inequality. If a nonnegative
selector with row sums at most one captures \(1-\varepsilon\) of the
maximum squared derivative correlation, with \(0\le\varepsilon\le2^{-9}\),
then the function and selector
are simultaneously within \(24\varepsilon\), in normalized squared
\(L^2\) error and missing graph mass respectively, of a quadratic phase
and its derivative graph. A mixed version recovers a common quadratic
part and a relative character for two functions. The proof works on
every finite abelian group, including even-order groups, and the linear
order of the error is optimal.

Third, we retain every affine-rank stratum in a previously introduced
random graph restriction. For a fixed finite field and a fixed
translation-invariant linear system with \(s\) free coordinates, the
size threshold becomes proportional to \((\alpha\eta)^{-1}\), with
retention proportional to \(\alpha^{s+1}\eta^s|B|^s\). Repeated entries
and degenerate tuples are included exactly. A weaker coefficient removes
the threshold altogether. Complete proofs, finite checks, source
comparisons, and further research questions are supplied.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small
\noindent Unrefereed research manuscript. No new Lean formalization is claimed.
No improvement of the global Szemer\'edi bound is claimed.
\end{quote}
\label{gsr:fm:29:gmsr:intro}

The aim is to strengthen interfaces inside an inverse argument while
preserving the hypotheses under which they can be used. Three kinds of
information are retained here: the positive Fourier coefficients of an
autocorrelation, the orthogonal residual of a derivative spectrum, and
the actual affine rank of a configuration. Discarding these quantities
too early loses constants, stability rates, or size thresholds.

The original reference is Gowers's 2001 paper \cite{gowers}. Its
Lemma~3.10 bounds cube counts from uniformity, Proposition~6.1 extracts
additive structure from derivative correlations, and Lemma~9.3 improves
the proportion of relations respected after restriction. Our results
concern these local themes. The normalizations and domains below are
stated independently, so they can be compared with the corrected
repository interfaces without treating different hypotheses as
interchangeable.

\subsection{What is added to the inspected material}

The repository was inspected at the commit
\begin{center}\small\codetwentynine{e3125e6982abe2d44bd7cb9369063d4e69d41a2d}.\end{center}
The existing combined report \cite{repo29report} proves the sharp
real-centered \(U^3/U^2\) gap and an exact full-graph endpoint, and asks
about higher norm gaps and joint stability. The restriction manuscript
numbered source~17 \cite{repo29restriction} already introduces random
linear maps on augmented graph points and asks whether affine-rank
stratification can improve its exceptional-tuple threshold. These are
the immediate mathematical starting points.

Source~28, written from the same pin, proves overlapping bounds for $c_d^{\mathrm{odd}}$; neither cites the other.

The central-binomial estimate is an application of the classical
multinomial moment method; related Steinhaus expansions appear, for
example, in \cite[Section~8.3]{foucartrauhut}. Qualitative stability of
near-maximal Gowers norms is established by Eisner and Tao
\cite[Theorems~1.1 and~1.4]{eisnertao}. They also explain that their
methods yield effective polynomial rates. Our contribution in that
direction is the explicit joint derivative-selector interface, including
unbounded \(L^2\) functions and the mixed setting. The homomorphism
repair used in its proof belongs to the self-correction tradition of
Blum, Luby, and Rubinfeld \cite{blr}, with the test-error comparison
also familiar from \cite{benor}; we prove the precise version
needed. The derivative correlations are finite short-time Fourier
transforms. The quadratic geometry of their exact support minimizers is
established in Nicola's work \cite{nicola}; our statements quantify a
particular near-endpoint problem with a prescribed selector.

These are proved local extensions and answers to specified questions in
the repository. A targeted literature check is not an exhaustive
priority determination. In particular, the paper does not announce a
new qualitative inverse theorem, a sharp value of the higher norm
constants, or a solution of the unrestricted weighted relative-energy
stability problem. The general bound of Leng, Sah, and Sawhney
\cite{lssbounds},
\[
 r_k(N)\ll_k N\exp\bigl(- (\log\log N)^{c_k}\bigr),\qquad k\ge5,
\]
is a literature benchmark for comparison; no substitution through an
entire density-increment iteration is performed here.

\subsection{Guide to the manuscript}

Sections~\ref{gsr:cc:29:gmsr:notation}--\ref{gsr:cc:29:gmsr:constants} develop the higher-norm
bounds and their precise sharpness limitations.
Sections~\ref{gsr:en:29:gmsr:joint}--\ref{gsr:en:29:gmsr:mixed} establish joint quadratic
rigidity and its consequences.
Section~\ref{gsr:en:29:gmsr:restriction} proves the restriction results, including
the generic higher-error-rank improvement.
The final sections explain integration, verification, and open research
directions. Every theorem in the three main families is proved in this
manuscript; the included code supplies finite checks of identities and
examples rather than substitutes for those proofs.

Archive \file{Gowers\_Fixed\_Radius\_Bohr\_Invariance.zip} (arrival \texttt{12da35673}), manuscript \file{article.tex} (1,278 lines, 19 pages), pin \texttt{8d65d3c9f} (its \file{SOURCE\_AUDIT.md}, shipped as \file{30-fixed-radius-bohr-SOURCE\_AUDIT.md}). Printed below: the abstract, the integration target and status lines after it, and Section~1; Sections~2--9 are in Part~II (Section~\ref{gsr:en:sec:section10}), Sections~10--12 and Appendix~A in Part~V. Its macros \texttt{\textbackslash defect} (an operator, not this report's $\varepsilon$) and \texttt{\textbackslash pin} are renamed \texttt{\textbackslash defectthirty} and \texttt{\textbackslash pinthirty}; its `question' environment (``Question'', on its own counter) is set in this report's `Question' style, and its Questions~1--12 keep their indices. It numbers equations consecutively through the manuscript; here they are numbered within sections.}
\begin{partabstract}{30}
We give a direct fixed-radius replacement for the Bohr translation estimate
in Lemma 10.10 of Gowers's proof of Szemer\'edi's theorem. For a rectangular
Bohr set $B$ defined by $r$ characters, with widths at most $1/4$, a shift
whose coordinates are at most $1/(2m)$ of the corresponding widths satisfies
\[
 2m\bigl(|B|-|B\cap(B+d)|\bigr)
 \le |B(3\boldsymbol\rho/2)|-|B|
 \le (3^r-1)|B|.
\]
The proof packs two families of disjoint outward translates of the escape
sets into a larger Bohr shell. It uses neither a regular-radius selection nor
a lower bound for the density of $B$ in the ambient group. The first
inequality is exactly sharp already for intervals in cyclic groups.

As a consequence, the corrected radius
$\rho^r/(2^{r+4}r)$ in Corollary 10.11 can, for $0<\rho\le1/4$, be
replaced by $\rho/[8(3^r-1)]$ while preserving its overlap margins, or by
$\rho/(6\cdot3^r-4)$ for the extension conclusion alone. We give a
higher-order extension theorem, an explicit density-sensitive version of
the compatibility step underlying Lemma 10.12, and exact finite checks.
An explicit Chinese-remainder construction shows that exponential dependence
on the number of characters is unavoidable in a universal fixed-radius
translation bound, even for cyclic groups of composite order. The upper
and lower exponential bases do not match. These are local refinements with
complete mathematical proofs; no new global bound for Szemer\'edi's theorem,
literature-priority claim, or proof-assistant verification is asserted.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small
\noindent\textbf{Integration target.} \path{Combinatorics/Ramsey/Research/GowersSzemeredi/}
\par\noindent\textbf{Status.} Unrefereed research manuscript. Exact checks supplement, and do
not replace, the proofs. The existing repository is not modified by this package.
\end{quote}
\label{gsr:fm:30:sec:introduction}

\subsection{The local loss being removed}
Let $G=\Z/N\Z$ and let $K$ be a set of $r$ frequencies. We use the angular
normalization
\[
 B(K,\rho)=\{x\in G:\normt{kx/N}\le\rho\text{ for every }k\in K\},
 \qquad \T=\R/\Z.
\]
Gowers's Lemma 10.10 gives the estimate
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:30:eq:old}
 |B\cap(B+d)|\ge
 \bigl(1-2^{r+1}r\rho^{-r}\zeta\bigr)|B|,
 \qquad d\in B(K,\zeta).
\end{equation}
Its proof first bounds the number of points near coordinate boundaries in
terms of the ambient cardinality $N$, and then compares $N$ with $|B|$.
The latter comparison introduces a power $\rho^{-r}$. This is the specific
loss targeted here, not the much larger collection of losses elsewhere in
the Szemer\'edi argument \cite[Section 10]{gowers}.

The repository's corrected Corollary 10.11 uses
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:30:eq:oldradius}
 \zeta_{\mathrm{old}}=\frac{\rho^r}{2^{r+4}r}.
\end{equation}
It explicitly divides by $r$. The printed paper instead multiplies by $r$;
that expression does not give the overlap claimed in the proof. Our
comparison is with the corrected repository expression, not with the
misprint. The exact declarations inspected are \path{lemma_10_10} and
\path{corollary_10_11} in \path{Section10.lean} at the pin recorded in
Section~\ref{gsr:fz:30:sec:audit} \cite{repo30}.

\subsection{What is proved here}
Write $c_r=3^r-1$. The principal conclusions are as follows.

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*)]
\item \textbf{An intrinsic escape bound.} If $B=B(\boldsymbol\chi,
\boldsymbol\rho)$, $0<\rho_i\le1/4$, and
$\normt{\chi_i(d)}\le\rho_i/(2m)$, then
\[
 2m\defectthirty_B(d)\le
 |B(\boldsymbol\rho+m\boldsymbol v)|-|B|
 \le |B(3\boldsymbol\rho/2)|-|B|,
 \quad v_i=\normt{\chi_i(d)}.
\]
Here $\defectthirty_B(d)=|B|-|B\cap(B+d)|$. This holds in every finite abelian
group, for unequal widths, without changing $B$.
\item \textbf{A larger extension neighborhood.} At density $7/8$ inside
$B$, the radius $\rho/[8c_r]$ preserves the original $7/8$, $5/8$, and
$1/8$ overlap margins. The still larger radius $\rho/(6c_r+2)$ suffices
for the Freiman extension conclusion itself.
\item \textbf{A rank obstruction.} For $r=2s+1$, a universal estimate of
$\defectthirty_B(d)/|B|$ by a coefficient depending only on $r$ times the
relative shift must have coefficient at least $3^s/2$ in the
small-shift limit. The examples can be taken in cyclic groups, but their
orders are composite.
\end{enumerate}

The auxiliary extension and compatibility arguments retain their exact
hole and error budgets. This yields a general order-$k$ statement and, in
the setting spelled out in Section~\ref{gsr:en:30:sec:compatibility}, the sufficient
condition $\sqrt\theta<5/14$ instead of the coarser $5/16$ obtained by
measuring both exceptional direction sets against $|B|$.

\subsection{Relation to regular and smoothed Bohr sets}
Regular-radius arguments and smoothing are established tools, not new
ideas of this manuscript. Green explains the radial boundary problem and
Bourgain's regular-radius remedy, and develops smoothed Bohr
neighborhoods \cite[Sections 3--4]{greenregularity}. The distinction here is that the
input set, its radius, the dense subset, and the partial map are all kept
unchanged. Changing the radius after a partial map has been constructed
may change its domain and its relative density. The present argument pays
an exponential cost in the number of characters to avoid that operation.

In particular, our result is not a radial regularity theorem. A Bohr set can
have many points exactly on its boundary, so even a tiny radial contraction
can remove many points. A translation by an actually available small group
element is a different operation. The proof below exploits that element's
orbit and the long interval of non-return after a boundary exit.

\subsection{Scope and novelty discipline}
All numbered assertions labeled theorem, lemma, proposition, or corollary
below have proofs. Questions are stated separately. The new research focus
is the fixed-radius escape inequality and its quantitative consequences;
the elementary packing and Freiman telescoping arguments are presented
as supporting tools, not as newly discovered principles. The literature
check is targeted, not exhaustive. The explicit family in
Section~\ref{gsr:en:30:sec:obstruction} refutes a precisely formulated possible
polynomial-rank improvement; we do not identify that possibility as a
previously published open conjecture.

The work does not change the formal status of any repository result. It
does not establish a new bound for the largest progression-free subset of
$\{1,\ldots,N\}$, and does not assert an improved full Theorem 10.13 merely
from substitution into one local step.

\section[{Source 31: The problem, the contributions, and their scope}]{Source 31. The problem, the contributions, and their scope}\label{gsr:fm:31:sec:d1}
\srcnote{31}{Section 1}
\partsource{\textbf{Added in the sixth write, 6~October 2026. Delivered title block.} ``Weighted Derivative Spectra and Sharp Local Rigidity / Explicit Freiman restriction, an optimal near-extremal $U^3$ profile, and the limits of stability for correlation weights / Prepared for Vladimir Reshetnikov / Mathematical development and verification with ChatGPT / 6 October 2026''; \emph{the PDF author field reads ``Research developed with ChatGPT for Vladimir Reshetnikov''}. Archive \file{gowers\_weighted\_spectrum\_rigidity.zip} (arrival \texttt{12da35673}), manuscript \file{gowers\_weighted\_spectrum\_rigidity.tex} (1,745 lines, 25 pages), pin \texttt{e3125e698} (its \file{SOURCE\_LEDGER.json}, shipped as \file{data/31-weighted-spectra-SOURCE\_LEDGER.json}). Printed below: the abstract and Section~1; Sections~2--5 and~9 are in Part~II (Section~\ref{gsr:en:sec:endpoint}), Sections~6--8 and Appendix~A in Part~II (Section~\ref{gsr:en:sec:weighted7}), Sections~10--11 and Appendix~B in Part~V. Its macros \texttt{\textbackslash Energy} (a sans-serif $\mathsf E$) and \texttt{\textbackslash ip} are renamed \texttt{\textbackslash Energythirtyone} and \texttt{\textbackslash ipthirtyone}; its `question' environment (``Research question'', on the shared counter) is set in this report's `Research question' style.}
\begin{partabstract}{31}
We develop three connected refinements at the Fourier-to-structure interface
of Gowers' proof of Szemer\'edi's theorem. The first is an exact local
extremal result. For every finite abelian group and every nonzero complex
function $f$, put $\kappa=\|f\|_{U^3}^8/\|f\|_2^8$. If
$\delta=1-\kappa<1/120$, then the best squared correlation with a normalized
quadratic phase supported on a subgroup coset is at least
\[
 1-\Rsharp(\delta),\qquad
 \Rsharp(\delta)=\frac{1-\sqrt{(1+\sqrt{1-4\delta})/2}}{2}.
\]
This function is optimal uniformly over finite abelian groups, with equality
already on the two-element group. A spectral subgroup argument gives an
explicit preliminary bound independent of the group exponent; a quartic
energy calculation then gives the exact profile. We obtain a sharper
full-graph endpoint: a derivative graph of score at least $1-\varepsilon$
admits a symmetric homomorphism with at most $\varepsilon$ errors, and
quadratic-phase infidelity at most
$(1-\sqrt{1-2\varepsilon})/2$, for $\varepsilon\le1/400$.

Second, we carry prescribed nonnegative correlation weights through
additive-energy extraction and an exact Freiman restriction. A weighted
version of the prime-field restriction has retention
$1/(kC^{2k+1})$, compared with $1/(8kC^{4k})$ in Gowers' Lemma~7.5.
The underlying smaller sumset argument is already present in Green--Tao;
we give its finite weighted form and an explicit composition retaining the
original derivative correlation. An order-eight specialization improves
the historical Corollary~7.6 parameters to $2^{-363}c^{171}$ by an elementary
route, with a separate modern comparison using Reiher--Schoen.

Third, we prove a defect inequality that controls Fourier uniformity on the
extremal subgroup and the squared masses of other cosets. An exact
total-variation identity gives linear transfer to a nearby input.
Explicit examples
show why near equality cannot control the weights in normalized $L^1$
without additional complexity assumptions. All principal refinements have
proofs. The article distinguishes these results from classical inverse
theorems, gives reproducible finite checks, and proposes further research.
It does not claim a new global Szemer\'edi bound or Lean certification.
\end{partabstract}

Gowers' argument turns information about Fourier coefficients of derivatives
into additive structure of the frequency labels. Several losses can occur
between these two descriptions: selecting one frequency from a large fiber,
replacing a weight by the size of its support, extracting a small-doubling
subset, and restricting further until every relevant additive relation is
respected. Near an extremal configuration, a different question becomes
available: can the entire function and its selected frequencies be recovered
with an explicit error bound?

This article treats both regimes. For arbitrary positive correlation it
gives weighted extraction with explicit, though deliberately conservative,
polynomial losses. Near the maximum it identifies an exact optimal
stability profile. The same derivative spectrum connects the two arguments.

\subsection{The repository checkpoint}

The source checkpoint is the following revision of
\file{VladimirReshetnikov/ProveIt}:
\begin{center}\small
\texttt{e3125e6982abe2d44bd7cb9369063d4e69d41a2d}.
\end{center}
We inspected the Ramsey transcription of Gowers' paper, the consolidated
\emph{Local Quantitative Refinements} report, the relevant Lean declarations,
and the three newly arrived reports on characteristic five, degree
stratification, and sharp thresholds \cite{repo31,repo31prior,repo31incoming}.
The present subject is distinct from their centered cube-count expansions,
polynomial-coloring thresholds, and arrangement-degeneracy estimates.

Two questions in the consolidated report are especially relevant. Its
Theme~II asks for a structural extraction that retains specified derivative
correlation, and for a description of near equality in the coupled
function--weight energy inequality. The weighted restriction below answers
a prime-cyclic bounded-fiber version of the first question. The sharp phase
theorem and the weight counterexamples provide a positive theorem and a
necessary limitation for the second. These are precise local answers;
compatibility across the later multilinear slices remains a separate issue.

\subsection{Relation to established results}

The qualitative critical-norm statement is established mathematics.
Eisner--Tao \cite[Theorem~1.4]{eisnertao} classify extremizers and near-extremizers
of the critical Gowers norm inequality on locally compact abelian groups.
At order three the critical Lebesgue exponent is two, and the extremizers
are precisely normalized quadratic phases on cosets. We reprove the finite
case needed here and determine an explicit sharp local modulus.

The phase-space language also overlaps directly with stabilizer-state
testing. Gross--Nezami--Walter \cite[Sections~2--3]{gnw} use Weyl
characteristic functions, isotropic subspaces, and large-coefficient
arguments. Our finite-group argument first forces a subgroup by a
small-difference-set lemma and then proves isotropy by averaging operators.
This avoids a lower bound for the separation between distinct roots of
unity. The resulting constants do not depend on the exponent of the group.
The exact local quartic envelope is proved below. A bounded literature
search did not establish an earlier occurrence of this exact profile;
independent bibliographic priority is not certified.

Weighted Balog--Szemer\'edi--Gowers principles are also classical; see
\cite{taonotes,bggt}. The smaller vertical-defect sumset used in
Section~\ref{gsr:en:31:sec:freiman} already appears in Green--Tao
\cite[proof of Lemma~6.2]{greentaoUthree}. We credit that mechanism explicitly.
The contributions at this interface are the weighted finite statement,
the parameter ledger, and the preservation of a specified correlation
through the entire local extraction. The modern set theorem of
Reiher--Schoen \cite{reiherschoen} is stronger than the elementary extraction used for
our self-contained numerical comparison; both routes are recorded.

\paragraph{Meaning of sharpness.}
The modulus in Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:31:thm:sharp} is optimal over the class of all
finite abelian groups. The two bounds in Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:31:thm:graph} are
separately optimal. We do not claim that its joint error inequality, the
cutoff $1/120$, the odd-order quartic envelope, or the extraction exponents
are optimal. A result proved here is not thereby asserted to be a new
global inverse theorem or a solution of an unrestricted open problem.

\section[{Source 32: The theorem and its scope}]{Source 32. The theorem and its scope}\label{gsr:fm:32:sec:d1}\label{gsr:fm:32:sec:main}
\srcnote{32}{Section 1}
\partsource{\textbf{Added in the sixth write, 6~October 2026. Delivered title block.} ``Threshold free quadratic density increments on cyclic groups / Report276 / Research report prepared for Vladimir / 6 October 2026''; the PDF author field reads ``Research report prepared for Vladimir''. Archive \file{Report276\_Threshold\_Free\_Quadratic\_Density\_Increments.zip} (arrival \texttt{6c2e2172b}), manuscript \file{article.tex} (533 lines, 12 pages), pin \texttt{c94998a5d} (its \file{SOURCES.md}, shipped as \file{32-quadratic-increments-SOURCES.md}). Printed below: the abstract and Section~1; Sections~2--5 continue source~26's chapter of Part~I (Section~\ref{gsr:dt:sec:cor58}), Sections~6--7 are in Part~V. It numbers equations consecutively through the manuscript; here they are numbered within sections.}
\begin{partabstract}{32}
Let $A\subseteq\Z/N\Z$ have density $\delta$. Suppose that $M$ disjoint proper modular arithmetic progressions cover $A$, their lengths are pairwise within a factor of two, and degree at most two polynomial phases have summed balanced correlation at least $\alpha N$, where $\alpha>0$. We prove, for every cyclic modulus and with no additional scale hypothesis, that a proper progression $Q$ satisfies
\[
 |Q|\ge\max\left\{1,\frac{(N/M)^{1/39}}{17}\right\},
 \qquad \frac{|A\cap Q|}{|Q|}\ge\delta+\frac\alpha3.
\]
The proof includes an explicit quadratic recurrence estimate, a lossless phase-flat partition, and an all-moduli second-moment argument that handles the small-correlation regime. An explicit singleton comparison shows that the length guarantee also dominates $(N/M)^{1/64}/8$, hence the whole degree-two specialization of a pinned repository Corollary 5.8. All constants and rounding choices are included. The recurrence and localization mechanisms are classical; the report makes no literature-priority, formal-verification, or global Ramsey or Szemer\'edi bound claim. Its executable companion checks bounded exact identities and regressions, rather than certifying the real-parameter theorem numerically.
\end{partabstract}

Write $G=\Z/N\Z$, where $N\ge2$ is an integer. For $t\in\R$ let
\[
 e(t)=\exp(2\pi i t),\qquad
 \norm{t}=\min_{m\in\Z}|t-m|.
\]
For $y\in G$, define $e_N(y)=e(\widetilde y/N)$ using any integer representative $\widetilde y$. A \emph{proper modular arithmetic progression} is a set
\[
 P=\{u+jd:0\le j<n\}\subseteq G
\]
whose displayed parameterization is injective; its length is $n$. A nonzero step need not be invertible. Singletons are proper, and progressions are allowed to wrap in their standard integer representatives.

Let $A\subseteq G$, $\delta=|A|/N$, and $f=\one_A-\delta$. The phases in this report are ordinary coefficient polynomials over $G$:
\[
 \phi_i(x)=a_ix^2+b_ix+c_i,\qquad a_i,b_i,c_i\in G.
\]
Thus degree at most two includes affine and constant phases. No broader definition by vanishing third differences is assumed over composite moduli.

\begin{theorem}[Quadratic local cover increment]\label{gsr:fm:32:thm:main}
Let $M\ge1$ and let $P_1,\ldots,P_M$ be nonempty, pairwise disjoint, proper modular progressions. Suppose
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:32:eq:cover}
 A\subseteq U:=\bigcup_{i=1}^M P_i,
 \qquad |P_i|\le2|P_j|\quad(1\le i,j\le M).
\end{equation}
Let $\phi_i$ have the form above, and suppose $\alpha>0$ and
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:32:eq:corr}
 \sum_{i=1}^M\left|\sum_{x\in P_i}f(x)e_N(-\phi_i(x))\right|
 \ge\alpha N.
\end{equation}
There is a nonempty proper modular progression $Q$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:32:eq:main}
 |Q|\ge\max\left\{1,\frac{(N/M)^{1/39}}{17}\right\},
 \qquad |A\cap Q|\ge\left(\delta+\frac\alpha3\right)|Q|.
\end{equation}
There is no lower bound on $\alpha$ or $N/M$, and no primality or least-prime-factor condition on $N$. The progression $Q$ need not be contained in $U$.
\end{theorem}

Archive \file{Gowers\_Respected\_Arrangement\_Stability.zip} (arrival \texttt{17dd7886c}), manuscript \file{article.tex} (1,623 lines, 24 pages), pin \texttt{9f83dbe0f} (its \file{SOURCE\_AUDIT.md}, shipped as \file{33-arrangement-stability-SOURCE\_AUDIT.md}).
