\section[{Source 42: The arithmetic increment and its meaning}]{Source 42. The arithmetic increment and its meaning}\label{gsr:fm:42:sec:d1}\label{gsr:fm:42:sec:main}
\srcnote{42}{Section 1}
\partsource{\textbf{Added in the eighth write, 7~October 2026. Delivered title block.} ``Sharp quadratic scale density increments on cyclic groups / Report278 / Research report prepared for Vladimir / 7 October 2026''; \emph{the PDF author field reads ``Research report prepared for Vladimir''; no statement on AI assistance is made}. The title page is dated 7~October 2026; the archive arrived at 17:40 on 6~October 2026 (Pacific time). Archive \file{Report278\_Sharp\_Quadratic\_Scale\_Density\_Increments.zip} (arrival \texttt{a6eea2a19}), manuscript \file{article.tex} (688 lines, 15 pages), pin \texttt{b16ce380d} for this report's article, with sources~41 and~26 identified by SHA-256 (its \file{SOURCES.md}, shipped as \file{42-quadratic-scale-SOURCES.md}). Printed below: the abstract and Section~1; Sections~2--7 follow source~41 in the chapter of Part~I (Section~\ref{gsr:dt:sec:alldegree}), Sections~8--9 are in Part~V.}
\begin{partabstract}{42}
Let $N\ge L\ge2$, let $A\subset\Z/N\Z$ have density $0<\delta<1$, and set
$m=\max\{h:h\mid N,\ h<L\}$ and $q=N/m$.
There is a proper $L$-term modular arithmetic progression of density at least
\[
 \delta+\frac{1-\delta}{L}\frac{\max\{q-L,0\}}{q-1}.
\]
An independent-difference step distribution makes every off-diagonal covariance nonnegative while excluding every nonzero short-order step. Its support size and zero-step mass are exactly optimal in natural classes; the stronger positive-definite weight statement is an instance of the classical Tur\'an packing bound. In particular, the gain $(1-\delta)/(2L)$ holds when $N\ge2(L-1)^2+1$. For each real $C>1$, the best constant uniform over all nontrivial densities under $N\ge CL^2$ is $1-1/C$ in front of $(1-\delta)/L$. Prime-quotient sets attain the arithmetic formula exactly. A separate sliding-window argument gives gain greater than $\delta(1-\delta)/(2L)$ when $N>L(L-1)$, with a sharp strict threshold even at densities bounded away from zero and one. We also prove finite-abelian and bounded-function versions and a sparse affine-cover consequence with a square-root modulus cap. The proofs are self-contained; the accompanying exact computations are bounded diagnostics, not formal certificates or substitutes for proof. No literature-priority or global quantitative Szemer\'edi or Ramsey claim is made.
\end{partabstract}
Let $G=\Z/N\Z$ with its additive group law. A \emph{proper modular arithmetic progression} of length $L$ is
\[
 P(a,d;L)=\{a+jd:0\le j<L\}
\]
with an injective displayed parameterization. Equivalently, the additive order of $d$ is at least $L$. Modular wrapping is allowed, and $d$ need not be a unit modulo $N$. A singleton is also called proper. All group averages in this report are normalized.

For $N\ge L\ge2$ define
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:42:eq:mq}
 m=m(N,L):=\max\{h\in\Z_{\ge1}:h\mid N,\ h<L\},
 \qquad q=q(N,L):=\frac Nm.
\end{equation}
The set defining $m$ contains $1$. Since $m<L\le N$, one has $q\ge2$. For a nonempty proper subset $A$ of $G$, put
\[
 \delta=\frac{|A|}{N},\qquad
 M_L(A)=\max_{\ord(d)\ge L}\frac1L\sum_{j=0}^{L-1}\one_A(a+jd),
 \qquad H_L(A)=M_L(A)-\delta,
\]
where the maximum also ranges over $a\in G$. Proper steps exist because the step $1$ has order $N$.

\begin{theorem}[Arithmetic increment]\label{gsr:fm:42:thm:main}
If $N\ge L\ge2$ and $0<\delta<1$, then
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:42:eq:main}
 H_L(A)\ge \frac{1-\delta}{L}\frac{\max\{q-L,0\}}{q-1}.
\end{equation}
When $q>L$, a progression giving the displayed gain can be chosen with step represented by an integer $d$ such that $0<|d|<q$.
\end{theorem}

The exact arithmetic parameter matters. If $N$ is prime, then $m=1$ and $q=N$, so the coefficient is $(N-L)/(N-1)$. In contrast, when $N=q(L-1)$ with $q\ge L$ prime, the largest divisor below $L$ is $L-1$. In this second family the theorem is attained by sets of density $1/q$. Thus a large modulus alone is not a substitute for tracking its short-order directions.

The useful size-only conclusions have a simpler form.
\begin{corollary}[Quadratic scale]\label{gsr:fm:42:cor:scale}
Let $D=\lfloor(N-1)/(L-1)\rfloor$. Then
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:42:eq:geometric}
 H_L(A)\ge\frac{1-\delta}{L}\max\left\{1-\frac{L-1}{D},0\right\}.
\end{equation}
In particular:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item $N>L(L-1)$ guarantees a strictly positive increment;
\item $N\ge2(L-1)^2+1$ guarantees $H_L(A)\ge(1-\delta)/(2L)$;
\item for every real $C>1$, $N\ge CL^2$ guarantees
$H_L(A)\ge(1-1/C)(1-\delta)/L$.
\end{enumerate}
The coefficient in \textup{(iii)} is best possible uniformly over $N,L,A$ satisfying that size condition. This optimality includes densities tending to zero; it is not an optimality assertion at a fixed positive density.
\end{corollary}

\begin{writenote}[7 October 2026; sources 40--46]
Since $2(L-1)^2+1<L^3$ for every $L\ge2$, part~(ii) weakens the hypothesis of the variance lemma of sources~26, 32 and~41 (Lemma~\ref{gsr:dt:41:lem:variance}); that lemma, with $L^3\le N$, is the formal \file{exists_proper_progression_density_increment} (\file{Proofs05VarianceIncrement.lean}, line~89, at HEAD \texttt{6d4942222}). Source~41's exponents do not change: its high branch needs $N/M>(4L)^{D_k}$, far above $L^3$.
\end{writenote}

Although the density-uniform coefficient degenerates at the quadratic endpoint, Section~\ref{gsr:dt:42:sec:endpoint} proves a density-sensitive gain there. In particular, $N>L(L-1)$ gives $H_L(A)>\delta(1-\delta)/(2L)$. This is compatible with the sparse equality family and provides a positive coefficient when density is confined away from zero and one.

The standalone variance lemma in Report277~\cite{repo42alldegree} gave the gain in (ii) under $N\ge L^3$. The present quadratic sufficient condition genuinely strengthens that lemma. It does not change the separate phase-localization exponents in Report277. Section~\ref{gsr:dt:42:sec:affine} gives a precise consequence where the improved variance scale changes a modulus-dependent cap.

The argument has three ingredients. Sampling a step as the difference of independent identically distributed variables gives a square identity for every covariance, including multipliers that are not units. An arithmetic interval makes every nonzero sampled step proper. Finally, removing the zero step and applying the elementary variance--range inequality gives a one-sided density increment. Sections~\ref{gsr:dt:42:sec:moment}--\ref{gsr:dt:42:sec:weights} separate these ingredients and their exact optimization; Section~\ref{gsr:dt:42:sec:sharp} establishes the sharpness claims.

\section[{Source 43: The research problem and the principal results}]{Source 43. The research problem and the principal results}\label{gsr:fm:43:sec:d1}\label{gsr:fm:43:bpi:sec:intro}
\srcnote{43}{Section 1}
\partsource{\textbf{Added in the eighth write, 7~October 2026. Delivered title block.} ``Sharp Boolean Phase Integration from Gowers Derivative Spectra / Exact cubic obstruction ranks, repeated-variable certification, finite-abelian orthogonality, and a quartic reduction / Research manuscript prepared with ChatGPT for Vladimir Reshetnikov and the ProveIt project / 6 October 2026''; \emph{the PDF author field reads ``Research manuscript prepared with ChatGPT for Vladimir Reshetnikov''}. Archive \file{Boolean\_Phase\_Integration\_Research.zip} (arrival \texttt{7382d8c44}), manuscript \file{boolean\_phase\_integration.tex} (1,938 lines, 26 pages), pin \texttt{797aa3cfe} (its \file{data/source\_audit.json}, shipped as \file{data/43-boolean-phase-source\_audit.json}). Printed below: the abstract, the integration note of its title page and Section~1; Sections~2--9 follow source~46 in a chapter of Part~IV (Section~\ref{gsr:fp:sec:binary}), Sections~10--13 are in Part~V. Its labels already carry the stem \texttt{bpi:}, kept under this report's prefix. Its macro \texttt{\textbackslash shortpin} is renamed \texttt{\textbackslash shortpinfortythree}; its `question' environment (``Research question'', numbered 1--10 on its own counter) is set in this report's `Research question' style, numbered within its section.}
\begin{partabstract}{43}
A multilinear frequency pattern with large derivative Fourier energy need
not integrate to a polynomial phase in small characteristic, even when
it is symmetric. We study the exact obstruction for one bounded function.
For a symmetric trilinear form $T$ over $\Ftwo$, put
$\Omega_T(a,b)=T(a,a,b)+T(a,b,b)$. We prove that the largest possible tested
energy is exactly $2^{-\rk\Omega_T/2}$, and that $\rk\Omega_T/2$ is also the
least codimension of a subspace on which $T$ has a nonclassical cubic
primitive. Explicit extremizers establish both assertions sharply.
In every degree $d\ge2$, energy greater than $1-2^{1-d}$ certifies a
nonclassical primitive and gives lossless phase removal; this threshold
is sharp. The additional repeated-variable identities are detected by an
exact shear identity and an alternating-rank profile.
A division-free orthogonality theorem treats every finite abelian group,
including characteristic two and composite moduli. Its mixed version
improves the exponent eight in a related bilinear correlation estimate to
the optimal exponent four, and gives a codimension
$2\log_2(1/\delta)$ refinement of Tidor's symmetric trilinear repair lemma.
Finally, the nonintegrable symmetric quartic extremum is $11/16$ in
dimension two; in all dimensions the remaining extremal problem reduces
to one explicit two-coordinate tensor. The proofs are given in full.
The underlying nonclassical integration theorem and finite Heisenberg
algebra are established background, not claimed discoveries. These are
local research results, not a new end-to-end Szemer\'edi bound; priority
and proof-assistant verification have not been established.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small
\noindent\textbf{Integration note.} The comparison with the formal
project uses snapshot \shortpinfortythree. Labels in this manuscript have prefix
\texttt{bpi:}. The package contains exact finite checks, a source audit,
and a proposed formalization interface; it does not change the
repository's checked theorem count.
\end{quote}

\subsection{From a selected Fourier coefficient to an integrable tensor}
Gowers's phase-removal step in Section 17 of
\cite{gowers} converts a coherent family of derivative Fourier
coefficients into polynomial structure. Proposition 17.2 is a global
model for the localized argument that follows. The corrected formal
statement in ProveIt explicitly uses degree $k+1$ and factorial
invertibility \cite{repo43}. The question here is what survives when
the ambient group is a vector space in characteristic two, where division
by that factorial is unavailable and symmetry is not the entire
integrability condition.

Throughout the Boolean parts, $V=\Ftwo^n$, all averages are uniform and
normalized, and
\begin{equation}
 \partial_h f(x)=f(x+h)\overline{f(x)},\qquad
 \widehat g(\xi)=\E_xg(x)(-1)^{\xi(x)}.
 \label{gsr:fm:43:bpi:eq:conventions}
\end{equation}
For a $d$-linear form $T:V^d\to\Ftwo$, $d\ge2$, define
\begin{equation}
 \en_T(f)=\E_{h_1,\ldots,h_{d-1}}
 \abs{\E_x\partial_{h_1}\cdots\partial_{h_{d-1}}f(x)
                (-1)^{T(h_1,\ldots,h_{d-1},x)}}^2.
 \label{gsr:fm:43:bpi:eq:energy-intro}
\end{equation}
Thus $T$ includes the frequency-evaluation variable, not just the
derivative directions. We assume $\norm f_\infty\le1$ unless an
amplitude-sensitive statement says otherwise.

A \emph{nonclassical polynomial} of degree at most $d$ is a function
$P:V\to\Torus=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ whose $(d+1)$-fold additive differences
vanish. A primitive of $T$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \Delta_{h_1}\cdots\Delta_{h_d}P(x)=\tfrac12T(h_1,\ldots,h_d)
 \quad\text{in }\Torus.
 \label{gsr:fm:43:bpi:eq:primitive-intro}
\end{equation}
Here $t\mapsto t/2\pmod1$ is the additive embedding of $\Ftwo$ in $\Torus$.
The value group is essential; a primitive taking values only in
$\{0,1/2\}$ generally does not exist.

\subsection{An exact cubic invariant}
For a symmetric trilinear $T$ set
\begin{equation}
 \Omega_T(a,b)=T(a,a,b)+T(a,b,b),\qquad
 \MM(T)=\max_{\norm f_\infty\le1}\en_T(f).
 \label{gsr:fm:43:bpi:eq:cubic-invariants}
\end{equation}
The maximum exists because the domain is finite and the closed unit
polydisc is compact. Our central conclusion is
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\quad
 -\log_2\MM(T)=\frac12\rk\Omega_T
 =\min\{\codim U:T|_{U^3}\text{ integrates}\}.
 \quad}
 \label{gsr:fm:43:bpi:eq:central}
\end{equation}
The rank is the rank of the alternating bilinear form $\Omega_T$, not
the partition rank of $T$. Section~\ref{gsr:fp:43:bpi:sec:cubic} proves the formula,
gives normal forms and extremizers, and retains the stronger amplitude
factor $\norm{|f|^2}_{U^2}^4$.

In particular, $\en_T(f)>1/2$ forces a symmetric cubic tensor to integrate.
At energy $1/2$ there is a genuine nonintegrable example. At smaller
energies, the exact logarithmic codimension law remains informative:
\begin{equation}
 \en_T(f)\ge a>0
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \text{an integrable restriction of codimension at most }
 \lfloor\log_2(1/a)\rfloor.
 \label{gsr:fm:43:bpi:eq:repair-intro}
\end{equation}
This is a statement about a prescribed tensor. It is more specific than
merely correlating $f$ with some polynomial phase.

\subsection{All-degree certification and a first quartic obstruction}
The cubic result sits inside a general certification theorem:
\begin{equation}
 \en_T(f)>1-2^{1-d}
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \exists P\text{ satisfying \eqref{gsr:fm:43:bpi:eq:primitive-intro}},\qquad
 \en_T(f)=\norm{f e(-P)}_{U^d}^{2^d},
 \label{gsr:fm:43:bpi:eq:main-intro}
\end{equation}
where $e(t)=\exp(2\pi i t)$. The threshold is sharp in every dimension
at least two. No symmetry hypothesis on $T$ is needed in
\eqref{gsr:fm:43:bpi:eq:main-intro}; it is first forced by the energy.

Once symmetry is already known, a stronger estimate detects the remaining
obstruction. For $d\ge3$ define
\begin{equation}
 \Omega_{\zz}(a,b)=T(a,a,b,\zz)+T(a,b,b,\zz),
 \qquad \zz\in V^{d-3}.
 \label{gsr:fm:43:bpi:eq:defect-intro}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \en_T(f)\le\E_{\zz}2^{-\rk\Omega_{\zz}/2}.
 \label{gsr:fm:43:bpi:eq:repeat-profile-intro}
\end{equation}
In particular a nonzero repeated-variable obstruction forces
$\en_T(f)\le1-2^{2-d}$. This bound is sharp for $d=3$. Its optimal
higher-degree replacement is a separate question.

For $d=4$, we give more than an interval for that question. Every
nonintegrable symmetric quartic with energy greater than $5/8$ is,
up to an integrable summand and linear coordinates, the pullback of
\begin{equation}
 C_4(h_1,h_2,h_3,h_4)
 =\sum_{i=1}^4 v(h_i)\prod_{j\ne i}u(h_j)
 \label{gsr:fm:43:bpi:eq:C4-intro}
\end{equation}
for two independent linear forms $u,v$. In dimension two its exact
maximum energy is $11/16$. In larger dimensions the remaining issue is
whether extra directions on which the tensor is zero can increase this
maximum. Section~\ref{gsr:fp:43:bpi:sec:quartic} proves the reduction and the
exact two-dimensional theorem.

\subsection{What is strengthened, and what is not claimed}
The preceding research manuscript \cite{repo43previous} established an
odd-characteristic symmetry threshold and explicitly asked for
characteristic-two, nonclassical-certification, and composite-modulus
extensions. The present results answer its characteristic-two question,
its nonclassical-certification question over $\Ftwo$ in all degrees, and
its finite-abelian bilinear/rank-profile question. They do not answer
nonclassical certification in every odd small characteristic.

The algebraic characterization and integration of nonclassical symmetric
multilinear forms are existing results; see Tao--Ziegler
\cite{taozieglerlow} and Tidor \cite{tidor}. We give a direct Boolean
construction so the new energy arguments have a complete, explicit
endpoint. Likewise, the finite Heisenberg representation mechanism has
established antecedents \cite{prasadvemuri}; it is not presented as a new
representation theory.

The proposed contributions are the exact derivative-spectrum obstruction
laws, their sharp phase-removal consequences, the normalized
finite-abelian estimates, and the refinements developed from them. In
Section~\ref{gsr:fp:43:bpi:sec:mixed}, the bilinear exponent and the symmetric
trilinear codimension comparison are made under the actual published
hypotheses, rather than by substituting a one-function theorem into a
seven-function problem. A targeted source comparison is not a proof of
priority. None of these results supplies the missing global selector,
handles the boundary of an arithmetic box, or changes a final
Szemer\'edi bound without further work.

\begin{writenote}[7 October 2026; sources 40--46]
\emph{Identifications and credit within this report.} \cite{repo43previous} is source~36 (Section~\ref{gsr:fm:36:sec:d1}), read from the user's library; its questions \texttt{ssc:q:two}, \texttt{ssc:q:nonclassical} and \texttt{ssc:q:composite} are Research questions~\ref{gsr:fz:36:ssc:q:two}, \ref{gsr:fz:36:ssc:q:nonclassical} and~\ref{gsr:fz:36:ssc:q:composite} here (item~\ref{gsr:fz:q:IV:lowchar}). \cite{repo43} is this repository at \texttt{797aa3cfe}. \emph{Source~46, of the same day, proves the main theorem independently} (its Theorem~\ref{gsr:fp:46:thm:sharp}, eight functions) and the same codimension $2\log_2(1/\delta)$ (its Theorem~\ref{gsr:fp:46:thm:seven}); neither cites the other, and their texts share $0.6\,\%$ (intake). Source~46 is printed first in the chapter of Part~IV (Section~\ref{gsr:fp:sec:binary}); this source is a second route there, with its further results.

\emph{The four claims the intake did not check} (checked at the write; script \file{check43.py} of the write record). (a)~Theorem~\ref{gsr:fp:43:bpi:thm:orthogonality}: the bound held for random $g,h$ and eleven biadditive forms on groups including $(\Z/2\Z)^3$, $\Z/2\Z\times\Z/4\Z$, $(\Z/4\Z)^2$, $(\Z/6\Z)^2$, $\Z/8\Z\times\Z/4\Z$ and $(\Z/12\Z)^2$ (largest ratio $0.988$); $d_B$ was an integer in every case; the proof's construction (a self-annihilating $H$ of index $d_B$ and a joint eigenvector of unit modulus on each coset) attained $1/d_B$ exactly in all nine cases with $|G|\le36$; the Smith-form example on $(\Z/12\Z)^2$ was reproduced for $s=1,2,3,4,6$. (b)~Theorem~\ref{gsr:fp:43:bpi:thm:boolean-certification}: on $\F_2^2$, over all $16$ bilinear and all $256$ trilinear forms and all $4{,}096$ functions with values among the eighth roots of unity, the energy of forms outside $\ncs^d$ never exceeded $1-2^{1-d}$ and attained it, symmetric ones outside $\ncs^3$ stayed at most $1/2$, and a search over all candidate primitives confirmed Theorem~\ref{gsr:fp:43:bpi:thm:integration} ($8$ integrable forms for $d=2$ and $d=3$); the extremizer of degree four has energy exactly $7/8$. (c)~Theorem~\ref{gsr:fp:43:bpi:thm:triangle}: the bias identity held exactly on six forms, alternating maximization over unit vectors reached $d_B^{-1/2}$ and never exceeded it, and the $\F_2^2$ extremizer gives $|L|^4=1/4$ exactly; Tidor's Lemma~4.1, re-read in the arXiv HTML of version~2, concludes the bias bound $\delta^8$, so the fourth power is a strict local refinement of that display, as stated. (d)~Theorem~\ref{gsr:fp:43:bpi:thm:quartic-two}: the 29-monomial identity agreed with the energy to $10^{-15}$ for random complex $f$; $\en_{C_4}(1)=11/16$; the cosine bound $56$ is attained; random ascent found $0.6874999$; all $24$ symmetric quartics on $\F_2^2$ outside $\ncs^4$ have maximum exactly $11/16$ over the sixteenth roots of unity. The proofs were read; the finite checks are evidence for them, not replacements.

\srcnote{44}{Section 1}

Delivered title page.} ``Additive combinatorics / finite geometry / Finite-Grid Formulae and Exact Core-Avoidance Laws for Gowers Arrangements / Computing the second degeneracy coefficient in polynomially many arithmetic operations / An AI-assisted research manuscript prepared for Vladimir Reshetnikov and the ProveIt repository / 6 October 2026''; \emph{the PDF author field reads ``AI-assisted research manuscript prepared for Vladimir Reshetnikov''}. Archive \file{gowers\_grid\_core\_research.zip} (arrival \texttt{0b4890a1c}), manuscript \file{article.tex} (1,632 lines, 24 pages), pin \texttt{8c12c906e} (its \file{SOURCE\_AUDIT.md}, shipped as \file{44-grid-core-SOURCE\_AUDIT.md}). Printed below: the abstract, the status statement of its title page and Section~1; Sections~2--10 form a chapter of Part~II (Section~\ref{gsr:en:sec:gridcore}), Sections~11--13 and Appendix~A are in Part~V. Its macros \texttt{\textbackslash T} (the set $\{-1,0,1\}$), \texttt{\textbackslash card} (an absolute value) and \texttt{\textbackslash sha} (its pin) are renamed \texttt{\textbackslash Tfortyfour}, \texttt{\textbackslash cardtwentyfive} (source~25's macro of the same definition) and \texttt{\textbackslash shafortyfour}; its `question' environment (``Question'', on the shared counter) is set in this report's `Question' style. Its ``Baseline~A'' and ``Baseline~B'' are sources~25 and~27 (note in its Section~1).}
\begin{partabstract}{44}
We resolve two explicit questions in the recent ProveIt research on Gowers's
arrangement-degeneracy lemma: computation of the cross-section intersection
statistic in arbitrary dimension, and classification of the intermediate-characteristic core directions. The second Whitney coefficient $b_{2,d}$ of
the balanced ternary cross-section arrangement is expressed through subsets
of the fixed nine-point grid $\{-1,0,1\}^2$. The resulting algorithm takes
$O(d^3)$ exact arithmetic operations, with a constant independent of $d$.
A finite rational certificate compresses the answer to eight elementary
lattice-walk energies. In particular,
\[
 b_{2,8}=3\,280\,234\,631\,541.
\]
This supplies the previously unevaluated second coefficient in the
$8$-arrangement case used in Section 15. A determinant argument makes that
coefficient characteristic-independent for $p>\max(2d,16)$.

We also count the union of all core events exactly, replacing pairwise
inclusion--exclusion by a product. For every characteristic $p\ge5$ the
conditional avoidance probability is
$\prod_{i<k}(1-(2^{2d}-1+2i)/q^2)$; in characteristics two and three it is
$\prod_{i<k}(1-p^{2d-1+i}/q^2)$. The width classification requires no
hypothesis involving $k$. These laws give contrasting growing-dimension
limits and universal degeneracy thresholds. Finally, the deficit of
$b_{2,d}$ from $\binom{H_d}{2}$ has an explicit triangular-lattice
asymptotic of order $49^d/d$.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small
\noindent\textbf{Status.} Conventional proofs, with a separately identified finite
rational certificate for the eight-shape compression. Executed exact checks
are supplied. No independent referee review, proof-assistant verification,
or literature-priority certification is claimed. These are local
strengthenings of the degeneracy analysis, not a new global quantitative
Szemer\'edi theorem.
\end{quote}
\label{gsr:fm:44:sec:intro}

Gowers's Lemma 15.4 controls exceptional labelled arrangements before the
Riesz-product selection in Lemma 15.5. Its prime-field bound, in the notation
below, is $k3^{2d2^k}/q$ for the exceptional proportion
\cite[Section 15, pp.~562--565]{gowers}. The full definition tests every
squarefree coordinate moment, including those containing the final
coordinate. We retain that definition throughout.

Two earlier manuscripts are important baselines. The first classifies the
codimension-one obstructions \cite{repo44a}. The second classifies the
core, or second-order, coefficient directions, gives a cubic remainder, and
expresses the second asymptotic coefficient using a cross-section
intersection invariant $b_{2,d,p}$ \cite{repo44b}. In particular, the
core count $k(2^{2d}-1)+k(k-1)$ and the second coefficient for $d=2$ are
\emph{not} claimed as new here. The latter manuscript explicitly asks for
an efficient exact algorithm for $b_{2,d,p}$, especially for $d=8$, and for
the core classification when $5\le p\le2k+2$.

The main advances of this manuscript are as follows. The fixed-grid formula
in Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:44:thm:grid} solves the first problem in the stable
characteristic regime for every $d$, rather than merely computing a few
small examples. Lemma~\ref{gsr:en:44:lem:width} solves the second problem for every
$p\ge5$, including all intermediate characteristics. Theorems
\ref{gsr:en:44:thm:oddproduct} and \ref{gsr:en:44:thm:smallproduct} count the complete core
union, not just its first two inclusion--exclusion terms. Theorem
\ref{gsr:en:44:thm:stability} supplies a dimension-independent determinant cutoff for
the relevant finite-field incidence structure. Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:44:thm:defectasy}
gives a second, exponentially smaller scale in the growth of the
cross-section statistic.

\subsection{A headline specialization}
Let $Z_{k,d}(q)$ count degenerate labelled $d$-arrangements of $k$-cubes, and
put $D=(2d+1)k+2d-1$. For every fixed $k\ge1$, uniformly over finite fields
of characteristic greater than $16$, the results below give
\begin{align}
 Z_{k,8}(q)
 &= (k+2\,585\,444)q^{17k+14}\\
 &\quad+\left\{\binom{k}{2}-2\,519\,909k
             -3\,280\,234\,631\,541\right\}q^{17k+13}
       +O_k(q^{17k+12}).\label{gsr:fm:44:eq:eightheadline}
\end{align}
The second coefficient is exact, including its negative sign. It is not
obtained by fitting counts at a few prime powers. The large negative
contribution records overlaps among the cross-section hyperplanes.

The statement is a fixed-$k$ asymptotic with a uniform characteristic
range. It is not an estimate with a small implied constant uniformly in
$k$. The explicit remainder in Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:44:thm:sandwich} still contains a
large inventory of non-core directions.

\subsection{Source and novelty boundaries}
The inspected repository interface is
\gitpath{Combinatorics/Ramsey/Lean/GowersSzemeredi/Sections14_15.lean}
at commit \shafortyfour\ \cite{repo44}. We follow its modular-multiple exclusion,
not an exclusion of only two integer arrays. The exact results in the two
baseline manuscripts are attributed there, and the argument here reproves
the finite-dimensional ingredients needed to use them.

The finite-field method and Whitney coefficients of hyperplane
arrangements are classical \cite{athanasiadis,stanley}. Related
mid-hyperplane arrangements also encode equal subset sums
\cite{kamiya}; their existence does not identify their characteristic
polynomials with the balanced restriction considered here. Our contribution
is the specific fixed-grid reduction and its consequences. A targeted
source comparison does not establish historical priority for every
individual identity.

\srcnote{45}{Section 1}
\partsource{\textbf{Added in the eighth write, 7~October 2026. Delivered title block.} ``Rigidity gaps in Gowers's Szemer\'edi framework / Exact additive-energy levels, punctured cosets, and a real fourth-uniformity inequality / Research report prepared with ChatGPT for Vladimir Reshetnikov / 7 October 2026''; \emph{the PDF author field reads the same}. The title page is dated 7~October 2026; the archive arrived at 17:55 on 6~October 2026 (Pacific time). Archive \file{Gowers\_Rigidity\_Gaps\_Research.zip} (arrival \texttt{f70d42385}), manuscript \file{gowers\_rigidity\_gaps.tex} with nine section files and a BibTeX database (3,589 lines in ten files, 45 pages), pin \texttt{6ce33539e} (its \file{data/source\_manifest.json}, shipped as \file{data/45-rigidity-gaps-source\_manifest.json}). Printed below: the abstract, the status statement after it and Section~1; Sections~2--3 form a chapter of Part~II (Section~\ref{gsr:en:sec:energylevels}), Sections~4--5 a chapter of Part~III (Section~\ref{gsr:cc:sec:ufourgap}), Section~6 and Appendices~A--C are in Part~V. Its labels carry the stems \texttt{en:}, \texttt{co:}, \texttt{un:}, \texttt{col:} and \texttt{ap:} of its own sections (\emph{not} this report's Part prefixes), kept under this report's prefix. Its `question' environment (``Question'', numbered on its own counter within sections) is set in this report's `Question' style; its Questions~6.1--6.16 keep their indices. Its BibTeX citations (style \texttt{alpha}) point into this report's bibliography.}
\begin{partabstract}{45}
We develop three local refinements of the additive-energy and cube-counting
framework in Gowers's proof of Szemer\'edi's theorem, with complete proofs and
reproducible exact-arithmetic certificates. First, for every $m\ge5$, the
three largest distinct additive energies of $m$-element subsets of a
torsion-free abelian group are
$M_m$, $M_m-4(m-2)$, and $M_m-8(m-3)$, where
$M_m=(2m^3+m)/3$. We classify every set at the second value using a
unit-defect theorem for positive Schur triples. The first gap has a prior
derivation from inverse Pollard theory; the additional classification and
third gap are the refinements developed here.

Second, writing $\varepsilon=1-E(A)/|A|^3$, we extend the existing sharp
coset-distance envelope to $\varepsilon<1/9$ in every abelian group. We
identify the canonical closest coset, classify every positive-defect equality case as a
coset with a subcoset removed, and prove a second, recursive stability
envelope with optimal asymptotic constant one. Its equality cases are
described by two nested subcosets. An analogous equality theorem for coordinate-cube
collisions forces the deletion into one coordinate.

Third, for real centered functions on finite abelian groups of odd order,
we prove
$\|f\|_{U^4}^{16}\ge(4795/832)\|f\|_{U^2}^{16}$.
An exact example on $\Z/5\Z$ and a dual-cube calculation rule out all real
single-character functions as global extremizers of the corresponding
norm quotient. The resulting interval is
$0.55743364\ldots\le c_4^{\mathrm{odd}}\le0.64540701\ldots$.
We give the resulting improvement to the quartic term in Gowers's cube
bound, a source and normalization crosswalk for ProveIt, and a research
agenda. The optimal fourth-uniformity constant and a new global
Szemer\'edi bound are not established.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small
\noindent\textbf{Status.} This is an AI-assisted research manuscript with
complete mathematical arguments and supplementary finite checks. It has
not undergone external peer review or proof-assistant verification.
Priority claims are limited to the comparisons explicitly documented
below. The repository audit is pinned to the commit recorded in
Appendix~\ref{gsr:fz:45:app:sources}.
\end{quote}
\label{gsr:fm:45:sec:introduction}

Gowers's proof of Szemer\'edi's theorem connects uniformity norms, additive
quadruples, structural inverse theorems, and density increments
\cite{gowers}. Several inequalities in that chain have useful extremal
questions of their own: what is the first loss from equality, which sets
produce it, and which features of an extremizer survive at the next
uniformity level? These questions can be answered locally without
reworking the entire density-increment iteration. This report studies
three of them.

The starting point is the Ramsey directory of ProveIt and its existing
research collection \cite{repo45}. That collection already contains many
refinements of the original paper. Reproving a result from an earlier
report and presenting it as a new improvement would obscure the actual
mathematical progress. We therefore fix a repository revision, inspect
the relevant prior reports, and distinguish three kinds of assertions:
credited inputs, theorems established in this manuscript, and remaining
questions. The proofs of the new assertions do not depend on the finite
searches supplied with the article.

\subsection{The three endpoints}

For a finite subset $A$ of an abelian group, its additive energy is
\[
 E(A)=\#\{(a,b,c,d)\in A^4:a+b=c+d\}.
\]
There are two different cardinality-constrained extremal problems.
In a torsion-free group the maximum for $|A|=m$ is
\[
 M_m=\frac{2m^3+m}{3},
\]
attained by arithmetic progressions. In a general group the universal
maximum is $m^3$, attained by finite subgroup cosets. The two maxima
represent different structures and cannot be interchanged by a change
of normalization.

Section~\ref{gsr:en:45:en:section} treats the torsion-free maximum. For $m\ge5$, put
\[
 H_m=\{0,1,\ldots,m-2,m\},\qquad
 J_m=\{0,1,\ldots,m\}\setminus\{2\}.
\]
We prove that the three largest energy values are precisely
\begin{equation}
 M_m,\qquad M_m-4(m-2),\qquad M_m-8(m-3).
 \label{gsr:fm:45:intro:three-values}
\end{equation}
At the second value every set is a translate and dilation of $H_m$, with
reflection allowed. The set $J_m$ attains the third value. A full
classification at the third value remains a separate problem. The key
certificate is the exact integer identity
\begin{equation}
 \frac{M_m-E(A)}4
 =\#\{x<y<z\text{ in }A:x+z-y\notin A\},
 \label{gsr:fm:45:intro:ordered-defect}
\end{equation}
first proved for real sets and then transported to arbitrary torsion-free
abelian groups. It turns a near-extremal inequality into a classification
of a small number of failed additive completions.

Section~\ref{gsr:en:45:co:section} treats the coset maximum. For
\[
 \varepsilon=1-\frac{E(A)}{m^3},\qquad
 \tau(s)=\frac{1-\sqrt{1-4s}}2,
\]
we prove, throughout $0\le\varepsilon<1/9$, that there is a unique closest
finite subgroup coset $C$ and
\begin{equation}
 \frac{|A\triangle C|}{m}\le\tau(\varepsilon).
 \label{gsr:fm:45:intro:coset}
\end{equation}
Its subgroup is obtained directly from the autocorrelation:
$H=\{d:|A\cap(A+d)|>m/2\}$. Equality with positive defect occurs
exactly when $A=C\setminus K$ and $K$ is a subcoset of index at least
nine in $C$. A remainder term measures both points outside $C$ and the
failure of the hole $K$ to be a coset. More precisely, set
$\delta=|A\triangle C|/m$ and
$\eta=\varepsilon-\delta(1-\delta)$. When $\delta>0$ and
$0\le s=\eta/\delta^3<1/9$, we prove the second envelope
\[
 \Delta_C(A):=\frac1m\min_{D\subsetneq C}
     |A\triangle(C\setminus D)|\le\delta\tau(s),
\]
where $D$ ranges over nonempty subgroup cosets. Its optimal
asymptotic leading constant in the scale $\eta/\delta^2$ is one.
All positive equality cases are $(C\setminus D)\cup J$, with two
nested subcosets $J\subsetneq D\subsetneq C$ and inner index at
least nine. For coordinate-cube collisions, positive-defect equality
in the original coset-distance envelope requires a Cartesian product
with just one punctured coordinate.

Section~\ref{gsr:cc:45:un:section} concerns a functional endpoint. With normalized
Gowers norms, define
\begin{equation}
 c_d^{\mathrm{odd}}
 =\sup_{\substack{G\text{ finite abelian of odd order}\\
                  f:G\to\R,\ \E f=0,\ f\ne0}}
       \frac{\|f\|_{U^2}^{4}}{\|f\|_{U^d}^{4}}.
 \label{gsr:fm:45:intro:cd}
\end{equation}
The existing report establishes $c_3^{\mathrm{odd}}=1/\sqrt2$ and asks
for the higher-dimensional constants \cite{repo45}. We prove
\begin{equation}
 \left(\frac{39037448}{404304625}\right)^{1/4}
 \le c_4^{\mathrm{odd}}
 \le \left(\frac{832}{4795}\right)^{1/4}.
 \label{gsr:fm:45:intro:c4}
\end{equation}
The upper estimate comes from a mean-sensitive $U^3$ inequality,
positive Fourier coefficients of an autocorrelation, and a rational
quadratic certificate. The lower estimate is attained by the particular
test function $(2,1,-2,-2,1)$ on $\Z/5\Z$, without any assertion that it
maximizes the quotient. A dual-cube identity supplies an improving
direction at every real single-character function whose character has
odd order at least five; order three is treated separately. Thus the
single-character extremal model valid for the preceding norm comparison
does not answer the fourth-uniformity problem.

\subsection{What is inherited and what is added}

\begin{table}[htbp]
\centering\small
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.18}
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.22\textwidth}
 >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
Problem & Credited starting point & Extension proved here \\
\midrule
Torsion-free energy & The progression maximum in Gowers, Section~7;
the first gap follows from inverse Pollard; endpoint calculations also
appear in Hegyv\'ari & Complete second-level classification, an exact
third energy value, and a unit-Schur-defect theorem \\
Coset approximation & The sharp quadratic envelope for
$\varepsilon\le1/100$ in report source~14 & The range
$\varepsilon<1/9$, canonical subgroup, all equality cases, and
quantitative stability of the hole \\
Coordinate-cube collisions & The product-coset result in the same small
range & The extended range and all positive-defect equality domains \\
Real uniformity norms & $c_3^{\mathrm{odd}}=1/\sqrt2$ and consequently
$c_4^{\mathrm{odd}}\le1/\sqrt2$ in the report & A smaller upper bound,
an exact five-point lower bound, and exclusion of all single-character
global extremizers \\
Cube counting & Exact quartic coefficient $P_d$ and centered expansion
in prior report sources & The improved coefficient
$P_d(832/4795)^{1/4}$ for $d\ge4$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\caption{Scope of the comparisons. The repository reference is
\cite{repo45}; the published energy sources are
\cite{gowers,pollardequality,hegyvari}.}
\label{gsr:fm:45:tab:provenance}
\end{table}

The baseline and first energy gap are not assigned a new priority claim.
The first gap is a short consequence of the equality classification in
Pollard's theorem \cite{pollardequality}; we include an elementary endpoint
proof because it leads efficiently to the second-level classification
and third-level exclusion.
Hegyv\'ari's energy-spectrum paper already provides the endpoint
recurrence, the congruence modulo four, and the construction producing
that gap \cite{hegyvari}. The second-level classification and third
exclusion interval were not found in the primary sources inspected.
That statement records the extent of the audit; it does not establish
worldwide publication priority.

Shao's work on large additive energy gives structural conclusions in a
different, macroscopic regime \cite{shao}. Our exact torsion-free
window has an absolute deficit of order $m$, hence relative deficit of
order $m^{-2}$ from $M_m$. It should not be read as a replacement for
constant-error inverse theory. Likewise, the extremal-norm results of
Eisner and Tao concern near-maximal Gowers norms under magnitude-norm
constraints \cite{eisnertao}; the real centered quotient in
\eqref{gsr:fm:45:intro:cd} imposes a different comparison.

\subsection{Conventions and logical scope}

All groups are abelian and written additively, except that characters
take values multiplicatively on the unit circle. A coset in a distance
minimization is a coset of a finite subgroup. All unmarked cardinality
counts are ordered counts, including degenerate additive cubes. On a
finite group $G$ we use probability averages
$\E_x=|G|^{-1}\sum_{x\in G}$ and normalized Fourier coefficients
\[
 \widehat f(\xi)=\E_x f(x)\overline{\xi(x)}.
\]
The dual-group sums are unnormalized. For $d\ge1$,
\begin{equation}
 \|f\|_{U^d}^{2^d}
 =\E_{x,h_1,\ldots,h_d}
   \prod_{\omega\in\{0,1\}^d}
        \mathcal C^{|\omega|}f(x+\omega\cdot h),
 \label{gsr:fm:45:intro:gowers}
\end{equation}
where $\mathcal C$ denotes complex conjugation. In the real-valued
sections the conjugations may be suppressed. We use the standard cube
Cauchy--Schwarz inequality, Fourier orthogonality, and monotonicity
$\|f\|_{U^d}\le\|f\|_{U^{d+1}}$; these are the elementary Gowers-norm
facts developed in Section~3 of \cite{gowers}.

The torsion-free, arbitrary-group, and odd-order hypotheses belong to
different theorems. In particular, the ordered energy maximum cannot be
applied to an arbitrary subset of a cyclic group without rectification,
and the real norm comparison cannot be extended to arbitrary complex
functions: a nontrivial character has $U^j$ norm equal to one for every
$j\ge2$.
All finite searches below are diagnostic or certify a specified finite
sum. The universal statements are proved analytically. Their local
improvements have not been propagated through Gowers's complete
iteration, so no new numerical upper bound for the global Szemer\'edi
threshold or for $r_k(N)$ is claimed.

\section[{Source 46: Research target, contribution, and boundaries}]{Source 46. Research target, contribution, and boundaries}\label{gsr:fm:46:sec:d1}\label{gsr:fm:46:sec:intro}
\srcnote{46}{Section 1}
\partsource{\textbf{Added in the eighth write, 7~October 2026. Delivered title block.} ``Sharp Cubical Correlation and Characteristic Barriers in Gowers' Polarization Step / Exact binary cubic norms, improved restriction bounds, optimal phase depth, and trace-multiplication tensors / Research contribution prepared for the ProveIt project / 6 October 2026''; \emph{the PDF author field reads ``Research contribution prepared for ProveIt''; no statement on AI assistance is made}. Archive \file{gowers\_polarization\_barriers.zip} (arrival \texttt{f2baec573}), manuscript \file{article.tex} (1,503 lines, 23 pages); \emph{no pin}: its \file{SOURCE\_AUDIT.md} (shipped as \file{46-polarization-barriers-SOURCE\_AUDIT.md}) records two blob identifiers. Printed below: the abstract, its keywords and Section~1; Sections~2--9 form a chapter of Part~IV (Section~\ref{gsr:fp:sec:binary}), Sections~10--12 and Appendix~A are in Part~V. Its `question' environment (``Research question'', on the shared counter, in italic type) is set in this report's `Research question' style, and its remarks, which it sets in upright type, in this report's remark style.}
\begin{partabstract}{46}
Let $T:V^3\to\F_2$ be symmetric and trilinear, and let
$C_T(a,b)=T(a,a,b)+T(a,b,b)$ have rank $r$. We prove that the exact norm of the
$T$-twisted, eight-function cubic average on the unit ball of $\ell^\infty(V)$ is
$2^{-r/2}$. Equality is attained with all eight functions equal to one
nonclassical cubic phase taking values among the eighth roots of unity.
The proof converts the cube into a family of quadratic convolution operators;
a symplectic decomposition then supplies matching extremizers. Consequences
include an exact approximate-polarization threshold, a spectral stability
identity, and the improvement of the codimension bound in Tidor's symmetric
seven-function restriction proposition from $8\log_2(1/\delta)$ to
$2\log_2(1/\delta)$.

To connect these results to Gowers' Lemma~17.1 and Proposition~17.2, we give
explicit all-characteristic scalar polarization with the optimal root-of-unity
alphabet. For $T_{c,d}(h_1,\ldots,h_d)=\Tr(c h_1\cdots h_d)$ over $\F_{p^n}$,
we classify exact nonclassical integrability in every degree, compute the first
obstruction's rank, and determine the largest integrable subspaces and the
exact number of elementary symmetric corrections. The general integration
criterion is established prior work; the paper uses it with explicit proofs in
the degrees needed here. All analytic assertions are proved, rather than
inferred from experiments. Reproducible exact finite checks, a source audit,
and a formalization roadmap accompany the article. No improved global bound
for Szemer\'edi's theorem or exhaustive priority claim is made.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small
\noindent\textbf{Keywords.} Gowers norms; polarization; low characteristic;
nonclassical polynomials; symmetric multilinear forms; finite-field trace;
symplectic restriction; sharp correlation bounds.
\end{quote}

The late stages of Gowers' proof of Szemer\'edi's theorem turn structured
multilinear frequency information into polynomial phases. The familiar
polarization formula divides by a factorial. In the prime-field setting this
is harmless when the characteristic is larger than the degree; outside that
range it conceals two different phenomena. Sometimes the appropriate repair
is merely to enlarge the phase alphabet. Sometimes no circle-valued phase
can integrate the given tensor at all.

The corrected source in the ProveIt Ramsey directory explicitly assumes
$k<N$ in Lemma~17.1 and $k+1<N$ in Proposition~17.2, with $N$ prime
\cite{gowers,repo46source}. We investigate this boundary rather than changing
a constant in an unrelated early density-increment argument. The central
question is quantitative: when exact integration fails, how much twisted
cubical correlation remains possible, and how much restriction or correction
is necessary to remove the obstruction?

\subsection{Main conclusions}
For a symmetric binary trilinear form, a single alternating bilinear form
controls several a priori different quantities. Writing $r=\rank C_T$ and
$m=r/2$, we prove
\begin{align}
\sup_{\norm{f_\eps}_\infty\leq1}\abs{\Lambda_T((f_\eps))}
 &=2^{-m},\label{gsr:fm:46:eq:intro-main}\\
\min\{\codim W:T|_{W^3}\text{ integrates}\}&=m,\label{gsr:fm:46:eq:intro-codim}\\
\max\Pr(\text{a vertex-separated polarization identity holds})
 &=\frac{1+2^{-m}}2.\label{gsr:fm:46:eq:intro-agree}
\end{align}
The average $\Lambda_T$ is defined precisely in Section~\ref{gsr:fp:46:sec:sharp}.
The first supremum is unchanged if all eight functions are required to be a
single suitable eighth-root cubic phase. The second identity follows from
alternating-form geometry; the first and third supply exact analytic
counterparts, not just a qualitative obstruction.

A related seven-function correlation $\Gamma_T$ satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:46:eq:intro-seven}
 |\Gamma_T|\leq 2^{-r/4}.
\end{equation}
Consequently, correlation at least $\delta>0$ forces an integrable restriction
of codimension at most $2\log_2(1/\delta)$. This improves the bound
$8\log_2(1/\delta)$ in Proposition~4.6 of Tidor \cite{tidor}, under exactly
its symmetry and boundedness hypotheses. We do \emph{not} assert that the
new seven-function bound is sharp; the eight-function bound is sharp.

For extension-field trace tensors, we obtain a complete exact-integration
classification and a closed formula for $m$. These give explicit families in
which the required codimension grows linearly with the extension degree,
together with matching sharp cubical norms. The scalar prime-field case, in
contrast, always integrates after passing to an optimal higher-order
root-of-unity alphabet.

\subsection{What is inherited and what is proved here}
The theory of nonclassical polynomials is essential background, not a new
invention of this note. Tao--Ziegler establish the necessary repeated-variable
conditions for total derivatives and the coordinate description of
nonclassical polynomials \cite{taozieglerlow}. Tidor proves the converse integration
statement for all orders \cite[Proposition~3.5]{tidor}. Quadratic Gauss-sum
magnitudes, symplectic decomposition, and Gowers--Cauchy--Schwarz are standard
ingredients.

The main results proved in this note are the exact mixed cubic norm and its
explicit extremizers, the quantitative agreement and stability consequences,
the sharpened symmetric seven-function restriction estimate, and explicit
trace-tensor classification and repair formulas. The scalar constructions
are effective refinements of the established nonclassical framework. They
are included because they identify precisely what an all-characteristic
replacement of Gowers' polarization step must say.

The source audit also records Mili\'cevi\'c's 2026 preprint on general
$U^4$ inverse theory \cite{milicevicufour}. Its existence makes an unrestricted
priority claim especially inappropriate: the present argument is
self-contained, but we have not exhaustively compared every result in that
large preprint or the entire literature. ``Proved here'' describes the
content of this manuscript, not a certified first publication. Nor do these
local improvements by themselves alter the global bound for progression-free
sets. Recent global work such as \cite{lssbounds} concerns a different scale of
quantitative improvement.

\section[{Source 47: The problem and the main results}]{Source 47. The problem and the main results}\label{gsr:fm:47:sec:d1}\label{gsr:fm:47:boe:sec:intro}
\srcnote{47}{Section 1}
\partsource{\textbf{Added in the ninth write, 7~October 2026. Delivered title block.} ``Exact Boolean Obstruction Energies / Derivative periods, sharp quartic--sextic integration, and dimension-free higher-degree extremizers / Research manuscript prepared with ChatGPT for Vladimir Reshetnikov and the ProveIt project / 6 October 2026''; \emph{the PDF author field reads ``Research manuscript prepared with ChatGPT for Vladimir Reshetnikov''}. Archive \file{Boolean\_Obstruction\_Energies\_Research.zip} (arrival \texttt{b6a8ee966}), manuscript \file{article.tex} (1,512 lines, 23 pages), pin \texttt{5c9a442d2} (an ``observed branch ref''; its \file{SOURCE\_AUDIT.md}, shipped as \file{47-boolean-energies-SOURCE\_AUDIT.md}, records two blob identifiers). It continues source~43 (note in this section). Its macros \texttt{\textbackslash F} (the field $\F_2$), \texttt{\textbackslash Torus} ($\R/\Z$), \texttt{\textbackslash Sym} and \texttt{\textbackslash ip} are set as this report's \texttt{\textbackslash Ftwo}, \texttt{\textbackslash Tcirc}, \texttt{\textbackslash sym} and \texttt{\textbackslash ipthirtyone}, which print the same; its `question' environment (``Research question'', numbered 1--9 on its own counter) is set in this report's `Research question' style, numbered within its section.}
\begin{partabstract}{47}
A selected derivative Fourier coefficient carries constraints that disappear
when the derivative is replaced by an arbitrary bounded function.  Over
$\mathbb F_2^n$, every even sum of the derivative directions is an exact
translation period.  Retaining this elementary constraint resolves the
higher-dimensional quartic extremal question posed in the preceding
Boolean phase-integration draft.  More generally, for the symmetric tensor
$C_d=\sum_i v(h_i)\prod_{j\ne i}u(h_j)$ with $u,v$ independent, we prove
that its maximum selected energy is exactly $1-(d+1)/2^d$ in every degree
$d\ge3$ and every dimension $n\ge2$; arbitrary optimizing functions may use
all the coordinates.  A defect classification and a sharp $7/32$ support
theorem for non-pure symmetric trilinear maps then give the exact universal
symmetric nonintegrability thresholds $11/16$, $13/16$, and $57/64$ in
degrees four, five, and six.  In all degrees the universal upper bound is
$1-\min\{d+1,7\}/2^d$, improving the previous repeated-variable rank-profile
bound.  We also classify one-dimensional defect images, give a nonnegative
deficit recursion, and retain explicit margins for corrupted selectors.
Full proofs of the bounds and the required integration and shear identities
are included.  Nonclassical integration and the earlier shear method are
credited as background; the new claims are
accompanied by exact finite checks and a formalization plan.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small
\noindent\textbf{Scope and status.} Unrefereed research manuscript.  The
quartic question is a question in the preceding project draft, not a claim
about a previously published famous open problem.  Literature priority and
proof-assistant verification are not asserted.  These are local
phase-integration results, not a new end-to-end bound for Szemer\'edi's theorem.
\end{quote}

\subsection{The selected energy}
Throughout, $V=\Ftwo^n$ is a finite-dimensional Boolean vector space, all
averages are normalized, and
\[
 \partial_h f(x)=f(x+h)\overline{f(x)},\qquad
 \Delta_h P(x)=P(x+h)-P(x),\qquad e(t)=\exp(2\pi i t).
\]
For a genuinely $d$-linear map $T:V^d\to\Ftwo$, define
\begin{equation}
 \En_T(f)=\E_{h_1,\ldots,h_{d-1}}
 \left|\E_x \partial_{h_1}\cdots\partial_{h_{d-1}}f(x)
       (-1)^{T(h_1,\ldots,h_{d-1},x)}\right|^2.
 \label{gsr:fm:47:boe:eq:energy}
\end{equation}
The last slot of $T$ is the frequency-evaluation variable.  The assumption
$\norm f_\infty\le1$ will always be stated or in force; under it,
$0\le\En_T(f)\le1$.  Write
\[
 \Mcal(T)=\max_{\norm f_\infty\le1}\En_T(f).
\]
This is a maximum, since a finite product of closed complex unit discs is
compact and the energy is continuous.

A symmetric $d$-linear form is \emph{integrable} if it is the constant top
derivative of a degree-at-most-$d$ nonclassical polynomial $P:V\to\Tcirc$:
\begin{equation}
 \Delta_{h_1}\cdots\Delta_{h_d}P(x)=\tfrac12T(h_1,\ldots,h_d).
 \label{gsr:fm:47:boe:eq:primitive}
\end{equation}
Nonclassical degree means that all $(d+1)$-fold additive differences vanish.
Denote the subspace of integrable tensors by $\Ical_d(V)$.  This is the
space usually denoted $\mathrm{nCSM}^d(V)$, not the space of all symmetric
multilinear forms.  Section~\ref{gsr:fp:47:boe:sec:calculus} proves the precise
criterion and an explicit primitive.

\subsection{A dimension-free extremal formula}
For independent $u,v\in V^*$, put
\begin{equation}
 C_d^{u,v}(h_1,\ldots,h_d)
 =\sum_{i=1}^d v(h_i)\prod_{j\ne i}u(h_j),\qquad
 b_d=1-\frac{d+1}{2^d}.
 \label{gsr:fm:47:boe:eq:canonical}
\end{equation}
We normally omit the superscripts.  The tensor depends on two coordinates;
the function in its extremal problem need not.

\begin{theorem}[Exact canonical energies]\label{gsr:fm:47:boe:thm:main-canonical}
For every $d\ge3$, $n\ge2$, and independent $u,v\in V^*$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\quad \Mcal(C_d^{u,v})=b_d=1-\frac{d+1}{2^d}.\quad}
 \label{gsr:fm:47:boe:eq:main-canonical}
\end{equation}
The constant function attains equality.  The same maximum holds for
$C_d^{u,v}+S$ whenever $S\in\Ical_d(V)$.
\end{theorem}
The proof is in Section~\ref{gsr:fp:47:boe:sec:canonical}.  It does not assume that an
optimizer factors through $V/(\ker u\cap\ker v)$, and it does not obtain an
upper bound by tensoring a two-dimensional computation.

\subsection{Sharp low-degree thresholds and a uniform higher-degree bound}
Define the universal symmetric nonintegrable extremum in dimension $n$ by
\begin{equation}
 M^{\mathrm{sym}}_{d,n}
 =\max_{T\in\sym^d(V)\setminus\Ical_d(V)}\Mcal(T),\qquad n\ge2.
 \label{gsr:fm:47:boe:eq:universal-definition}
\end{equation}
Here $\sym^d(V)$ denotes symmetric multilinear \emph{maps}; no use of
symmetric tensor coinvariants in characteristic two is intended.

\begin{theorem}[Universal bounds and exact quartic--sextic thresholds]
\label{gsr:fm:47:boe:thm:main-universal}
For every $d\ge3$ and $n\ge2$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\quad
 1-\frac{d+1}{2^d}\ \le\ M^{\mathrm{sym}}_{d,n}
 \ \le\ 1-\frac{\min\{d+1,7\}}{2^d}.
 \quad}\label{gsr:fm:47:boe:eq:main-universal}
\end{equation}
In particular, independently of dimension,
\begin{equation}
 M^{\mathrm{sym}}_{3,n}=\frac12,\qquad
 M^{\mathrm{sym}}_{4,n}=\frac{11}{16},\qquad
 M^{\mathrm{sym}}_{5,n}=\frac{13}{16},\qquad
 M^{\mathrm{sym}}_{6,n}=\frac{57}{64}.
 \label{gsr:fm:47:boe:eq:sharp-low-degrees}
\end{equation}
If a symmetric tensor has energy strictly above the corresponding upper
bound in \eqref{gsr:fm:47:boe:eq:main-universal}, it is integrable.  For a primitive
$P_T$ one then has the lossless identity
\begin{equation}
 \En_T(f)=\norm{f e(-P_T)}_{U^d}^{2^d}.
 \label{gsr:fm:47:boe:eq:lossless-intro}
\end{equation}
The strict thresholds in degrees three through six cannot be decreased.
\end{theorem}

\begin{writenote}[7 October 2026; sources 60--69]
\emph{Exact in every degree} (sources~65 and~69, Section~\ref{gsr:fp:sec:alldegree}): the maximum over nonintegrable symmetric tensors equals $1-(d+1)/2^d$ for every $d\ge3$, and its maximizers are the canonical tensors modulo integrable ones (their Theorems~\ref{gsr:fm:65:bsi:thm:main} and~\ref{gsr:fm:69:bad:thm:main}); at $d=7$ the value is $15/16$.
\end{writenote}
The distinction between \emph{energy} and the Gowers norm itself is
important: the normalization in \eqref{gsr:fm:47:boe:eq:energy} corresponds to the
$2^d$th power of the $U^d$ norm after phase removal.

\begin{center}
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}ccccc@{}}
\toprule
Degree & Canonical & Previous profile & New universal & Exact?\\
 & maximum & upper bound & upper bound & \\
\midrule
$3$ & $1/2$ & $1/2$ & $1/2$ & yes\\
$4$ & $11/16$ & $3/4$ & $11/16$ & yes\\
$5$ & $13/16$ & $7/8$ & $13/16$ & yes\\
$6$ & $57/64$ & $15/16$ & $57/64$ & yes\\
$7$ & $15/16$ & $31/32$ & $121/128$ & not established\\
$8$ & $247/256$ & $63/64$ & $249/256$ & not established\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
The previous column is the bound $1-2^{2-d}$ from the repeated-variable
rank profile in the preceding draft~\cite{repo47prior}.  It is a comparison with
that specific local estimate, not a claim about the best published global
inverse theorem.  For $d\ge7$, the gap left here is exactly
$(d-6)/2^d$ between our lower and upper bounds.

\subsection{What is new relative to the inspected sources}
Gowers's Section~17 turns structured derivative frequencies into a phase
removal step~\cite{gowers}.  In small characteristic, symmetry alone no
longer characterizes top derivatives; the appropriate nonclassical
integration theorem is established background~\cite{tidor}.  The present
problem asks how much selected energy a genuinely nonintegrable symmetric
tensor can support.

The preceding project manuscript~\cite{repo47prior} proved the cubic rank law,
the general shear profile, the two-dimensional quartic value $11/16$, and
a reduction of the universal quartic problem to the pullback of $C_4$.
Its Research Question~1 asked whether the $11/16$ value persists when the
optimizing function may depend on extra coordinates.  Theorem
\ref{gsr:fm:47:boe:thm:main-canonical} answers that question affirmatively and gives
an all-degree formula.  Theorem~\ref{gsr:fm:47:boe:thm:main-universal} extends the
sharp universal conclusion through degree six.  The derivative-constrained
rank-one estimate, the pure-defect classification, the support argument,
and the ensuing deficit recursion are the new proof components developed
here.  Background components are reproved so that no unreviewed earlier
theorem must be accepted on trust.

\section[{Source 48: The research target and the resulting strengthening}]{Source 48. The research target and the resulting strengthening}\label{gsr:fm:48:sec:d1}
\srcnote{48}{Section 1}
\partsource{\textbf{Added in the ninth write, 7~October 2026. Delivered title block.} ``Collision-aware derandomization of Gowers's restriction step / Exact energy inventories, prescribed-cardinality subsets, and constructive restriction for linear systems / Research manuscript prepared with ChatGPT for the ProveIt project / 6 October 2026''; \emph{the PDF author field reads the same}. Archive \file{Gowers\_Collision\_Aware\_Derandomization.zip} (arrival \texttt{b6a8ee966}), manuscript \file{article.tex} (1,763 lines, 27 pages), pin \texttt{0b4890a1c} (its \file{SOURCE\_AUDIT.md}, shipped as \file{48-derandomization-SOURCE\_AUDIT.md}). It continues source~17 (note in this section). Printed below: the abstract, its keywords and Section~1; Sections~2--9 form a chapter of Part~II (Section~\ref{gsr:en:sec:derandomization}), Sections~10--13 and Appendices~A--B are in Part~V. Its macros \texttt{\textbackslash cost} ($C_s$, not this report's calligraphic $\mathcal C$) and \texttt{\textbackslash pin} are renamed \texttt{\textbackslash costfortyeight} and \texttt{\textbackslash pinfortyeight}; its `question' environment (``Research question'', on the shared counter) is set in this report's `Research question' style.}
\begin{partabstract}{48}
Gowers's random-restriction argument improves the proportion of additive
relations respected by a function. Turning its existence proof into an
explicit algorithm requires conditional expectations of high-order tuple
counts. Ordinary weighted convolution is not sufficient: a repeated label
is selected once, not independently at each occurrence.

We construct an exact finite group-algebra inventory that records these
collisions without enumerating tuples. For order $s$, $n$ labels and ambient
group size $D$, it evaluates the Bernoulli expectation and deterministically
rounds an arbitrary rational signed combination of energy counts in
$O(s^4nD)$ rational operations and $O(s^2D)$ storage. A single branching
decision needs only $O(s^2)$ coefficient probes; the remaining work consists
of explicit translations of coefficient arrays. A distinct-support
extension gives the corresponding theorem for a uniformly sampled subset
of any prescribed cardinality, with no multiplicative dependence on that
cardinality. The method extends to arbitrary fixed systems of linear
equations, including zero coefficients, repeated entries, and composite
moduli; repeated column types substantially reduce its complexity.

As a source-specific application, we give a fully deterministic,
rational-arithmetic version of polynomial-loss Fej\'er restriction. It
retains the existing bound $|B|^{2s-1}/(2\eta L^{2s})$ with no additional
loss. The complete prime-cyclic search takes $O_s(np^5)$ rational
operations, whereas rounding after a filter is fixed takes $O_s(np^2)$.
These two costs are distinguished throughout. The contribution resolves a
specific algorithmic question in the inspected companion research, not a
new global bound for Szemer\'edi's theorem. Complete proofs, exact tests
through order eight, executable reference code, and integration notes are
included. Literature priority and formal Lean verification are not claimed.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small
\noindent\textbf{Keywords.} Additive energy; Gowers restriction; conditional
expectation; repeated entries; divided powers; fixed-size sampling;
constructive additive combinatorics.
\end{quote}
\label{gsr:fm:48:gcr:sec:scope}

\subsection{What is being made constructive}
In Lemma~9.3 of his 2001 paper, Gowers restricts a function
$\phi:B\to\Z/p\Z$ so that a large proportion of its surviving additive
sixteen-tuples are respected~\cite{gowers}. The random choice is structured:
first choose phase parameters, then include distinct points independently
with the resulting probabilities. The second stage is independent across
points, but not across the occurrences of one point in a tuple.

The inspected companion manuscript~\cite{repo48companion} replaces the long
product of elementary filters by one normalized Fej\'er kernel and obtains
polynomial losses in the initial respected fraction and the desired error.
Its further-research question on efficient certification and extraction
asks for an algorithm that handles conditional Bernoulli choices, repeated
entries, and vector-valued graph data without listing all tuples. Its
existence argument explicitly does not supply such a running-time theorem.
We address that question for balanced additive relations, and then for
arbitrary fixed linear systems.

The method of conditional expectations is classical~\cite{raghavanpacking}.
Our contribution is not the averaging principle itself. It is the exact
coefficient representation, the local replacement identity, the resulting
complexity bound, the prescribed-cardinality extension, and the
source-specific rational implementation of the full restriction step.

\subsection{The main computational theorem}
For a finite abelian group $K$ and labelled group elements $g_1,\ldots,g_n$,
put
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:48:gcr:eq:energy-intro}
 E_s(S;g)=\#\left\{(i_1,\ldots,i_{2s})\in S^{2s}:
       \sum_{j=1}^{s}g_{i_j}=\sum_{j=s+1}^{2s}g_{i_j}\right\}.
\end{equation}
Labels, rather than group images, are independently selected. The images
$g_i$ need not be distinct. In the graph application the labels are the
distinct elements of $B$, with two images $x$ and $(x,\phi(x))$.

Suppose a statistic is a rational signed sum
\[
 F(S)=\sum_{\nu=1}^{v}c_\nu E_s(S;g^{(\nu)}),\qquad c_\nu\in\Q,
 \qquad D=\sum_{\nu=1}^{v}|K_\nu|.
\]
The common label set is essential: all energies are evaluated on the same
selected subset. Write
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:48:gcr:eq:Cs}
 \costfortyeight=\binom{s+2}{2}^{\!2}.
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[Headline rounding theorem]\label{gsr:fm:48:gcr:thm:headline}
Let each label $i$ initially be selected independently with rational
probability $p_i\in[0,1]$. There is a deterministic exact algorithm returning
$S\subseteq[n]$ such that
\[
 F(S)\ge \E F(S_{\boldsymbol p}).
\]
Using explicit arrays indexed by the groups, its arithmetic cost is
$O(\costfortyeight nD)$ and its storage is $O((s+1)^2D)$ rational numbers.
After initialization, choosing the value of one indicator requires
$O((s+1)^2v)$ coefficient probes and rational operations; maintaining the
full state costs $O(\costfortyeight D)$ per changed indicator.

For every prescribed $k\in\{0,\ldots,n\}$, there is also a deterministic
algorithm returning $|S|=k$ with
\[
 F(S)\ge\frac1{\binom nk}\sum_{|A|=k}F(A).
\]
Its arithmetic cost is $O(\costfortyeight(2s+1)^2nD)$ and its storage is
$O((s+1)^2(2s+1)D)$. In particular, there is no factor $k$ in this bound.
\end{theorem}

The first assertion is proved in Sections~\ref{gsr:en:48:gcr:sec:inventory}--\ref{gsr:en:48:gcr:sec:rounding};
the second in Section~\ref{gsr:en:48:gcr:sec:fixed}. The bounds are not claims of
polynomial time in $\log D$. A group specified by a short modulus can be
much larger than its bit description. Dense ambient-group storage is an
explicit, and sometimes expensive, part of the algorithm.

\subsection{The source-specific quantitative conclusion}
Let $m=2s\ge4$, $p$ be prime, $B\subseteq\F_p$ have size $n=\beta p>0$,
and $\phi:B\to\F_p$. Write $\calT_s(B)$ for all balanced $m$-tuples in $B$
and $\calR_s(B,\phi)$ for those whose images satisfy the same relation.
Suppose
\[
 \calR_s(B,\phi)\ge\alpha n^{m-1},\qquad 0<\alpha,\eta\le1,
 \qquad L=\left\lceil\frac{m+1}{\alpha\eta}\right\rceil.
\]
Under the explicit size hypothesis
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:48:gcr:eq:intro-threshold}
 p>2L-2,\qquad
 p\ge 2L^m(2L-1)^{m-1}\beta^{-(m-1)},
\end{equation}
Section~\ref{gsr:en:48:gcr:sec:source} constructs, rather than merely proves the
existence of, a set $B'$ satisfying
\begin{align}
 \calR_s(B',\phi)&\ge(1-\eta)\calT_s(B'),\label{gsr:fm:48:gcr:eq:intro-quality}\\
 \calT_s(B')&\ge\frac{n^{m-1}}{2\eta L^m}
 \ge\frac{\alpha^m\eta^{m-1}}{2(m+2)^m}n^{m-1}.
 \label{gsr:fm:48:gcr:eq:intro-retention}
\end{align}
The retention estimate is inherited from the companion Fej\'er argument;
we reprove the needed estimate and preserve it exactly during rational
approximation and derandomization. This distinction matters: the new
result is a constructive strengthening, not a second claim to the same
quantitative improvement.

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}p{.46\textwidth}p{.43\textwidth}@{}}
\toprule
Task in the prime-cyclic graph setting & Arithmetic cost for fixed $s$\\
\midrule
Evaluate one exact Bernoulli expectation & $O_s(np^2)$\\
Round after phase parameters are fixed & $O_s(np^2)$\\
Search all translated Fej\'er parameters and round & $O_s(np^5)$, hence $O_s(p^6)$\\
Search unshifted parameters, with a larger size threshold & $O_s(np^4)$, hence $O_s(p^5)$\\
Round to a prescribed size from uniform sampling & $O_s(np^2)$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\subsection{Status, novelty, and limitations}
The original restriction mechanism, the companion's polynomial retention
bound, and conditional-expectation rounding are prior ingredients.
The exact array identities and their algorithmic consequences are proved
below. No exhaustive bibliographic priority claim is made for these
identities, which are related to familiar exponential generating functions
and multilinearization. The manuscript resolves the stated algorithmic
subproblem with an ambient-size polynomial bound; it does not resolve
near-linear extraction, sparse high-dimensional extraction, or all of the
companion's algorithmic questions.

No new global estimate for progression-free sets is asserted. For example,
the modern bound of Leng, Sah and Sawhney uses quasipolynomial inverse
theorems and a density-increment strategy~\cite{lssbounds}; improving the
implementation of one older restriction step is not by itself an
improvement of that global result. The present manuscript also leaves the
separate Section~16 closing-parameter problem untouched.

\srcnote{49}{Section 1}

Printed below: the abstract, the status statement of its title page and Section~1; Sections~2--6 form a chapter of Part~II (Section~\ref{gsr:en:sec:twocube}), Section~7 a chapter of Part~III (Section~\ref{gsr:cc:sec:dualtest}), Section~8 stands in the Part~II chapter on Lemma~16.10 after source~50 (Section~\ref{gsr:en:sec:branchcover}), Sections~9--11 are in Part~V. Its plot is drawn with \texttt{pgfplots}, now loaded by this report. Its `question' environment (``Question'', numbered within sections) is set in this report's `Question' style.}
\begin{partabstract}{49}
We develop three refinements of the framework underlying Gowers'
quantitative proof of Szemer\'edi's theorem. First, in sufficiently large
prime characteristic we classify the
derivative-rank-two multiaffine polynomials that are ternary-valued on a
Boolean cube. Their translation certificates contribute no new component
outside the signed-coordinate arrangement. This determines the second
coefficient in the degeneracy probability of two congruent coordinate
cubes in every fixed dimension, gives a finite cubic-order remainder
bound, and proves exact formulas in dimensions one and two. An exhaustive
integer certificate extends exactness to dimension three for every odd
prime. The exact low-dimensional formulas extend to every finite field
of characteristic at least five. A full-subfield alphabet theorem gives
an exact all-dimensional formula in characteristic three. More generally,
the prime-field degeneracy probability is eventually a fixed Laurent
polynomial in the prime.

Second, the complete fourth dual function of a two-harmonic test improves
the real, centered uniformity comparison on every finite abelian group
of odd order to
$\|f\|_{U^4}^{16}\ge(29/4)\|f\|_{U^2}^{16}$ and
$\|f\|_{U^5}^{4}\ge(50/29)\|f\|_{U^2}^{4}$.
The fourth factor improves to $15/2$ when a largest Fourier coefficient
has character order different from five. The finite coefficient lemma is
proved by a reproducible exact-arithmetic enumeration.

Third, from seven explicitly stated earlier structural interfaces we
prove a replacement cover theorem with recurrences that strictly decrease
the active dimension. It separates the global core, graph count, width
exponent, and minimum-width threshold, and yields a conditional recursive
replacement for the Section~16 multilinear inverse conclusion.

The manuscript distinguishes prior project results, new deductive proofs,
computer-assisted finite proofs, and imported hypotheses. It supplies
complete certificate generators and a research agenda. No sharp norm
constant or new global Szemer\'edi bound is claimed.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small
\noindent\textbf{Status.} Research manuscript; not peer reviewed or formally
verified. The exact finite verifiers are included. The Section~16
replacement is an implication from the stated interfaces, whose deep
source proofs are not newly certified here.
\end{quote}
\label{gsr:fm:49:sec:overview}

Gowers' proof~\cite{gowers} organizes a quantitative density-increment
argument around uniformity norms, additive structure, multiaffine phase
models, and the counting of coordinate-cube arrangements. These are
separate quantitative interfaces. Improving one of them is a mathematical
result, but a stronger final bound for Szemer\'edi's theorem requires a
complete propagation through the remaining interfaces. This article
concentrates on three places where a precise improvement can be proved
and independently checked.

The immediate baseline is the ProveIt Ramsey development~\cite{repo49},
including its corrected transcription of the paper and the earlier
project manuscripts. In particular, the degree-filtration report
\cite{repo49degree} already identifies the first-order two-cube
degeneracy coefficient and the affine translation arrangement. The
prime-torsion report~\cite{repo49primegap} already establishes a balanced
Fourier-moment profile and the upper bound $c_4^{\mathrm{odd}}\le2/3$.
The interpolation report~\cite{repo49interpolation} already improves
sampling and shared refinement and audits the closing numerical
comparison in Section~16. Those ingredients are credited and restated
where needed; they are not presented as new discoveries.

\subsection{The degeneracy result}

Let $\delta_{k,1}(p)$ be the proportion of degenerate ordered pairs of
congruent $k$-dimensional coordinate cubes over $\F_p$, in the precise
one-arrangement convention of section~\ref{gsr:en:49:sec:deg-setup}. Write
\begin{equation}
 L_k(p)=1-(1-p^{-1})^k\prod_{i=1}^k\left(1-\frac{2i+1}{p}\right).
 \label{gsr:fm:49:eq:L-intro}
\end{equation}
The prior argument gave $\delta_{k,1}(p)=L_k(p)+O_k(p^{-2})$.
We replace its possible codimension-two error by a codimension-three
error. In particular,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\displaystyle
 \delta_{k,1}(p)=\frac{k^2+3k}{p}
 -\frac{k(3k^3+14k^2+15k-14)}{6p^2}+O_k(p^{-3}).}
 \label{gsr:fm:49:eq:second-intro}
\end{equation}
An explicit error constant is given in theorem~\ref{gsr:en:49:deg:finite}. More strongly,
\begin{equation}
 \delta_{k,1}(p)=L_k(p)\qquad(k=1,2,3; p\text{ any odd prime}).
 \label{gsr:fm:49:eq:exact-intro}
\end{equation}
The cases $k\le2$ have elementary proofs. The case $k=3$ uses an exact
finite certificate, together with an algebraic argument reducing all
large primes to that certificate. Thus \eqref{gsr:fm:49:eq:exact-intro} is not an
extrapolation from checking a collection of primes.

The field extension is explicit. For $q=p^m$ with $p\ge5$, the same
product formula holds at $k\le3$ with $q$ in place of $p$. In
characteristic three there is a different, exact formula in every
dimension:
\begin{equation}
 \delta_{k,1}(3^m)
 =1-(1-3^{-m})^k\prod_{i=1}^k(1-3^{i-m}).
 \label{gsr:fm:49:eq:char3-intro}
\end{equation}
It follows from a linear-independence count over the prime subfield,
not from the rank-two classification; see corollary~\ref{gsr:en:49:deg:char-three}.

The underlying structural point is a classification of derivative rank
two in sufficiently large prime characteristic. Total degree is at most
derivative rank for a multiaffine polynomial.
A polynomial of rank two is therefore quadratic, and its quadratic part
splits across two disjoint sets of coordinates. Ternary Boolean values
force both sets to have size at most two. The resulting very small list
has no translation locus outside the already known signed-coordinate
hyperplanes. This answers the earlier exactness question through dimension
three and determines the next coefficient in all fixed dimensions.

\subsection{The real uniformity bounds}

All norms in this subsection use normalized counting measure. For a
complex function on a finite abelian group, our convention is
\begin{equation}
 \|f\|_{U^d}^{2^d}
 =\E_{x,h_1,\ldots,h_d}
    \prod_{\omega\in\{0,1\}^d}
       \mathcal C^{|\omega|}f(x+\omega\cdot h),
 \label{gsr:fm:49:eq:gowers-definition}
\end{equation}
where $\mathcal C$ is conjugation. On real functions all conjugations
disappear. Define
\[
 c_d^{\mathrm{odd}}=
 \sup\left\{\frac{\|f\|_{U^2}^4}{\|f\|_{U^d}^4}:
   |G|\text{ odd},\ f:G\to\R,\ f\ne0,\ \E f=0\right\}.
\]
The new estimates are
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\displaystyle
 c_4^{\mathrm{odd}}\le(4/29)^{1/4}=0.6094183098\ldots,
 \qquad c_5^{\mathrm{odd}}\le\frac{29}{50}=0.58.}
 \label{gsr:fm:49:eq:norm-intro}
\end{equation}
For functions whose largest Fourier coefficient can be chosen at a
character of order different from five, the fourth bound improves to
$(2/15)^{1/4}=0.6042750794\ldots$. The prior upper bound $2/3$ and the
new one refer to precisely the same normalized ratio.

The improvement uses a two-harmonic function as a dual test for an
\emph{arbitrary} $f$. The earlier report had used such a function as
an example giving a lower bound on the extremal constant. Computing
its complete dual reveals a much smaller unwanted Fourier tail and
turns that example into a useful upper-bound certificate. A moment
bound handles spread-out Fourier mass, while the dual test handles
concentrated mass. Character orders five, seven, nine, and eleven are
checked exactly rather than excluded. The fifth-order result combines
the new dual test with its own higher autocorrelation moment.

The earlier lower example remains valid:
\begin{equation}
 \frac{4804}{5465198316262956^{1/4}}
 =0.5587293909\ldots
 \ \le c_4^{\mathrm{odd}}\le0.6094183098\ldots.
 \label{gsr:fm:49:eq:c4-interval}
\end{equation}
This is an improved interval, not a determination of the exact constant.
The lower endpoint is from \cite{repo49primegap}.

\subsection{The replacement model theorem}

The third contribution is a complete new induction from stated source
interfaces. Its logical form is
\[
 \text{I1--I7}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \text{a cover theorem with explicit decreasing-dimension recurrences}.
\]
The global exceptional set is chosen before the local box and its error
tolerance. A separate ambient dimension is retained throughout the
induction, so a common-difference box partition is never lifted from
fewer coordinates without proof. Four controls remain distinct:
the prime threshold $N$, graph count $Q$, width exponent $c$, and
minimum width $T$. For fixed active and ambient dimensions, and
$u=a\gamma\varepsilon$, they satisfy bounds of the form
\begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
 N&\le(C/(a\gamma))^C,\qquad Q\le(C/u)^C,\\
 c&\ge\exp(-(C/u)^C),\qquad
 T\le\exp\bigl(\exp((C/u)^C)\bigr).
 \end{split}
 \label{gsr:fm:49:eq:rec-intro}
\end{equation}
The exact recurrences and their proof are in section~\ref{gsr:en:49:ac:section}.
This conditional result supplies the local multilinear-model conclusion
needed at the end of Section~16, with the new controls. The article does
not identify those controls with the original printed ones, certify all
earlier deep lemmas, or propagate a global progression bound.
