\section[{Source 50: The obstruction and its significance}]{Source 50. The obstruction and its significance}\label{gsr:fm:50:sec:d1}\label{gsr:fm:50:bc:sec:intro}
\srcnote{50}{Section 1}
\partsource{\textbf{Added in the ninth write, 7~October 2026. Delivered title page.} ``Combinatorics / Ramsey / Gowers--Szemer\'edi / Sharp Branch-Cover Profiles and a Counterexample to the Two-Input Form of Lemma 16.10 / Local quantitative obstructions in Gowers's Szemer\'edi framework / Research manuscript prepared for the ProveIt project / 6 October 2026''; \emph{the PDF author field reads ``Research manuscript prepared for the ProveIt project''; no statement on AI assistance is made}. Archive \file{ramsey\_branch\_cover\_obstructions.zip} (arrival \texttt{b6a8ee966}), manuscript \file{article.tex} (1,734 lines, 27 pages), pin \texttt{588552b79} (its \file{SOURCE\_AUDIT.md}, shipped as \file{50-branch-cover-SOURCE\_AUDIT.md}, records four blob identifiers). Printed below: the abstract, the status statement of its title page and Section~1; Sections~2--9 form, with source~49's Section~8 after them, a chapter of Part~II on Lemma~16.10 (Section~\ref{gsr:en:sec:branchcover}), Sections~10--13 and Appendices~A--C are in Part~V. Its macro \texttt{\textbackslash code} (\texttt{\textbackslash texttt\{\textbackslash detokenize\{\#1\}\}}) is set as this report's \texttt{\textbackslash filename}, the same definition, and its \texttt{\textbackslash pin} renamed \texttt{\textbackslash pinfifty}; its `question' environment (``Research question'', numbered 1--10 on its own counter) is set in this report's `Research question' style, numbered within its section; its listings are set in this report's listing style.}
\begin{partabstract}{50}
We study the minimum number of polynomial graphs required to cover a prescribed
fraction of a finite-alphabet function on long arithmetic progressions and on
partitions into product boxes. For a word whose symbol masses on a progression
are $b_1\ge\cdots\ge b_R$, a list of $q$ degree-at-most-$d$ polynomials covers at
most $\max_s\{b_1+\cdots+b_s+(q-s)dR\}$ points. If $b_q\ge dR$, the optimum is
exactly $b_1+\cdots+b_q$. Strict inequality gives rigidity and a quantitative
deficit for every list containing nonconstant polynomials. We extend this law to
product boxes, prove a global polynomial stability bound, and construct words
with any prescribed branch-mass profile simultaneously on all long modular
progressions. The construction is derandomizable by exact conditional
expectations. A second construction improves the sufficient scale to
$O(R(d+1)\log p)$ for growing alphabets at fixed relative error.

The main application is a counterexample to the precise two-premise
\filename{lemma_16_10} recorded in ProveIt's pinned Section 16 catalogue. At
$k=\theta=\gamma=1$, and for every sufficiently large prime modulus, the two
premises hold for a full-domain function $F(h,y)=a(y)$, but the conclusion fails.
The failure persists after arbitrary adaptive partitions into proper boxes and
is separated from the required retained mass by a fixed positive margin. This
is stronger than the previously documented failure of a numerical comparison.
The conclusion concerns the stated abstraction, not Szemer\'edi's theorem or
all the additional hypotheses in Gowers's upstream construction. We give a
parameter-preserving repair interface, exact finite verification artifacts, a
formalization plan, and further research questions. We also prove that the full-domain
product property at $\gamma=1$ forces multiaffinity, excluding these witnesses
from that stronger upstream hypothesis.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small
\noindent\textbf{Status.} The results are proved in the mathematical manuscript. The new
counterexample is not a Lean-kernel-checked theorem and has not undergone
independent review. The elementary probabilistic and root-counting ingredients
are classical; no comprehensive priority claim is made for their combination.
No improved global bound for progression-free sets is asserted.
\end{quote}

\subsection{Which problem is being resolved?}
Gowers's proof of Szemer\'edi's theorem passes through multiple multilinearity
and a local-to-global lifting step in Section 16~\cite{gowers}. In the ProveIt
implementation, the catalogue entry \filename{lemma_16_10} isolates two inputs:
multiple multilinearity of the cross-sections obtained by fixing the final
coordinate, and the fibrewise affine covers supplied by the preceding
lemma~\cite{repo50section16}. The repository already warns that the advertised
closing numerical comparison is not justified. A separate file proves an
obstruction to that comparison, while explicitly distinguishing it from a
counterexample to the assertion~\cite{repo50comparison}.

Our principal result closes that particular logical gap in the negative:
\emph{the two-input implication itself is false with the recorded quantitative
controls}. It is not enough to replace the unsuccessful numerical calculation
by a more efficient argument. At least one hypothesis, conclusion, or control
function must change.

This is a local research result, rather than a new global Szemer\'edi bound.
Its significance is that the false abstraction sits at a proof interface:
trying to prove it, or using it as though it were established, would obstruct a
sound completion of the argument. The affirmative results identify the
quantitative information that is lost at that interface.

\subsection{The model example}
Let $a:\F_p\to\{v_1,\dots,v_R\}$ be a word over $R$ distinct field elements and
put
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:50:bc:eq:model}
 F(h,y)=a(y),\qquad h\in\F_p^k,\quad y\in\F_p.
\end{equation}
Every fixed-$y$ cross-section is constant. Every final-coordinate fibre is
covered, with no exceptional points, by the $R$ constant affine maps
$y\mapsto v_j$. These are exceptionally strong qualitative hypotheses.
Nevertheless, a nonconstant affine function takes any one value $v_j$ at most
once. On a long progression on which all symbols have nearly equal masses, one
constant graph covers about $1/R$ of the word, and a nonconstant affine graph
covers at most $R$ points. Thus $q$ graphs cannot cover much more than $q/R$ of
the progression. The same statement holds on every cell of a box partition.

The issue is not an inability to find suitable anchors or to interpolate.
All $R$ branches are already global constants. The obstruction is the attempted
removal of branch complexity from the output budget.

\subsection{An overview of the results}
The exact one-dimensional cover law is Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:50:bc:thm:exact}; its
product-box and stability versions are Theorems~\ref{gsr:en:50:bc:thm:product} and
\ref{gsr:en:50:bc:thm:global}. Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:50:bc:thm:balanced} constructs words balanced on
all sufficiently long modular progressions, and
Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:50:bc:thm:derandomize} gives an exact deterministic construction.
Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:50:bc:thm:profile} realizes every finite probability profile as a
local polynomial-cover profile.

Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:50:bc:thm:counterexample} then refutes the pinned two-input form of
Lemma 16.10, with every witness and numerical inequality written out. A
particularly concrete choice is
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:50:bc:eq:overview-parameters}
 E=2^{1024},\qquad Q=2^E,\qquad R=4Q,\qquad c=Q^{-1}.
\end{equation}
For every prime $p>2^{4096Q^4}$ there is a word $a$ for which both inputs hold,
whereas every permitted output cover retains at most $5p^2/16$, less than the
required $p^2/2$. The size is enormous because we instantiate the repository's
own controls. The mechanism has no enormous-constant dependence: the general
cover laws apply to small parameters as well.

\begin{partabstract}{51}
For arbitrarily large prime moduli we construct a genuine Section 13 context, complete Stage 13.4 and 13.5 data, and explicit Stage 13.6--13.9 data satisfying all six numerical budgets in the pinned bilinear-extraction theorem and the retained upper length bound $|R|\le |Q|$. Nevertheless, the chosen product $S\times U$ contains no proper common-step square of side length two. Thus these hypotheses and retained predicates do not imply the source's exact square-grid predicate for arbitrary witnesses. The construction uses a horizontal strip, the zero function, a uniformly controlled Fourier spectrum, and two progressions with disjoint nonzero difference sets. Its density $\alpha=\lfloor N/8\rfloor/N$ varies with $N$; every asymptotic estimate is uniform on $[1/16,1/8]$.

This refutes a universal retained-data implication, not existential extraction, particular proof-term witnesses, Corollary 13.10, or Szemer\'edi's theorem. We also prove a constructive counterpart for suitably selected witnesses. Preserving the short parent from the actual budget construction, a balanced aligned partition and short-carrier rectification connect the existing all-scale coefficient theorem to the already available quarter-density cover. The direct selection attains the original effective density and width constants while bypassing the unchanged Stage 13.9 interface. The geometric proofs are self-contained; the analytic coefficient theorem is explicitly imported from pinned source. The final compared source already constructs a complete square with one large-prime threshold uniform above any fixed positive lower density bound; we distinguish this from its older fixed-exact-density API. No new Lean verification is claimed. The companion uses bounded exact diagnostics and curated source hashes, never astronomical numerical witnesses.
\end{partabstract}
The question concerns information retained between successive extraction steps. A source theorem can construct suitable witnesses without its recorded output predicates characterizing every witness that would work in a later proof. Confusing these two assertions is consequential here: the Stage 13.9 step relation is modular, whereas a square-cover argument needs a quantitative relation between ordinary integer indices.

We use the source definitions at commit \texttt{aad4789f} of the public repository \emph{VladimirReshetnikov/ProveIt}. The stage definitions, explicit budget theorem, and exact-grid definition are unchanged at the later commit \texttt{330102ae}. That later commit adds a conditional common-step covering theorem, discussed in Section~\ref{gsr:en:51:sec:cover}. Later pinned sources add aligned parent selection, complete fixed-density square extraction, and finally a threshold uniform over varying actual densities; Sections~\ref{gsr:en:51:sec:alignedstatus}--\ref{gsr:en:51:sec:uniformcurrent} record those developments. The complete file map and byte-verification scope appear in Appendix~\ref{gsr:fz:51:sec:sources}.

A modular progression is an indexed object
\[
 P(a,d;L)=\{a+jd:0\le j<L\}\subseteq\Z/N\Z.
\]
It is \emph{proper} when its displayed parameterization is injective, equivalently when its carrier has cardinality $L$. Modular wrapping is permitted. Nonzero step is a separate requirement in the source, including for singleton progressions. We write $\lenfiftyone P=L$ and $\stfiftyone P=d$. For proper progressions we freely identify their lengths with their carrier cardinalities.

\begin{theorem}[Full-budget failure of the universal grid implication]\label{gsr:fm:51:thm:main}
For every sufficiently large prime $N$, there exist:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item a \codefiftyone{Section13Context} with
$\alpha=\lfloor N/8\rfloor/N\in[1/16,1/8]$, $\eta=2^{-44}$, and $\phi=0$;
\item data $D,E$ satisfying the complete predicates \codefiftyone{IsStage134Data} at the cutoff $\theta=\lambda_{10}(\alpha^{32}/16)$ and \codefiftyone{IsStage135Data};
\item a positive integer $m$ satisfying all six explicit budgets of the theorem\\
\codefiftyone{section13\_\allowbreak bilinear\_\allowbreak extraction\_\allowbreak of\_\allowbreak budgets};
\item data $F,G,H,J$ satisfying all four predicates \codefiftyone{IsStage136Data}, \codefiftyone{IsStage137Data}, \codefiftyone{IsStage138Data}, and \codefiftyone{IsStage139Data}, as well as $\lenfiftyone R\le\lenfiftyone Q$;
\end{enumerate}
for which $y=0$, the final retained set is exactly $S\times U$, and
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:51:eq:diffintersection}
 (S-S)\cap(U-U)=\{0\}.
\end{equation}
Consequently $S\times U$ contains no product of two proper progressions of the same nonzero step and length at least two. In particular, \codefiftyone{Corollary1310Grid} is false for these selected data.
\end{theorem}

Section~\ref{gsr:en:51:sec:constructive} proves the positive counterpart: suitable witness selection under the same budgets yields a bilinear square with the intended effective constants. The negative theorem gives a counterexample to the universal assertion
\[
 \text{full antecedent and all retained predicates}
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \text{grid for those same retained witnesses}.
\]
It leaves the following existential statements untouched:
\begin{itemize}
\item The budget theorem asserts the existence of $F,G,H,J$ satisfying its output predicates. Our chosen data themselves satisfy those predicates.
\item The newer context-to-extraction theorem constructs a whole chain at each fixed positive density at most $1/6$, once the prime modulus is sufficiently large. We neither rerun nor replace that construction.
\item Section~\ref{gsr:en:51:sec:constructive} arranges additional geometry by suitable reselection. The counterexample does not identify the witnesses chosen by any particular Lean proof term.
\item The catalogue conclusion of Corollary 13.10 does not require its output square to lie inside $S\times(U+y)$, or its output set to lie inside $J.D$. Since $\phi=0$ everywhere here, that conclusion is readily satisfied by a full step-one square.
\end{itemize}
These distinctions are part of the claim, rather than qualifications added after it.

\begin{partabstract}{52}
The preserved propositions \codefiftyone{lemma\_\allowbreak 13\_\allowbreak 7\_\allowbreak without\_\allowbreak domain} and
\codefiftyone{lemma\_\allowbreak 13\_\allowbreak 7\_\allowbreak without\_\allowbreak prime\_\allowbreak assumption} are false at the pinned source interface. We give exact finite counterexamples: a short progression of even residues in $\Z/2^k\Z$ supports an order-eight Freiman map given by division of its integer coordinates by two, while every ambient affine function agrees with it at at most one point. The Stage 13.7 length and mass requirements are therefore incompatible. Every field of the context and every Stage 13.6 conjunct is verified directly, with the source's unnormalized arrangement count.

A second explicit construction also satisfies the genuine Stage 13.4 and 13.5 predicates. A further variant makes the input progressions have unit step; ambient affine agreement is then bounded by two points per row. Thus adding the initial-stage predicates alone, or requiring a unit common input step alone, does not repair the statements. The explicit unit-step construction satisfying both initial-stage predicates has $\len R>\len Q$. A separate nonunit-step family removes that limitation: it has genuine initial stages at the exact Section 10 cutoff, $R\subseteq Q$, and all six numerical budgets of the source extraction theorem, while still admitting no Stage 13.7 output. The prime hypothesis of that theorem is false for these examples. The elementary obstruction extends to every fixed prime-power family, and a two-point model in $\Z/18\Z$ explains why bounded-order Freiman identities need not imply ambient affine extendability. These are mathematical refutations of unproved encoded propositions, not counterexamples to the prime-corrected Lean theorem, a new Lean verification, a priority claim, or a claim about the global Szemer\'edi argument. The companion performs bounded exact checks without constructing the astronomical moduli.
\end{partabstract}
The key distinction is between affine dependence on a progression parameter and affine dependence on the ambient residue. Over a field these descriptions are interchangeable when the progression step is nonzero. Over a composite modulus that conversion can fail, even when all short additive relations are preserved. In the present interface it is the ambient meaning that is required.

All source claims in this report are pinned to the public repository
\emph{VladimirReshetnikov/ProveIt}, commit
\begin{center}\small\texttt{5c9a442d263632fdcd4e9690154c12c2dcc70b53}.\end{center}

The complete byte contents of \codefiftyone{Definitions.lean} and \codefiftyone{Sections12\_13.lean} agree with the earlier construction pin \texttt{77f7d8c1}; the hashes and precise source ranges are recorded in Appendix~\ref{gsr:fz:52:app:sources}. We do not track unrelated changes after this fixed source comparison.

\begin{theorem}[An explicit counterexample with minimal input requirements]\label{gsr:fm:52:thm:base}
Let
\[
 k=939\cdot2^{1892}+5,\qquad N=2^k,\qquad m=N/16.
\]
There are a genuine \codefiftyone{Section13Context} $S_0$ of density $\alpha=1/16$ and records $D,E,F$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item \codefiftyone{IsStage135Data} and \codefiftyone{IsStage136Data} hold;
\item $D.P=E.Q=F.R=(0,2,m)$, so $\len R=\len Q$;
\item no record $G$ satisfies \codefiftyone{IsStage137DataWithoutDomain}.
\end{enumerate}
In particular both preserved all-moduli Stage 13.7 propositions are false. No Stage 13.4 predicate is asserted for this first construction.
\end{theorem}
Here ``minimal input requirements'' describes the logical premises being used. It is not a claim that $N$ is the smallest counterexample modulus.

\begin{theorem}[Genuine initial stages and unit input steps]\label{gsr:fm:52:thm:strengthening}
There is a second, explicitly specified dyadic modulus with a context of density $1/16$, an allowed spectral threshold $\theta=\alpha^{32}/4$, and records $D,E,F$ satisfying all three predicates
\[
 \codefiftyone{IsStage134Data},\quad \codefiftyone{IsStage135Data},\quad
 \codefiftyone{IsStage136Data},
\]
for which no weak Stage 13.7 output exists. This can be done with $D.P$, $E.Q$, and $F.R$ all of step $1$. In this genuine-initial-stage construction,
\[
 \len(D.P)=\len(E.Q)=5<\len(F.R).
\]
Separately, there is an explicit unit-step counterexample with $D.P=E.Q=F.R$ and genuine Stage 13.5 and 13.6 predicates, without a Stage 13.4 certificate.
\end{theorem}
Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:52:thm:budgets} further gives a nonunit-step family with genuine initial stages, $R\subseteq Q$, the exact Section 10 cutoff and all six numerical budgets. Theorem~\ref{gsr:fm:52:thm:strengthening} deliberately separates its two sets of extra properties. It does not refute a statement requiring \emph{simultaneously} the genuine Stage 13.4 predicate, a unit common step, and $\len R\le\len Q$.

\paragraph{What is refuted.}
The two target declarations are \codefiftyone{def ... : Prop}. They universally quantify over a nonzero natural modulus, a context and records, then assume only \codefiftyone{IsStage136Data}. Their conclusions assert the existence of $G$ satisfying respectively the weak and full Stage 13.7 predicates. A record called \codefiftyone{Stage134Data} does not contain a certificate of \codefiftyone{IsStage134Data}; the latter is a separate predicate. The same distinction applies at Stage 13.5. These quantifiers are material to Theorem~\ref{gsr:fm:52:thm:base}, although Theorem~\ref{gsr:fm:52:thm:strengthening} removes that particular concern by checking both extra predicates directly.

\paragraph{What remains separate.}
The corrected proposition \codefiftyone{lemma\_13\_7} quantifies over $N$ with \codefiftyone{Fact N.Prime}. The pinned file \codefiftyone{Proofs13CompleteRowExtraction.lean} contains the theorem \codefiftyone{lemma\_13\_7\_holds : lemma\_13\_7}. Our moduli are composite and cannot instantiate that hypothesis. We have read its statement and source, but have not rerun its Lean dependency build or kernel audit. Nothing here challenges that corrected result, later prime-modulus square extraction, or a correlation theorem that takes ambient polynomial coefficients as part of its input.

\srcnote{53}{Section 1}

It numbers its equations consecutively through the manuscript; here they are numbered within sections.}
\begin{partabstract}{53}
We give a single explicit threshold for bilinear square extraction from the prime-modulus Section 13 context, uniformly over all actual densities above a prescribed positive lower bound. If $0<a_0\le a\le1$, the threshold depends only on $a_0$, while both the side exponent and retained density use the actual $a$. The seven sufficient scale and rounding conditions collapse exactly to
\[
 N_0(a_0)=\left\lceil\left(\frac8{c(a_0)}\right)^{1/\gamma(a_0)}\right\rceil.
\]
Here $c$ and $\gamma$ are explicit positive functions given below. At this same threshold, suitable choices in the all-density construction give a proper common-step square of side at least
$\tfrac12N^{4\gamma(a)}-1\ge N^{3\gamma(a)}$, retaining density at least $2^{-137}a^{704}$ and agreement with the original phase on the retained set.

The geometric improvement preserves the actual short parent in the Stage 13.6 witness, rectifies two subprogressions, uses balanced aligned parents, and retains the full coefficient-localization exponent. The scalar threshold comparison and geometric lemmas are proved here; the analytic extraction theorems are explicitly imported from pinned source. The basic density-uniform square theorem is already upstream. This report supplies a mathematical quantitative refinement, without claiming a new Lean implementation, kernel replay, priority result, arbitrary-witness catalogue repair, or global Szemer\'edi bound. Bounded exact diagnostics accompany the proof and never evaluate the astronomical thresholds.
\end{partabstract}
For $0<a\le1$, define
\begin{align}
 K(a)&=2^{114}a^{-320},& Q(a)&=2^{1048576}a^{-2097152},\label{gsr:fm:53:eq:KQ}\\
 c(a)&=\tfrac12\,2^{-228K(a)}a^{576K(a)},&
 \beta(a)&=2^{-13Q(a)},\label{gsr:fm:53:eq:cbeta}\\
 f(a)&=2^{-100}a^{448},& g(a)&=2^{-284}a^{1408},\label{gsr:fm:53:eq:fg}\\
 \gamma(a)&=\frac{\beta(a)f(a)g(a)}4
           =2^{-386}a^{1856}2^{-13Q(a)}.\label{gsr:fm:53:eq:gamma}
\end{align}
All real powers in this report have positive bases. Natural lengths, floors and ceilings are regarded as real numbers when used in such powers.

\begin{theorem}[Explicit uniform extraction with actual density]\label{gsr:fm:53:thm:main}
Fix $0<a_0\le1$ and put
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:53:eq:N0}
 N_0(a_0)=\left\lceil\left(\frac8{c(a_0)}\right)^{1/\gamma(a_0)}\right\rceil.
\end{equation}
For every prime $N\ge N_0(a_0)$ and every Section 13 context $(A,\phi,a)$ with $a_0\le a\le1$, there are proper progressions $V,W$ in $\F_N$ with the same nonzero step and the same length $k$, and a set $B$, such that
\begin{align}
 k&\ge D(a)N^{4\gamma(a)}-1
      \ge\tfrac12N^{4\gamma(a)}-1
      \ge N^{3\gamma(a)},\label{gsr:fm:53:eq:mainlength}\\
 B&\subseteq A\cap(V\times W),&
 |B|&\ge2^{-137}a^{704}k^2,\label{gsr:fm:53:eq:mainmass}
\end{align}
where
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:53:eq:D}
 D(a)=2^{-g(a)}c(a)^{f(a)g(a)}>\tfrac12.
\end{equation}
There are coefficients $c_{00},c_{10},c_{01},c_{11}\in\F_N$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:53:eq:bilinear}
 \phi(x,z)=c_{00}+c_{10}x+c_{01}z+c_{11}xz\qquad((x,z)\in B).
\end{equation}
The context assumptions are stated in Section~\ref{gsr:en:53:sec:context}. In particular, the theorem does not concern an arbitrary dense set with an arbitrary phase.
\end{theorem}

 =\left\lceil 2^{\,2^{\,14\cdot2^{1048576}a_0^{-2097152}}}\right\rceil

\section[{Source 54: The result and its place in the proof}]{Source 54. The result and its place in the proof}\label{gsr:fm:54:sec:d1}
\srcnote{54}{Section 1}
\partsource{\textbf{Added in the tenth write, 7~October 2026. Delivered title block.} ``A Single Quadratic Phase Across All Translates / Spectral extraction, offset rigidity, and sharp stability in Gowers's Section 8 / Research manuscript prepared for the ProveIt project / 6 October 2026''; \emph{the PDF author field reads the same; no statement on AI assistance is made}. Archive \file{Gowers\_Single\_Phase\_Research.zip} (arrival \texttt{aa1d86f6f}), manuscript \file{article.tex} (1,387 lines, 20 pages), pin \texttt{6a6d7961c} (its \file{SOURCE\_AUDIT.md}, shipped as \file{54-single-phase-SOURCE\_AUDIT.md}, records four blob identifiers and the README blob \texttt{b2e25fa}). Printed below: the abstract and Section~1; Sections~2--9 form a chapter of Part~II on Proposition~8.1 (Section~\ref{gsr:en:sec:singlephase}), Sections~10--12 are in Part~V. Its macro \texttt{\textbackslash ee} (the letter $\mathrm e$, not this report's one-argument $\mathrm e(\cdot)$) is set as this report's \texttt{\textbackslash e}, which prints the same; its `question' environment (``Question'', on the shared counter) is set in this report's `Question' style.}
\begin{partabstract}{54}
We strengthen the quadratic-bias extraction in Proposition 8.1 of Gowers's
2001 proof of Szemer\'edi's theorem. One global quadratic polynomial suffices
simultaneously on every translate of the input set; no arithmetic-progression
hypothesis is needed for the extraction itself. For the balanced function of
a set of density $\delta$, the coefficient $1/\sqrt2$ can be replaced by
$[\delta(1-\delta)\max(\delta,1-\delta)]^{-1}$, which is at least $27/4$.
The underlying statement is an exact mixed, weighted Fourier factorization
with a spectral-overlap parameter and optimal coefficient one. Quadratic
refinements extend it to every finite abelian group, including even-order
groups with genuinely nonclassical quadratic phases.

We also identify the exact global energy ceilings for an affine selector's
intercept: after removing its quadratic part, an offset of order $1,2,3$, or
at least $4$ has normalized ceiling $1,1/2,1/3$, or $1/4$, respectively.
We classify all equality cases and prove dimension-free stability. Orders
at most four have the optimal $L^2$ recovery exponent $1/2$; every order at
least five has the optimal exponent $1/4$. A four-frequency construction
proves that the latter loss cannot be removed. A graph formulation extends
the ceilings to simultaneous intercepts via the classical Motzkin--Straus
theorem. All assertions are proved in the article; finite checks and an
integration plan accompany it. These are local structural improvements,
not a claim of an improved end-to-end Szemer\'edi bound.
\end{partabstract}
\label{gsr:fm:54:sec:intro}

\subsection{The Section 8 interface}
Let $N$ be odd, let $A\subseteq\Z/N\Z$ have density
$0<\delta<1$, and write $f=\one_A-\delta$. Put
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:54:eq:sigmaB}
 \sigma=\E_x|f(x)|^2=\delta(1-\delta),\qquad
 B=\norm f_\infty=\max(\delta,1-\delta).
\end{equation}
Here and throughout, group averages are normalized. For comparison with
Gowers, define the \emph{unnormalized} derivative Fourier coefficient
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:54:eq:gowers-coeff}
 D_h(r)=\sum_{x\in\Z/N\Z}f(x)\overline{f(x-h)}\e(-rx/N),
 \qquad \e(t)=\exp(2\pi i t).
\end{equation}
The conjugation does not change this expression for a balanced function,
which is real-valued.

Proposition 8.1 of \cite{gowers} starts with an arithmetic progression $P$ of
cardinality $T$ and an affine selector $h\mapsto\lambda h+\mu$ satisfying
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:54:eq:input}
 \sum_{h\in P}|D_h(\lambda h+\mu)|^2\geq\beta N^2T.
\end{equation}
It produces quadratic polynomials $\psi_s$, allowed to depend on the
translate, for which
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:54:eq:old}
 \sum_s\left|\sum_{z\in P+s} f(z)\e(-\psi_s(z)/N)\right|
 \geq \frac{\beta NT}{\sqrt2}.
\end{equation}
The corrected repository statement explicitly records oddness of $N$;
its proof module is \texttt{Proofs08QuadraticBias.lean} \cite{repo54}.

\begin{theorem}[One common quadratic polynomial]\label{gsr:fm:54:thm:main}
Let $N$ be odd and let $\varnothing\ne P\subseteq\Z/N\Z$ be arbitrary.
Assume $\beta>0$ and \eqref{gsr:fm:54:eq:input}. There is one $r\in\Z/N\Z$ such that the polynomial
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:54:eq:psi}
 \psi(z)=2^{-1}\lambda z^2+rz\quad\text{in }\Z/N\Z
\end{equation}
satisfies
\begin{align}
 \sum_s |f(s)|
 \left|\sum_{z\in P+s}f(z)\e(-\psi(z)/N)\right|
 &\geq \frac{\beta NT}{\sigma},\label{gsr:fm:54:eq:main-weighted}\\
 \sum_s
 \left|\sum_{z\in P+s}f(z)\e(-\psi(z)/N)\right|
 &\geq \frac{\beta NT}{B\sigma}
 \geq \frac{27}{4}\beta NT.\label{gsr:fm:54:eq:main-unweighted}
\end{align}
More precisely, $\sigma$ in both denominators can be replaced by the
spectral overlap $\Ov_\mu(g)$ defined in Section~\ref{gsr:en:54:sec:factor}, where
$g(z)=f(z)\e(-2^{-1}\lambda z^2/N)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{writenote}[7 October 2026; sources 54--59]
\emph{Against Proposition~8.1 and the formal statement} (checked at the write). For $0<t=\min(\delta,1-\delta)\le1/2$, $B\sigma=t(1-t)^2$ has derivative $(1-t)(1-3t)$, so its maximum is $4/27$ at $t=1/3$ and $1/(B\sigma)\ge27/4>1/\sqrt2$. Taking $\psi_s=\psi$ for every $s$ therefore gives Gowers's conclusion, with a polynomial of degree two in $z$ (the inverse $2^{-1}$ exists because $N$ is odd), for every nonempty $P$, so in particular for the progression of the formal statement. \file{proposition_8_1} (\file{Sections08\_09.lean}, line~29) assumes $N$ odd and a progression $P$ (\file{ModAP}) and asks for translate-dependent polynomials $\psi_s$ of degree at most two with the constant $1/\sqrt2$; for densities $0$ and $1$ the balanced function vanishes and its hypothesis forces $\beta\le0$. The theorem thus implies the catalogue statement on paper; the catalogue statement is already exact (\file{proposition_8_1_holds}, \file{Proofs08QuadraticBias.lean}, line~1069), and nothing of this source is formalized. The constant $27/4$ is the uniform consequence of the amplitude bound, not an optimum over balanced indicators (Remark after the proof; item~\ref{gsr:fz:q:II:commonphase}).
\end{writenote}

The same $\psi$ occurs in \emph{every} summand. The theorem does not assert a
lower bound on every individual translate, nor does it assert that the same
polynomial works for every choice of $P$. Its improvements over the cited
interface are the common phase, the amplitude dependence, the explicit
constant, and the removal of the progression hypothesis. The last point
concerns extraction only: later recurrence and partition arguments may
still require progression geometry.

The theorem follows from a short Fourier factorization, but that
factorization also retains information normally lost by pointwise
Cauchy--Schwarz. We develop its mixed form, its equality deficit, and a
constructive selector before studying its extremal consequences.

\subsection{Offset rigidity and its stability}
For a finite abelian group $G$, let $\widehat G$ be its character group,
written additively as homomorphisms $G\to\T=\R/\Z$. For $g:G\to\C$ define
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:54:eq:ambiguity-intro}
 A_\eta(g)(h)=\E_x g(x+h)\overline{g(x)}\e(-\eta(x)),
 \qquad \En_\eta(g)=\E_h|A_\eta(g)(h)|^2.
\end{equation}
Let $\sigma=\norm g_2^2>0$. The exact identity proved below is
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:54:eq:power-intro}
 \frac{\En_\eta(g)}{\sigma^2}
 =\sum_{\xi\in\widehat G}p_\xi p_{\xi-\eta},\qquad
 p_\xi=\frac{|\widehat g(\xi)|^2}{\sigma}.
\end{equation}
Thus the relevant extremal problem is a quadratic program on disjoint
cycles. Its value is a specialization of classical graph optimization
\cite{motzkinstraus}; the explicit stability statement is developed here.

\begin{theorem}[Exact offset ceilings and recovery exponents]
\label{gsr:fm:54:thm:overview-offset}
Put $m=\ord(\eta)$ and
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:54:eq:cm}
 c_m=\begin{cases}
 1,&m=1,\\
 1/2,&m=2,\\
 1/3,&m=3,\\
 1/4,&m\geq4.
 \end{cases}
\end{equation}
Then $\En_\eta(g)\leq c_m\sigma^2$, and every constant is best possible.
All extremizers are described by the power-spectrum table in
Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:54:thm:ceilings}.

If $0\leq\varepsilon\leq1/16$ and
$\En_\eta(g)\geq(c_m-\varepsilon)\sigma^2$, there is an exact extremizer
$g_*$ with $\norm{g_*}_2^2=\sigma$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:54:eq:overview-stability}
 \norm{g-g_*}_2\leq
 \begin{cases}
 K_m\sqrt\sigma\,\varepsilon^{1/2},&m\leq4,\\
 3\sqrt\sigma\,\varepsilon^{1/4},&m\geq5,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad (K_1,K_2,K_3,K_4)=(\sqrt2,\sqrt5,\sqrt{10},3).
\end{equation}
The exponents are optimal, uniformly over the ambient group whenever the
indicated nontrivial families exist. The constants $K_m$ and $3$ are not
claimed optimal.
\end{theorem}

For $m\geq5$, an extremizer has at most three Fourier frequencies in a
single $\eta$-orbit, with half the power at the central frequency and half
on its two neighbors. Near an intersection of two such extremal families,
a small fourth frequency costs only the square of its power. This is the
source of the fourth-root recovery exponent, not a defect of a repeated
Cauchy--Schwarz argument.

\subsection{Scope and attribution}
The ingredients used here---finite Fourier inversion, quadratic
refinements, elementary graph quadratic programs, and conversion from
power-spectrum distance to $L^2$ distance---are standard. No novelty claim
is made for them or for the Motzkin--Straus extremal value. The proposed
contribution is their precise common-phase formulation at the Section 8
interface, the resulting constants, the full offset classification, and
the explicit sharp-exponent recovery theorem and localization consequences.
The inspected repository index and source audit were checked for overlap;
the entire research corpus was not exhaustively audited. Priority in the
wider literature is therefore not certified.

A local improvement must not be confused with the current global
quantitative problem. For example, Leng--Sah--Sawhney prove
$r_k(N)\ll N\exp(- (\log\log N)^{c_k})$ for $k\geq5$ \cite{lssbounds}.
The September 2026 preprint of Mili\'cevi\'c gives a high-characteristic
quasipolynomial inverse theorem via Freiman multihomomorphisms
\cite{milicevic}. Neither result is a proof dependency here, and neither
is superseded by the present local extraction.

\section[{Source 55: The endpoint problem and its place in Gowers's proof}]{Source 55. The endpoint problem and its place in Gowers's proof}\label{gsr:fm:55:sec:d1}
\srcnote{55}{Section 1}
\partsource{\textbf{Added in the tenth write, 7~October 2026. Delivered title page.} ``ProveIt research manuscript / Sharp Second-Order Stability at the Polynomial-Phase Endpoint of Gowers Norms / A parity-sensitive refinement of the Szemer\'edi framework / Prepared with ChatGPT for Vladimir Reshetnikov / October 2026''; \emph{the PDF author field reads ``ChatGPT; research manuscript prepared for Vladimir Reshetnikov''}. Archive \file{gowers\_endpoint\_stability.zip} (arrival \texttt{aa1d86f6f}), manuscript \file{article.tex} (1,498 lines, 21 pages), pin \texttt{128f514af} (its \file{SOURCE\_AUDIT.md}, shipped as \file{55-endpoint-stability-SOURCE\_AUDIT.md}, also names the earlier commit \texttt{6a6d7961c}). Printed below: the abstract, the status statement of its title page and Section~1; Sections~2--11 form, with source~57's Section~5 after them, a chapter of Part~II on the Proposition~6.1 endpoint (Section~\ref{gsr:en:sec:phaseendpoint}), Sections~12--13 and Appendices~A--B are in Part~V. It uses \texttt{cleveref} (options \texttt{nameinlink}, \texttt{noabbrev}); its references are written out as cleveref prints them (lowercase names). Its macro \texttt{\textbackslash U} ($\mathcal U_d$, not this report's $\mathcal U$) is renamed \texttt{\textbackslash Ufiftyfive}; its `question' environment (``Question'', on the shared counter) is set in this report's `Question' style.}
\begin{partabstract}{55}
Let $d\ge2$, let $G$ be a nontrivial finite abelian group, and let
$|f|\le1$. Write $\eps=1-\norm f_{U^d(G)}^{2^d}$ and let $D_d(f)$ be
the squared normalized $L^2$ distance from $f$ to the phase polynomials
of degree at most $d-1$, including nonclassical phases. We prove
\[
 D_d(f)\le 2^{1-d}\eps+b_d(G)\eps^2+O_d(\eps^3),
 \qquad
 b_d(G)=
 \begin{cases}
 (3^d-1)/(2\cdot4^d),& |G|\text{ odd},\\
 (1-4^{-d})/3,& |G|\text{ even}.
 \end{cases}
\]
The error and the sufficiently small range are uniform in $G$.
Both coefficients are sharp on every fixed nontrivial group of the indicated
parity. We also prove a torsion-profile refinement and classify the tangent
perturbations of second-order extremizers: a conjugate pair of characters in
odd order, and a single order-two character in even order.

The local estimate has a fully explicit radius and cubic error. Its central
ingredient is a fifth-order cancellation for bounded complex functions,
obtained from triple independence of cube vertices and the pointwise constraint
$|f|\le1$. A four-vertex lattice census identifies the two-torsion contribution.
The passage from near-maximal norm to the explicit local neighborhood uses
the published qualitative theorem of Eisner and Tao. No new global bound in
Szemer\'edi's theorem is asserted.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small
\noindent\textbf{Status.} AI-assisted research draft with complete mathematical proofs
and reproducible finite checks. It has not been refereed or verified in a proof
assistant. Publication priority for the sharpened statements is not established.
The distinction between imported results, proved refinements, and proposed
research questions is maintained throughout.
\end{quote}

Gowers's proof of Szemer\'edi's theorem organizes the analysis of arithmetic
patterns around iterated multiplicative differences, uniformity, and the
extraction and integration of structured phase information
\cite{gowers}. Its small-uniformity counting estimates and its inverse steps
are complementary: the former control pseudorandom errors, while the latter
locate algebraic structure. This article concerns the extreme structured end
of that framework, where a normalized Gowers norm is close to its maximum.

This is not the general inverse problem at a fixed small positive norm.
Here the objective is sharper: determine the best possible distance to an
exact polynomial phase as the cubical defect tends to zero. The resulting
estimate can be applied after an inverse or integration argument has already
produced a sufficiently accurate phase candidate. It does not, by itself,
improve the density range in the full Szemer\'edi iteration.

\subsection{Normalization and the question answered}

All expectations below are normalized counting averages. Put
$q=2^d$, and for a function $f:G\to\C$ define
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:55:eq:cube}
 \Ufiftyfive(f)=\norm f_{U^d(G)}^q
 =\E_{x,h_1,\ldots,h_d\in G}
   \prod_{\omega\in\{0,1\}^d}
       \cC^{|\omega|} f(x+\omega\cdot h),
\end{equation}
where $\cC$ is complex conjugation and $|\omega|$ is the sum of the coordinates.
The quantity in \eqref{gsr:fm:55:eq:cube} is real and nonnegative. For example, this
follows by induction from the multiplicative-difference recursion and
$\norm f_{U^1}^2=|\E f|^2$. If $|f|\le1$, then $0\le\Ufiftyfive(f)\le1$.

\begin{definition}\label{gsr:fm:55:def:phase}
The set $\cP_{d-1}(G)$ consists of the maps $P:G\to S^1$ for which
\[
 \prod_{\omega\in\{0,1\}^d}\cC^{|\omega|}P(x+\omega\cdot h)=1
 \quad\text{for every }x,h_1,\ldots,h_d\in G.
\]
Define
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:55:eq:distance}
 D_d(f)=\min_{P\in\cP_{d-1}(G)}\E|f-P|^2,
 \qquad \eps(f)=1-\Ufiftyfive(f).
\end{equation}
\end{definition}

Thus ``degree'' refers to multiplicative differences, not to a chosen
coordinate formula. In small characteristic the definition includes
nonclassical phases. Replacing this class by classical polynomials would
change the problem and would invalidate the general statement.
The minimum exists: $\cP_{d-1}(G)$ is a closed subset of the finite product
$(S^1)^G$, hence compact. Multiplication by any of its elements preserves
$\Ufiftyfive$.

Our principal question is the asymptotic behavior of
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:55:eq:modulus}
 \mathfrak S_{d,G}(e)=
 \sup\{D_d(f): |f|\le1,\ \eps(f)\le e\}.
\end{equation}
It will be determined through order $e^2$, with a uniform $O_d(e^3)$ error.

\subsection{Published input and the repository comparison}

Eisner and Tao's compact-group near-extremizer theorem states that
$\norm f_{U^d}\to1$, under $|f|\le1$, forces $L^1$ distance to a
polynomial phase to tend to zero, uniformly in the group
\cite[Theorem 1.1]{eisnertao}. Their Remark 1.6 notes effective polynomial
rates without optimizing or displaying them. We use only the qualitative
entry statement. Everything after entry into an explicitly specified
neighborhood is proved directly here.

The inspected ProveIt collection already contains several local cube
expansions, torsion-sensitive counting estimates, moment inequalities, and
rigidity statements for additive energy \cite{repo55}. In particular, the
fourth-order arithmetic of cube configurations is not presented as a wholly
new idea. The additions developed here are the uniform sharp distance
expansion, the bounded-complex fifth-order cancellation that makes its error
cubic, the order-two spectral profile, and the associated second-order
rigidity theorem. The contemporary work of Kova\v c and Rogers on $L^p$
variants and near-extremizers \cite{kovacrogers} was also consulted; this
manuscript addresses the specific normalized $L^\infty$ endpoint distance
problem \eqref{gsr:fm:55:eq:modulus}.

The comparison is with an inspected repository snapshot, not a claim to have
refereed every earlier manuscript. Searches and the primary sources consulted
are recorded in \texttt{SOURCE\_AUDIT.md}. No claim that the results are the
first published formulations of these constants is needed for their proofs.

\srcnote{56}{Section 1}
\partsource{\textbf{Added in the tenth write, 7~October 2026. Delivered title block.} ``Nearly Sharp Relative Affine Repair on Fourier-Uniform Domains / Weighted Freiman tests, error-independent uniformity, and explicit quadratic-level-set consequences / Research draft prepared for the ProveIt project / 6 October 2026''; \emph{the PDF author field reads ``Research draft for ProveIt''}. Archive \file{gowers\_relative\_affine\_repair.zip} (arrival \texttt{aa1d86f6f}), manuscript \file{article.tex} with thirteen section files under \file{sections/} (1,593 lines in all, 25 pages; the main file \texttt{\textbackslash input}s the sections, which are printed here in that order), pin \texttt{b6a8ee966} (itself the arrival commit of sources~47--50), with \texttt{128f514af} recorded as a later search head ``not used as pin'' (its \file{source\_manifest.json}, shipped as \file{data/56-relative-affine-repair-source\_manifest.json}). Printed below: the abstract, the status statement after it and Section~1; Sections~2--9 stand in the Part~II chapter on affine rigidity after source~59 (Section~\ref{gsr:en:sec:affinerepair}), Sections~10--12 and Appendix~A are in Part~V. Its macro \texttt{\textbackslash Q} (calligraphic $\mathcal Q$, not this report's $\mathbb Q$) is set as source~49's \texttt{\textbackslash Qcal}, the same definition; its `question' environment (``Question'', on the shared counter) is set in this report's `Question' style.}
\begin{partabstract}{56}
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, let $H$ be an arbitrary abelian group,
and let $w:G\to[0,1]$ have mean $\alpha>0$. We prove an explicit relative
stability theorem for the additive-quadruple test. If
$\norm{w-\alpha}_{U^2(G)}^4\le\alpha^5/1024$ and a map on the support of $w$
violates an $\eps\le1/1024$ fraction of the weighted additive quadruples,
then it agrees with a unique affine map except on weighted relative mass
at most $13\eps/50$. The uniformity requirement is independent of $\eps$.
A two-sided error profile improves the coefficient to $1/4+o(1)$ as
both the normalized uniformity parameter and $\eps$ tend to zero;
$1/4$ is optimal. The proof retains autocorrelation weights through
modal difference selection, uses an exact triangle second-moment identity,
applies classical homomorphism self-correction, and then counts quadruples
with exactly one error. For a quadratic level set cut out by $r$ equations
over $\F_p$, $p$ odd, the same conclusion follows when every nonzero
quadratic combination has matrix rank $R$ with $p^{R-4r}\ge2^{14}$.
This is an affine-repair conclusion on a quadratic domain, not a
quadratic-repair theorem. Exact rational verification code, finite tests,
a source comparison, and a formalization plan accompany the proofs.
Linear repair itself is classical; the contribution proposed here is the
explicit weighted relative theorem and its quantitative refinements.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small
\noindent\textbf{Status.} Complete mathematical proofs are given below. This is an
AI-generated research manuscript, not externally refereed or proof-assistant
verified. Computational tests are diagnostics, not proofs of the universal
statements. Publication priority beyond the sources inspected is not asserted.
\end{quote}

The approximate-homomorphism stages of Gowers's proof convert information
about many respected additive configurations into genuine algebraic structure
\cite{gowers}. A useful strengthening in the high-agreement regime should
not merely find a small structured restriction. It should repair almost the
whole original domain. On an arbitrary sparse domain this is false: the
additive relations may fail to determine any global affine extension.
The question studied here is whether a quantitatively uniform domain makes
that repair possible with an error proportional to the observed violation
rate, without tightening the uniformity assumption every time the violation
rate decreases.

Our answer is affirmative under an explicit $U^2$ condition. All averages in
this article are probability averages. In particular, the fourth power of a
$U^2$ norm contains no hidden factor of $|G|$.

\subsection{Weighted tests and distance}
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of order $N$, and let $H$ be an abelian group,
written additively. No finiteness assumption on $H$ is needed. Fix
$w:G\to[0,1]$ with
\[
\alpha=\E_xw(x)>0,
\qquad u=\norm{w-\alpha}_{U^2(G)}.
\]
A map $\phi$ need only be specified on $\supp w$; elsewhere it can be extended
arbitrarily. Define the weighted configuration mass and defect by
\begin{align}
\Qcal(w)&=\E_{a,b,c\in G}w(a)w(b)w(c)w(a+b-c),\label{gsr:fm:56:eq:Q-def}\\
\Def_w(\phi)&=\E_{a,b,c\in G}w(a)w(b)w(c)w(a+b-c)
\ind_{\phi(a)+\phi(b)\ne\phi(c)+\phi(a+b-c)}.\label{gsr:fm:56:eq:D-def}
\end{align}
Thus the actual test error is
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:56:eq:epsilon-def}
\eps=\frac{\Def_w(\phi)}{\Qcal(w)}.
\end{equation}
The denominator is positive because $\Qcal(w)\ge\alpha^4$.
Every tuple is ordered, and repeated vertices are included. An affine map
$\Phi:G\to H$ means $\Phi(x)=L(x)+c$, with $L\in\Hom(G,H)$ and $c\in H$.
Its relative error on the weighted domain is
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:56:eq:distance-def}
t_w(\phi,\Phi)=\frac{\E_x w(x)\ind_{\phi(x)\ne\Phi(x)}}{\alpha}.
\end{equation}
For $w=\ind_A$, these definitions are exactly the fraction of additive
quadruples in $A$ that are violated and the fraction of points of $A$ that
must be changed.

\begin{theorem}[Explicit weighted relative affine repair]\label{gsr:fm:56:thm:main}
Suppose that
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:56:eq:main-hyp}
u^4\le\frac{\alpha^5}{1024},
\qquad 0\le\eps\le\frac1{1024}.
\end{equation}
There is a unique affine map $\Phi:G\to H$ satisfying
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:56:eq:main-bound}
t_w(\phi,\Phi)\le\frac{13}{50}\eps.
\end{equation}
It is obtained by three finite modal selections: first of differences on
weighted pairs, then of differences of the selected map on $G$, and finally
of the constant residual on the original domain.
\end{theorem}

\begin{writenote}[7 October 2026; sources 70--81]
\emph{The infimum over all weights} (sources~75--81, Section~\ref{gsr:en:sec:hereditary}): for maps defined on all of an abelian group, without a uniformity hypothesis, the infimum $r(a)$ of this theorem's fixed-weight relative statistic over all finite weights exceeds $3/4$ exactly for affine maps (source~76), and outside the affine maps and one index-two family it is at most $\rho=0.6837\ldots$, optimal (sources~78 and~79). Those results are exact and global; this theorem's is approximate repair for one weight.
\end{writenote}

Uniqueness in this statement means uniqueness \emph{within the displayed
error radius}. It does not assert that $G$ admits only one affine map.
An externally supplied upper bound for the test error can replace the actual
$\eps$ in the theorem. The proof first obtains the weaker but simple estimate
$t\le\eps/3$, and then improves it to \eqref{gsr:fm:56:eq:main-bound}.

\begin{corollary}[Subset formulation]\label{gsr:fm:56:cor:subset-main}
Let $\varnothing\ne A\subseteq G$ have density $\alpha$. If
\[
\norm{\ind_A-\alpha}_{U^2(G)}\le 2^{-5/2}\alpha^{5/4}
\]
and $\phi:A\to H$ respects at least a $1-\eps$ fraction of the additive
quadruples in $A$, where $0\le\eps\le2^{-10}$, then $\phi$ agrees with a
unique affine map on at least $(1-13\eps/50)|A|$ points of $A$.
\end{corollary}

The condition is a hypothesis on the domain, not on the labels. In particular,
it does not involve $\eps$. It applies in every characteristic, on cyclic
groups of composite order, and on products of finite abelian groups.

\subsection{The nearly sharp profile}
The useful scale-free quantities are
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:56:eq:parameters}
\lambda=\frac{u^2}{\alpha^{5/2}},\qquad
\kappa=\frac{u^4}{\alpha^4}=\lambda^2\alpha,\qquad
s=\frac{u^2}{\alpha^2}=\lambda\sqrt\alpha.
\end{equation}
The main hypothesis is $\lambda\le1/32$. The following statement holds
without that hypothesis and without an upper bound on $\eps$.

\begin{theorem}[Two-sided local error profile]\label{gsr:fm:56:thm:profile-intro}
For every affine map $\Phi$, put $t=t_w(\phi,\Phi)$. Then
\begin{align}
\eps(1+\lambda^2\alpha)
&\ge 4\bigl(1-\lambda\sqrt{1-\alpha}\bigr)t
       -12t^2-12\lambda t^{3/2},\label{gsr:fm:56:eq:profile-lower}\\
\eps(1+\lambda^2\alpha)
&\le 4\bigl(1+\lambda\sqrt{1-\alpha}\bigr)t.
\label{gsr:fm:56:eq:profile-upper}
\end{align}
For the repaired map in Theorem~\ref{gsr:fm:56:thm:main}, one has in addition
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:56:eq:refined-intro}
t\le
\frac{(1+\lambda^2\alpha)\eps}
 {4(1-\lambda\sqrt{1-\alpha})-4\eps-4\sqrt3\lambda\sqrt\eps}.
\end{equation}
The denominator in \eqref{gsr:fm:56:eq:refined-intro} is positive under
\eqref{gsr:fm:56:eq:main-hyp}.
\end{theorem}

Consequently, along any family with $\eps>0$, $\eps\to0$, and $\lambda\to0$,
the repaired distance satisfies $t/\eps\to1/4$. A single changed label on a
large group proves that $1/4$ cannot be replaced by a smaller limiting
coefficient. The density exponent $5/4$, the threshold $1/1024$, and the
finite-error coefficient $13/50$ are \emph{not} asserted to be optimal.

\subsection{Relation to existing results and limits of the claim}
Linear repair is not new. Kazhdan--Ziegler's polynomial splining theorem
already gives $C\eps$ repair on sufficiently uniform subsets of finite-field
vector spaces, with a condition of the form $u<(\alpha\eps)^B$
\cite[Theorem 1.7]{kazhdanziegler}. Their exact extension theorem is also relevant.
Peluse's recent elementary relative affine lemma gives error
$16\eps^{1/4}$ under $u<(\alpha\eps)^{32}$ and $0<\eps<2^{-15}$
\cite[Lemma 7.4]{peluserelative}. In that overlapping regime,
Corollary~\ref{gsr:fm:56:cor:subset-main} has both weaker uniformity requirements and
a smaller error bound. This comparison is with that local lemma, not with
Peluse's global inverse theorem.

The proposed contribution is the explicit error-independent condition
$u^4\le\alpha^5/1024$, the weighted formulation on arbitrary finite abelian
domains, the quantitative profile, and the consequences proved here.
The classical self-correction step is attributed to the
Blum--Luby--Rubinfeld method \cite{blr}. Earlier qualitative repair results
can sometimes be bootstrapped to an error-independent hypothesis; we do not
claim that this phenomenon itself has no precedent.

Within the inspected ProveIt material, the existing full-domain affine energy
profiles and local Bohr/Freiman extension results address different
hypotheses \cite{repo56}. The present theorem is not a replacement for those
statements on all their inputs. It supplies a new high-agreement branch when
the domain has the required Fourier uniformity. No improved global bound
for Szemer\'edi's theorem, no improved general Balog--Szemer\'edi exponent,
and no new global $U^4$ inverse bound is deduced in this article.

\begin{partabstract}{57}
We develop quantitative and structural refinements of the framework in
Gowers's 2001 proof of Szemer\'edi's theorem, using a pinned snapshot of
the ProveIt Ramsey development as the starting point. First, we combine
an earlier Fej\'er arrangement-selection theorem with the repository's
uniform common-square extraction. Keeping exact intermediate exponents
reduces the prepared density loss to
$(\alpha/2)^{2\,996\,201\,429}$. An elementary near-maximal $U^4$
argument completes the range near $\alpha=1$. Together these give a
written proof of the printed Theorem~13.12 length bound
$p^{2^{-\alpha^{-2^{70}}}}$, with the retained-density exponent improved
from $2^{76}$ to $2^{41}$. We also prove explicit near-maximal
frequency-extraction estimates at every uniformity order, a finite
abelian group extension, and an explicit cubic-phase approximation
bound in characteristic at least five.

Second, if a positive real $n$-set has Schur-triple deficit $s$ and
$n\ge5s-1$, we prove that it is a positive dilation of
$\{j+\lambda_j:1\le j\le n\}$, where the nonnegative nondecreasing
integers $\lambda_j$ sum to $s$. Thus there are exactly $p(s)$ eventual
dilation classes. A sharper treatment of deficit two classifies all
third-level additive-energy extremizers for $m\ge7$, with the optimal
threshold and its six-point exception. These answer two explicit
questions in the preceding repository research.

All added results have written proofs. We identify the inherited
inputs precisely, supply exact-arithmetic checks, and propose a
research programme. The manuscript does not claim a new final
Szemer\'edi bound, a new Lean proof, or established publication priority.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small
\noindent\textbf{Repository baseline.}
\path{128f514afce0bf7eb48133fb30dd3f8e034ea3a2}
(7 October 2026 UTC). This is an AI-assisted research manuscript
prepared for mathematical review and repository integration.
\end{quote}

Gowers's argument \cite{gowers} converts a large uniformity norm into
structured Fourier information, then uses that structure in a density
increment. Two places in this framework invite a precise improvement.
The first is quantitative: a loss in the density of an intermediate
frequency graph appears later inside a very large exponent. The
second is structural: extremal additive energy records how an ordered
set can fail to complete additive configurations. We treat both
questions, with the proof dependencies kept separate.

\subsection{A strengthened Section 13 extraction theorem}

For the statement below,
$\widehat f(r)=p^{-1}\sum_xf(x)\exp(-2\pi i rx/p)$ and
$\D_hf(x)=f(x+h)\overline{f(x)}$.

\begin{theorem}[Printed length, stronger retained density]\label{gsr:fm:57:main:extraction}
For every $0<\alpha<1$ there is an integer $N_0(\alpha)$ such that,
for every prime $p\ge N_0(\alpha)$ and every $f:\Fp\to\C$ with
$|f|\le1$ and $\|f\|_{U^4}^{16}>\alpha$, the following objects exist:
proper arithmetic progressions $P,Q\subseteq\Fp$, with the same
nonzero common difference and the same integer length $m$; a set
$B\subseteq P\times Q$; and coefficients
$c_{00},c_{10},c_{01},c_{11}\in\Fp$. They satisfy
\begin{align}
 m&\ge p^{\,2^{-\alpha^{-2^{70}}}},\label{gsr:fm:57:main:length}\\
 |B|&\ge(\alpha/2)^{2^{41}}m^2,\label{gsr:fm:57:main:mass}\\
 \left|\widehat{\D_h\D_kf}
 (c_{00}+c_{10}h+c_{01}k+c_{11}hk)\right|
 &\ge\alpha/2\qquad((h,k)\in B).\label{gsr:fm:57:main:coefficient}
\end{align}
\end{theorem}

\begin{writenote}[7 October 2026; sources 70--81]
\emph{Proved independently by source~70} (Section~\ref{gsr:en:sec:sectionthirteenagain}), whose pin precedes this source's arrival, as an asymptotic statement with the printed constants (its Theorem~\ref{gsr:fm:70:thm:printed}); that headline is superseded by this theorem and by the formal \file{theorem_13_12_holds} (\texttt{d48e8af00}), which both precede source~70's arrival. What source~70 adds is a lower-range side exponent linear in $\log(1/\alpha)$, conditional on Lau's recurrence theorem, and the near-maximal branch on every cyclic modulus.
\end{writenote}

In Gowers's unnormalized convention, the last bound is $\alpha p/2$.
The length in \eqref{gsr:fm:57:main:length} is the printed Theorem~13.12 target.
The stronger mass in \eqref{gsr:fm:57:main:mass} replaces its exponent $2^{76}$
by $2^{41}$. The statement uses the sufficiently-large-prime
quantifier order already present in the pinned Lean catalogue.
The case $\alpha=1$ in that catalogue is vacuous because its
nonuniformity hypothesis is strict.

The inspected development already proves a complete geometric square
extraction, but its older input density led to an exponent explicitly
proved smaller than the printed target \cite{repo57}. We resolve
that \emph{written-proof gap relative to the pinned snapshot}. The
classical theorem itself is Gowers's; our quantitative improvement
and proof route are the additions.

Put $a=\alpha/2$ and $d=2\,996\,201\,429$. The comparison is:
\begin{center}
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}L{0.24\textwidth}L{0.31\textwidth}L{0.34\textwidth}@{}}
\toprule
Quantity & Previous inspected route & This article\\
\midrule
Density supplied to the square extraction
& $a^{2^{66}}$ & $a^d$, and hence at least $a^{2^{32}}$\\[3pt]
An explicit length valid for every $0<\alpha<1$
& $p^{2^{-(2/\alpha)^{2^{88}}}}$
& $p^{2^{-(2/\alpha)^{2^{53}}}}$\\[3pt]
Retained density on the square
& $a^{2^{76}}$ & $a^{2^{41}}$\\[3pt]
Near-maximal range
& Not supplied by that propagation
& Whole ambient square; good-pair density at least $1-332(1-\alpha)$
when $1-\alpha\le2^{-10}$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

The proof is modular. Gowers's original Fourier and Freiman inputs
produce a separately Freiman frequency graph. The earlier
Fej\'er selection theorem in repository source~40 \cite{repo57fejer},
reproved in the required specialization below, improves its
purification loss. The existing density-uniform geometric theorem
then supplies actual proper progressions. A separate elementary
near-maximal argument covers the interval near one where the factors
$\alpha$ and $\alpha/2$ cannot be interchanged inside exponentials.
The detailed size threshold is recorded in
Remark~\ref{gsr:en:57:qt:threshold-remark}.

\subsection{Explicit rigidity near maximal uniformity}

The endpoint argument yields more than the preceding application
requires. If $Q_4(f):=\|f\|_{U^4}^{16}\ge1-\varepsilon$ and
$\varepsilon\le2^{-10}$, Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:57:ep:near-u4} supplies a scalar
$c\in\Fp$ and a set of at least $(1-332\varepsilon)p^2$ pairs with
\[
 |\widehat{\D_h\D_kf}(chk)|\ge\tfrac34-4\varepsilon.
\]
The argument combines a dimension-independent phase-normalization
estimate, elementary additive correction, and the exact symmetry of
mixed derivatives. It requires no inverse theorem as an input.

For $s$ derivative parameters, Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:57:ep:prime-all-orders} replaces
$332$ by $216s+8$ and the frequency $chk$ by $ch_1\cdots h_s$.
The finite abelian group version Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:57:ep:group-all-orders} supplies
an $s$-additive frequency map, with an explicit recurrence for its
error constant. In characteristic at least five the cubic frequency
can be integrated: Corollary~\ref{gsr:en:57:ep:cubic-inverse} gives, for
$0\le\varepsilon<1/17604$, a polynomial $P$ of degree at most three
with
\[
 |\E_x f(x)\ep(-P(x))|
 \ge\sqrt{1-6194\varepsilon}-\varepsilon.
\]
The corresponding squared $L^2$ error is at most $12390\varepsilon$.
More generally, Corollary~\ref{gsr:en:57:ep:all-degree-inverse} gives polynomial-phase
approximation of degree at most $k-1$ when $p\ge k$, with explicit
constant
$K_k=2\prod_{r=1}^{k-2}(108r+1)$ multiplying the uniformity deficit.
The numerical constants are not asserted to be optimal, but the
linear order of the squared error cannot be improved uniformly.
Eisner--Tao's general near-extremizer theorem \cite{eisnertao} is the
appropriate earlier context; the present results make a particular
elementary route and its constants explicit.

\subsection{A partition theorem and a complete energy equality case}

For a positive real set $C=\{c_1<\cdots<c_n\}$, define
\[
 h(C)=\binom n2-\#\{(x,y,z)\in C^3:x+y=z\}.
\]
Both orders of a pair of distinct summands are counted, and equal
summands are permitted. The maximum Schur count and its equality
case are classical \cite{huczynska}. We prove the following exact
classification beyond a linear threshold:
\[
 h(C)=s,\quad n\ge5s-1
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 C=u\{j+\lambda_j:1\le j\le n\},
\]
where $u>0$, the integers $\lambda_j$ are nonnegative and
nondecreasing, and $\sum_j\lambda_j=s$.
There are therefore exactly $p(s)$ positive dilation classes.
The perturbed positions lie among the last $s$ entries. This is
Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:57:st:partitions}; the threshold is sufficient, with its optimal
value left open for general $s$.

For $s=2$, Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:57:st:schur-two} improves the threshold to the optimal
$n=6$. This sharpened endpoint classification identifies every
equality case at the third energy level. Let
\[
 E(A)=\#\{(a,b,c,d)\in A^4:a+b=c+d\},\qquad
 M_m=(2m^3+m)/3.
\]
For $m\ge7$, the $m$-element real or torsion-free sets satisfying
$E(A)=M_m-8(m-3)$ are exactly the affine images of
\[
 J_m=\{0,1,\ldots,m\}\setminus\{2\},
 \qquad K_m=\{0,2,3,\ldots,m-1,m+1\}.
\]
At $m=6$ there is precisely one further affine class,
$\{0,1,2,4,5,6\}$. Thus seven is the optimal threshold for the
two-class statement. The earlier numerical energy levels and the
second-level classification are credited to repository source~45
\cite{repo57levels}; the endpoint recurrence has earlier literature
precedents \cite{hegyvari}. The new classification answers the
first two research questions posed in that source.

\subsection{What the results establish}

The Fourier statements concern prime cyclic groups, with a separate
finite abelian group near-maximal extension. The energy statements
concern ordered real sets and their torsion-free transfers.
Moving the latter to finite cyclic groups requires a suitable
Freiman isomorphism or rectification theorem; arbitrary integer
representatives do not suffice.

The final density-increment iteration is not carried out here.
Consequently these local refinements establish no new upper bound
for $r_k(N)$, the largest size of a subset of $[N]$ with no $k$-term
progression. For perspective, Leng, Sah, and Sawhney
\cite{lssbounds} prove
$r_k(N)\ll N\exp(-(\log\log N)^{c_k})$ for $k\ge5$ by a different
modern inverse-theorem route. This article makes no comparison
claim against that global bound.

Every added theorem below has a written proof. The exact finite
computations are supplementary checks, not proofs of unbounded
families. The substantial imported geometric theorem is identified
by its declaration and commit. No new Lean module, repository
status change, or fresh compilation of the full formal development
is claimed. The literature check establishes relevant precedents
and repository-relative additions; publication priority remains
unestablished.

\begin{partabstract}{58}
Gowers's restriction lemma extracts a set on which almost all additive
sixteen-tuples are respected by a given map, while retaining a controlled
number of configurations. We prove a version for every cyclic modulus and
arbitrary finite abelian target in which the retention exponent is $54$,
in place of $2^{19}$, with the explicit sufficient hypothesis
$|B|\ge (4/(\alpha\eta))^{54}$. The proof amplifies a fixed positive Fourier
filter and accounts explicitly for both small torsion and repeated entries.
For a general balanced relation of length $m$, the central estimate has
nonprincipal error
$\tau_G(2D)(R_m^k-P^k)|B|^{m-2}$ and collision error
$\binom m2 R_2^k|B|^{m-2}$. It yields polynomial restriction with exponent
$O(m\log m)$ on every cyclic group.

We also determine the optimal leading exponent within the normalized
nonnegative Fourier-filter class. If a nonzero target discrepancy may have
fixed order $a\ge2$, then
$\inf_K[-\log P_m(K)/\log(P_m(K)/Q_{m,a}(K))]
=m\log m/(2\log a)+O_a(m\log\log m)$.
The lower bound uses an elementary coefficient rearrangement inequality;
powered cosine filters attain the leading term. All statements count ordered
tuples with repetitions. The article includes full proofs, exact integer
certificates, a source comparison, integration interfaces, and a research
programme. These are local restriction results; no stronger global
Szemer\'edi bound or completed Lean formalization is asserted.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small
\noindent\textbf{Keywords.} Quantitative additive combinatorics; approximate
homomorphisms; Fourier restriction; finite abelian groups; small torsion;
Szemer\'edi's theorem.
\end{quote}
\label{gsr:fm:58:sec:introduction}

The quantitative inverse step in Gowers's proof of Szemer\'edi's theorem
requires more than a large subset of a graph. It requires a subset on which
almost every additive configuration has an additive image, while enough
configurations survive to feed the subsequent argument. Lemma~9.3 of
\cite{gowers} supplies such a restriction for sixteen entries. Its
retained configuration proportion is
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:58:eq:old-retention}
 \left(\frac{\alpha\eta}{4}\right)^{2^{19}}.
\end{equation}
The exponent is a local cost in a much longer proof. Reducing it does not,
on its own, determine the final density-increment bound.

We use the following notation throughout. For $m=2r\ge4$, a subset $B$ of
a finite abelian group $G$, and a map $\phi:B\to H$ to another finite
abelian group, let $\TT_m(B)$ be the number of ordered tuples in $B^m$
with equal sums of the first and last $r$ entries. Let $\GGfiftyeight_m(B,\phi)$
count those tuples for which the corresponding sums of the images are
also equal. Every count includes repeated entries. Write $b=|B|$.

\begin{theoremA}[Sixteen-variable restriction on every cyclic group]
\label{gsr:fm:58:thm:A}
Let $N\ge1$, let $B\subseteq\Z/N\Z$, and let $\phi:B\to H$, where $H$
is any finite abelian group. Suppose $0<\alpha,\eta\le1$ and
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:58:eq:A-hyp}
 b\ge\left(\frac4{\alpha\eta}\right)^{54},
 \qquad \GGfiftyeight_{16}(B,\phi)\ge\alpha b^{15}.
\end{equation}
Then there is $B'\subseteq B$ such that
\begin{align}
 \GGfiftyeight_{16}(B',\phi)&\ge(1-\eta)\TT_{16}(B'),\label{gsr:fm:58:eq:A-quality}\\
 \TT_{16}(B')&\ge
 \left(\frac{\alpha\eta}{4}\right)^{54}b^{15}.\label{gsr:fm:58:eq:A-mass}
\end{align}
Consequently $|B'|\ge(\alpha\eta/4)^{54/15}|B|$.
\end{theoremA}

\begin{writenote}[7 October 2026; sources 54--59]
\emph{Checked at the write} (exact integers). With $A=\sum_{|n|\le25}\binom{50}{25+n}^{16}$ and $B$ its even-$n$ part: $A\ge2^{750}$, $250A\ge481B$, $481^{53}\ge2^{50}250^{53}$, $481^{50}\ge2^{47}250^{50}$, $\binom{100}{50}\le2^{97}$, $4(50+\binom{16}2)=680$, $680\cdot2^{97}/2^{108}=85/256<1$ and $2^{108}/2^{105}=8$ (Appendix~\ref{gsr:fz:58:sec:dA}). \emph{Against the formal statement.} \file{lemma_9_3} (\file{Sections08\_09.lean}, line~77) quantifies over all $N\ge N_0$, $|B|=\beta N$ and maps $\Z/N\Z\to\Z/N\Z$, with input $\alpha\beta^{15}N^{15}\le$\,\file{phiAdditiveTupleCount}~$8$ (that is, $\GGfiftyeight_{16}(B,\phi)\ge\alpha b^{15}$; for nonempty $B$ it forces $\alpha\le1$) and asks for $(\alpha\eta/4)^{2^{19}}\beta^{15}N^{15}\le$\,\file{additiveTupleCount}~$8$ and \file{GammaHomOfOrder}~$8$~$B'$~$\phi$~$(1-\eta)$; with $N_0=\lceil\beta^{-1}(4/(\alpha\eta))^{54}\rceil$ this theorem gives both, since $0<\alpha\eta/4<1$ and $54<2^{19}$. So it implies \file{lemma_9_3} on paper with an explicit threshold; the catalogue statement is already exact (\file{lemma_9_3_holds}, \file{Proofs09Restriction.lean}, line~376), and this theorem is not formalized.
\end{writenote}

\begin{writenote}[7 October 2026; sources 60--69]
\emph{Exponent $53$ by source~68} (Section~\ref{gsr:en:sec:allmoduli}): the same statement with $53$ in place of $54$, through a degree-twelve rational filter (its Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:68:ff:thm:53}); for cyclic targets source~62's powers $\alpha^{31}\eta^{30}$ are better when $\alpha^{22}\eta^{23}(1-\eta)<2^{-139}$ (note in that chapter).
\end{writenote}

The map in this statement need not be a homomorphism on $B$, and $N$ may
have any small prime factors. The sufficient threshold is explicit but
large. The integer $54$ is a convenient certified exponent, not a claimed
best constant. Section~\ref{gsr:en:58:sec:explicit} gives a more precise version
whose retained powers are approximately
$\alpha^{53.2064}\eta^{52.2064}$, at a threshold with power approximately
$49.3412$ in $(\alpha\eta)^{-1}$.

The proof separates two phenomena. Small torsion in the \emph{target}
controls how many principal Fourier frequencies an incorrect relation
can pass. Small torsion in the \emph{domain} controls how many solutions
an additional, nonprincipal integer relation can have. The former is
handled by a spectral gap; the latter by the kernel sizes of multiplication
maps. Repeated tuples require a third estimate, because selecting a point
once is different from selecting each of its occurrences independently.

The general expectation estimate, proved in
Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:58:thm:expectation}, keeps all three costs explicit. A filter
of degree $D$ has nonnegative symmetric decreasing coefficients $c_n$;
we set
\[
 P=\sum_n c_n^m,\qquad Q=\sum_{2\mid n}c_n^m,
 \qquad R_s=\int_{\T}K(t)^s\,dt.
\]
After $k$ independent layers, good tuples have expected survival at least
$P^k$. The bad-tuple expectation is at most
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:58:eq:intro-error}
 Q^k\UU_m(B,\phi)+
 \left\{\tau_G(2D)(R_m^k-P^k)
       +\binom m2R_2^k\right\}b^{m-2},
\end{equation}
where $\UU_m=\TT_m-\GGfiftyeight_m$ and
$\tau_G(L)=\max_{1\le d\le L}|\ker(d:G\to G)|$.
For a cyclic group, $\tau_G(2D)\le2D$, independently of its modulus.

There is also a sharp asymptotic result about the method itself. For a
normalized nonnegative trigonometric polynomial with nonnegative Fourier
coefficients, define
\[
 P_m(K)=\sum_n c_n^m,\qquad
 Q_{m,a}(K)=\sum_{a\mid n}c_n^m,
 \qquad
 \mathcal A_{m,a}(K)=
 \frac{-\log P_m(K)}{\log(P_m(K)/Q_{m,a}(K))}.
\]
The ratio is assigned $+\infty$ if $P_m=Q_{m,a}$.

\begin{theoremB}[Optimal leading exponent in the positive-filter class]
\label{gsr:fm:58:thm:B}
For each fixed integer $a\ge2$, as the integer $m$ tends to infinity,
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:58:eq:optimal-intro}
 \inf_K\mathcal A_{m,a}(K)
 =\frac{m\log m}{2\log a}+O_a(m\log\log m).
\end{equation}
The infimum is over finite real even trigonometric polynomials satisfying
$0\le K\le1$, $K(0)=1$, and $c_n\ge0$; monotonicity of the coefficients
is not required for the lower bound. Powered cosine filters attain the
displayed leading term.
\end{theoremB}

\begin{writenote}[7 October 2026; sources 60--69]
Source~68 bounds the principal cost uniformly in the arity $m$ and the order $a$, with $\cI_{m,a}/m\to1+1/(2c)$ when $a=m^{c+o(1)}$ (its Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:68:uf:thm:uniform} and Corollary~\ref{gsr:en:68:uf:cor:regimes}), the growing-order regime this theorem leaves open.
\end{writenote}

For arbitrary targets the relevant worst possible discrepancy has order
two. Thus the leading constant is $1/(2\log2)$ in the exponent cost of
this filtering scheme. Theorem~B is a limitation of a specified method,
not a lower bound on every possible combinatorial restriction theorem.

\subsection{Source comparison and contribution boundary}

The point of departure is the original paper and the research materials
already present in the requested repository. The repository was inspected
at commit \commitfiftyeight, dated 7 October 2026. Its combined report contains
sources 01--27; later source packages and their audits were also consulted
where directly relevant. The principal comparisons are as follows.

\begin{center}
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}L{0.20\linewidth}L{0.33\linewidth}L{0.39\linewidth}@{}}
\toprule
Source & Existing contribution & Relation to this article\\
\midrule
Gowers \cite{gowers}, Lemma 9.3
 & All-modulus restriction with sixteen-variable exponent $2^{19}$.
 & Theorem A retains the all-modulus scope and gives exponent $54$ with a numerical size hypothesis.\\[5pt]
Shkredov \cite{shkredovsystems}, Lemma 2.1
 & A broader restriction construction for systems of equations, with large explicit parameter losses.
 & A relevant predecessor for the selection architecture; our quantitative claims concern one balanced relation.\\[5pt]
\reposc\ source 04 \cite{repo58}
 & Powered cosine filters, weighted exceptional-relation control, and polynomial restriction over prime fields.
 & These ingredients are credited as prior work; we amplify a fixed filter and account for small torsion.\\[5pt]
\reposc\ source 17 \cite{repo58}
 & A single Fej\'er filter, a signed selection objective, and prime-field retention with powers $\alpha^m\eta^{m-1}$.
 & Those powers are better in that restricted setting. The present result treats every cyclic modulus.\\[5pt]
\reposc\ sources 29 and 40 \cite{repo58}
 & Finite-field rank refinements; an exact small-torsion principal spectrum in a one-filter arrangement argument.
 & The spectrum itself is not claimed as new. The decaying multi-layer error and uniform all-modulus theorem are the contributions here.\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

In particular, source~04 already proves, for $m=2r$, a prime-field
restriction with retained coefficient
\[
 \frac{\alpha^{2r}\eta^{2r-1}}{2(400r)^r}
\]
under an explicit threshold of power $2r$ in $(\alpha\eta)^{-1}$.
Source~17 gives the coefficient
$\alpha^m\eta^{m-1}/(2(m+2)^m)$ with a different threshold.
Neither should be replaced by a claim that exponent $54$ improves all
known prime-field estimates. The new statement instead answers the
small-prime composite-modulus extension problem recorded in the
repository's research questions, in the form of a uniform cyclic-group
theorem and a torsion-sensitive finite-group theorem.

The literature comparison is targeted, rather than a claim of exhaustive
priority verification. We have not found the present expectation estimate,
the numerical all-modulus corollary, or Theorem~B in the inspected sources.
The proofs below are self-contained. Modern improvements to the global
Szemer\'edi bound, such as \cite{lssbounds}, use substantially
more of the inverse-theorem machinery; this article makes no claim to
improve those global results.

\srcnote{59}{Section 1}
\partsource{\textbf{Added in the tenth write, 7~October 2026. Delivered title block.} ``Sharp Character Separation and Affine Rigidity in Gowers' Inverse Steps / Torsion-sensitive Freiman restrictions, signed energy inequalities, and a research programme for the ProveIt Ramsey project / Research manuscript prepared with ChatGPT for Vladimir Reshetnikov / 7 October 2026''; \emph{the PDF author field reads ``Research manuscript prepared with ChatGPT for Vladimir Reshetnikov''}. The title page is dated 7~October 2026; the archive arrived at 21:44 on 6~October 2026 (Pacific time). Archive \file{gowers-character-affine-refinements.zip} (arrival \texttt{9458a55a9}), manuscript \file{gowers-character-affine-refinements.tex} (1,878 lines, 32 pages), pin \texttt{bec460a33} (the sixth write of this report; its \file{source\_manifest.json}, shipped as \file{data/59-character-affine-source\_manifest.json}, records the article, the README and the transcription by blob and SHA-256). \begin{partabstract}{59}
We develop two local refinements of the additive-combinatorial inverse steps surrounding Sections 6 and 7 of Gowers's proof of Szemer\'edi's theorem. First, a strict averaging argument gives the exact worst-case number of characters needed to separate a finite symmetric forbidden set at explicit radii. If the set has $q$ sign orbits, the universal answer at radius $1/5$ is $\lfloor\log_2(q+1)\rfloor$; for odd-order defects at radius $1/7$ it is $\lfloor\log_3(2q+1)\rfloor$. Both ranks, and the corresponding rank--radius pairs, are sharp. A prime-primary variant, exact order profiles, finite-image rounding, and weighted localization yield Freiman restrictions over arbitrary abelian targets, independently of target size or rank. This refines a classical Green--Tao separation method; an order-five calculation also identifies a failure in a displayed probability estimate in its published proof.

Second, an exact signed graph expansion and a three-position kernel average strengthen the local cubic affine-rigidity profile. For targets without involutions, the sufficient error-support radius increases from the repository's $1/7$ to $4/9$; excluding order-three elements increases it to $1/2$. Equality requires a single nonzero error value on a subgroup coset; the first endpoint is strict, and the second has precisely the index-two coset extremizers. Quantitative support and color remainders are retained, with sharp support coefficients in the underlying kernel bounds. Classical homomorphism correction then gives sharp-profile recovery for graph defect below $2/9$ and the exact non-affine energy maximum for domains of size at least $16$; these global conclusions are credited as applications of prior correction theory. Full proofs, exact verification scripts, source comparisons, and concrete further questions are included. No improved global bound in Szemer\'edi's theorem or solution of the lonely runner conjecture is asserted.
\end{partabstract}
