Claims of refinement are relative to the cited statements and the pinned repository; mathematical priority remains subject to specialist review.
\end{quote}
\label{gsr:fm:59:sec:introduction}

Gowers's proof of Szemer\'edi's theorem passes from analytic non-uniformity to structured additive relations, and then from many respected relations to an exact local algebraic object. Two interfaces are especially suitable for a precise audit: the graph-energy conclusion of Proposition~6.1 and the extraction of a higher-order Freiman restriction in Lemma~7.5 \cite{gowers}. This article concentrates on these interfaces. It also develops the near-extremal affine problem that the \reposc\ project places next to Proposition~6.1.

The repository was inspected at commit
\begin{center}\small\texttt{bec460a3335f8da421459b4bf69d082e674560a6}.\end{center}
The comparison uses the combined article and research README in
\path{Combinatorics/Ramsey/Research/GowersSzemeredi/local-quantitative-refinements/}. In particular, ``source~11'', ``source~14'', and ``source~24'' below mean the internally numbered manuscripts in that pinned project, not separately refereed publications \cite{repo59}. The combined article contains sources~01--33; the inspected README also records later reports through source~46. This distinction matters when describing what has already been done.

\subsection{Exact separation of forbidden values}

Let $H$ be abelian and let $F\subset H\setminus\{0\}$ be finite and symmetric. Count one representative of each orbit under $f\mapsto-f$, including a singleton for an involution, and write $q=|F/\{\pm1\}|$. A family of characters $\chi_j:H\to\T$ separates $F$ at radius $\theta$ if every $f\in F$ satisfies $\distT{\chi_j(f)}\ge\theta$ for at least one $j$. Here $\T=\R/\Z$ and $\|\cdot\|_{\T}$ is distance from the nearest integer.

Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:59:thm:sharp-separation} proves the following exact worst-case bounds:
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}p{0.35\linewidth}cc@{}}
\toprule
Finite orders allowed among $F$ & Radius & Number of characters\\
\midrule
Arbitrary & $1/5$ & $\lfloor\log_2(q+1)\rfloor$\\
Odd & $1/7$ & $\lfloor\log_3(2q+1)\rfloor$\\
Powers of a fixed prime $p$ & $1/(2p)$ & $\lfloor\log_p((p-1)q+1)\rfloor$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
Infinite-order defects are allowed in every row. The conditions concern the defects, and need not hold for the whole target group. Each rank is sharp for every positive integer $q$. The radii $1/5$ and $1/7$ are sharp if their respective rank bounds are retained for every $q$. The prime-primary radius has a different, more limited optimality statement: it is best for its uniform probability contraction, while its optimal separation radius remains undetermined here.

The key gain is strict averaging. At a stage with $s$ forbidden sign orbits, the expected number surviving one character is at most $s/b$. A neighborhood of the zero character makes all $s$ survive. Thus some character leaves strictly fewer than $s/b$, so the surviving count is at most $\lfloor(s-1)/b\rfloor$. Iterating this integer recurrence gives the displayed ranks. Projective-line obstructions give matching lower bounds.

For the graph $\Gamma=\{(x,\phi(x)):x\in B\}$ of a map on a finite subset of an abelian group, let
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:59:eq:intro-defect}
 F_k^0=\{h\in H:(0,h)\in k\Gamma-k\Gamma\},\qquad
 F_k=F_k^0\setminus\{0\}.
\end{equation}
Localizing all character values to translated short arcs produces a subset on which $\phi$ is an exact Freiman homomorphism of order $k$. In the universal case its size is at least
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:59:eq:intro-extraction}
 \frac{|B|}{(5k)^{\lfloor\log_2(q+1)\rfloor}},
 \qquad q=|F_k/\{\pm1\}|.
\end{equation}
The same bound holds for any prescribed nonnegative weight in place of cardinality. Finite character images improve the loss by an exact rounding formula. For targets of exponent $p$, this recovers finite-field fibers with loss $p^{\lfloor\log_p((p-1)q+1)\rfloor}$, independently of $k$. For infinite-order defects, one character instead gives a linear loss $2kq$.

These are refinements of an established architecture. Green--Tao explicitly use character separation and Bohr localization in Lemmas~8.3 and~9.2 of their $U^3$ inverse theorem \cite{greentaoUthree}. Gowers--Mili\'cevi\'c use a random finite-field kernel to avoid vertical defects in Lemma~3.3 \cite{gowersmilicevicufour}. We do not claim the architecture or dimension-independent finite-field extraction as new. The exact ranks, order accounting, weighted formulation, and finite-image optimization are the refinements developed here.

\subsection{A stronger affine-rigidity inequality}

For $f:G\to W$, with $|G|=N$, let $\mathcal E(f)$ count ordered quadruples respecting addition both in the domain and in the target, and set $\varepsilon(f)=1-\mathcal E(f)/N^3$. Suppose $W[2]=\{0\}$, where $W[r]=\{w:rw=0\}$. Subtract an arbitrary affine reference map $\ell$ and let $S=\{x:f(x)\ne\ell(x)\}$, $t=|S|/N$. If $c_b$ counts the nonzero error value $b$, define
\[
a=\frac{|S|^2-\sum_{b\ne0}c_b^2}{N^2},\qquad
 \Psi(t)=4t-10t^2+6t^3.
\]
Write $d=t^3-E(S)/N^3$ for the normalized support-energy deficit.
Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:59:thm:affine-local-third} establishes the structural inequality
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:59:eq:intro-structural}
 \varepsilon(f)\ge\Psi(t)
 +6\left(t^3-\frac{E(S)}{N^3}\right)+2(1-3t)a,
 \qquad 0\le t\le\frac12.
\end{equation}
It improves the repository's color coefficient $2(1-7t)$ and, below $t=1/3$, separately controls failure of the support to be a coset and failure of the errors to have one value.

A second estimate averages the signed quartic kernel over the three ways to choose one negative position among three free positions. It gives the larger sufficient ranges in Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:59:thm:affine-four-ninths}:
\begin{align}
 \varepsilon(f)&\ge\Psi(t)+3d+\left(2-\frac92t\right)a,
 &&0<t<\frac49,\quad W[2]=\{0\};\label{gsr:fm:59:eq:intro-four-ninths}\\
 \varepsilon(f)&\ge\Psi(t)+4d+\min\{2-3t,4-8t\}\,a,
 &&0<t<\frac12,\quad W[2]=W[3]=\{0\}.\label{gsr:fm:59:eq:intro-one-half}
\end{align}
In either open range, equality with $\Psi(t)$ holds exactly when the error is one nonzero constant on a subgroup coset. These are statements relative to any affine reference; no nearest-map hypothesis is needed. The radii are sufficient, not asserted optimal.

Corollary~\ref{gsr:en:59:cor:affine-endpoints} also resolves both boundaries: at $t=4/9$ the first class has strict inequality, while at $t=1/2$ in the second class equality holds exactly for a single nonzero error value on an index-two coset. The coefficients $3$ and $4$ are sharp in the underlying signed-kernel bounds with their other terms fixed.

The cubic itself and its coset extremizers are already in source~11. Our contribution is a stronger support/color decomposition and an enlarged local range. In contrast, the global recovery range $\varepsilon<2/9$, the cutoff $N\ge16$ for the exact non-affine maximum, and the corresponding partial-graph application can already be obtained by combining that prior cubic with the published correction theorem of Ben-Or--Coppersmith--Luby--Rubinfeld \cite{bclr,dss}. We supply complete proofs and record the improved repository consequences, without presenting them as a new homomorphism-testing theorem.

\subsection{What the bounds do and do not improve}

The results are local improvements to the inverse step. If $|\Gamma-\Gamma|\le C|\Gamma|$, then $|F_k^0|\le C^{2k+1}$ by a classical sum-difference estimate and a vertical injection. Thus \eqref{gsr:fm:59:eq:intro-extraction} is polynomial in $C$, uniformly over arbitrary abelian targets. This answers the concrete request for an explicit mixed-torsion continuation of the repository's finite-field restriction, though it does not optimize its exponent and does not improve the best prime-cyclic bound already in source~10.

For comparison, Gowers's original Lemma~7.5 retains $|B|/(8kC^{4k})$ in its prime-cyclic setting. The present universal exponent $(2k+1)\log_2(5k)$ can be larger than $4k$. Its advantage is its unrestricted target, exact forbidden-set parameter, and torsion-sensitive alternatives. Any comparison should keep all those hypotheses visible.

An improvement to the final bound for progression-free sets would require compatible gains through the remaining inverse, phase-localization, and density-increment steps. We do not provide that chain. Modern global bounds, such as those of Leng--Sah--Sawhney \cite{lssbounds}, involve substantially more than the interfaces studied here. Similarly, the one-character problem contains the integer lonely runner conjecture exactly; we identify that connection and transfer known bounds, rather than claiming to solve it.

\subsection{Conventions}

All groups are written additively, and $C_n=\Z/n\Z$. A character means a homomorphism into $\T$, with the domain given the discrete topology. For finite sets $A$, the notation $rA-sA$ allows repetitions. Energies are unnormalized ordered counts. A Freiman homomorphism of order $k$ respects every equality of two $k$-term sums, including repeated summands. A finite nonempty set is a coset precisely when it is closed under $x-y+z$. We distinguish $q$, the number of sign orbits, from $|F|$: if $i(F)$ counts the nonzero involutions in $F$, then
\[
 q=\frac{|F|+i(F)}2.
\]
All probability arguments can be restricted to a finitely generated subgroup containing the finitely many values under discussion. This keeps infinite-target assertions separate from any finiteness assumption on the domain.

\section[{Source 60: Research context and principal conclusions}]{Source 60. Research context and principal conclusions}\label{gsr:fm:60:sec:d1}\label{gsr:fm:60:sec:introduction}
\srcnote{60}{Section 1}
\partsource{\textbf{Added in the eleventh write, 7~October 2026.} \textbf{Delivered title block.} ``Fourier limits, exact arrangement repair, and translated restriction in Gowers's quantitative framework / Research prepared with ChatGPT for Vladimir Reshetnikov / ProveIt research programme / 7 October 2026 \textbar\ Research manuscript, version 1.0''; \emph{the PDF author field reads ``Research prepared with ChatGPT for Vladimir Reshetnikov''}. The title page is dated 7~October 2026; the archive arrived at 22:07 on 6~October 2026 (Pacific time). Archive \file{Gowers\_Fourier\_Arrangement\_Refinements.zip} (arrival \texttt{0d93c1eac}), manuscript \file{gowers\_fourier\_arrangements.tex} (3,145 lines, 49 pages), pin \texttt{89c1cbc38} (``7 October 2026, 04:12:28 UTC''; its \file{audit/SOURCE\_AUDIT.json}, shipped as \file{data/60-fourier-limits-SOURCE\_AUDIT.json}, records the README, this article and the transcription by blob). Printed below: the abstract, its scope paragraph and Section~1; Section~2 (the norm limit) stands in Part~III after source~63 (Section~\ref{gsr:cc:sec:oddlimit}), Sections~3--8 form a chapter of Part~II on arrangement repair (Section~\ref{gsr:en:sec:arrangementpolynomial}), Section~9 (translated restriction) stands in the Part~II restriction chapter (Section~\ref{gsr:en:sec:allmoduli}), Sections~10--12 and Appendix~A are in Part~V. Its macros \texttt{\textbackslash V} (calligraphic $\mathcal V$, not this report's $V_d$) and \texttt{\textbackslash pin} (its own pin) are renamed \texttt{\textbackslash Vcal} and \texttt{\textbackslash pinsixty}; its `problem' environment (``Research question'', numbered 1--14 on its own counter) is set in this report's `Research question' style, numbered within its section, which keeps the indices; its figure is shipped as \file{figures/60-fourier-limits-arrangement\_profiles.pdf}. It loads \texttt{cleveref} and does not use it.}
\begin{partabstract}{60}
We develop four quantitative refinements around Gowers's proof of Szemer\'edi's theorem and the research already collected in the ProveIt repository. First, the limiting comparison constant between the fourth powers of the real, centered $U^2$ and $U^d$ norms on finite odd-order abelian groups is exactly a bounded Fourier extremum. A uniform Fourier-tail estimate justifies passage through varying groups and unbounded functions. It reduces the previous interval $[1/3,1/2]$ to
\[
 \frac13\le c_\infty^{\rm odd}
 \le\frac12-\frac8{\pi^2}+\frac{64}{\pi^4}
 =0.3464533951\ldots.
\]
When the degree and the least prime divisor of the group order both tend to infinity, the exact limiting constant is $1/3$, by combining the compactness theorem with a Riesz--Sobolev inequality of Christ and Iliopoulou.

Second, for every even number $s\ge4$ of vertical differences in a respected-arrangement test, we prove an explicit polynomial lower bound for its defect, classify every interior equality case, and determine every coefficient of the optimal small-error inverse expansion. This resolves the higher-order coefficient and exact-equality questions left by repository source~33. Third, we prove a sharp robust-intersection theorem for the two directional model classes, and obtain biaffine repair with optimal inverse coefficients through degree $s-2$. Finally, a translated Fej\'er selector retains the existing polynomial restriction count while reducing the prime-uniform size threshold from a proposed power $L^m$ to $L^{m-1}$; an exact certificate records small torsion and repeated tuples. All new assertions receive proofs. Exact finite diagnostics, source provenance, and a prioritized research programme accompany the article.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small
\noindent\textbf{Scope of the claims.}
The advances are local extremal and restriction theorems. They do not supply a new global bound for progression-free sets, close Gowers's entire quantitative induction, or constitute a Lean formalization. Claims of improvement are made against the inspected repository snapshot, with published inputs identified explicitly; no claim of publication priority is inferred from a literature search.
\end{quote}

Gowers's proof of Szemer\'edi's theorem links uniformity norms, additive relations on graphs, restriction to approximate homomorphisms, and structural repair \cite{gowers}. Several estimates in this chain have a meaningful extremal problem of their own. Improving such an estimate can clarify which configurations force a loss, even when a global density-increment iteration has additional bottlenecks.

The present article studies four such problems. They are connected by a common principle: retain the distribution or Fourier mass responsible for an error before replacing it by a worst-case bound. For high-order norm comparisons this means controlling the whole tail of the Fourier fourth powers. For arrangement repair it means coupling the constant Fourier coefficient with the remaining spectrum. For two-direction testing it means retaining both conditional variances. For restriction it means summing the actual nonprincipal Fourier weights after an additional translation average.

\subsection{The baseline and the research standard}

The repository was inspected at commit
\begin{center}
 \texttt{\pinsixty},
\end{center}
dated 7 October 2026, 04:12:28 UTC. At that snapshot the consolidated research article incorporates sources~01--33, while sources~34--46 are separately staged. We compared the main targets with the consolidated article, its source inventory and open questions, and the relevant later audits. The numbered ``repository sources'' below refer to this inventory, not to published papers \cite{repo60}.

The closest predecessors are source~29 for odd-order norm comparisons, source~33 for high-agreement arrangement repair, and sources~04 and~17 for polynomial restriction \cite{repo60twentynine,repo60thirtythree,repo60four,repo60seventeen}. Source~45 records a stronger finite-$U^4$ comparison than source~29; our asymptotic theorem does not replace that finite-degree estimate. A crosswalk and exact source identifiers are supplied in Section~\ref{gsr:fz:60:sec:integration} and in the archive.

Every theorem asserted here has a written proof, including its normalization, range of parameters, and use of earlier results. Separate derivations were compared during preparation, and bounded exact computations were used to test equality cases, small torsion, repeated coordinates, and algebraic constants. These checks are evidence against implementation and algebra errors. They are not substitutes for the universal proofs and have not been certified by a proof assistant.

\subsection{A limiting norm problem becomes a bounded Fourier problem}

For $d\ge2$, define
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:60:intro:cd}
 c_d^{\rm odd}
 =\sup_{G,f}\frac{\norm{f}_{U^2(G)}^4}{\norm{f}_{U^d(G)}^4},
 \qquad
 \beta_{\rm odd}
 =\sup_{G,f}\frac{\norm{f}_{U^2(G)}^4}{\norm{f}_\infty^4},
\end{equation}
where $G$ ranges over finite abelian groups of odd order and $f:G\to\R$ ranges over nonzero functions with $\E f=0$. All averages are normalized. Monotonicity gives a decreasing sequence $c_d^{\rm odd}$. Source~29 proves that its limit lies in $[1/3,1/2]$ \cite{repo60twentynine}.

We prove that
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:60:intro:norm-main}
 \lim_{d\to\infty}c_d^{\rm odd}=\beta_{\rm odd},
 \qquad
 \frac13\le\beta_{\rm odd}
 \le\frac12-\frac8{\pi^2}+\frac{64}{\pi^4}.
\end{equation}
For a fixed finite group, $\norm{f}_{U^d}\to\norm{f}_\infty$ is not enough to prove this assertion: the group and the function in the supremum can change with $d$. The central new estimate prevents Fourier fourth-power mass from escaping to more and more small coefficients. A compact dual-group construction then preserves the relevant mass while converting high-degree norm control into an $L^\infty$ bound.

The final numerical upper bound uses the sharp coefficient inequality
\[
 |\widehat f(\chi)|\le\frac1q\cot\frac\pi{2q}<\frac2\pi
\]
for real centered $|f|\le1$ and a character of odd order $q$. Parseval then constrains how the remaining Fourier mass can be distributed. The resulting interval has width approximately $0.01312006183$, compared with $1/6$ previously. In particular, the possibility that the limit is $1/2$ is excluded.

There is also an exact result in a more specific limiting regime. If the least prime divisor of $|G|$ tends to infinity along with $d$, the compact limit is connected. The Riesz--Sobolev inequality in \cite[Theorem~1.2]{christiliopoulou} then gives the exact limiting value $1/3$. Neither conclusion supplies an effective rate in $d$. The unrestricted identity $\beta_{\rm odd}=1/3$ remains a precise open problem.

\subsection{The complete arrangement polynomial and its extremizers}

Let $G,H,K$ be finite abelian groups and $s\ge4$ even. Sample $h\in H$, independent $y_1,\ldots,y_s\in H$, and a uniform balanced relation
\[
 x_1+\cdots+x_{s/2}=x_{s/2+1}+\cdots+x_s
\]
in $G$. A map $\phi:G\times H\to K$ passes when the same balanced relation holds among its vertical differences $D_h\phi(x_i,y_i)$. Write $\eps_s(\phi)$ for the failure probability. Its exact model class is
\[
 \Vcal=\{a(x)+B(x,y)+\ell(y):
       a\text{ arbitrary},\ B\text{ biadditive},\ \ell\text{ additive}\}.
\]
Let $\delta$ be the normalized Hamming distance to $\Vcal$.

The new polynomial is
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:60:intro:Bs}
 B_s(\delta)=\frac{1-(1-4\delta)^s}{4}
       -2^{2s-3}\delta^{s-1}(1-2\delta).
\end{equation}
For $0\le\delta\le1/4$ we prove $\eps_s\ge B_s(\delta)$. For every even $s\ge6$, this strictly improves the earlier polynomial throughout $0<\delta<1/4$. At $s=4$ it recovers the earlier sharp cubic
$4\delta-24\delta^2+32\delta^3$ and adds its complete interior equality classification.

For $0<\delta<1/4$, equality holds exactly when, after adding an exact model,
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:60:intro:equality}
 \phi(x,y)=a\,\1_C(x)\ell_2(y),
 \qquad 2a=0,\quad a\ne0,
\end{equation}
where $C$ is a coset of a subgroup of $G$ of index $n\ge3$, and $\ell_2:H\to\Z/2\Z$ is a surjective homomorphism. Then $\delta=1/(2n)$. Both even and odd indices are allowed. Thus the extremal errors fill half of the points in a coset of horizontal rows.

Under the inherited explicit activation condition
$\eps_s\le1/[240(s-1)]$, the appropriate small inverse branch $\rho_s=B_s^{-1}$ satisfies $\delta\le\rho_s(\eps_s)$. For $s\ge6$,
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:60:intro:inverse-series}
 \rho_s(u)=\frac us+\frac{2(s-1)}{s^2}u^2
       +\frac{8(s-1)(2s-1)}{3s^3}u^3+O_s(u^4).
\end{equation}
Every Taylor coefficient is optimal in succession, with all preceding coefficients fixed. This is stronger than identifying the cubic coefficient alone. It does not mean that $B_s$ is the exact pointwise envelope at every real distance: its nonzero equality distances are discrete.

For Gowers's eight-arrangements, $s=16$, so
\[
 \delta\le\frac{\eps}{16}
       +\frac{15}{128}\eps^2
       +\frac{155}{512}\eps^3+O(\eps^4).
\]
The common-prime case, in which all three groups equal $\F_p$, has a different second-order extremal problem. A separate construction and an odd-target cancellation estimate improve both sides of its coefficient bracket:
\[
 \frac{s-1}{s^2}\le c_s^{\rm prime}\le\frac{3s-2}{2s^2}.
\]
For $s=16$ this is $15/256\le c_{16}^{\rm prime}\le23/256$. It does not determine the optimal coefficient.

\subsection{Removing the arbitrary row function by a second test}

Let $\HH$ be the horizontal analogue of $\Vcal$, and let
\[
 \A=\{c+B(x,y)+m(x)+\ell(y)
       :B\text{ biadditive},\ m,\ell\text{ additive}
   \}
\]
be the fully biaffine class. If $d_v=\dist(\phi,\Vcal)$,
$d_h=\dist(\phi,\HH)$ and $\eta=d_v+d_h<1/4$, we prove
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:60:intro:intersection}
 \dist(\phi,\A)\le
 J(\eta):=\frac{1+\eta-\sqrt{1-2\eta}}2.
\end{equation}
Binary unions of one horizontal and one vertical strip show that this is the optimal continuous modulus from $\eta$ alone.

Write $e=\eps_s^v+\eps_s^h$ for the sum of directional failure probabilities and $\delta_A=\dist(\phi,\A)$. The local defect bound is
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:60:intro:two-profile}
 e\ge P_s(\delta_A):=2(1-\delta_A)B_s(\delta_A)
 \qquad(\delta_A\le1/4).
\end{equation}
It gives an explicit inverse repair theorem when $e\le1/(1920s)$, with
\[
 \delta_A\le\frac e{2s}+\frac{2s-1}{4s^2}e^2+O_s(e^3).
\]
More generally, all inverse coefficients through degree $s-2$ are optimal in succession. This answers source~33's two-direction question locally, including its request for sharp first-order constants. The full finite-error envelope is still open.

\subsection{A stronger restriction threshold with the same retention}

For even $m\ge4$, let $B\subseteq\F_p$ have size $b$, and suppose a map $\phi:B\to\F_p$ respects at least $\alpha b^{m-1}$ ordered balanced $m$-tuples. For $0<\alpha,\eta\le1$, put
\[
 L=\left\lceil\frac{m+1}{\alpha\eta}\right\rceil.
\]
We prove that the condition
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:60:intro:restriction-threshold}
 b\ge 2\left(1+\binom m2\right)L^{m-1}
\end{equation}
guarantees a subset $B'\subseteq B$ on which at least a fraction $1-\eta$ of the balanced tuples are respected and whose total number of balanced tuples is at least
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:60:intro:restriction-retention}
 \frac{\alpha^m\eta^{m-1}}{2(m+2)^m}\,b^{m-1}.
\end{equation}
This retains source~17's coefficient while improving the proposed combined threshold of sources~04 and~17 by one power of $L$. It also improves source~17's original threshold, whose degree is $2m-1$ in the inverse accuracy parameters. Fixed-characteristic affine-rank restriction is a separate regime where source~29 has stronger parameter dependence; our assertion is uniform as the prime modulus varies.

At $m=16$, a respected-quadruple count $\gamma b^3$ yields a respected $16$-tuple count $\gamma^7b^{15}$ by graph-energy interpolation. Thus one may take
\[
 L=\left\lceil\frac{17}{\gamma^7\eta}\right\rceil,
 \qquad b\ge242L^{15},
\]
and retain at least $\gamma^{112}\eta^{15}b^{15}/(2\cdot18^{16})$ balanced $16$-tuples. The proof also gives an exact finite-group certificate that records short-torsion leakage instead of assuming it absent.

\subsection{Notation and organization}

Every finite set carries its uniform probability measure. Compact abelian groups carry normalized Haar measure. Unless a section explicitly specifies a different local convention, character groups are written additively when recording algebraic relations and multiplicatively when evaluating characters; $\overline\chi=\chi^{-1}$ makes the convention explicit. Fourier coefficients are normalized, but frequency sums are not:
\[
 \widehat f(\chi)=\E_x f(x)\overline{\chi(x)},
 \qquad \sum_\chi|\widehat f(\chi)|^2=\E_x|f(x)|^2.
\]
For maps with values in a finite group, distance always means the uniform fraction of unequal values. The symbol $s$ denotes the even number of vertical differences in an arrangement; an $s$-difference arrangement has $2s$ point occurrences. In the restriction section $m$ denotes the even number of entries in a balanced relation. Elsewhere $m$ can be a local moment index or the half-arity $s/2$, as specified there. The restriction section uses additive circle-valued characters and explicitly switches to unnormalized Fourier coefficients in its graph-energy calculation.

The proofs of the norm limits, arrangement bounds, two-direction repair and restriction theorem occupy the next sections. The final sections discuss integration, computational evidence, and further research. The coarse majority decoder needed only to activate the local inverse bounds is reproduced in an appendix and credited to its repository and testing predecessors.

\section[{Source 61: Research objective, source comparison, and main results}]{Source 61. Research objective, source comparison, and main results}\label{gsr:fm:61:sec:d1}
\srcnote{61}{Section 1}
\partsource{\textbf{Added in the eleventh write, 7~October 2026.} \textbf{Delivered title page.} ``Combinatorics / Ramsey Theory / Exact Freiman Restriction in Arbitrary Finite Abelian Groups / Torsion-uniform coloring, relation-energy retention, and logarithmic order barriers / Mathematical development and exact computational checks with ChatGPT / Prepared for the ProveIt project / 6 October 2026''; \emph{the PDF author field reads ``ChatGPT; prepared for the ProveIt project''}. Archive \file{Gowers\_Torsion\_Exact\_Restriction.zip} (arrival \texttt{0d93c1eac}), manuscript \file{ramsey\_torsion\_exact\_restriction.tex} (1,249 lines, 23 pages), pin \texttt{5ea1d06dd} (its \file{SOURCE\_AUDIT.md}, shipped as \file{61-exact-restriction-SOURCE\_AUDIT.md}, records three blobs). Printed below: the abstract, the status statement of its title page and Section~1; Sections~2--9 stand in the Part~II restriction chapter (Section~\ref{gsr:en:sec:allmoduli}), Sections~10--13 and Appendix~A are in Part~V. Its macro \texttt{\textbackslash repo} (in small capitals) is renamed \texttt{\textbackslash reposc}, as for sources~58 and~59; its `question' environment (``Question'', on the shared counter) is set in this report's `Question' style; its `conjecture' environment is defined and not used.}
\begin{partabstract}{61}
We develop an exact-restriction alternative to two local steps in Gowers's proof of Szemer\'edi's theorem. If the graph $\Gamma$ of a map between finite abelian groups satisfies $|\Gamma-\Gamma|\leq K|\Gamma|$, then its entire domain can be partitioned into at most
\[
5mK^{(2m+1)\log_2(5m)}
\]
sets on which the map is a Freiman homomorphism of order $m$. No assumption on the orders, ranks, or exponents of the ambient groups is imposed. The partition retains weighted additive energies and any one prescribed scalar correlation with explicit losses.

Combining this with a self-contained, deliberately conservative Balog--Szemer\'edi--Gowers argument gives an order-eight restriction containing at least $2^{-2193}\alpha^{911}|B|$ points and at least $2^{-35277}\alpha^{14655}|B|^{15}$ additive sixteen-tuples, all respected exactly, whenever the original graph has at least $\alpha|B|^{15}$ such tuples. This strengthens the numerical conclusion of Gowers's Lemma 9.3, removes its size threshold, and replaces approximate respect by exact respect.

The underlying forbidden-difference coloring problem has a universal power exponent $b_m$ satisfying
\[
\floor{\log_2m}+1\leq b_m\leq\log_2(5m)\qquad(m\geq2).
\]
Thus its leading logarithmic dependence on the relation order is determined. Explicit $2$-primary examples also force every exact graph restriction to be a singleton and quantify a separate obstruction to improving the graph theorem. Complete proofs, exact finite checks, an integration plan, and further research problems are supplied.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small
\noindent\textbf{Status and scope.} This is an AI-assisted, unrefereed research manuscript. The stated results are supported by the proofs below; their formulations are offered for mathematical evaluation, not certified publication priority. No proof-assistant verification or improved global Szemer\'edi bound is claimed. Existing lemmas used as ingredients are explicitly attributed.
\end{quote}
\label{gsr:fm:61:ter:introduction}

The restriction of an approximately additive map to an exactly additive domain is one of the structural transitions in Gowers's argument \cite{gowers}. Two quantities matter simultaneously: how much of the domain survives, and how many additive relations survive. A large subset by itself does not give the desired relation count at the original density normalization. Moreover, an argument that chooses a scalar multiplier in a prime field does not automatically extend to a group with mixed torsion.

This manuscript separates the restriction mechanism into three steps. First, a finite forbidden set in the codomain is separated from zero by a short list of characters. Second, narrow character cells prevent every balanced relation of bounded length from having a forbidden defect. Third, graph small-difference estimates bound the number of possible vertical defects. This produces a partition rather than a single favorable restriction, which makes several retention statements automatic.

\subsection{What is and is not being improved}

The repository snapshot used here is
\begin{center}
\code{5ea1d06dd2f2d3a30e96016b236e3f1e3dfb048f}.
\end{center}
The formal statement of Lemma 7.5 in that snapshot assumes a prime modulus and supplies a restriction of size $|B|/(8mK^{4m})$. Lemma 9.3 is stated for all nonzero cyclic moduli, with a sufficiently-large-modulus hypothesis and an approximate-respect conclusion. The file \code{Proofs09Restriction.lean} already contains a theorem named \code{lemma\_9\_3\_holds}. Thus this manuscript does \emph{not} announce that an unproved repository statement has been closed. It gives a stronger, different route to the mathematical conclusion \cite{repo61statements,repo61proofs}.

The research collection already records substantially better \emph{prime-modulus} restrictions, including an order-eight size bound $2^{-209}\gamma^{103}|B|$ under an additive-energy hypothesis, and polynomial approximate-restriction bounds obtained by other methods \cite{repo61research}. The exponent $911$ proved here is not competitive with $103$ in that special setting. The contribution advanced for evaluation is instead the arbitrary-finite-abelian-group partition, its relation-energy consequences, and the logarithmic torsion obstruction. Neither the general Balog--Szemer\'edi--Gowers principle nor the Pl\"unnecke--Ruzsa inequalities are claimed as new.

There is a second important limitation. Keeping a chosen scalar correlation is not the same as preserving the complete derivative spectrum or the compatibility of a family of cross-sections. The latter issues arise later in Gowers's proof. No step below justifies replacing all of Sections 12--16, and no revised global bound for Szemer\'edi's theorem is deduced.

\subsection{Principal statements}

All groups in the principal results are finite and abelian, written additively. For a nonempty set $B\subseteq G$ and a map $\phi:B\to H$, write
\[
\Gamma=\{(x,\phi(x)):x\in B\},\qquad n=|B|.
\]
Definitions of the relation energies appear in Section~\ref{gsr:en:61:ter:notation}.

\begin{theorem}[Exact partition from graph growth]
\label{gsr:fm:61:ter:main-partition}
Let $m\geq1$ and $|\Gamma-\Gamma|\leq K n$. Put
\[
a_m=(2m+1)\log_2(5m),\qquad
\Def_m(\Gamma)=\{h\in H:(0,h)\in m\Gamma-m\Gamma\}.
\]
There is a partition of $B$ into $R$ nonempty sets $B_1,\ldots,B_R$ such that every $\phi|_{B_j}$ is a Freiman homomorphism of order $m$, and
\begin{equation}
\label{gsr:fm:61:ter:main-R}
R\leq (5m)^{\ceil{\log_2|\Def_m(\Gamma)|}}
\leq 5mK^{a_m}.
\end{equation}
In particular, some exact restriction has size at least $n/(5mK^{a_m})$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{writenote}[7 October 2026; sources 60--69]
\emph{Against source~59} (Section~\ref{gsr:en:sec:charseparation}; checked at the write). Source~59's Corollary~\ref{gsr:en:59:cor:doubling} gives $|B'|\ge C^{-(2k+1)\log_2(5k)}|B|$ from the same hypothesis, larger than this theorem's $n/(5mK^{a_m})$ by the factor $5m$, and its separation rank $\lfloor\log_2(q+1)\rfloor$ for $q$ sign orbits is at most this theorem's $\lceil\log_2|\Def_m(\Gamma)|\rceil$; this theorem's partition of the whole domain, with every cell exact, is its own form.
\end{writenote}

The defect-sensitive first bound is often preferable to its uniform relaxation. If the defect set consists only of zero, the partition has one cell and nothing is lost.

\begin{theorem}[Order-eight relation restriction]
\label{gsr:fm:61:ter:main-eight}
Suppose $0<\alpha\leq1$ and
\[
\Energy_8^\phi(B)\geq\alpha n^{15}.
\]
There exists a nonempty $B'\subseteq B$ on which $\phi$ is an exact Freiman homomorphism of order eight, such that simultaneously
\begin{align}
|B'|&\geq 2^{-2193}\alpha^{911}n,
\label{gsr:fm:61:ter:main-eight-size}\\
\Energy_8(B')=\Energy_8^\phi(B')
&\geq 2^{-35277}\alpha^{14655}n^{15}.
\label{gsr:fm:61:ter:main-eight-energy}
\end{align}
The same conclusions hold if the hypothesis is replaced by
$\Energy_2^\phi(B)\geq\alpha n^3$.
\end{theorem}

The constants are intentionally rounded to integral powers of two. A general-order formula, with less rounding and a modular interface for stronger energy-to-growth inputs, is proved in Section~\ref{gsr:en:61:ter:high-energy}.

\begin{theorem}[Leading order of the universal coloring exponent]
\label{gsr:fm:61:ter:main-exponent}
For $m\geq2$, let $b_m$ be the infimum of the real numbers $b$ for which a constant $C_m$ exists with the following property: for every finite abelian $H$ and every symmetric $D\subseteq H\setminus\{0\}$, one can partition $H$ into at most $C_m(|D|+1)^b$ cells $S$ satisfying
\[
(mS-mS)\cap D=\varnothing.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
\label{gsr:fm:61:ter:exponent-bracket}
\floor{\log_2m}+1\leq b_m\leq\log_2(5m).
\end{equation}
Consequently $b_m=\log_2m+O(1)$ and
$\lim_{m\to\infty}b_m/\log_2m=1$.
\end{theorem}

The lower bound concerns the coloring problem itself, not merely a particular character construction. It does not prove that the exponent $a_m$ in Theorem~\ref{gsr:fm:61:ter:main-partition} is optimal. Section~\ref{gsr:en:61:ter:torsion} distinguishes these two optimization problems.

\subsection{Proof architecture and provenance}

Sections~\ref{gsr:en:61:ter:characters}--\ref{gsr:en:61:ter:partition-proof} prove the character-separation and exact-partition statements. The Pl\"unnecke argument follows the minimal-growth method of Petridis \cite{petridis}, with its proof included. Section~\ref{gsr:en:61:ter:bsg} supplies a conservative energy-to-growth estimate by a standard popular-difference and dependent-random-choice method; see Gowers \cite{gowers} and Fox--Sudakov \cite{foxsudakov} for the surrounding methodology. Section~\ref{gsr:en:61:ter:high-energy} tracks every constant in the combination. Section~\ref{gsr:en:61:ter:torsion} gives the obstructions and proves Theorem~\ref{gsr:fm:61:ter:main-exponent}.

Our comparison with existing work is targeted: the original paper, relevant repository statements and research descriptions, and primary references for the standard ingredients. It is not an exhaustive review of every formulation of Freiman restriction or higher-order difference coloring. The proofs and the source-comparison claims should be evaluated separately from any future claim of priority.

\srcnote{62}{Section 1}
\partsource{\textbf{Added in the eleventh write, 7~October 2026.} \textbf{Delivered title block.} ``Unit-Dilation Restriction on Cyclic Groups / Polynomial losses for Gowers' approximate homomorphisms and exact weighted degeneracy constants / Research manuscript prepared with ChatGPT / For the ProveIt Ramsey research collection / 6 October 2026''; \emph{the PDF author field reads ``Research manuscript prepared with ChatGPT''}. Archive \file{ProveIt\_All\_Moduli\_Restriction.zip} (arrival \texttt{0d93c1eac}), manuscript \file{article.tex} (1,317 lines, 20 pages), pin \texttt{17123532a} (its \file{SOURCE\_AUDIT.md}, shipped as \file{62-unit-dilation-SOURCE\_AUDIT.md}, records four blobs; \file{data/62-unit-dilation-CLAIMS.json} the same revision). Printed below: the abstract, its status statement and Section~1; Sections~2--9 stand in the Part~II restriction chapter (Section~\ref{gsr:en:sec:allmoduli}), Sections~10--13 are in Part~V. Its macros \texttt{\textbackslash ee} ($\exp(2\pi i\,\cdot)$, not this report's $\mathrm e(\cdot)$), \texttt{\textbackslash U} (roman $\mathrm U$, not this report's $\mathcal U$) and \texttt{\textbackslash R} (calligraphic $\mathcal R$, not the reals) are renamed \texttt{\textbackslash eexp}, \texttt{\textbackslash Urm} and \texttt{\textbackslash Rcal}; its `question' environment (``Question'', on the shared counter) is set in this report's `Question' style.}
\begin{partabstract}{62}
We give a one-stage restriction argument for maps between cyclic groups of
arbitrary, possibly different, orders. The argument extends the polynomial-loss
Fej\'er restriction method beyond prime moduli. Its two main ingredients are
averaging the codomain dilation over units, which distinguishes nonzero defects
of small order, and a weighted gcd count, which avoids deleting every tuple
satisfying an additional short relation.

For the order-eight interface of Gowers' Lemma 9.3, suppose that
$B\subseteq\Z/N\Z$ has size $\beta N$ and a map $\phi:B\to\Z/M\Z$ respects at
least $\alpha|B|^{15}$ additive sixteen-tuples. A completely elementary version
produces a restriction that respects a proportion at least $1-\eta$, retaining
at least $2^{-245}\alpha^{31}\eta^{30}|B|^{15}$ respected tuples whenever
$N\ge 2^{253}(\alpha\eta)^{-31}\beta^{-15}$.
A more precise parameter choice gives retention
$\gg\alpha^{16}\eta^{15}|B|^{15}/
[\log\log(\e^{\e}/(\alpha\eta))]^{15}$, with a polynomial size threshold;
this sharper envelope uses the classical explicit totient estimate of Rosser
and Schoenfeld.

We also determine the exact weighted exceptional-tuple constant at each filter
length, identify moduli attaining it, and prove that its limit is
$\zeta(m-2)/\zeta(m-1)$ for $m$-tuples. A primorial construction shows that a
uniform constant bound for the primitive-dilation response of these kernels is
impossible: the double logarithm has the correct worst-case scale for this
specific detector. All new statements are proved below. Exact finite checks,
an integration crosswalk, and a research agenda accompany the manuscript.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small
\noindent\textbf{Status and scope.}
This is an AI-assisted mathematical research draft, not an independently
refereed paper or a Lean-kernel-checked development. The claims of proof below
refer to the written arguments. No publication-priority claim is made.
The result improves a local restriction step; it does not establish a new
end-to-end bound for Szemer\'edi's theorem or a Ramsey number.
\end{quote}

Gowers' restriction step asks how to turn a positive density of respected
additive relations into an almost perfectly respected family on a subset.
The method is useful because it does not first require an exact Freiman
homomorphism. Lemma 9.3 of \cite{gowers} is the order-eight instance.
The present article addresses the quantitative restriction problem itself,
rather than the subsequent extension or phase-integration steps.

The repository's current research summary records polynomial-loss restriction
results over prime moduli and fixed finite fields, while distinguishing these
from the all-moduli interface \cite{repo62research}. The obstruction to simply
reusing prime-modulus averaging is real. If a nonzero target defect has order
$q$, averaging a dilation over \emph{all} scalars leaves every Fourier mode
whose index is divisible by $q$. Increasing the filter length does not remove
this effect. We calculate the obstruction explicitly in
Section~\ref{gsr:en:62:sec:obstructions}.

Our replacement averages the target dilation over units. The resulting
response is a Ramanujan-sum transform of a positive trigonometric kernel.
This has two advantages: every nonzero defect is tested through primitive
$q$th roots, and the response is bounded independently of the ambient modulus.
Separately, we sum the weights of exceptional short relations instead of
counting their supports. The resulting error is $O_m(N^{m-2})$, with a
constant independent of filter length, even over composite cyclic groups.

The distinction from the existing formal development is important.
At the inspected repository revision, the module
\texttt{Proofs09Restriction.lean} already contains
\texttt{lemma\_9\_3\_holds} \cite{repo62proof}.
Thus the contribution is a stronger estimate and a different proof mechanism,
not a claim that the old all-moduli statement has no proof.

\paragraph{Main mathematical outputs.}
The principal restriction theorem is Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:62:thm:main}.
The fully explicit polynomial order-eight consequence is
Corollary~\ref{gsr:en:62:cor:polynomial8}. The exact arithmetic error formula and its
limiting constant are Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:62:thm:kappa}.
Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:62:thm:primitive-lower} identifies a genuine limitation of the
unit-Fej\'er detector. Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:62:thm:profile-restriction} preserves the entire
defect-order distribution, and Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:62:thm:labels} extends the argument to
labelled domains of bounded fibre multiplicity.

\section[{Source 63: Introduction and principal results}]{Source 63. Introduction and principal results}\label{gsr:fm:63:sec:d1}\label{gsr:fm:63:intro:section}
\srcnote{63}{Section 1}
\partsource{\textbf{Added in the eleventh write, 7~October 2026.} \textbf{Delivered title page.} ``ProveIt / Combinatorics / Ramsey / Asymptotically Sharp Constants in Gowers' Szemer\'edi Framework / Odd-order norm limits and efficient local phase removal / Prepared for Vladimir Reshetnikov and the ProveIt project / Mathematical development and manuscript by ChatGPT / 7 October 2026''; \emph{the PDF author field reads ``ChatGPT; prepared for Vladimir Reshetnikov and the ProveIt project''}. Its macro \texttt{\textbackslash T} (the circle $\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$, not this report's $\mathbb T$) is renamed \texttt{\textbackslash Tquot}; its `question' environment (``Research question'', on the shared counter) is set as this report's `Research question'; its two figures are shipped as \file{figures/63-asymptotic-constants-norm\_upper\_bounds.pdf} and \file{figures/63-asymptotic-constants-localization\_retention.pdf}.}
\begin{partabstract}{63}
\noindent
We prove two asymptotically sharp results for intermediate problems
arising from Gowers' proof of Szemer\'edi's theorem. For real centered
functions on arbitrary finite abelian groups of odd order, the optimal
constant in $\|f\|_{U^2}^4\le c_d\|f\|_{U^d}^4$ tends to exactly
$1/3$, resolving the limiting-constant question posed in the inspected
ProveIt reports. We give the uniform rate
$c_d\le1/3+10\,2^{-\lfloor d/8\rfloor}$ for $d\ge80$.
The argument uses a sharp bounded inequality with the exact
order-$N$ coefficient $1/3-4/(3N^2)+1/N^3$, a Fourier-tail estimate,
positive smoothing, and uniform recovery of a supremum norm.
It also identifies the asymptotically sharp quartic coefficient
in centered cube-count upper expansions.

For local phase removal, an exact positive measure on the faces
of a box improves the preceding sliding-window localization
coefficient. The retained factor is
$2^{k+1}/((k+2)!D_k)$, where
$1\le D_k\le\exp(2/[3(k+2)])$.
A matching geometric ceiling proves that the best local coefficient
is asymptotic to $2^{k+1}/(k+2)!$. We supply a finite theorem with
explicit rounding factors, extend the cover identity to positive
real powers, and formulate further extremal, stability, and
formalization problems. Complete proofs, exact supplementary checks,
source provenance, and internal review notes accompany the article.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small
\noindent Research contribution for integration into the Ramsey collection.
Theorems are stated with their full scope; fixed-degree and global questions are distinguished explicitly.
\end{quote}

Gowers' proof of Szemer\'edi's theorem combines uniformity norms,
additive structure, polynomial phases, and localization to arithmetic
progressions \cite{gowers}. Its intermediate estimates give several
well-defined extremal problems even when improvements at those steps
do not change the final asymptotic bound for progression-free sets.
This article addresses two such problems: the comparison between
second and high-order uniformity norms for real centered functions,
and the amount of local cube mass that survives removal of a
multilinear derivative phase.

The first problem is uniform over all finite abelian groups of odd
order. Earlier reports in the ProveIt research collection established
an exact answer at order three and left the high-order limit between
$1/3$ and $1/2$ \cite{repo63}. We prove that the limit is $1/3$,
and give an explicit convergence rate. A short sharp inequality for
bounded functions supplies the endpoint; the main work is to pass
from that inequality to an estimate uniform over groups of arbitrary
size. The second problem concerns Proposition~17.7 of Gowers' paper.
An earlier report replaced the enumeration of carry patterns by
sliding windows and positive covers \cite{localphase63}. We construct
a more efficient cover and prove that its coefficient approaches the
universal geometric ceiling as the degree increases.

\subsection{The odd-order norm limit}

For $d\ge2$, define
\[
 c_d^{\mathrm{odd}}
 =\sup_{\substack{|G|\text{ odd},\ G\text{ finite abelian}\\
                   f:G\to\R,\ \E f=0,\ f\ne0}}
     \frac{\|f\|_{U^2(G)}^4}{\|f\|_{U^d(G)}^4}.
\]
All norms use probability normalization. Theorem~\ref{gsr:cc:63:norm:main} proves
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:63:intro:norm}
 \boxed{\displaystyle\lim_{d\to\infty}c_d^{\mathrm{odd}}=\frac13},
 \qquad
 \frac13\le c_d^{\mathrm{odd}}
 \le\frac13+10\,2^{-\lfloor d/8\rfloor}\quad(d\ge80).
\end{equation}
The supremum includes both $G$ and $f$. Establishing convergence for
each fixed group would leave open the possibility that increasingly
large groups retain a larger ratio. The Fourier-tail estimate,
positive smoothing, and finite-spectrum recovery proved in
Section~\ref{gsr:cc:63:norm:section} eliminate that possibility.

The bounded-function ingredient is itself exact. If $N\ge3$ is odd,
$|G|=N$, and $f:G\to\R$ is centered, then
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:63:intro:finite}
 \|f\|_{U^2}^4
 \le\left(\frac13-\frac4{3N^2}+\frac1{N^3}\right)\|f\|_\infty^4.
\end{equation}
For each $N$, a cyclic square wave attains equality. Thus the
coefficient is the exact optimum among groups of that order. Its
uniform limit is the sharp constant $1/3$. The proof is based on
the autocorrelation constraint
\[
 1+R_f(2h)\ge2|R_f(h)|\qquad (\|f\|_\infty\le1),
\]
together with measure preservation under doubling. It also yields a
compact-group theorem and an exact defect identity.

The norm result has a direct counting consequence. The quartic
term of the centered $d$-cube expansion at background density $\delta$ is
\[
 P_d\delta^{2^d-4}\|f\|_{U^2}^4,\qquad
 P_d=\frac{6^d-2\cdot4^d+2^d}{8}.
\]
Consequently the optimal quartic coefficient measured in
$\|f\|_{U^d}^4$ is asymptotic to $P_d/3$.
Section~\ref{gsr:cc:63:cube:section} retains the higher-order remainder explicitly
and explains the precise small-perturbation sense of this assertion.

\subsection{Efficient phase removal}

For the local problem, the natural geometric coefficient is
\[
 v_k=\frac{2^{k+1}}{(k+2)!}.
\]
It is the leading normalized number of $(k+1)$-cubes inside a long
interval. We use the same local output normalization throughout:
if a partition has $M$ cells, each of size at most $U$, divide its
total $(k+1)$-cube mass by $MU^{k+2}$.

For an input box of odd width $m$ in a prime cyclic group of order
$N\ge m^2$, under its stated derivative-energy and width hypotheses,
Theorem~\ref{gsr:fp:63:loc:thm:finite} gives a phase of degree at most $k+1$
and a partition with cell lengths
$\lceil m/(3k)\rceil$ or $\lceil m/(3k)\rceil+1$.
As $m\to\infty$ for fixed $k$, the retained coefficient is
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:63:intro:phase}
 \frac{v_k}{D_k},\qquad
 D_k=\sum_{j=0}^k\binom kj\left(\frac2{3k}\right)^j
                          \frac{(k-j+2)!}{(k+2)!}.
\end{equation}
If $c_k^{\mathrm{loc}}$ denotes the optimal asymptotic coefficient
for this output class, then
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:63:intro:ceiling}
 e^{-2/[3(k+2)]}v_k\le\frac{v_k}{D_k}
 \le c_k^{\mathrm{loc}}\le v_k,
 \qquad \boxed{c_k^{\mathrm{loc}}\sim v_k}.
\end{equation}
The local-scale limit precedes the degree limit. The exact finite
theorem records all rounding losses and its width condition, so the
asymptotic statement does not conceal restrictions on finite inputs.

The geometric mechanism is useful independently of phase removal.
We put explicit positive densities on all faces of a box, with
codimension-$j$ density
$(k-j+2)!w^j/(k+2)!$. Convolution with
$(w-\|x\|_1)_+^2$ is given by a sum of nonnegative terms, the first
of which is the full integral of the kernel. Mean-preserving rounding
passes the cover to lattice points without increasing its mass.
The same identity extends to every positive real power of the kernel;
the lattice statement holds for powers at least one.

\subsection{Scope and relation to the source collection}

The comparison baseline is the inspected ProveIt snapshot
\texttt{d7b83fa1fe60}, together with the
separate manuscript \emph{Local Phase Removal and Cubic Rigidity in
Gowers' Szemer\'edi Framework} \cite{localphase63}. The source audit
in Appendix~\ref{gsr:fz:63:audit:section} records the relevant files, report
numbers, and provenance. In that collection, Source~29 gave
$c_d^{\mathrm{odd}}\le B_d$ with $B_d\downarrow1/2$, while the lower
construction approached $1/3$. The limiting-constant question posed
there is answered by \eqref{gsr:fm:63:intro:norm}. The new cover closes the
constant-factor asymptotic gap in the preceding local phase-removal
coefficient.

The distinctions between these statements matter. The exact values
of $c_d^{\mathrm{odd}}$ at fixed $d\ge4$ remain undetermined here.
The inspected later report~45 improves the fourth-order upper bound
to $(832/4795)^{1/4}$; this article's high-order result is compatible
with that sharper fixed-order estimate and does not replace it.
Likewise, \eqref{gsr:fm:63:intro:ceiling} determines the first-order behavior of
the optimal local coefficient but leaves its fixed-degree value and
its next relative term open. Finally, we do not propagate these
improvements through all the subsequent density-increment steps of
Gowers' proof. No new final quantitative bound for Szemer\'edi's
theorem is asserted.

The article presents complete mathematical proofs of its principal
claims, with supplementary exact finite checks. The development and
separate proof reviews were carried out by ChatGPT instances; the
review notes are included so their scope can be assessed. They are
not external peer review or a formal proof-assistant certificate.
The stated research advance is relative to the inspected project
questions and comparison theorems. A targeted literature search is
recorded in the accompanying audit, without a claim of historical
priority over all published work.

\section[{Source 64: The problem, the results, and their position in the literature}]{Source 64. The problem, the results, and their position in the literature}\label{gsr:fm:64:sec:d1}
\srcnote{64}{Section 1}
\partsource{\textbf{Added in the eleventh write, 7~October 2026.} \textbf{Delivered title block.} ``Binomial separation and endpoint bounds for uniform progression counts / A six-variable digit construction, an exact nine-copy transfer, and obstructions to perfect cyclic codes / Research manuscript prepared for the ProveIt project / 6 October 2026''; \emph{the PDF author field reads the same; neither the manuscript nor its delivery files make a statement on AI assistance}. Archive \file{gowers\_binomial\_separation\_research.zip} (arrival \texttt{0d93c1eac}), manuscript \file{article.tex} (1,268 lines, 19 pages); \emph{no pin}: its \file{SOURCE\_AUDIT.md}, shipped as \file{64-binomial-separation-SOURCE\_AUDIT.md}, records the blob \texttt{987daf1} of \file{Section04.lean} and two ``search snapshots'' \texttt{17123532a} and \texttt{176e155e5}, ``not a claim that the entire repository was checked at either immutable commit''. Printed below: the abstract, its status statement and Section~1; Sections~2--8 form a chapter of Part~III on Gowers's Section~4 conjectures (Section~\ref{gsr:cc:sec:binomial}), Sections~9--11 are in Part~V. It uses \texttt{cleveref} (options \texttt{capitalize}, \texttt{nameinlink}, \texttt{noabbrev}); its references are written out with the name of the statement referred to, capitalized. \emph{Its delivered PDF names every statement on the shared counter ``Theorem''} (for example ``Theorem~2.4'' for Proposition~2.4 and ``Theorem~4.1'' for Lemma~4.1), as source~57's did; the names printed here are those of the statements. Its one-argument macro \texttt{\textbackslash repo} (a path in typewriter type, not this report's \texttt{ProveIt}) is renamed \texttt{\textbackslash repopath}; its `question' environment (``Question'', on the shared counter) is set in this report's `Question' style.}
\begin{partabstract}{64}
We study the quantitative separation between uniformity and arithmetic-progression
counts that underlies the conjectures in Section~4 of Gowers's 2001 paper.
The alphabet $D=\{0,1,4,13\}$ makes the map
$(a,b,c)\mapsto a+5b+10c$ injective modulo $80$.
A digit-lifting argument therefore constructs sets with no nontrivial solutions to
the six-binomial equation at reciprocal growth exponent
$\bSix=\log_4 80=3.1609640474\ldots$, improving the exponent $5$ supplied by the
general construction recorded by Deng--Tidor--Zhao.
We give an exact transfer from a symmetric-progression-free $r$-coloring of an
interval of length $N$ to a $9r$-coloring of the circle: the symmetric
$k$-progression probability is exactly $1/(9(k-1)N)$, independently of the
number of colors. Combined with binomial-separating labels, this yields an
explicit torus construction with exactly computable progression density.
Using the prime-indexed colorings of Shi--Dong, rather than fixing and tensoring
one coloring, gives the endpoint bounds
$\rho_4(\alpha)\ll\alpha^5$ and
$\rho_6(\alpha)\ll\alpha^{5+9/\log_4 80}$, without an epsilon loss in the exponents.
We also prove that no non-singleton cyclic digit alphabet for the weights
$(1,5,10)$ can attain the counting limit $|D|^3=B$, and give an exact
Chevalley--Warning dimension barrier for degree-$(k-1)$ polynomial colorings.
All claimed improvements have mathematical proofs; finite checks are supplied
separately. The conjectural value $\beta_6=3$ and the superpolynomial-decay
questions remain open here.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small
\noindent\textbf{Status and scope.}
This is a research manuscript, not a declaration of formal verification or of
publication priority. The improvements established below are compared with
specific inspected sources. The Shi--Dong coloring theorem is credited as a
2026 preprint input. The general analytic realization theorem is credited to
Deng--Tidor--Zhao; an independent prime-modulus proof sufficient for the present
indicator constructions is included. No improvement to the general quantitative
Szemer\'edi theorem or to classical graph Ramsey numbers is claimed.
\end{quote}
\label{gsr:fm:64:sec:introduction}

\subsection{Uniformity one order below the counting threshold}
For $G=\Z/M\Z$ and $f:G\to\C$, put
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:64:eq:AP}
 \Lambda_k(f)=\E_{x,d\in G}\prod_{i=0}^{k-1}f(x+id).
\end{equation}
All progressions are ordered, and the term $d=0$ is included. Its contribution
is negligible as $M\to\infty$ for the fixed-density asymptotic questions here.
We use normalized Gowers norms:
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:64:eq:gowers}
 \norm{f}_{U^s(G)}^{2^s}
 =\E_{x,h_1,\ldots,h_s\in G}
   \prod_{\omega\in\{0,1\}^s}
       \mathcal C^{|\omega|}f(x+\omega\cdot h),
\end{equation}
where $\mathcal C$ denotes complex conjugation.

We use the definition of $\rho_k$ in \cite[Definition~1.11]{dengtidorzhao}:
$\rho_k(\alpha)$ is the largest $u$ such that, for every $\eps>0$, there are
$\eta>0$ and $M_0$ for which
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:64:eq:rho-def}
 M\ge M_0,\quad A\subseteq\Z/M\Z,\quad
 \norm{\1_A-\alpha}_{U^{k-2}}\le\eta
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \Lambda_k(\1_A)\ge u-\eps.
\end{equation}
In particular, a sequence of examples along primes suffices for an upper bound
on this quantity, even though the definition quantifies over all sufficiently
large moduli.

Gowers's Section~4 conjectures concerned lower bounds of random-set order under
one less degree of uniformity than the standard counting theorem requires
\cite{gowers}. Gowers's later construction already gave a counterexample at
length four \cite{gowersuniformfour}. The 2026 Shi--Dong preprint gives the corresponding
negative conclusion for every even length \cite{shidong}. Those disproofs are
\emph{not} contributions claimed here. Our target is the sharper quantitative
question: how small can the progression count be, and which parts of the
coloring-to-uniform-set construction lose exponent?

\subsection{Main quantitative statements}
Set
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:64:eq:exponents}
 \bSix=\frac{\log 80}{\log4}=3.160964047443681\ldots,
 \qquad
 \tSix=5+\frac9{\bSix}=7.847232636916081\ldots.
\end{equation}
Here $\bSix$ is the exponent furnished by our construction; $\beta_6$ below
continues to denote an extremal parameter, not a quantity asserted to equal
$\bSix$.

\begin{theorem}[Principal consequences]\label{gsr:fm:64:thm:principal}
The following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item For every positive integer $r$ and every integer $m>256r^{\bSix}$ there is
an $r$-element set $S\subseteq\Z/m\Z$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:64:eq:six-binomial}
 x_0-5x_1+10x_2-10x_3+5x_4-x_5=0,\quad x_i\in S,
\end{equation}
forces $x_0=x_5$, $x_1=x_4$, and $x_2=x_3$.
Consequently $3\le\beta_6\le\bSix$, where $\beta_6$ is the reciprocal
asymptotic growth exponent for sets avoiding nontrivial six-binomial solutions.
\item There are constants $C_4,C_6,\alpha_0>0$, independent of $\alpha$, such that
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:64:eq:main-rho}
 \rho_4(\alpha)\le C_4\alpha^5,
 \qquad
 \rho_6(\alpha)\le C_6\alpha^{\tSix}
 \qquad(0<\alpha\le\alpha_0).
\end{equation}
For each fixed such $\alpha$, these bounds are realized by deterministic
indicator sets along primes, with density tending to $\alpha$ and centered
$U^{k-2}$ norm tending to zero.
\item If $D\subseteq\Z/B\Z$, $|D|=r>1$, and
$(a,b,c)\mapsto a+5b+10c$ is injective on $D^3$, then $B>r^3$.
Thus no one fixed cyclic digit alphabet attains reciprocal exponent $3$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

Part~(i) is proved in Section~\ref{gsr:cc:64:sec:digits}; part~(ii) follows from the exact transfer
in Sections~\ref{gsr:cc:64:sec:circle} and \ref{gsr:cc:64:sec:vertical} and the scale-selection argument in
Section~\ref{gsr:cc:64:sec:endpoints}; part~(iii) is proved in Section~\ref{gsr:cc:64:sec:tiling}.
An additional barrier in Section~\ref{gsr:cc:64:sec:polynomial} shows that the dimension $k^2/4$
in the scalar degree-$(k-1)$ polynomial stage of the Shi--Dong construction
cannot be increased within that precisely specified model.

\subsection{What is strengthened, and what is inherited}
The comparison points are deliberately specific.
The six-binomial construction improves the universal exponent $k-1=5$ in
\cite[Lemma~3.3 and Definition~3.4]{dengtidorzhao}, and is a six-variable counterpart of
that paper's special four-variable label lemma. The circle construction retains
only full mirror symmetry, which is sufficient when the labels force mirror
pairings. This removes the need to eliminate additional monochromatic patterns
that enter the more general reduction. The endpoint argument uses all scales
of the available prime family, so constants depending on a single chosen prime
never turn into an exponent loss.

For four-term progressions the resulting exponent $5$ is the endpoint of the
$5-\eps$ family stated in \cite[Corollary~1.4]{shidong}. For six terms the
combination with the generic exponent $5$ yields a limiting exponent $34/5$
before an epsilon loss; replacing the labels and avoiding that loss gives
$\tSix>34/5$. Since $\alpha<1$, the larger exponent is the stronger upper bound.
These are not statements that the displayed exponents are optimal.

The language of injective weighted sums is the standard language of
\emph{Sidon sets for linear forms} \cite{nathansonsidon}. Digital constructions are
not new as a general method; see also the distinct setting of greedy weighted
Sidon sets in \cite{chenggreedy}. The proposed contributions are the explicit
six-binomial parameters, the exact transfer and its endpoint use, and the
precise obstructions proved here. The literature and repository searches
recorded in the accompanying source audit are not an exhaustive priority

\section[{Source 65: The extremal problem and the main results}]{Source 65. The extremal problem and the main results}\label{gsr:fm:65:sec:d1}\label{gsr:fm:65:bsi:sec:main}
\srcnote{65}{Section 1}
\partsource{\textbf{Added in the eleventh write, 7~October 2026.} \textbf{Delivered title block.} ``Sharp Boolean Phase Integration in Every Degree / Defect-radical slicing, exact nonintegrability thresholds, and extremal tensor rigidity in Gowers's framework / Research manuscript prepared with ChatGPT for Vladimir Reshetnikov and the ProveIt project / 6 October 2026''; \emph{the PDF author field reads ``Research manuscript prepared with ChatGPT for Vladimir Reshetnikov''}. Archive \file{Gowers\_All\_Degree\_Boolean\_Integration.zip} (arrival \texttt{0281fcb05}, 7~October 2026, 08:30), manuscript \file{all\_degree\_boolean\_integration.tex} (1,459 lines, 21 pages), pin \texttt{8c40adc24} (its \file{SOURCE\_AUDIT.md}, shipped as \file{65-all-degree-boolean-SOURCE\_AUDIT.md}, records the blobs of \file{Sections17\_18.lean} and \file{Definitions.lean}). Printed below: the abstract, its status statement and Section~1; Sections~2--8 open the Part~IV chapter on Boolean phase integration in every degree (Section~\ref{gsr:fp:sec:alldegree}), Sections~9--12 and Appendices~A--B are in Part~V. Its macros \texttt{\textbackslash F} ($\mathbb F_2$, not this report's $\mathbb F$), \texttt{\textbackslash TT} (the circle $\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$, not this report's $\mathsf T$) and \texttt{\textbackslash pin} (its own pin) are set as this report's \texttt{\textbackslash Ftwo}, the same definition, as \texttt{\textbackslash Tquot} and as \texttt{\textbackslash pinsixtyfive}; its `question' environment (``Research question'', numbered 1--9 on its own counter) is set in this report's `Research question' style, numbered within its section, which keeps the indices.}
\begin{partabstract}{65}
For a symmetric $d$-linear frequency tensor $T$ on $\mathbb F_2^n$, let
$\En_T(f)$ be its normalized selected derivative Fourier energy. We prove
that the largest possible energy of a nonintegrable symmetric tensor is
exactly $1-(d+1)/2^d$, for every $d\ge3$ and $n\ge2$. This closes the
septic and all-degree questions in the preceding project manuscript,
which established the universal value only through degree six.
The key is an exact identification: the directions producing integrable
contractions are precisely the radical of the repeated-variable defect.
A noncanonical defect has radical codimension at least two, so at least
three quarters of its contractions remain nonintegrable. Slicing and
induction then give the strictly smaller cap $1-3d/2^{d+1}$.
Consequently every extremal tensor, in every degree, is a canonical
two-coordinate obstruction modulo an integrable tensor. We give an
explicit recovery algorithm, count these obstruction classes, classify
all their integrable restrictions, and obtain a dimension-independent
rigidity window and robust phase-removal criteria. Full proofs include
the needed cubic spectral bound and the prior canonical energy formula.
The integration criterion and canonical-family result are credited as
existing ingredients; the all-degree closure and its rigidity consequences
are the contributions of this manuscript.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small
\noindent\textbf{Status and scope.} Unrefereed research manuscript with exact
finite regression checks, not a proof-assistant verification. The resolved
questions are explicitly identified project questions. Literature priority
is not asserted. This is a sharp characteristic-two local phase-integration
result, not a new end-to-end bound for Szemer\'edi's theorem.
\end{quote}

\subsection{Normalization and integrability}
Let $V=\Ftwo^n$. All averages are uniform and normalized. For a function
$f:V\to\C$ and a direction $h\in V$, write
\[
 \partial_hf(x)=f(x+h)\overline{f(x)},\qquad
 \Delta_hP(x)=P(x+h)-P(x),\qquad e(t)=\exp(2\pi i t).
\]
A tensor in this article is genuinely multilinear in all its slots, not
merely a polynomial that is affine in each slot. Write $\Sym^d(V)$ for
symmetric multilinear maps $V^d\to\Ftwo$. For a $d$-linear tensor $T$ define
\begin{equation}
 \En_T(f)=\E_{h_1,\ldots,h_{d-1}}
 \left|\E_x\partial_{h_1}\cdots\partial_{h_{d-1}}f(x)
 (-1)^{T(h_1,\ldots,h_{d-1},x)}\right|^2,
 \qquad
 \M(T)=\max_{\norm f_\infty\le1}\En_T(f).
 \label{gsr:fm:65:bsi:eq:energy}
\end{equation}
The last slot evaluates the selected frequency. The maximum exists by
compactness of a finite product of closed complex unit discs. In this
normalization $0\le\En_T(f)\le1$ for $\norm f_\infty\le1$.

A map $P:V\to\Tquot$ is a nonclassical polynomial of degree at most $d$ when
all its $(d+1)$-fold additive differences vanish. A symmetric tensor $T$
is \emph{integrable} when some such $P$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \Delta_{h_1}\cdots\Delta_{h_d}P(x)
     =\tfrac12T(h_1,\ldots,h_d)\pmod1
 \quad\text{for all }x,h_1,\ldots,h_d.
 \label{gsr:fm:65:bsi:eq:integrable}
\end{equation}
The integrable tensors form a linear subspace $\I_d(V)$.
Circle-valued phases are essential here: restricting the primitive to an
$\Ftwo$-valued classical polynomial would change the problem.

For independent $u,v\in V^*$ put
\begin{equation}
 C_d^{u,v}(h_1,\ldots,h_d)
   =\sum_{i=1}^d v(h_i)\prod_{j\ne i}u(h_j),
 \qquad b_d=1-\frac{d+1}{2^d}.
 \label{gsr:fm:65:bsi:eq:canonical}
\end{equation}
Call a tensor \emph{canonical modulo integration} when it equals
$C_d^{u,v}+S$ with $u,v$ independent and $S\in\I_d(V)$.

\subsection{The universal theorem}
\begin{theorem}[Sharp all-degree symmetric threshold]\label{gsr:fm:65:bsi:thm:main}
For every $d\ge3$ and $n\ge2$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\quad
 \max_{T\in\Sym^d(V)\setminus\I_d(V)}\M(T)
        =1-\frac{d+1}{2^d}.
 \quad}\label{gsr:fm:65:bsi:eq:universal}
\end{equation}
Moreover, for a nonintegrable symmetric tensor $T$,
\begin{equation}
 \M(T)=b_d
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 T=C_d^{u,v}+S
 \quad\text{for independent }u,v\in V^*,\ S\in\I_d(V).
 \label{gsr:fm:65:bsi:eq:endpoint}
\end{equation}
If $\En_T(f)>b_d$, then $T$ is integrable. For any primitive $P_T$,
\begin{equation}
 \En_T(f)=\norm{f e(-P_T)}_{U^d}^{2^d}.
 \label{gsr:fm:65:bsi:eq:phase-removal}
\end{equation}
The strict inequality cannot be replaced by a non-strict one.
\end{theorem}

\begin{writenote}[7 October 2026; sources 60--69]
\emph{Proved twice} (Section~\ref{gsr:fp:sec:alldegree}): source~69's Theorem~\ref{gsr:fm:69:bad:thm:main} is the same statement for the maximum, with the equality classification for $d\ge4$. \emph{Checked at the write} (exact rationals): the table above, $b_d$ for $3\le d\le10$, the noncanonical caps $1-3d/2^{d+1}$ for $4\le d\le10$ and $1/4$ at $d=3$, the gaps $(d-2)/2^{d+1}$, source~47's caps $1-\min\{d+1,7\}/2^d$ and the gain $(d-6)/2^d$.
\end{writenote}
Here the Gowers quantity is normalized by
$\norm g_{U^d}^{2^d}=\En_0(g)$. The conclusion concerns the prescribed
tensor $T$, not the construction of a tensor from an arbitrary large
Gowers norm. Full symmetry includes the final frequency-evaluation slot.

\subsection{The quantitative separation behind the theorem}
For $d\ge3$, the repeated-variable defect is
\begin{equation}
 \Phi_T(z_1,\ldots,z_{d-3})(a,b)
 =T(a,a,b,z_1,\ldots,z_{d-3})
   +T(a,b,b,z_1,\ldots,z_{d-3}).
 \label{gsr:fm:65:bsi:eq:defect}
\end{equation}
For $d=3$ denote this alternating bilinear form by $\Omega_T$.
For $d\ge4$ define
\begin{equation}
 K_T=\{z\in V:\Phi_T(z,z_2,\ldots,z_{d-3})=0
                   \text{ for every }z_2,\ldots,z_{d-3}\},
 \qquad r(T)=\codim K_T.
 \label{gsr:fm:65:bsi:eq:radical}
\end{equation}
When $d=4$ there are no remaining frozen variables. The zero on the
right means the zero alternating form in $a,b$.

\begin{theorem}[Radical-sensitive cap and strict noncanonical gap]
\label{gsr:fm:65:bsi:thm:gap}
Let $d\ge4$ and $T\in\Sym^d(V)$ be nonintegrable. If $r(T)=1$, then $T$
is canonical modulo integration and $\M(T)=b_d$. If $r(T)\ge2$, then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\quad
 \M(T)\le 1-(1-2^{-r(T)})\frac{d}{2^{d-1}}
 \le 1-\frac{3d}{2^{d+1}}
 =b_d-\frac{d-2}{2^{d+1}}.
 \quad}\label{gsr:fm:65:bsi:eq:gap}
\end{equation}
For $d=3$, the exact formula is
$\M(T)=2^{-\rk\Omega_T/2}$; the noncanonical cap is $1/4$.
\end{theorem}
The bound in \eqref{gsr:fm:65:bsi:eq:gap} is \emph{not} asserted to be the optimal
second extremal value. Its strict separation from $b_d$ is enough to
classify all endpoint tensors.

\subsection{The project question that is closed}
The manuscript \emph{Exact Boolean Obstruction Energies}~\cite{repo65boe}
proved the canonical-family formula $\M(C_d)=b_d$ in every degree, but
its universal argument gave only
\[
 b_d\le \max_{T\notin\I_d(V)}\M(T)
       \le1-\frac{\min\{d+1,7\}}{2^d}.
\]
Its Research Questions~1 and~2 asked for the septic value and the universal
all-degree value. Its Research Question~4 also asked for the quintic and
sextic endpoint tensors and functions. Theorem~\ref{gsr:fm:65:bsi:thm:main} answers
the first two questions and the \emph{tensor} part of the fourth, in fact
in every degree. Classification of all maximizing functions remains a
different question.

\begin{tabular}{@{}ccccc@{}}
\toprule
Degree & Prior universal cap & Sharp value here & Noncanonical cap here & Gap below sharp value\\
\midrule
$3$ & $1/2$ & $1/2$ & $1/4$ & $1/4$\\
$4$ & $11/16$ & $11/16$ & $5/8$ & $1/16$\\
$5$ & $13/16$ & $13/16$ & $49/64$ & $3/64$\\
$6$ & $57/64$ & $57/64$ & $55/64$ & $1/32$\\
$7$ & $121/128$ & $15/16$ & $235/256$ & $5/256$\\
$8$ & $249/256$ & $247/256$ & $61/64$ & $3/256$\\

The all-degree gain over the preceding universal cap is $(d-6)/2^d$ for
$d\ge7$. More significantly, there is now a complete extremal theorem
rather than a sequence of isolated low-degree support estimates.

\subsection{What is an existing ingredient and what changes}
The Boolean nonclassical integration criterion is established
background~\cite[Definition~3.1 and Proposition~3.5]{tidor}.
The cubic spectral law, the shear argument, and the canonical-family
formula were developed in the preceding project drafts~\cite{repo65bpi,repo65boe}.
We reprove exactly the pieces needed, so the new conclusions do not depend
on accepting an unchecked earlier proof.

The new step is to count \emph{integrable contractions}, not merely the
support of $\Phi_T$. Their set is exactly $K_T$. Radical codimension one
is the already understood canonical case; radical codimension at least
two leaves at least three quarters of the slices nonintegrable. The
sharp theorem in degree $d-1$ therefore supplies a stronger estimate than
a degree-independent support bound. This also gives the endpoint
classification, its finite rigidity window, and the reconstruction and
counting consequences below.
