\section[{Source 66: Scope, previous results, and principal contributions}]{Source 66. Scope, previous results, and principal contributions}\label{gsr:fm:66:sec:d1}
\srcnote{66}{Section 1}
\partsource{\textbf{Added in the eleventh write, 7~October 2026.} \textbf{Delivered title block.} ``Partition Normal Forms for Small Schur Defect / Sharp endpoint bounds and the first four additive-energy levels / A local strengthening of the ordered-energy step in Gowers's proof / Research manuscript prepared with ChatGPT for Vladimir Reshetnikov / 6 October 2026''; \emph{the PDF author field reads the same}. Archive \file{Gowers\_Endpoint\_Partitions.zip} (arrival \texttt{0281fcb05}), manuscript \file{article.tex} (1,637 lines, 24 pages); \emph{no pin}: its \file{SOURCES.md}, shipped as \file{66-endpoint-partitions-SOURCES.md}, records three blobs as ``audit anchors'' (the transcription, this directory's README and source~45's energy review) and says that ``no uniform snapshot of the whole repository is claimed''. Printed below: the abstract, its keywords and Section~1; Sections~2--11 stand in the Part~II chapter on the energy levels after source~68 (Section~\ref{gsr:en:sec:energygap}), Sections~12--14 and Appendices~A--C are in Part~V. Its macros \texttt{\textbackslash E} (roman $\mathrm E$, the additive energy, not this report's expectation $\mathbb E$), \texttt{\textbackslash D} (roman $\mathrm D$, the energy defect, not this report's $\Delta$), \texttt{\textbackslash ep} (roman $\mathrm e$, the endpoint defect), \texttt{\textbackslash card} ($\lvert\cdot\rvert$, not this report's operator) and \texttt{\textbackslash wt} (``wt'', not this report's ``wid'') are set as \texttt{\textbackslash Erm}, \texttt{\textbackslash Drm}, this report's \texttt{\textbackslash e} (the same definition), \texttt{\textbackslash cardbars} and \texttt{\textbackslash wtop}; its `question' and `conjecture' environments (on the shared counter) are set as this report's `Question' and a `Conjecture' environment added here; its delivered \file{data/partition\_spectrum.csv} has CRLF line ends and is shipped byte for byte.}
\begin{partabstract}{66}
For a finite real set $A$ of size $m$, write
$\Erm(A)=\cardbars{\{(a,b,c,d)\in A^4:a+b=c+d\}}$ and
$M_m=(2m^3+m)/3$.  Gowers's Section~7 recalls the sharp inequality
$\Erm(A)\le M_m$, with arithmetic progressions as the equality cases.
We refine this endpoint through a classification of small Schur defects.
If $0<c_1<\cdots<c_n$ and at most $r$ of the differences $c_i-c_j$
with $j<i$ are absent from the set, then, for $n\ge3r+1$, there is a
$d>0$ such that $c_i=d(i+\lambda_i)$, where the $\lambda_i$ are
nonnegative, nondecreasing integers and their sum is exactly the defect.
Consequently, defect $r$ has precisely $p(r)$ positive-dilation classes.
Reflection gives partition-indexed, bounded-hole normal forms for endpoint
extensions of ordered sets.  Their full energy is an explicit affine
function of $m$, and the sharp conditional bound is
$\Erm(A)\le M_m-4r(m-1-r)$ when the last endpoint has defect $r$ and
$m-1\ge3r+1$.  Equality forces a single hole at position $r$.
Using the cases $r\le3$, we classify all third-level extremizers for
$m\ge8$ and all fourth-level extremizers for $m\ge11$.  In particular,
the first four energy levels for $m\ge11$ consist of eight oriented
arithmetic templates.  Every set in these levels lies in an $(m+2)$-term
progression and contains an $(m-2)$-term progression.  The energy
classifications extend to torsion-free abelian groups.  All general
statements have elementary written proofs; exact finite checks accompany
the article.  Publication priority is not established, and no improved
global bound for Szemer\'edi's theorem is claimed.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small
\noindent\textbf{Keywords.} Additive energy; Schur triples; inverse theorems;
arithmetic progressions; integer partitions; Gowers's proof.
\end{quote}
\label{gsr:fm:66:epnf:sec:introduction}

\subsection{The precise interface with Gowers's argument}
Immediately before Theorem~7.2 of \cite{gowers}, Gowers considers the
invariant
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:66:epnf:eq:energydef}
 \Erm(A)=\sum_t\cardbars{A\cap(A+t)}^2
      =\cardbars{\set{(a,b,c,d)\in A^4:a+b=c+d}}.
\end{equation}
For an $m$-element subset of the integers, the maximum is
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:66:epnf:eq:maximum}
 M_m=m^2+2\sum_{j=1}^{m-1}j^2=\frac{2m^3+m}{3},
\end{equation}
and equality characterizes arithmetic progressions.  The ensuing
Balog--Szemer\'edi statement and Proposition~7.3 extract a large structured
subset from a set with energy at least $c_0m^3$.  The graph furnished by
the preceding inverse step is one reason this energy invariant is useful.

Our subject is the fine structure very near the \emph{ordered} maximum
\eqref{gsr:fm:66:epnf:eq:maximum}.  We retain exact integer deficits instead of replacing
them by density parameters.  This is not the finite-subgroup endpoint
$m^3$: a torsion-free set has a different extremal geometry.  The results
below therefore apply directly to ordered sets and torsion-free lifts,
not automatically to an arbitrary subset of a finite cyclic group.

\subsection{What is prior, and what is added here}
The repository's source-45 energy proof review \cite{repo66levels} records the
ordered-defect identity, an elementary proof of the first energy gap,
the complete second-level classification, a unit-Schur-defect lemma,
and the sharp third-level exclusion bound.  Those facts are credited and
reproved here so that the new arguments have no dependency on an
unverified repository theorem.  The first gap is also implicit in the
published equality theory for Pollard's inequality
\cite{pollardequality}; it is not presented as a new inequality.

The additions developed in this article are the all-$r$ partition normal
form, its exact boundary-hole energy law and sharp conditional envelope,
and the complete third- and fourth-level equality analyses.  The latter
are refinements of the third-level bound recorded in \cite{repo66levels}, not
merely new examples attaining that bound.  We also give a full-set
inverse conclusion and an affine graph consequence in the corresponding
energy window.

A bounded literature search and a reading of the relevant repository
materials do not establish publication priority.  In particular, the
absence of a matching statement in the sources inspected is not evidence
that no equivalent theorem exists elsewhere.  The mathematical claims
are the explicitly stated theorems and their proofs; claims of priority
are deliberately more limited.  The manuscript is AI-assisted,
unrefereed, and not proof-assistant verified.  The included program
checks finite instances only.

\subsection{Main statements in one place}
Throughout, $\intr{u}{v}=\{u,u+1,\ldots,v\}$ for integers $u\le v$.
An oriented affine copy means $b+dS$ with $d>0$.  Keeping the orientation
is necessary when discussing the \emph{last} endpoint.

For a positive ordered set $C=\{c_1<\cdots<c_n\}$, define
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:66:epnf:eq:schurdef}
 \sigma(C)=\#\{(i,j):1\le j<i\le n,\ c_i-c_j\notin C\}.
\end{equation}
Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:66:epnf:thm:partition} proves that, when $n\ge3r+1$ and
$\sigma(C)\le r$,
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:66:epnf:eq:mainnormalform}
 c_i=d(i+\lambda_i),\qquad
 0\le\lambda_1\le\cdots\le\lambda_n,\qquad
 \lambda_i\in\Z,\qquad \sum_i\lambda_i=\sigma(C).
\end{equation}
For exact defect $r$, the positive entries form an integer partition of
$r$.  Thus there are exactly $p(r)$ possibilities up to positive dilation,
independently of $n$ in this range.

For $A=B\cup\{a\}$ with $a>\max B$, the \emph{endpoint defect} is
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:66:epnf:eq:endpointdef}
 \e(B,a)=\#\{(z,x)\in B^2:z<x,\ a-x+z\notin B\}.
\end{equation}
This is not the total energy defect.  Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:66:epnf:thm:envelope} proves
that, if $|A|=m$, $\e(B,a)=r\ge1$, and $m-1\ge3r+1$, then
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:66:epnf:eq:intro-envelop}
 \Erm(A)\le M_m-4r(m-1-r).
\end{equation}
Equality holds precisely for an oriented affine copy of
$\intr{0}{m}\setminus\{r\}$.  A stronger statement classifies every
possible $A$ under the endpoint hypothesis, not only equality.

Finally, Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:66:epnf:thm:fourlevels} gives the four largest distinct
values of $\Erm(A)$, for $m\ge11$:
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:66:epnf:eq:fourvalues}
 M_m,\qquad M_m-4(m-2),\qquad M_m-8(m-3),\qquad M_m-8m+20.
\end{equation}
Their equality cases are respectively one, two, three, and two oriented
arithmetic templates.  In particular,
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:66:epnf:eq:introinverse}
 \Erm(A)\ge M_m-8m+20
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 A\text{ lies in an $(m+2)$-term arithmetic progression}.
\end{equation}
The same hypothesis produces an $(m-2)$-term progression inside $A$.
It is a much stronger conclusion than a positive-fraction extraction,
but it requires a correspondingly much stronger hypothesis.

\section[{Source 67: Research position and the exact improvements}]{Source 67. Research position and the exact improvements}\label{gsr:fm:67:sec:d1}
\srcnote{67}{Section 1}
\partsource{\textbf{Added in the eleventh write, 7~October 2026.} \textbf{Delivered title block.} ``Exact Local Profiles and Structural Barriers in Gowers' Szemer\'edi Framework / Unequal Fourier budgets, characteristic-three rigidity, optimal interpolation lists, and norm layers without a degree cap / Research manuscript prepared with ChatGPT for Vladimir Reshetnikov and the ProveIt Ramsey project / 7 October 2026''; \emph{the PDF author field reads ``Research manuscript prepared with ChatGPT for Vladimir Reshetnikov''}. Archive \file{Gowers\_Exact\_Local\_Profiles\_TeX\_and\_PDF.zip} (arrival \texttt{0281fcb05}), manuscript \file{gowers\_exact\_local\_profiles.tex} (3,295 lines, 44 pages), the single-file assembly of its front matter, four section files and end matter by its \file{code/assemble.py} (shipped as \file{code/67-exact-profiles-assemble.py}; the assembly was reproduced byte for byte at the write); \emph{no pin}: its \file{SOURCE\_LEDGER.json}, shipped as \file{data/67-exact-profiles-SOURCE\_LEDGER.json}, identifies its inputs by blob and SHA-256 and says that moving-branch paths ``are not asserted to be immutable commit snapshots''. It defines no macros; its `question' environment (``Question'', on the shared counter) is set in this report's `Question' style; its two figures are shipped as \file{figures/67-exact-profiles-fourier\_curvature.pdf} and \file{figures/67-exact-profiles-rigidity\_profile.pdf}. The comments of its assembly inside sections are kept; those marking the joins between section files are dropped with the section breaks.}
\begin{partabstract}{67}
We develop four sets of exact refinements of local problems arising in
Gowers' proof of Szemer\'edi's theorem and in the existing ProveIt research
series. First, a supported moment problem gives an exact matrix formula
for missing-arc mass under unequal Fourier budgets, on an explicitly
certified region containing neighbourhoods of every interior point of
the known equal-budget branch. We determine the entire optimality
polytope of the old certificate, the rank of the value Hessian, and a
quadratic aligned-grid error bound. Second, for maps from any finite
abelian group to an elementary abelian $3$-group, the cubic affine-error
profile holds throughout its positive range, with explicit color and
target-rank remainders and a complete equality classification. The exact
universal strict thresholds for unique affine recovery are $1/4$ for
arbitrary domains and $4/9$ for elementary abelian $3$-domains.
The exact non-affine energy maximum in this target class has the
optimal domain-size cutoff $N\ge13$. Third,
the interpolation cost at Gowers' Lemma~16.10 is reduced to the elementary
symmetric polynomial of the anchor list sizes, and matching dense
examples prove this cost optimal for the stated local interface, even
with controlled deletion. Fourth, sums of independent field-norm blocks
are classified without any degree cap in characteristic $p>2m$:
for progression lengths $2m=4,6,8$, or for general length $2m$
over sufficiently large fields,
their exact maximum source dimension is $rm^2$ for $r$ output coordinates.
The small-field eight-term case is closed by eleven explicit
irreducibility certificates. Proofs, equality cases, quantitative bounds,
reproducible checks, source comparisons, and a research programme are
included. These are local theorems and structural obstructions; no
improved global Szemer\'edi bound or solution of the unrestricted
quintic-colouring problem is claimed.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small
\noindent\textbf{Keywords.} Additive energy; Fourier moments; affine
recovery; Gowers norms; polynomial interpolation; finite-field norms;
symmetrically coloured arithmetic progressions.
\end{quote}
\label{gsr:fm:67:sec:introduction}

Gowers' proof turns information about arithmetic progressions into
successive statements about Fourier coefficients, derivatives,
approximately additive graphs, polynomial behaviour on structured
sets, and density increments \cite{gowers}. Each passage has its own
extremal problem. A local constant can be sharpened only after one
identifies which information is retained by that passage and what the
next passage actually needs. Conversely, a sharp local obstruction
can identify information that an improved argument must recover.

The ProveIt Ramsey collection already contains a substantial sequence
of refinements of this framework \cite{repo67}. We take that
work as a baseline. In particular, the common-budget Fourier profile,
the cubic $4t-10t^2+6t^3$, the shared-anchor sampling improvement, and the
low-degree layered norm construction are established inputs, not
discoveries of this article. The contribution is to solve several
remaining extremal problems attached to those inputs, and to push
others to precise finite obstructions.

The word ``exact'' is used with a specified scope throughout. An exact
Fourier formula is asserted on a stated matrix-certificate region.
An exact interpolation cost is relative to explicitly given slice-list
and fibre hypotheses. An exact dimension classification is for sums of
independent norm blocks. A universal recovery threshold refers to the
particular four-point graph-energy test and the named class of groups.
These scopes are part of the theorems.

\subsection{Four results and their relation to the baseline}

\paragraph{A. Unequal Fourier budgets and their curvature.}
For probability measures on the circle, fix an open arc
$I_a=\{\theta:|\theta|_\circ<a\}$ and bounds
$|\widehat\mu(j)|\le\varepsilon_j$, $1\le j\le R$.
Let $V_{R,a}(\boldsymbol\varepsilon)$ be the least possible mass of
$I_a$. Source~37 obtains the exact common-budget answer in the window
\[
 \frac{\pi}{R+1}<a<\frac{2\pi}{R+1},\qquad a<\pi,
 \qquad
 V_{R,a}(e,\ldots,e)=\frac{\rho-e}{1+\rho},
\]
where
\[
 \rho=
 \left(R-\cot(a/2)\tan((R+1)a/2)\right)^{-1}
 \quad\text{and}\quad 0\le e\le\rho
 \qquad\text{\cite{repo67missing}}.
\]
The equal-budget certificate alone gives only a linear lower bound
after the budgets separate. We prove that the actual optimum is
\[
 V_{R,a}(\boldsymbol\varepsilon)
 =-\frac{1}{(1-\cos a)\,\mathbf e^T
       L(\boldsymbol\varepsilon)^{-1}\mathbf e}
\]
under finitely checkable strict hypotheses, where $L$ is an $R$-by-$R$
localizing matrix and $\mathbf e$ is the all-ones vector
(Theorem~\ref{gsr:dt:67:fourier:matrix}). The hypotheses hold on an open
neighbourhood of every $0<e<\rho$ on the equal-budget line.

The old certificate remains optimal on an explicitly described
polytope of local dimension $\lfloor R/2\rfloor+1$. At every point
of the strict matrix region, the Hessian of the actual value has
rank $\lfloor(R-1)/2\rfloor$. Thus for $R\ge3$ unequal perturbations
usually require a moving certificate. The rational three-frequency
example in Corollary~\ref{gsr:dt:67:fourier:example} exhibits the exact positive
quadratic gain. Theorem~\ref{gsr:dt:67:fourier:grid} also improves the elementary
grid approximation to order $N^{-2}$ when the endpoints are aligned;
it separately retains the order-$N^{-1}$ endpoint drift.

\paragraph{B. The full positive cubic range in characteristic three.}
For $f:G\to W$, where $G$ is finite abelian of size $N$ and $W$ is an
elementary abelian $3$-group, write
\[
 \mathcal E(f)=\#\{x_1+x_2=x_3+x_4:
       f(x_1)+f(x_2)=f(x_3)+f(x_4)\},
 \qquad \varepsilon=1-\mathcal E(f)/N^3.
\]
For any affine reference $\ell$, let
$t=N^{-1}|\{x:f(x)\ne\ell(x)\}|$ and
$\Psi(t)=4t-10t^2+6t^3$. Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:67:cthree:local} proves
\[
 \varepsilon\ge\Psi(t)\qquad(0\le t\le2/3)
\]
with a positive remainder measuring multiple error colors and
target rank. For $0<t<2/3$, equality holds exactly when
$f-\ell$ is one nonzero constant on a subgroup coset and zero
elsewhere. The endpoint $t=2/3$ has a different, fully described
affine equality family. The common cubic and the one-color coset
examples occur in the previous reports; the enlarged range and
the new projection-sensitive remainder are proved here
\cite{repo67affine,repo67charaffine}.

This local theorem combines with a Fourier argument to give unique
nearest-affine recovery whenever $\varepsilon<1/4$ on arbitrary
finite abelian domains, or whenever $\varepsilon<4/9$ on elementary
abelian $3$-domains (Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:67:cthree:global}). Both thresholds
are best possible as universal strict thresholds: explicit maps
at their endpoints have multiple nearest affine maps. Below either
threshold the distance is at most the inverse of the increasing
small branch of $\Psi$. These conclusions are specific to the
four-point test above. They are not statements about the identical
threshold for every version of a three-query homomorphism test.

A further consequence is the exact non-affine maximum
\[
 \mathcal E(f)\le N^3-4N^2+10N-6\qquad(N\ge13),
\]
with equality precisely for one-point modifications of affine
maps (Corollary~\ref{gsr:en:67:cthree:nonaffine-gap}). The cutoff thirteen
is optimal: a parity-class example at $N=12$ exceeds the displayed
value. The last order requires a separate exact ternary
quantization bound for thirteen character phases.

\paragraph{C. The exact interpolation list cost.}
Suppose an anchor $a_i$ has a list of $L_i$ base functions, while
the fibre classes have degree less than $t$. A point is certified
when it is sampled or its class contains $t$ anchors. Source~39
uses
\[
 \sum_iL_i+E_t(L_1,\ldots,L_r),\qquad
 E_t(L_1,\ldots,L_r)=\sum_{|I|=t}\prod_{i\in I}L_i
 \qquad\text{\cite{repo67anchor}}.
\]
We remove the first term: the ordinary $t$-anchor interpolants also
cover every sampled point. The answer is exactly $E_t$ in the
universal fixed-cell interface, with a separate complete formula
when fewer than $t$ lists are nonempty. In particular, for
$r\ge2$ and $L\ge1$, the affine case improves
$rL+\binom r2L^2$ to $\binom r2L^2$.

The exactness is not inferred from the upper count. We construct
dense examples with one polynomial class per fibre that force all
$E_t$ candidates, even if the competing candidates have an arbitrary
fixed degree in the base variable. For $M$ candidates we give a
product lower bound on the uncovered mass. This implies the
asymptotically sharp lower bound $M\ge(1-\delta-o(1))E_t$ when
a fraction $\delta$ may be deleted, with integer rounding in the
matching construction, and a cell-count/list-size tradeoff.
The construction also shows exactly why a further compression
must use information beyond this local interface.

\paragraph{D. Independent norm layers with no degree cap.}
Let $q$ have characteristic $p>2m$. Consider
\[
 C(x_1,\ldots,x_s)=c+\sum_{j=1}^s v_j
      N_{\mathbb F_{q^{d_j}}/\mathbb F_q}(x_j),
 \qquad v_j\in\mathbb F_q^r,
\]
on the full direct product of its norm blocks. For $m=2,3,4$,
and for all $m\ge2$ when $q\ge(2m-1)^2$, the map avoids all
nontrivial symmetrically coloured $2m$-term progressions if and
only if every $d_j$ is odd and less than $2m$, and the coefficient
vectors of each fixed degree are linearly independent
(Theorem~\ref{gsr:cc:67:norm:classification}). The exact maximum dimension
is therefore $rm^2$, without assuming any degree bound in advance.

The low-degree extremizing construction is due to Shi and Dong
\cite{shidong}, and the repository already proves related
degree-capped optimality statements \cite{repo67norm}.
The new part excludes every higher norm degree. Character sums
give quantitative progression counts; exact positivity handles
lengths four and six, and eleven explicit degree-nine
irreducibility certificates handle the remaining eight-term fields.
For general $m$, only degree $2m+1$ over finitely many small prime
fields remains outside the classification.

\subsection{What is closed, and what remains open}

\begin{longtable}{@{}L{0.27\textwidth}L{0.66\textwidth}@{}}
\toprule
Problem in the preceding work & Resolution and precise boundary \\
\midrule
\endfirsthead
\toprule
Problem in the preceding work & Resolution and precise boundary \\
\midrule
\endhead
Unequal Fourier budgets near the common-budget branch
& Exact formula, unique extremizer, fixed-certificate polytope,
and Hessian rank. Farther phase regions remain open. \\
\addlinespace
Range of the cubic affine-error profile
& Entire positive range for exponent-three targets, with equality
and stability. General odd-order targets remain a separate problem. \\
\addlinespace
Universal ternary affine-recovery thresholds
& Sharp strict thresholds $1/4$ and $4/9$ for the two specified
domain classes. An exact envelope for every attainable defect is
not asserted. \\
\addlinespace
Generic interpolation compression and lower bounds
& Exact local cost, dense matching examples, and deletion/partition
tradeoffs. Additional product-property information may still compress
the lists. \\
\addlinespace
Whether higher independent norm layers can improve the construction
& Complete negative answer for lengths $4,6,8$ and the stated
large-field regime; an exact classification of all such layers. \\
\addlinespace
Unrestricted scalar quintics for four-term symmetry
& Still open. Interacting polynomial terms fall outside the
independent norm-block theorem. \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

The distinction between a local theorem and a complete quantitative
Szemer\'edi theorem matters. An improvement at one step must survive
all subsequent losses, with compatible hypotheses at every scale,
before it implies a new bound for the largest progression-free set
$r_k(N)$. For comparison, Leng, Sah, and Sawhney prove a global
bound of the form
$r_k(N)\ll_k N\exp(-(\log\log N)^{c_k})$ for $k\ge5$
and a positive $c_k$ \cite{lssbounds}. No result of that form is
derived in this article. The contributions here are exact local
theorems, equality classifications, and barriers that can be
inserted into a further quantitative analysis.

\subsection{Attribution, proof status, and organization}

The main historical inputs are Gowers' proof, the specified ProveIt
reports, the supported Toeplitz moment criterion of Yang--Xie,
elementary finite Fourier analysis, Lagrange interpolation, and
the multiplicative Weil bound \cite{gowers,repo67,yangxie,weilsums,lidlniederreiter}. General stability of nearly
extremal uniformity norms has a substantial prior literature;
Eisner--Tao is one relevant reference \cite{eisnertao}. We do not
present near-extremizer stability itself as a new concept.
Recent work of Mittal--Roy develops much broader low-soundness
homomorphism tests using group-dependent query distributions
\cite{mittalroy}. Our thresholds concern the fixed uniform
four-point graph-energy test, with explicit ternary equality cases.

The contribution statements are relative to a recorded repository
and working-manuscript baseline. A targeted primary-source and
repository audit was undertaken, including the more recent
character/affine and bilinear-extraction manuscripts. It does not
establish exhaustive historical priority for every corollary.
The supplied source ledger records the inspected inputs without
silently identifying a moving branch with an immutable snapshot.

Every asserted theorem has a proof below. The general results do
not rest on random experiments. There is one explicit finite
certificate component: the eleven irreducibility checks in the
small-field eight-term norm argument. Their criterion, polynomials,
and exact verifier are provided. Other exhaustive checks and
numerical diagnostics serve to test calculations, endpoint cases,
and normalizations. The manuscript received independent internal
proof reviews during its preparation; it has not been externally
refereed or formally verified in Lean.

Sections~\ref{gsr:dt:67:fourier:section}--\ref{gsr:cc:67:norm:section} contain the four
research developments. Section~\ref{gsr:fz:67:sec:research} proposes further
questions with explicit targets and obstructions.
Section~\ref{gsr:fz:67:sec:reproducibility} describes the verification package
and a practical route to repository integration and formalization.
The sections use local notation; in particular the letter $R$ in
the Fourier section and $r$ in the interpolation or norm sections
refer to different parameters.

\section[{Source 68: Introduction and contribution map}]{Source 68. Introduction and contribution map}\label{gsr:fm:68:sec:d1}
\srcnote{68}{Section 1}
\partsource{\textbf{Added in the eleventh write, 7~October 2026.} \textbf{Delivered title block.} ``Sharp energy gaps and efficient restriction / Coset rigidity, puncture stability, and Fourier-filter bounds in Gowers' Szemer\'edi framework / Research contribution prepared for Vladimir Reshetnikov / ProveIt / Combinatorics / Ramsey / Mathematical derivation and manuscript assisted by OpenAI ChatGPT / 7 October 2026''; \emph{the PDF author field reads ``Research contribution prepared for Vladimir Reshetnikov with ChatGPT''}. \begin{partabstract}{68}
We prove several local strengthenings of the additive-energy and
restriction machinery surrounding Gowers' proof of Szemer\'edi's
theorem. For a finite set $A$ of size $m$ in any abelian group, with
energy defect $\eps=1-E(A)/m^3$, we establish the sharp universal
inequality
$m\,r_A(d)(m-r_A(d))\le m^3-E(A)$.
An exact nonnegative remainder gives a mixed-set extension, a bounded
weight version using minimum overlap, all one-translation equality
cases, and a multilevel bound from the attained overlap spectrum.
These yield a canonical subgroup and the sharp coset-distance
envelope $|A\symdiff C|/m\le(1-\sqrt{1-4\eps})/2$ throughout
$\eps\le1/4$. The threshold $1/4$ is optimal even in finite cyclic
groups; uniqueness of the closest coset has the distinct sharp
threshold $2/9$.
We also prove an exact nested-puncture repair profile with outer defect
below $1/4$ and inner defect at most $1/4$, classify its equality cases, and obtain an
oriented repair theorem from one nearly saturated translation.

For Gowers' sixteen-variable restriction step, a degree-twelve rational
filter with exact integer certificates improves the all-cyclic common
exponent from the repository's $54$ to $53$, with an explicit size
hypothesis and arbitrary abelian targets.
Finally, a circle rearrangement estimate and finite approximations to
theta filters give bounds uniform in arity $m$ and discrepancy order
$a$. In particular the optimal principal-spectrum cost divided by $m$
tends to $1+1/(2c)$ when $a=m^{c+o(1)}$.
The manuscript supplies full proofs, sharp examples, reproducible
certificates, a pinned source comparison, and a further research
programme. Its claims concern the stated local theorems and method
cost; no improved global bound for Szemer\'edi's theorem or
literature-wide priority claim is made.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small
\noindent\textbf{Keywords.}
Additive energy; stability; finite abelian groups; punctured cosets;
Fourier restriction; Riesz--Sobolev inequality; Szemer\'edi's theorem.
\end{quote}
\label{gsr:fm:68:sec:introduction}

Gowers' proof of Szemer\'edi's theorem uses quantitative relations
between additive configurations, approximate algebraic structure, and
restriction of a map to a more additive domain \cite{gowers}.
Two local questions are especially amenable to sharp analysis.
First, if a set has nearly the largest possible additive energy, how
precisely is its structure forced, and what do almost sharp
inequalities say about the missing points?
Second, how efficiently can a random Fourier filter suppress
unrespected additive relations while retaining respected ones?
This article advances both questions and relates its conclusions to
the existing ProveIt research sequence.

The first part is elementary finite additive combinatorics. Its basic
identity keeps the remainder of a union--intersection transformation
instead of discarding it. A single overlap gives a sharp quadratic
gap; two overlap levels give a larger structural range. The resulting
coset theorem has an optimal existence threshold and a different
optimal uniqueness threshold. A second exact identity then reads the
energy of the missing set inside the canonical coset, giving a nested
repair theorem with a sharp nonlinear profile.

The second part keeps Gowers' random-restriction architecture and the
repository's all-cyclic expectation theorem. We improve its explicit
filter, and then study the extremal principal cost when both the
number of variables and the order of a failed target relation vary.
The finite coefficient improvement and the asymptotic theorem are
separate results: their proofs use different filters.

\subsection{Main statements in compact form}

For a nonempty finite $A\subset G$, let $m=|A|$,
$r_A(d)=|A\cap(A+d)|$, and $\eps=1-E(A)/m^3$.
Write $\tau(u)=(1-\sqrt{1-4u})/2$.
The first group of results is as follows.
\begin{enumerate}
 \item \textbf{Universal gap and spectrum refinement.}
 For every translation $d$,
 \[
  \frac{r_A(d)}m\left(1-\frac{r_A(d)}m\right)\le\eps.
 \]
 More generally, if $g_1,\ldots,g_\ell$ are the successive gaps
 between selected attained overlap values, together with $0$ and $m$,
 then
 \[
  E(A)\le\frac{2m^3+\sum_i g_i^3}{3}.
 \]
 Theorems~\ref{gsr:en:68:thm:pointwise} and \ref{gsr:en:68:thm:multilevel} prove these
 bounds. Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:68:thm:pointwise-equality} classifies all equality
 cases of the one-translation bound; Proposition~\ref{gsr:en:68:prop:weighted}
 supplies the minimum-overlap weighted extension.

 \item \textbf{Coset existence and uniqueness.}
 If $\eps\le1/4$, then
 $H=\{d:r_A(d)>m/2\}$ is a subgroup, and a most occupied $H$-coset
 $C$ satisfies $|A\symdiff C|\le\tau(\eps)m$.
 The threshold is optimal, including in cyclic groups.
 For $\eps<2/9$, $C$ is the unique closest subgroup coset; the
 threshold $2/9$ is also optimal.
 See Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:68:thm:coset}, Corollary~\ref{gsr:en:68:cor:unique}, and
 Proposition~\ref{gsr:en:68:prop:threshold-sharp}.

 \item \textbf{Nested and oriented repair.}
 For $\eps<1/4$, use the canonical $C$ and put
 $\delta=|A\symdiff C|/m>0$,
 $\eta=\eps-\delta(1-\delta)$.
 If $s=\eta/\delta^3\le1/4$, then
 \[
  \min_{D\subsetneq C}
    \frac{|A\symdiff(C\setminus D)|}{m}
  \le\delta\tau(s),
 \]
 with $D$ a nonempty subgroup coset.
 The analogous bound with $\eta$ replaced by
 $\theta_d=\eps-q(d)(1-q(d))$ forces $d\in H$ and allows a minimizing
 hole whose subgroup excludes $d$.
 Theorems~\ref{gsr:en:68:thm:puncture}--\ref{gsr:en:68:thm:oriented-puncture} and
 Proposition~\ref{gsr:en:68:prop:puncture-endpoint} include equality,
 endpoint, and uniqueness statements with their exact ranges.
\end{enumerate}

For restriction, let $B$ be a finite subset of a cyclic group,
$b=|B|$, and $\phi:B\to F$ a map to an arbitrary abelian group.
Let $T_{16}$ count ordered tuples satisfying
$x_1+\cdots+x_8=x_9+\cdots+x_{16}$ and $G_{16}$ count those also
respected by $\phi$. Repetitions are included.
If $G_{16}(B,\phi)\ge\alpha b^{15}$, $0<\alpha,\eta\le1$, and
\[
 b\ge\left(\frac4{\alpha\eta}\right)^{53},
\]
Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:68:ff:thm:53} gives one subset $B'\subset B$ with
\[
 T_{16}(B')\ge\left(\frac{\alpha\eta}{4}\right)^{53}b^{15},
 \qquad
 G_{16}(B',\phi)\ge(1-\eta)T_{16}(B').
\]
Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:68:rf:thm:expectation} records and proves the predecessor
expectation estimate used here. The change is a fully specified
rational filter and the resulting stronger certified constants.

For the asymptotic question, let $\cI_{m,a}$ be the infimum of
$-\log P_m/\log(P_m/Q_{m,a})$ over finite even trigonometric
polynomials $0\le K\le1$, $K(0)=1$, with nonnegative Fourier
coefficients $c_n$, where
$P_m=\sum_n c_n^m$ and $Q_{m,a}=\sum_{a\mid n}c_n^m$.
Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:68:uf:thm:uniform} proves, for every $m,a\ge2$,
\begin{align*}
 \cI_{m,a}&\ge
 \max\left\{m-1,\ m-1+\frac{m(\log m-20)}{2\log a}\right\},\\
 \cI_{m,a}&\le
 m-1+
 \frac{m\left[\log m+\log\log(e+\log m/\log a)+4\right]}{2\log a}.
\end{align*}
In particular, if $a=m^{c+o(1)}$ with fixed $c>0$, then
$\cI_{m,a}/m\to1+1/(2c)$.
The additive term $m-1$, negligible in the fixed-order leading
asymptotic, becomes essential in this joint regime.

\subsection{Dependencies, interpretation, and limits}

The energy part uses elementary finite counting, convolution,
concavity, and subgroup arguments. The restriction part uses character
orthogonality, H\"older's inequality, and the already established
decaying-error selection theorem from source 58, reproved here.
The uniform cost lower bound additionally uses the classical
Riesz--Sobolev rearrangement inequality on the circle
\cite{christiliopoulou}; the convolution concentration consequence
needed here is derived explicitly.
Poisson summation and finite Fej\'er approximation supply the upper
bound.

These results refine specific parts of the Gowers framework.
The near-maximal energy regime is stronger than the general
large-energy hypothesis in the discussion preceding his Theorem 7.2.
The exponent-53 theorem directly strengthens the quantitative
conclusion of Lemma 9.3 under its displayed explicit size condition.
Prime-field restriction results already in sources 04 and 17 have
better retention powers in their own setting
\cite{repo68four,repo68seventeen}; the all-cyclic theorem is not a dominance
claim over those results.
The quantity $\cI_{m,a}$ measures only principal-spectrum cost.
It is not a lower bound on every possible subset-selection method,
nor on every analysis of the same random subsets.

The report makes a targeted comparison with the inspected project and
the cited primary analytic inputs. An exhaustive literature-priority
determination is outside that comparison. In particular, standard
union--intersection transformations, maximal-energy coset
characterizations, character orthogonality, and random Fourier
restriction are credited as established methods.
All new mathematical assertions are the explicit statements proved
below. No claim of a new global bound for progression-free sets or
Ramsey numbers, a resolved longstanding major conjecture, or a new
Lean kernel-checked theorem is made.

\srcnote{69}{Section 1}
\partsource{\textbf{Added in the eleventh write, 7~October 2026.} \textbf{Delivered title block.} ``Sharp All-Degree Boolean Phase Integration / Contraction radicals, extremal flags, and optimal finite-dimensional obstruction models / Research manuscript prepared with ChatGPT for Vladimir Reshetnikov and the ProveIt project / 6 October 2026''; \emph{the PDF author field reads ``Research manuscript prepared with ChatGPT for Vladimir Reshetnikov''}. Archive \file{ramsey\_boolean\_phase\_integration.zip} (arrival \texttt{0281fcb05}), manuscript \file{article.tex} (1,636 lines, 25 pages), pin \texttt{0d93c1eac} (its \file{SOURCES.md}, shipped as \file{69-obstruction-models-SOURCES.md}, records the blob of \file{Sections17\_18.lean} there). Printed below: the abstract, its scope statement and Section~1; Sections~2--9 stand in the Part~IV chapter on Boolean phase integration after source~65 (Section~\ref{gsr:fp:sec:alldegree}), Sections~10--14 and Appendix~A are in Part~V. Its macros \texttt{\textbackslash F} ($\mathbb F_2$) and \texttt{\textbackslash Torus} (the circle $\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$, not this report's $\mathbb T$) are set as this report's \texttt{\textbackslash Ftwo}, the same definition, and as \texttt{\textbackslash Tquot}; its `question' environment (``Research question'', numbered 1--10 on its own counter) is set in this report's `Research question' style, numbered within its section, which keeps the indices.}
\begin{partabstract}{69}
For a symmetric $d$-linear frequency tensor over $\mathbb F_2^n$, we determine
exactly how much selected derivative Fourier energy is compatible with failure
of nonclassical integration.  The maximum is $1-(d+1)/2^d$ for every $d\ge3$
and every $n\ge2$.  This resolves the degree-seven question and the entire
higher-degree gap left by the preceding project manuscript, whose universal
answer was exact only through degree six.  The new induction counts contractions
that remain nonintegrable, rather than individual nonzero values of the
repeated-variable defect.  For $d\ge4$ it also classifies all extremal tensor
classes: they are indexed by flags consisting of a line inside a plane in the
dual space, and are separated from all other nonintegrable classes by an explicit
positive energy gap.

A second theorem gives the exact minimal quotient dimension of a tensor modulo
integrable tensors.  If its contraction-integrability radical has codimension
$\rho$, this dimension is at most
$\rho+\sum_{j=1}^{\min(\rho,d-2)}\binom{\rho}{j}$.
An explicit construction attains this bound for every $d\ge4$ and $\rho\ge1$.
The proof uses an integrable diagonal-lowering operator and a complete defect
radical; it also gives a linear normal form for every prescribed radical.  We give exact phase-removal and noisy-selector corollaries, algorithms
for finite certificates, full proofs of the required background, and further
research questions.  Exact finite checks accompany the manuscript.
\end{partabstract}

\subsection{Selected derivative energy}
Let $V=\Ftwo^n$.  All averages in this manuscript are uniform normalized averages.
For $f:V\to\C$ and $P:V\to\Tquot$, set
\[
 \partial_h f(x)=f(x+h)\overline{f(x)},\qquad
 \Delta_hP(x)=P(x+h)-P(x),\qquad e(t)=\exp(2\pi it).
\]
A function is \emph{one-bounded} if $\norm f_\infty\le1$; it need not have
unit modulus and may vanish.  Unless explicitly stated otherwise, all energy
inequalities below concern one-bounded functions; exact algebraic identities
may be applied to arbitrary complex functions.  Write $\SM_d(V)$ for the vector space of
symmetric, genuinely $d$-linear maps $V^d\to\Ftwo$.  This notation refers to
multilinear maps, not to symmetric tensor coinvariants in characteristic two.

For $T\in\SM_d(V)$ define
\begin{equation}
 \En_T(f)=\E_{h_1,\ldots,h_{d-1}}
 \left|\E_x\partial_{h_1}\cdots\partial_{h_{d-1}}f(x)
           (-1)^{T(h_1,\ldots,h_{d-1},x)}\right|^2.
 \label{gsr:fm:69:bad:eq:energy}
\end{equation}
The last slot of $T$ evaluates the selected Fourier frequency.  In particular,
$0\le\En_T(f)\le1$ for a one-bounded function.  Let
\begin{equation}
 \Ma(T)=\max_{\norm f_\infty\le1}\En_T(f).
 \label{gsr:fm:69:bad:eq:maximum}
\end{equation}
The maximum exists because this is a continuous function on a finite product
of compact complex discs.

A circle-valued function $P$ has additive degree at most $d$ when all its
$(d+1)$-fold additive differences vanish.  Let $\In_d(V)$ be the space of
\emph{integrable} symmetric tensors: $T\in\In_d(V)$ when some such $P$ has
\begin{equation}
 \Delta_{h_1}\cdots\Delta_{h_d}P(x)=\frac{T(h_1,\ldots,h_d)}2\pmod1
 \quad\text{for every }x,h_1,\ldots,h_d.
 \label{gsr:fm:69:bad:eq:primitive}
\end{equation}
The notation $T/2$ embeds $\Ftwo$ as the two-torsion subgroup of $\Tquot$.
A primitive need not be an $\Ftwo$-valued polynomial.

\subsection{The exact universal threshold}
Set
\begin{equation}
 b_d=1-\frac{d+1}{2^d}.
 \label{gsr:fm:69:bad:eq:bd}
\end{equation}
For independent $u,v\in V^*$ define the canonical obstruction
\begin{equation}
 C_d^{u,v}(h_1,\ldots,h_d)
   =\sum_{i=1}^d v(h_i)\prod_{j\ne i}u(h_j).
 \label{gsr:fm:69:bad:eq:canonical}
\end{equation}

\begin{theorem}[All-degree threshold and extremal classification]
\label{gsr:fm:69:bad:thm:main}
For every $d\ge3$ and $n\ge2$,
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\displaystyle
 \max_{T\in\SM_d(V)\setminus\In_d(V)}\Ma(T)
       =1-\frac{d+1}{2^d}.}
 \label{gsr:fm:69:bad:eq:universal}
\end{equation}
For $d\ge4$, equality $\Ma(T)=b_d$ holds precisely for the tensors
\begin{equation}
 T=C_d^{u,v}+S,\qquad u,v\text{ independent},\quad S\in\In_d(V).
 \label{gsr:fm:69:bad:eq:extremal-form}
\end{equation}
Every other nonintegrable symmetric tensor satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \Ma(T)\le1-\frac{3d}{2^{d+1}}
          =b_d-\frac{d-2}{2^{d+1}}.
 \label{gsr:fm:69:bad:eq:separation}
\end{equation}
Consequently, energy strictly larger than $b_d$ certifies integrability.
\end{theorem}

\begin{writenote}[7 October 2026; sources 60--69]
\emph{Second route} (Section~\ref{gsr:fp:sec:alldegree}): source~65's Theorem~\ref{gsr:fm:65:bsi:thm:main} proves the same maximum, with the classification also at $d=3$ and the radical-sensitive cap; the two inductions are the same in substance (integrable contractions form the radical $R(T)$, source~65's $K_T$), written independently.
\end{writenote}
The gap in \eqref{gsr:fm:69:bad:eq:separation} is a proved uniform separation, not a claim
that the largest noncanonical energy always equals the displayed upper bound.
The theorem classifies extremal \emph{tensors modulo integrable tensors}; it
does not classify all extremizing functions.

\subsection{Optimal obstruction models}
For $d\ge3$ the repeated-variable defect is
\begin{equation}
 \Phi_T(z_1,\ldots,z_{d-3})(a,b)
 =T(a,a,b,z_1,\ldots,z_{d-3})+T(a,b,b,z_1,\ldots,z_{d-3}).
 \label{gsr:fm:69:bad:eq:defect}
\end{equation}
The frozen tuple is empty for $d=3$.  For $d\ge4$, define
\begin{align}
 R(T)&=\{z\in V:T_z\in\In_{d-1}(V)\},
 &T_z(h_1,\ldots,h_{d-1})&=T(z,h_1,\ldots,h_{d-1}),
 \label{gsr:fm:69:bad:eq:R}\\
 \rho(T)&=\codim_V R(T).
 \label{gsr:fm:69:bad:eq:rho}
\end{align}
The subspace $R(T)$ is the radical of $\Phi_T$ in any one frozen slot.  Thus
$\rho$ is a specific matrix-flattening rank.  It is not the dimension of the
span of the values of $\Phi_T$, an alternating rank, or a partition rank.

Let $\eff(T)$ be the smallest integer $m$ for which
\begin{equation}
 T=S+q^*T_0,\qquad S\in\In_d(V),\quad
 q:V\twoheadrightarrow\Ftwo^m,\quad T_0\in\SM_d(\Ftwo^m).
 \label{gsr:fm:69:bad:eq:model}
\end{equation}
This measures the number of coordinates needed by the obstruction, after
subtracting an integrable tensor.

\begin{theorem}[Sharp effective-dimension theorem]
\label{gsr:fm:69:bad:thm:model-intro}
For $d\ge4$, put
\begin{equation}
 K(T)=\{a\in R(T):\Phi_T(\zz)(a,b)=0
                      \text{ for every }\zz\in V^{d-3},\ b\in V\}.
 \label{gsr:fm:69:bad:eq:K}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\displaystyle
 \eff(T)=\codim_V K(T)
 \le B_d(\rho(T)),\qquad
 B_d(r)=r+\sum_{j=1}^{\min(r,d-2)}\binom rj.}
 \label{gsr:fm:69:bad:eq:model-bound}
\end{equation}
For each $d\ge4$ and $r\ge1$, there is a symmetric tensor on
$\Ftwo^{B_d(r)}$ with $\rho(T)=r$ and $K(T)=0$.  Thus the bound is sharp for
every pair of parameters.
\end{theorem}

\subsection{What is being improved}
Gowers's phase-removal step, especially Proposition~17.2 of
\cite{gowers}, motivates the passage from structured derivative frequencies
to polynomial phases.  Tidor's nonclassical integration theorem
\cite[Definition~3.1 and Proposition~3.5]{tidor} supplies the correct
small-characteristic notion of integrability.  These are established inputs,
not new claims of this manuscript.

The immediate comparison is the project manuscript \emph{Exact Boolean
Obstruction Energies} \cite{repo69boe}, source~47 of the inspected research collection.
It already proves $\Ma(C_d^{u,v})=b_d$ in every degree, the classification of
pure defects, and the universal bounds
\begin{equation}
 b_d\le\max_{T\notin\In_d}\Ma(T)
 \le1-\frac{\min(d+1,7)}{2^d}.
 \label{gsr:fm:69:bad:eq:old}
\end{equation}
Its exact universal result therefore stops at degree six.  Its first research
question asks whether the degree-seven value is $15/16$, leaving the interval
$120/128\le M\le121/128$.  Theorem~\ref{gsr:fm:69:bad:thm:main} gives the exact value in
that question and every higher degree at once.

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}cccc@{}}
\toprule
Degree & Old universal upper bound & Exact value here & Improvement\\
\midrule
$4$ & $11/16$ & $11/16$ & already exact\\
$5$ & $13/16$ & $13/16$ & already exact\\
$6$ & $57/64$ & $57/64$ & already exact\\
$7$ & $121/128$ & $120/128=15/16$ & $1/128$\\
$8$ & $249/256$ & $247/256$ & $2/256$\\
$9$ & $505/512$ & $502/512$ & $3/512$\\
$d\ge7$ & $1-7/2^d$ & $1-(d+1)/2^d$ & $(d-6)/2^d$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
The new ingredients are the contraction-integrability induction, its
all-degree equality classification, and the sharp effective-dimension
bound with extremizers.  The canonical calculation, the integration criterion,
and the cubic spectral argument are reproved and explicitly credited.

\srcnote{70}{Section 1}
\partsource{\textbf{Added in the twelfth write, 7~October 2026.} \textbf{Delivered title block.} ``Recovering the printed Fourier square exponent / Report282 / Research report prepared for Vladimir / 7 October 2026''; \emph{the PDF author field reads ``Research report prepared for Vladimir''}; no statement on AI assistance. \begin{partabstract}{70}
We recover the printed exponent $2^{-\alpha^{-2^{70}}}$ in the repository's asymptotic Theorem 13.12 interface. The lower-density branch combines Lau's simultaneous polynomial recurrence theorem with the existing own-step partition mechanism and the pinned Section 13 analytic extraction results. A direct row constructor and a selected short parent give the local exponent $2^{-3100876}a^{9222672}$, uniformly for every actual context density $a$ above a prescribed positive lower bound. We provide a finite symbolic threshold with all rounding and source-threshold conditions visible. The threshold is non-numerical because Lau's starting constants are non-numerical.

An independent elementary branch covers $1-2^{-16}\le\alpha<1$: near-maximal $U^4$ produces the global frequency $cab$ on more than $(1-9792(1-\alpha))N^2$ pairs, with original-function Fourier coefficients greater than $3N/4$. Phase normalization, character separation, cocycle identities, and two dense extensions are proved with explicit constants. The ranges overlap and yield the exact progression, mass, bilinearity, and Fourier conclusions for all $0<\alpha\le1$ at sufficiently large prime modulus.

This is a mathematical assembly with explicitly attributed analytic inputs, not a new recurrence theorem or a new Lean proof. It does not establish the literal all-primes lower-density assertion of the source paper, a numerical starting threshold, or a global Szemer\'edi bound. An optional published-only Maynard variant and a separate all-cyclic near-maximal strengthening are included. Bounded exact diagnostics accompany the proofs.
\end{partabstract}

For an integer $N\ge2$, put $G=\Z/N\Z$. We use the negative-sign unnormalized Fourier transform and the backward multiplicative difference
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:70:eq:normalizations}
 \widehat g(r)=\sum_{x\in G}g(x)e^{-2\pi i rx/N},\qquad
 D_a f(x)=f(x)\overline{f(x-a)}.
\end{equation}
The two difference operators commute. For a disc-valued function, meaning $|f(x)|\le1$, write
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:70:eq:U4}
 \|f\|_{U^4}^{16}
 =\E_{a,b,c\in G}\left|\E_{x\in G}D_aD_bD_cf(x)\right|^2.
\end{equation}
The repository's predicate \codefiftythree{UniformOfDegree f alpha 3} is precisely the inequality $\|f\|_{U^4}^{16}\le\alpha$: its unnormalized expression is $N^5$ times \eqref{gsr:fm:70:eq:U4}. In particular the failure assumption below is a strict inequality with $\alpha$, not with $\alpha^{16}$.

A modular progression $P(x,d;L)$ has indexed points $x+jd$ for $0\le j<L$. It is proper when these points are distinct; its carrier then has cardinality equal to its length $L=\len P$. Full cycles $P(0,1;N)$ are proper under this definition. A function $\Phi:G^2\to G$ is bilinear in the convention of Section 13 when it has the form
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:70:eq:bilinear}
 \Phi(x,z)=c_{00}+c_{10}x+c_{01}z+c_{11}xz.
\end{equation}
Thus constant and linear terms are allowed. ``Bilinear on a set'' means agreement there with a function of this form.

\begin{theorem}[Recovery of the exact asymptotic interface]\label{gsr:fm:70:thm:printed}
Use the pinned analytic inputs specified below and Lau's recurrence theorem \cite{lau}. For every $0<\alpha\le1$ there is an integer $N_{\mathrm F}(\alpha)$ such that, for every prime $N\ge N_{\mathrm F}(\alpha)$ and every disc-valued $f:G\to\C$ satisfying
\[
 \|f\|_{U^4}^{16}>\alpha,
\]
there are proper progressions $P,Q$ with the same nonzero step and common length $k$, a set $B\subseteq P\times Q$, and a function $\Phi:G^2\to G$ bilinear on the entire product $P\times Q$, such that
\begin{align}
 k&\ge N^{E(\alpha)},& E(\alpha)&=2^{-\alpha^{-2^{70}}},\label{gsr:fm:70:eq:targetside}\\
 |B|&\ge(\alpha/2)^{2^{76}}k^2,\label{gsr:fm:70:eq:targetmass}\\
 |\widehat{D_aD_bf}(\Phi(a,b))|&\ge\alpha N/2
 &&((a,b)\in B).\label{gsr:fm:70:eq:targetFourier}
\end{align}
The threshold depends only on $\alpha$, not on $f$ or on the actual density of any intermediate domain.
\end{theorem}

\begin{partabstract}{71}
Fix an integer $r\ge2$ and an integer $s$ with $r^s\ge8r$, and set $a=r^{-s}$. For every sufficiently large modulus $N$ such that $r^s\mid N$ and every prime divisor of $N$ divides $r$, we construct one genuine Section 13 context of density $a$. It has selected genuine initial records at the exact Section 10 cutoff, all six literal numerical budgets, and an explicit genuine Stage 13.6 witness nested inside the initial progression.

For this same context, every genuine alternative initial pair $D,E$ at that cutoff fails: no Stage 13.6 record admits even a weak Stage 13.7 continuation. The alternative records need not carry a budget parameter or satisfy the other five numerical budgets. The common width inequality, depending only on $a,N$, forces their initial lengths and critical-height sets to be nonzero. The total floor map $x\mapsto\lfloor x.\mathrm{val}/r\rfloor$ has at most $r$ agreements with any ambient affine map. Thus output mass and width would give $W\le L\le r/\delta$, while $W\delta=2^{92}a^{-480}>r$.

A structural refinement shows that every genuine alternative Stage 13.5 progression $E.Q$ has step divisible by $r$. Width alone forces its normalized spectral radius below $1/4$; the exact annihilator spectrum and the sharp finite-subgroup radius $1/3$ then force divisibility. Consequently no genuine initial package with unit $E.Q$ step exists for these particular contexts and scales. The construction retains every floor, the exact ceiling-dependent radius, and all $r$ spectral aliases. Its eight thresholds are unchanged in the original prime-power subfamilies. The result does not classify all composite moduli or general unit-step contexts, contradict the prime-qualified source theorem, or claim Lean verification. The companion gives bounded exact checks and reproducible packaging without evaluating the enormous witnesses.
\end{partabstract}

\paragraph{Reading guide.}
Section~\ref{gsr:fm:71:sec:main} states the stronger quantifiers. Sections 2--8 give the full interface and selected six-budget construction. Section~\ref{gsr:en:71:sec:allinitial} rules out all alternative genuine initial records by the global row cap. Section~\ref{gsr:en:71:sec:step} separately forces divisibility of every admissible $E.Q$ step. Later sections state the precise refuted implication, the remaining scope boundaries, and the reproduction contract.

For a positive integer $N$, let $\operatorname{rad}(N)$ denote the product of its distinct prime divisors, with $\operatorname{rad}(1)=1$. Thus $\operatorname{rad}(N)\mid r$ says that every prime divisor of $N$ divides $r$.

\begin{theorem}[One context excluding every genuine initial choice]\label{gsr:fm:71:thm:main}
Fix an integer $r\ge2$ and an integer $s$ such that $r^s\ge8r$, and put $a=r^{-s}$. There is a finite integer $N_0=N_0(r,s)$ such that for every positive integer $N$ satisfying
\[
 N\ge N_0,\qquad r^s\mid N,\qquad\operatorname{rad}(N)\mid r,
\]
the following holds. Put $Z=\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z$, $m=N/r^s$ and
\[
 T=\{rj\bmod N:0\le j<m\},\quad A=T\times Z,\quad
 \phi(x,y)=\left\lfloor x.\mathrm{val}/r\right\rfloor\bmod N.
\]
Together with $\eta=2^{-44}$ these define a genuine context $S_N$ of exact density $a$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item There are selected records $D_0,E_0,M,F_0$ satisfying the full Stage 13.4 predicate at
\[
 \theta=\operatorname{section10Lambda}(a^{32}/16)=2^{-59}a^{176},
\]
the full Stage 13.5 and Stage 13.6 predicates, and all six numerical budgets in Section 2. Moreover,
\[
 M=\operatorname{len}(F_0.R)>0,\qquad
 [F_0.R]\subseteq[E_0.Q]=[D_0.P]\subseteq T,
\]
\[
 M+1\le\operatorname{len}(E_0.Q),
\]
and the three selected progressions have step $r\bmod N$.
\item For every pair $D,E$ satisfying genuine Stage 13.4 at the same exact cutoff and genuine Stage 13.5 for $S_N$, no pair $F,G$ satisfies Stage 13.6 and weak Stage 13.7.
\item Every such alternative $E.Q$ has step divisible by $r$: every integer representative $d_Q$ satisfies $r\mid d_Q$. In particular its step is nonunit.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

It overlaps source~57's Section~5, which arrived after its overlap check, without citing it (Section~\ref{gsr:en:sec:nearmaximal}).}
\begin{partabstract}{72}
For every finite abelian group and every $d\geq1$, an explicit near-maximal $U^{d+2}$ hypothesis forces a globally separately additive, dual-valued frequency map. More than $70\%$ of all $d$-tuples have a normalized Fourier coefficient of their $d$-fold multiplicative derivative greater than $3/4$ at the selected frequency. The sufficient cube-average defect is $[20\cdot6^{d-1}(2^{d+2}+1)]^{-1}$. The proof includes a quantitative dense extension induction using homomorphism-valued slices, exact character separation, and uniform return from polar normalization. On every cyclic group the frequency is $c a_1\cdots a_d$, and the ambient progressions may be full cycles.

We also prove a sharp support gap for nonzero separately additive maps, stronger-threshold uniqueness and symmetry, and a near-one selected-energy bound. On every cyclic group, rational shift antiderivatives give proximity to periodic rational polynomial phases with an explicit squared $L^2$ bound $(2A_k+1)\eps$, where $A_k=(2^k+1)6^{(k-2)(k-1)/2}$. Ordinary residue-ring polynomial phases are also available when $(k-1)!$ is invertible. A torsion example distinguishes the periodic rational target from the narrower classical target. The near-extremizer phenomenon and dense difference-map extension have established antecedents. The contribution here is a self-contained quantitative derivation and reproducible bounded diagnostics, with no historical-priority, arbitrary-uniformity inverse, global Ramsey, or formal-verification claim.
\end{partabstract}

\subsection{Conventions}
Throughout, $G$ is a finite abelian group, written additively, equipped with normalized counting measure. Its character group $\widehat G$ is also written additively, so $\chi_{\gamma+\gamma'}=\chi_\gamma\chi_{\gamma'}$. All $L^p$ norms are normalized, and $\T=\{z\in\C:|z|=1\}$. We write $e(t)=\exp(2\pi i t)$ for rational or real $t$, and $e_N(r)=e(r/N)$ for integer representatives of $r\in\Z/N\Z$. For $f:G\to\C$, define the backward multiplicative difference and normalized Fourier transform by
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:72:eq:conventions}
 D_a f(x)=f(x)\conjbar{f(x-a)},\qquad
 D_{\ba}f=D_{a_1}\cdots D_{a_d}f,\qquad
 \Fcal_f(\gamma)=\E_x f(x)\conjbar{\chi_\gamma(x)}.
\end{equation}
A map $\Phi:G^d\to\widehat G$ is \emph{separately additive} if it is a homomorphism in each coordinate when all other coordinates are fixed. No field structure is intended by the word multilinear in the title. Put
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:72:eq:constants}
 Q_k(f)=\norm{f}_{U^k}^{2^k},\qquad
 M_d=2^{d+2}+1,\qquad C_d=\frac{6^d-1}{5},\qquad
 \eps_d=\frac1{20\cdot6^{d-1}M_d}.
\end{equation}
The cube formula defining $Q_k$ and its normalizations are given in Section~\ref{gsr:en:72:sec:normalization}.

\subsection{The all characteristic Fourier theorem}
\begin{theorem}\label{gsr:fm:72:thm:main}
Let $d\geq1$, let $G$ be a finite abelian group, and let $f:G\to\C$ satisfy $|f|\leq1$. If
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:72:eq:mainhyp}
 0<\eps\leq\eps_d,\qquad Q_{d+2}(f)>1-\eps,
\end{equation}
then there exist a separately additive map $\Phi:G^d\to\widehat G$ and a set $B\subseteq G^d$ such that
\begin{align}
 \dens(B)&>1-(6^d-1)M_d\eps
 \geq\frac7{10}+\frac1{20\cdot6^{d-1}}>\frac7{10},\label{gsr:fm:72:eq:maindensity}\\
 \abs{\Fcal_{D_{\ba}f}(\Phi(\ba))}
 &>\sqrt{\frac45}-2^d\eps>\frac34\qquad(\ba\in B).\label{gsr:fm:72:eq:maincoeff}
\end{align}
The first inequality in \eqref{gsr:fm:72:eq:maindensity} is strict even at $\eps=\eps_d$. The second compares the displayed real lower-bound expressions. This theorem requires neither uniqueness nor symmetry of $\Phi$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{writenote}[7 October 2026; sources 70--81]
\emph{Overlap with source~57, not cited} (checked at the write). Source~57's Section~\ref{gsr:en:57:sec:d5} already has an all-order frequency extraction on finite abelian groups (Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:57:ep:group-all-orders}), with density loss $(18C_s+8)\varepsilon$, $C_1=2$, $C_s=6+38C_{s-1}$, under $18\cdot38^{s-1}\varepsilon<1/6$. Against this theorem's $(6^d-1)(2^{d+2}+1)\varepsilon$: $44$ against $45$ at $d=1$, and $1484$, $56204$ against $595$, $7095$ at $d=2,3$; this theorem has the smaller loss for every $d\ge2$. On prime fields source~57's $(216d+8)\varepsilon$ is smaller. Source~57 arrived on 6~October at 21:12, after this source's pin (18:36) and its overlap check \texttt{7ed8eec95} (19:39), so the omission is not this source's oversight. \emph{Identification:} its ``source~12'' is this report's source~12, whose dense extension above density $2/3$ is Corollary~\ref{gsr:en:12:cor:global} (the cited lines~12970--12979 at the pin).
\end{writenote}
The group may have any exponent, and there is no relation required between $|G|$ and $d$. The analytic statement includes the trivial group. The progression interpretation below assumes a nontrivial cyclic group.

\begin{corollary}\label{gsr:fm:72:cor:cyclic}
For $G=\Z/N\Z$, $N\geq2$, use $\chi_r(x)=e_N(rx)$, where $e_N(t)=\exp(2\pi i t/N)$, and the unnormalized transform
\[
 \widehat g(r)=\sum_{x\in\Z/N\Z}g(x)e_N(-rx)=N\Fcal_g(r).
\]
Under \eqref{gsr:fm:72:eq:mainhyp}, there is $c\in\Z/N\Z$ and a set $B$ satisfying \eqref{gsr:fm:72:eq:maindensity} such that
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:72:eq:cycliccoeff}
 \abs{\widehat{D_{\ba}f}(c a_1\cdots a_d)}
 >\left(\sqrt{\frac45}-2^d\eps\right)N>\frac{3N}{4}
 \qquad(\ba\in B).
\end{equation}
The ambient product of progressions can be $P_1\times\cdots\times P_d=G^d$, with each $P_i$ the full cycle of start $0$, step $1$, and length $N$.
\end{corollary}
A full cycle is proper under the cardinality convention because its $N$ indexed terms are distinct. Its step is nonzero for $N\geq2$, and all lengths and steps agree. The coefficient conclusion is on the dense subset $B$ of this ambient box; it does not assert that all points of the box are good. The scalar formula is cyclic-specific: the general theorem supplies a dual-valued map.

\subsection{Additional conclusions}
The rest of the article gives three refinements, distinguishing periodic rational phases from ordinary residue-ring phases.
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*,itemsep=3pt]
\item At the stronger defect threshold
\[
 \eps_d^{\rm sym}=\frac1{2^{d+1}(6^d-1)M_d},
\]
the witness is intrinsically unique among separately additive maps whose original-$f$ coefficients exceed $3/4$ on density greater than $1-2^{-d-1}$. It is symmetric in the $d$ derivative directions. No symmetry involving character evaluation is asserted.
\item For unit-valued $v$ and $0<\tau\leq[20\cdot6^{d-1}]^{-1}$, the hypothesis $Q_{d+2}(v)>1-\tau$ gives
\[
 \E_{\ba}\abs{\Fcal_{D_{\ba}v}(\Phi(\ba))}^2>1-6^d\tau.
\]
The unit-input estimate has no polar-normalization factor $M_d$.
\item For every $k\geq2$ and cyclic modulus $N\geq2$, set
\[
 A_k=(2^k+1)6^{(k-2)(k-1)/2}.
\]
If $|f|\leq1$, $Q_k(f)>1-\eps$, and $0<\eps\leq3/(10A_k)$, then there are $P\in\mathbb Q[x]$ of degree at most $k-1$, with $P(0)=0$ and $e(P)$ $N$-periodic on the integers, and $|z|=1$ such that
\[
 \norm{f-z e(P)}_2^2
 <2\bigl(1-\sqrt{1-A_k\eps}\bigr)+\eps
 \leq(2A_k+1)\eps.
\]
The exponential is periodic; the rational polynomial itself need not be. If additionally $\gcd((k-1)!,N)=1$, an approximant $z e_N(p)$ with an ordinary polynomial $p\in(\Z/N\Z)[x]$ is available with the same bound. Only this narrower classical target requires the factorial condition. This integration result is cyclic, while the Fourier and energy theorems hold on all finite abelian groups.
\end{enumerate}
The near-extremizer phenomenon is established in greater generality by Eisner and Tao~\cite{eisnertao}. We give explicit sufficient constants in the finite setting, not a replacement for their broader result or a claim of historical novelty. The dense one-variable extension also has an established source antecedent, discussed in Section~\ref{gsr:fz:72:sec:antecedents}. The argument is not an inverse theorem at arbitrary positive uniformity and does not by itself yield a density increment or a global Ramsey estimate.

\begin{partabstract}{73}
For every integer $d\ge2$, every nontrivial finite abelian group $G$, and every
$f:G\to\C$ with $|f|\le1$, put $q=2^d$ and
$\eps=1-\norm f_{U^d}^q$. We give a fully explicit version of the
near-maximal-norm entry step and combine it with the sharp local expansion
of upstream source 55. If $\eps\le10^{-d}$, then
\[
 D_d(f)\le\frac2q\eps+b_d(G)\eps^2+3q^3\eps^3,
\]
where $D_d$ is squared normalized $L^2$ distance to all degree-at-most
$d-1$ phase polynomials, including nonclassical phases, and
\[
 b_d(G)=\begin{cases}
 (3^d-1)/(2q^2),&|G|\text{ odd},\\
 (1-q^{-2})/3,&|G|\text{ even}.
 \end{cases}
\]
The local certificate has radius at least $q^{-5/2}$.
The entry proof quantitatively implements the small-cocycle argument of
Eisner and Tao. Its key induction preserves squared correlation, so its
error coefficient does not grow with degree. Convex interpolation reduces
the centered cube remainder to
$10\binom q5+\binom q6$, replacing a sum exponential in $q$.
These two estimates answer the numerical-entry and singly-exponential-radius
question explicitly posed in source 55. Its sharp linear and quadratic
coefficients, quartic census, and fifth-order cancellation are retained
and credited, not claimed as new results.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small\raggedright
\textbf{Scope and status.} Self-contained mathematical proofs and exact

asserted. All constants are uniform in the order, exponent, rank, and
characteristic of $G$.
\end{quote}
\subsection{Conventions and phase class}
All averages use normalized counting measure. For $k\ge1$ define
\[
 Q_k(f)=\norm f_{U^k(G)}^{2^k}
 =\E_{x,h_1,\ldots,h_k}\prod_{\omega\in\{0,1\}^k}
    \cC^{|\omega|}f(x+\omega\cdot h),
\]
where $\cC$ is conjugation. This quantity is real and nonnegative; the
multiplicative-difference recursion reduces that assertion to
$Q_1(f)=|\E f|^2$. In degree $d$ we also write $\Ufiftyfive(f)=Q_d(f)$ and $q=2^d$.
A phase polynomial of degree at most $s$ is a map $P:G\to S^1$ whose
$(s+1)$-fold multiplicative differences are all $1$. Let $\cP_s(G)$
denote this class. It is closed under products, quotients, translates, and
constant rotations. Define
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:73:eq:distance}
 D_d(f)=\min_{P\in\cP_{d-1}(G)}\E|f-P|^2,
 \qquad \eps=1-Q_d(f).
\end{equation}
The minimum exists by compactness of the closed subset $\cP_{d-1}(G)$ of
$(S^1)^G$. Multiplication by an element of this class preserves $Q_d$.
Degree here is defined by differences, not by a residue-ring coordinate
formula. On $\Z/2\Z$, for example, $P(0)=1$, $P(1)=i$ has degree two:
its first difference takes the values $i,-i$, its second difference is
constant $-1$, and its third is $1$. It is not a constant multiple of a
classical $\F_2$-valued polynomial phase. Such phases must be included.

\begin{theorem}[Explicit endpoint stability]\label{gsr:fm:73:thm:main}
Let $d\ge2$, let $G$ be a nontrivial finite abelian group, and let $|f|\le1$.
If
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:73:eq:entrycutoff}
 0\le\eps\le e_d:=10^{-d},
\end{equation}
then
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:73:eq:main}
 D_d(f)\le\frac2q\eps+b_d(G)\eps^2+R'_d\eps^3
 \le\frac2q\eps+b_d(G)\eps^2+3q^3\eps^3,
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:73:eq:b}
 b_d(G)=\begin{cases}(3^d-1)/(2q^2),&|G|\text{ odd},\\
 (q^2-1)/(3q^2),&|G|\text{ even},\end{cases}
\end{equation}
and the explicit sharper constant $R'_d$ is given in equation~\eqref{gsr:en:73:eq:R}.
The linear and quadratic coefficients are the sharp coefficients of
source 55; neither is changed by the entry refinement.
\end{theorem}

\subsection{What is inherited and what is refined}
Upstream source 55, \emph{Sharp Second-Order Stability at the
Polynomial-Phase Endpoint of Gowers Norms}, already proves the sharp
second-order expansion uniformly in finite abelian groups \cite{srcfiftyfive}.
Its question labeled \texttt{q:entry} asks for an explicit defect threshold
and singly exponential dependence in the degree for both entry and the
local radius. It uses the published qualitative near-extremizer theorem of
Eisner and Tao for the passage into its explicit local neighborhood.

The present report supplies two quantitative refinements: the
correlation-preserving induction in section~\ref{gsr:en:73:sec:entry}, and the convex
interpolation remainder in theorem~\ref{gsr:en:73:thm:expansion}. Their combination proves
theorem~\ref{gsr:fm:73:thm:main} with numerical constants. The bounded-function geometry,
four-vertex classification, quartic Fourier bound, fifth-order real-part
cancellation, local absorption and inversion scheme, and sharp coefficients
are imported from source 55 and reproved below for completeness.
Its tangent-rigidity theorem is not needed here and is not reasserted as an
additional result of this report.

Eisner--Tao's Theorem 1.1 and Section 2 supply the qualitative antecedent
and small-cocycle method; their Remark 1.6 already records effective
polynomial rates without displaying optimized constants \cite{eisnertao}.
Thus an explicit implementation of that argument is not a new qualitative
inverse theorem. No first-publication claim for the numerical improvements
is made. The historical Gowers proof supplies the uniformity and
phase-extraction framework \cite{gowers}; the present endpoint estimate
alone supplies no new density bound in Szemer\'edi's theorem.

\begin{partabstract}{74}
For every fixed $k\ge1$, $0<\gamma<1$, and every sufficiently large
integer $N$, we construct a full-domain map on $(\Z/N\Z)^{k+1}$ satisfying the two premises
of the pinned Section~16.10 cover interface, the full weighted function
and relation product properties, and the named structural and selection
predicates leading to that interface, but not its parameter-one conclusion.
The map is zero outside a slab of vanishing density. On a specified proper
box, every admissible target cover captures at most $5/16$ of the box,
whereas the conclusion requires at least $1/2$.

The construction combines two elementary estimates. Arbitrary values on a
set of size $m$ leave a respected-energy coefficient at least
$(1+(m^2/N)^{1/3})^{-3}$. Separately, for a short interval alphabet of size
$R$, one word simultaneously has balanced symbol counts and avoids every
nonconstant affine restriction on every sufficiently long proper modular
progression. This works for composite $N$, including nonunit steps.
It gives an exact optimal affine-list cover law, a stability deficit,
and an explicit nonvacuous range.

The result rules out repairing the recorded parameter reset merely by
restoring these product and selection predicates. It is compatible with
existential global reselection: removing the sparse slab leaves the zero
map. Source~50's earlier two-input counterexample and endpoint
characterization, and source~49's conditional retained-core theorem,
are expressly retained as prior results.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small\raggedright
\textbf{Scope and status.} Self-contained mathematical proofs with exact
finite diagnostics and a reproducible package. This is an AI-assisted
research manuscript, not a refereed publication or a Lean proof.
It neither refutes Gowers's contextual construction or Theorem~16.2 nor
improves a global Szemer\'edi bound. No publication-priority claim is made.
\end{quote}
\label{gsr:fm:74:sec:intro}

The local cover target in the current Section~16 catalogue quantifies over
\emph{every} proper input box. Its product-property input instead bounds
weighted additive energy relative to the \emph{ambient} group size. These
quantifiers leave room for a small region with complicated local behavior.
This report makes that incompatibility quantitative and verifies that it
survives the named upstream data, rather than only an abstract slice cover.

Throughout, $N$ is a positive integer. Write $\GN=\Z/N\Z$.
All logarithms are natural. A proper modular arithmetic
progression of length $L$ is a presentation
\[
 P=\{x_0+dt:0\le t<L\}\subseteq\GN
\]
with distinct displayed residues. Its difference need not be a unit.
A box is a product of progressions with a common difference; it is proper
when each axis is proper. The width is the minimum axis length. The
source assigns width zero in dimension zero. A multiaffine polynomial is
\[
 \mu(x_1,\ldots,x_D)=\sum_{A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,D\}}c_A\prod_{i\in A}x_i,
 \qquad c_A\in\GN.
\]
Thus constant and lower-degree terms are allowed. These conventions agree
with the pinned definitions~\cite{repo74defs,repo74section16}.

\begin{theorem}[Sparse obstruction at every nonendpoint parameter]
\label{gsr:fm:74:thm:main}
Fix an integer $k\ge1$ and $0<\gamma<1$. Set
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:74:eq:main-parameters}
 E_j=2^{2^{j+8}},\qquad E=E_{k+1},\qquad
 Q=(2/\gamma)^E,\qquad c=Q^{-1},\qquad R=\lceil4Q\rceil.
\end{equation}
Let the integer $N\ge2$ satisfy
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:74:eq:threshold}
 \log N\ge\frac{32768R}{c^2},\qquad
 N\ge\bigl(\gamma^{-8/3}-1\bigr)^{-9}.
\end{equation}
Put $m=\lfloor N^{1/3}\rfloor$ and $J=\{0,\ldots,m-1\}\subseteq\GN$.
There exists $a:\GN\to\{0,\ldots,R-1\}$, zero outside $J$, such that
$F(h,y)=a(y)$ on the full domain $\GN^k\times\GN$ has all of the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item It has the full weighted product property with parameter $\gamma$.
Its full graph has the relation product property and has size
$N^{k+1}\le\gamma^{-2}N^{k+1}$.
\item At $\theta=1$, it satisfies both exact premises of the pinned
\filename{lemma_16_10}, with its domain and all-ones map realized by the actual
named cube construction. All prescribed proper coordinate sections have
the required multiple-linearity controls.
\item It satisfies \filename{Section16StructuredPair} and the specific
spectrum, zero Bohr model, induced selection, good-domain, alternating
identity, and remainder-cover predicates detailed in
sections~\ref{gsr:en:74:sec:realization} and \ref{gsr:en:74:sec:dimension-lift}. For prime $N$, these include the named antecedents
of the actual numbered Lemma~16.9. For composite $N$, we assert the
predicates and construct the all-box line covers directly; we do not
apply that prime-only lemma.
\item It fails \filename{MultiplyLinearFunction gamma 1}. On $J^{k+1}$,
any putative target cover at loss $1/2$ covers at most $5m^{k+1}/16$ points,
strictly fewer than the required $m^{k+1}/2$.
\end{enumerate}
The construction works for every integer satisfying \eqref{gsr:fm:74:eq:threshold},
without a restriction on its smallest prime factor.
\end{theorem}

The thresholds are finite for each fixed $\gamma<1$. They are deliberately
conservative. No integer or word at this scale was computed. The proof
is given first in dimension two in
sections~\ref{gsr:en:74:sec:sparse}, \ref{gsr:en:74:sec:interface}, \ref{gsr:en:74:sec:obstruction} and \ref{gsr:en:74:sec:realization}, then for all
$k\ge1$ in section~\ref{gsr:en:74:sec:dimension-lift}.
Its cyclic-modulus input is the following positive theorem.

\begin{theorem}[Affine avoidance and exact list rigidity]
\label{gsr:fm:74:thm:word}
Let $R\ge2$ and $N\ge3R$ be integers. Define
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:74:eq:word-threshold}
 S=\{0,\ldots,R-1\}\subseteq\GN,\qquad
 K=2RN^3+N^5,\qquad
 L_0=\max\{8R,\lceil128R\log(2K)\rceil\}.
\end{equation}
There exists $b:\GN\to S$ such that, for every proper progression $P$
of length $L\ge L_0$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Every symbol count $b_v(P)=|\{x\in P:b(x)=v\}|$ obeys
\[
 \frac{7L}{8R}\le b_v(P)\le\frac{5L}{4R}\qquad(v\in S).
\]
\item Every ambient affine map whose restriction to $P$ is nonconstant
agrees with $b$ at at most $3L/(4R)$ points.
\item If $b_{(1)}\ge\cdots\ge b_{(R)}$ are the ordered symbol counts and
$B_q=\sum_{j=1}^q b_{(j)}$, then, for every $1\le q\le R$, the maximum
mass covered by $q$ affine graphs is exactly $B_q$. Every optimizer has
$q$ distinct constant restrictions on $P$, taking values in $S$, with
selected symbol mass $B_q$.
\item More precisely, a $q$-list with $s$ distinct useful constant
restrictions has deficit from $B_q$ at least $(q-s)L/(8R)$.
A useful constant restriction takes its value in $S$.
\end{enumerate}
Every single affine restriction therefore agrees at at most $5L/(4R)$
points. Moreover, $N\ge1024R\log(1024R)$ suffices for $L_0\le N$.
\end{theorem}

Here ``constant'' refers to the restriction to $P$, not its ambient
coefficient. Ties in the symbol counts can give several optimal subsets.
The theorem constructs special words for a short interval alphabet; it is
not a classification of affine covers of every word or every alphabet.

\subsection{Relation to the existing results}

Source~50 already proves the prime-field two-input counterexample,
finite-alphabet cover envelopes, balanced-word constructions, and the
full-domain $\gamma=1$ endpoint characterization~\cite{srcfifty}.
Its strict symbol-mass gap also gives the optimizer mechanism reused
below. Source~49 already establishes a loss-dependent retained-core
cover theorem conditional on seven finite interfaces~\cite{srcfortynine}.
Neither result is presented here as a new theorem.

The additional conclusions are the sparse weighted restoration barrier,
its exact downstream-data realization for every fixed $\gamma<1$, and
the affine short-interval word input that makes the obstruction work over
every sufficiently large cyclic modulus. The arithmetic coset estimate
in lemma~\ref{gsr:en:74:lem:active} gives a restricted affirmative development of
source~50's torsion question. It does not settle that question for arbitrary
alphabets, higher-degree polynomials, or products of cyclic groups.

\section[{Source 75: The two questions and their connection}]{Source 75. The two questions and their connection}\label{gsr:fm:75:sec:d1}\label{gsr:fm:75:sec:intro}
\srcnote{75}{Section 1}
\partsource{\textbf{Added in the twelfth write, 7~October 2026.} \textbf{Delivered title page.} ``ProveIt research report 287 / Global Deletion Costs and Hereditary Energy Rigidity / Quantitative local cover obstructions and a sharp cyclic affine threshold / Prepared for Vladimir Reshetnikov / 7 October 2026''; \emph{the PDF author field reads ``ChatGPT; research manuscript prepared for Vladimir Reshetnikov''}.
