Source~85 (Report~297) shows that the two candidates never tie, so $\mc_n$ is a singleton for every $n\ge3$ (Corollary~\ref{gsr:en:85:cor:unique}). Checked at the write: $C_n<3+2\sqrt2$ for $n\le400$, $\norm{H_{3000}}_{4\to4}$ within $10^{-7}$ below $\sqrt{1+\sqrt2}$, and for $n=3,\ldots,7$ a numerical maximization over general real vectors reaches $C_n$ (corroboration).
\end{writenote}

\paragraph{Connection with mixed-sign matrices.}
For the matrix $A(n,-a,b)$ with diagonal $-a$ and all off-diagonal entries $b$,
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:83:eq:matrix-reduction}
 A(n,-a,b)=-(a+b)T_{nb/(a+b)}.
\end{equation}
Thus Theorem~\ref{gsr:fm:83:thm:general} applies to every $a\ge0$, $b>0$, $n\ge3$, including the zero-diagonal case $a=0$. It proves the corresponding $p=4$ all-real-maximizer assertion in Conjecture~5.6 of Bouthat, Mashreghi and Morneau-Gu\'erin~\cite{bouthatnormal}. Our theorem allows all $\gamma>0$, beyond the interval $0<\gamma\le n$ corresponding to these matrix parameters. The precise literature comparison and endpoint cautions appear in Section~\ref{gsr:fz:83:sec:literature}.

\paragraph{Logical organization.}
Sections~\ref{gsr:en:83:sec:two-values}--\ref{gsr:en:83:sec:threshold} prove the general theorem without importing an external extremizer theorem. Sections~\ref{gsr:en:83:sec:reflection}--\ref{gsr:en:83:sec:finite-examples} solve the reflection scalar problem in radicals and supply exact finite illustrations. The energy application then uses finite Fourier analysis. Analytic arguments establish the all-parameter statements; the accompanying exact code verifies specified identities and finite certificates, without replacing those arguments by numerical optimization.

\begin{partabstract}{84}
For every real density $0<\delta\le1$, the two explicit five-term starting thresholds in the inspected ProveIt source satisfy
\[
 H_{\fej}(\delta)<H_{\old}(\delta)^{1/4}<H_{\old}(\delta).

In fact, writing $n_{\fej}=\lceil8/\beta_{\fej}\rceil$ for the exact Fej\'er iteration count and $R=\sigma_{\fej}/\sigma_{\old}$ for the exact size-exponent gain, we prove

 \log H_{\fej}<R^{-n_{\fej}}\log H_{\old}
 \le4^{-n_{\fej}}\log H_{\old}.

The argument is a complete real-variable proof about finite expressions. An inspected source theorem supplies the five-term progression implication. \textbf{Scope.} The comparison is between the two repository constructions at commit

No independent Lean compilation or complete imported-dependency verification is claimed. This is not a comparison with the paper's numerical threshold, an arbitrary-length result, or a literature-best claim.

\label{gsr:fm:84:sec:result}
A local improvement in a quantitative inverse theorem need not automatically improve a fully expanded density-iteration threshold. The local size exponent, surviving discrepancy, phase-removal constant, initial modulus, and iteration count all enter the final expression. Some enter through maxima and ceilings; some vary in opposing directions. This report compares the entire expressions, rather than only their most visible exponents.

At the source revision specified on the title page, set
\begin{align*}
 H_{\old}(\delta)&=\filename{fiveTermThreshold}\,(\delta),\\
 H_{\fej}(\delta)&=\filename{fejerFiveTermThreshold}\,(\delta).
\end{align*}
The labels ``old'' and ``Fej\'er'' distinguish the two explicit interfaces at that same revision. The old interface was introduced at the earlier commit listed in Section~\ref{gsr:fz:84:sec:provenance}. These labels do not compare the present source with an unspecified moving branch.

\begin{theorem}[Strict comparison]\label{gsr:fm:84:thm:main}
For every real $0<\delta\le1$, define
\[
 \alpha=\left(\frac{\delta^5}{64000}\right)^{16},\qquad
 x=\frac2\alpha,\qquad
 \Delta=2^{76}-2^{42},
\]
and let $\beta_{\fej}$ be the exact parameter in Section~\ref{gsr:fz:84:sec:definitions}. Put
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:84:eq:R}
 n_{\fej}=\left\lceil\frac8{\beta_{\fej}}\right\rceil,
 \qquad
 R=2^{\,x^{2^{88}}-x^{2^{53}}}\,x^{24718\Delta}.
\end{equation}
Then $R=\sigma_{\fej}/\sigma_{\old}\ge4$, and
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:84:eq:sharp-log}
 0<\log H_{\fej}
 <R^{-n_{\fej}}\log H_{\old}
 \le4^{-n_{\fej}}\log H_{\old}
 \le\tfrac14\log H_{\old}.
\end{equation}
Consequently
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:84:eq:main-chain}
 H_{\fej}<H_{\old}^{\,R^{-n_{\fej}}}
 \le H_{\old}^{\,4^{-n_{\fej}}}
 \le H_{\old}^{1/4}<H_{\old}.
\end{equation}
In particular the weaker but simpler bound $H_{\fej}<H_{\old}^{1/4}<H_{\old}$ holds on the entire source density range, including $\delta=1$.
\end{theorem}

\subsection{The progression implication}
The inspected statement \sourceeightyfour{Proofs18FejerFiveTerm}{\filename{natural_five_term_fejer}} has the following exact mathematical content. If $0<\delta\le1$, $N\in\N$, and $A$ is a finite subset of $\N$ with
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:84:eq:ap-hyp}
 A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\},\qquad |A|\ge\delta N,
 \qquad H_{\fej}(\delta)\le N,
\end{equation}
then there exist $a,d\in\N$ with $d>0$ such that
\[
 a,\ a+d,\ a+2d,\ a+3d,\ a+4d\in A.
\]
The definition \sourceeightyfour{Definitions}{\filename{HasNatAP}} makes the positive step requirement explicit. The theorem body directly applies the constructed Fej\'er cubic function-discrepancy bound through the common closed density-iteration theorem. No prime-modulus hypothesis appears in~\eqref{gsr:fm:84:eq:ap-hyp}.

Combined with Theorem~\ref{gsr:fm:84:thm:main}, this inspected source result gives a strictly smaller sufficient real-valued starting threshold than the older explicit construction. It does not identify the least sufficient integer threshold, or say that the old criterion was necessary. In particular, a comparison of sufficient bounds alone cannot classify sets below either bound. The finite-interval corollary here uses the source theorem as an input; the new analytic comparison itself is proved in full below.

Neither the new comparison nor all of the existing theorem's imported dependencies were independently checked by the Lean kernel in this work.

It is not evidence for a historical or literature-wide assertion of unresolvedness. \begin{partabstract}{85}
The fourth norm of the reflection $H_n=I-2J_n/n$ reduces to an optimization over coordinate multiplicities. We replace its radical branch comparison by the integer polynomial
\[W(n,m)=m(n-m)(n-2m)^4.\]
An elementary coprimality argument excludes every adjacent tie. Combined with unimodality, it proves that the optimal multiplicity is unique for every $n\ge3$.

The divisibility criterion from Report 295 then yields a complete classification: precisely $77$ finite abelian group orders at least three permit an order-two point spike to attain its spectral energy lower bound. The largest is $583$. The same list classifies subgroup-spike indices. A compact certificate uses just $27$ nontrivial integer comparisons; a separate exact route checks all $351{,}648$ branches in the analytically sufficient range $3\le n\le1186$.

We describe every point-spike equality weight, distinguish the weaker conclusions for a nontrivial subgroup kernel, and determine exactly when rational weights or indicators can attain the spectral bound. Among orders or indices at least three, that last possibility occurs only at four.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small\raggedright
\textbf{Scope.} Uniqueness refers to the optimal multiplicity; reflection extremizers still vary by permutation and nonzero scaling. This report computes no nonsaturating energy minimum, makes no global Ramsey or Szemeredi improvement, and asserts no novelty or priority. Reports 1--296 remain unchanged.
\end{quote}
For $n\ge3$ and $1\le m\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor$, set
\begin{align}
 u_{n,m}&=m(n-m),&d_{n,m}&=\frac{n-2m}{\sqrt{u_{n,m}}},\label{gsr:fm:85:eq:parameters}\\
 y_{n,m}&=\frac{n}{\sqrt{3u_{n,m}}}-1,&
 k_{n,m}&=\frac{d_{n,m}}{\sqrt{y_{n,m}}(y_{n,m}+3)}.\notag
\end{align}
All square roots are positive. In particular $y_{n,m}\ge2/\sqrt3-1>0$. Define
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:85:eq:constants}
 k_n=\max_m k_{n,m},\qquad
 \mc_n=\{m:k_{n,m}=k_n\},\qquad
 C_n=\frac{1+k_n}{1-k_n},\qquad \eta_n=\frac1{1+k_n}.
\end{equation}
Report 295 proves that $C_n=\norm{H_n}_{4\to4}^4$ over both real and complex scalars and transfers its equality cases to a weighted additive-energy problem. Section~\ref{gsr:en:85:sec:input} states precisely the operator input used here, while Sections~\ref{gsr:en:85:sec:energy} and~\ref{gsr:en:85:sec:subgroups} explain that transfer.

\begin{theorem}[Unique optimal split and all saturation orders]\label{gsr:fm:85:thm:main}
For every integer $n\ge3$, the set $\mc_n$ is a singleton $\{m_n\}$. For a point spike with a nonzero order-two value on any finite abelian group of order $n$, the spectral lower bound $\eta_n$ is attained if and only if
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:85:eq:classification}
 n=qm\quad\hbox{for one of the pairs in Table~\ref{gsr:fm:85:tab:classification}}.
\end{equation}
In each listed pair, $m=m_n$. The pairs give $77$ distinct orders, with largest order $583=11\cdot53$. The same classification holds for a subgroup spike when $n$ is the subgroup index.
\end{theorem}

\begin{writenote}[7 October 2026; sources 82--94]

This theorem answers source~83's question on ties (its Question~3). The phrase ``attained'' means equality for some nonzero nonnegative weight. Every finite abelian group of a listed order admits such a weight. For an unlisted order $n\ge3$, every such group satisfies a strictly larger minimum than $\eta_n$. This does not give its value or show that the nonsaturating minimum is independent of group structure.

Orders and indices $1,2$ are separate isometric cases: every nonzero nonnegative weight has energy ratio one. Including them gives $79$ possible positive orders or indices, of which $77$ are nonisometric. The theorem is about order-two spikes, not arbitrary maps to arbitrary targets.

\begin{partabstract}{86}
Let $H_{\fej}(\delta)$ be the complete Fej\'er five-term starting threshold in the pinned ProveIt source. For every real $0<\delta\le\tfrac12$, we prove
\[
 H_{\fej}(\delta)
 <2^{\,2^{\delta^{-2^{76}}}}
 <2^{\,2^{\delta^{-2^{16384}}}}
 =T_{\pap}(\delta),
\]
where $T_{\pap}$ is the five-term numerical threshold in Gowers' Theorem~18.2, with its explicitly right-associated power convention. A stronger intermediate estimate is
\[
 \log_2\log_2 H_{\fej}(\delta)\le x^{2^{67}},
 \qquad x=2/\alpha,\quad \alpha=(\delta^5/64000)^{16}.
\]
The proof expands the full numerical Fourier threshold, including both finite spectral maxima, the zero-spectrum convention, the integer Bohr-radius ceiling, the recurrence branch, and both square thresholds. It then controls all local Fej\'er constants and the complete density iteration. A standard-library companion checks finite arithmetic and pinned-source integrity without evaluating the enormous real expressions.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small\raggedright
\textbf{Scope.} This is a real-variable comparison at commit
\filename{af74fb522c24a6331886b11db76942642a6a0e42}.
The progression consequence uses an inspected source theorem as an input. No independent Lean-kernel check, complete imported-theorem audit, optimality, modern literature-best bound, or priority claim is made.
\end{quote}
Quantitative density-increment arguments combine many expressions that are individually explicit but grow at very different rates. Improving a local exponent does not by itself establish that the final sufficient starting length is below a stated numerical threshold. One must also bound every common starting condition and then propagate the result through the density iteration. The purpose of this report is to carry out that entire numerical comparison for the five-term Fej\'er construction at one fixed source revision.

Throughout, the repository is \href{https://github.com/VladimirReshetnikov/ProveIt/tree/af74fb522c24a6331886b11db76942642a6a0e42}{VladimirReshetnikov/ProveIt}, pinned at the commit on the title page. We write
\begin{align}
 H_{\fej}(\delta)&=\filename{fejerFiveTermThreshold}\,(\delta),\label{gsr:fm:86:eq:Hsource}\\
 T_{\pap}(\delta)&=\filename{szemerediThreshold}\,(\delta,5).
 \label{gsr:fm:86:eq:Tsource}
\end{align}
These names refer to finite expressions, not least possible sufficient lengths. Sections~\ref{gsr:fz:86:sec:geometric}--\ref{gsr:fz:86:sec:exactlocal} give their complete numerical reductions relevant here.

\begin{theorem}[Complete five-term envelope]\label{gsr:fm:86:thm:main}
For every real $0<\delta\le\tfrac12$, let
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:86:eq:alpha-x}
 \alpha=\left(\frac{\delta^5}{64000}\right)^{16},
 \qquad x=\frac2\alpha.
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:86:eq:intermediate}
 \log_2\log_2 H_{\fej}(\delta)\le x^{2^{67}},
\end{equation}
and consequently
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:86:eq:main}
 H_{\fej}(\delta)
 <2^{\,2^{\delta^{-2^{76}}}}
 <T_{\pap}(\delta)
 =2^{\,2^{\delta^{-2^{16384}}}}.
\end{equation}
All powers are ordinary real powers with positive bases. Both inequalities in~\eqref{gsr:fm:86:eq:main} are strict, including at $\delta=\tfrac12$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{writenote}[7 October 2026; sources 82--94]
\emph{Superseded by a formal theorem} (checked at HEAD \texttt{bf285410b}). After this source arrived the repository proved \file{fejerFiveTermThreshold_le_explicit_tower} with the inner exponent $2^{76}$ (\texttt{0d0033b0f}, 7~October 2026, 12:17; the commit names no source) and then $2^{73}$ (\texttt{3f61aea0a}, 12:59): at HEAD, $H_{\mathrm f}(\delta)\le2^{2^{\delta^{-2^{73}}}}$ for $0<\delta\le1/2$ (\file{Proofs18FiveTermSourceThreshold.lean}, line~12), which implies \eqref{gsr:fm:86:eq:main} with room to spare, and \file{theorem_18_2_five_holds} (line~100) is the exact five-term instance of Theorem~18.2. The intermediate estimate \eqref{gsr:fm:86:eq:intermediate} and the proof below remain this source's; this source records correctly the formal state at its own status check (Section~\ref{gsr:fz:86:sec:d11}).
\end{writenote}

The exponent $2^{76}$ is a deliberately conservative envelope. Its role is to make the complete proof short enough to check while retaining a very large separation from $2^{16384}$. We do not assert that $76$ is the smallest possible exponent label. The proof also establishes the intermediate estimate for $0<\delta\le1$; the restriction to $\delta\le\tfrac12$ is used in the final density-only conversion and agrees with the paper's stated range.

\subsection{Association in the paper's power chain}\label{gsr:fm:86:sec:paper}
Gowers' paper~\cite{gowers} introduces $a\uparrow b$ to mean $a^b$ and explicitly associates repeated arrows to the right. Its Theorem~18.2 gives the numerical threshold
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:86:eq:paperchain}
 2\uparrow2\uparrow\delta^{-1}\uparrow2\uparrow2\uparrow(k+9)
 =2^{\,2^{(\delta^{-1})^{\,2^{2^{k+9}}}}}.
\end{equation}
For $k=5$, $k+9=14$ and $2^{14}=16384$. Thus the exponent applied to $\delta^{-1}$ is $2^{16384}$, which proves the final equality in~\eqref{gsr:fm:86:eq:main}. Formula~\eqref{gsr:fm:86:eq:paperchain} is a power chain with a density-dependent base at one position; an unparenthesized description of its height would obscure the comparison.

The association and statement were checked against printed page~585 of the original paper (PDF page~121), the pinned TeX transcription, and the source definition in \srceightysix{Sections17_18}{\filename{Sections17_18.lean}}. The numerical source definition agrees with~\eqref{gsr:fm:86:eq:paperchain}. In the same file, \filename{theorem_18_2} is a \emph{Prop-valued definition of the target statement}. The name alone does not turn that declaration into a proved Lean theorem.

\subsection{A conditional progression consequence}\label{gsr:fm:86:sec:consequence}
For a finite set $A\subseteq\N$ and $k\in\N$, write $\operatorname{AP}_k(A)$ if there exist $a,d\in\N$ with $d>0$ and
\[
 a+id\in A\qquad\text{for every }i\in\N\text{ with }i<k.
\]
This is the source's \srceightysix{Definitions}{\filename{HasNatAP}} convention. In particular a five-term progression has a positive common difference.

\begin{proposition}[Inspected source implication]\label{gsr:fm:86:prop:imported}
Taking the inspected \href{https://github.com/VladimirReshetnikov/ProveIt/blob/af74fb522c24a6331886b11db76942642a6a0e42/Combinatorics/Ramsey/Lean/GowersSzemeredi/Proofs18FejerFiveTerm.lean\#L18-L27}{source theorem} and its imported mathematical inputs as given, the following implication holds. If $0<\delta\le1$, $N\in\N$, and $A$ is a finite subset of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:86:eq:sourcehyp}
 |A|\ge\delta N,\qquad H_{\fej}(\delta)\le N,
\end{equation}
then $\operatorname{AP}_5(A)$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{corollary}[A density-only sufficient length]\label{gsr:fm:86:cor:ap}
Under the imported-theorem qualification of Proposition~\ref{gsr:fm:86:prop:imported}, let $0<\delta\le\tfrac12$ and $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ have $|A|\ge\delta N$. If
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:86:eq:sufficient}
 N\ge2^{\,2^{\delta^{-2^{76}}}},
\end{equation}
then $A$ contains a nonconstant five-term arithmetic progression. For every integer $1\le k\le5$, its first $k$ terms give $\operatorname{AP}_k(A)$ under the same sufficient length.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
Theorem~\ref{gsr:fm:86:thm:main} and~\eqref{gsr:fm:86:eq:sufficient} imply $H_{\fej}(\delta)<N$, hence~\eqref{gsr:fm:86:eq:sourcehyp}. Apply Proposition~\ref{gsr:fm:86:prop:imported}. The prefix claim uses the same $a,d$ and the implication $i<k\le5\Rightarrow i<5$.
\end{proof}

The prefix observation is not a new optimization for shorter progressions and does not compare this envelope with any separate four-term construction. Section~\ref{gsr:fz:86:sec:chain} records the precise imported chain. The analytic inequalities in Theorem~\ref{gsr:fm:86:thm:main} are proved below independently of whether that chain has been compiled.

\begin{partabstract}{87}
For every integer $k\ge1$, the unasserted proposition
\filename{Section16ContextualLiftAt k} at the pinned ProveIt revision is false, even at the endpoint $\gamma=1$. Set
\[
 K=2^{\,2^{\,2^{k+9}}},\qquad \theta=\frac1{32K},\qquad
 N_*=(2^{26}K^6)^{2K}.
\]
For every prime $N\ge N_*$ we construct a partial function on a slab
$\F_N^k\times E$ of density at least the fixed positive constant $\theta$. It satisfies the original weighted product property, all proper-face and arrangement hypotheses, and every field of the actual common-base data structure. One admissible witness fails the demanded unit cover: on the box $E^{k+1}$ every permitted cover reaches at most $5/16$ of the points, although at least $1/2$ must be retained. A second admissible witness for the same input selects a modal colour class and has a constant graph. The obstruction therefore concerns the universal quantifier over witnesses; it leaves existential selection and Theorem~16.2 unresolved. We give all constants and field checks, a conditional existential repair, and an offline exact-arithmetic companion.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small\raggedright
\textbf{Scope and credit.} This is an ordinary-mathematical counterexample at commit
\filename{130fca9b1131fd983bd0af27565d36e8dfd2865a}.
An earlier unnumbered note already gives a $k=1$, $0<\gamma<1$ universal-witness obstruction. The endpoint, all-dimensional positive-density construction and its paired witnesses are the advances studied here. No new Lean compilation, upstream modification, or refutation of a global theorem is claimed.
\end{quote}
The final stage of the recorded Section~16 induction asks for a unit-parameter multiply-linear graph on a selected common-base domain. There are two logically different tasks: prove that every compatible selection works, or construct one selection that works. The interface examined here demands the former. The construction below satisfies its complete upstream hypotheses, produces a bad compatible selection, and then produces a good compatible selection from the same input.

All source names in this report refer to the repository
\href{https://github.com/VladimirReshetnikov/ProveIt/tree/130fca9b1131fd983bd0af27565d36e8dfd2865a}{VladimirReshetnikov/ProveIt} at the title-page revision. The precise target is a definition of a proposition, explicitly described in its source as unasserted. It is not an unconditional theorem declaration. Let $\CB_{\theta,\gamma}(B,\phi)$ denote its common-base data type, let $B_1(D)$ be a witness's good domain, and let $\phi_1(D)$ be its all-ones translated vertex map. The contract has the order
\begin{align}
 &\forall\,0<\theta,\gamma\le1\quad\exists N_0\quad
 \forall\text{ prime }N\ge N_0\quad\forall B,\phi,\notag\\[-2pt]
 &\qquad \PPop_\gamma(B,\phi)\ \land\ \SP_{\theta,\gamma}(B,\phi)
 \ \Longrightarrow\
 \forall D\in\CB_{\theta,\gamma}(B,\phi),\
 \ML_{\gamma,1}\bigl(B_1(D),\phi_1(D)\bigr).
 \label{gsr:fm:87:eq:universal}
\end{align}
Here $B\subseteq\F_N^{k+1}$, and $\phi$ is a total ambient function whose graph is tested only over $B$. This transcription preserves the decisive final universal quantifier; see \srclineeightyseven{Proofs16ContextualInduction}{17}{the exact source contract}.

\begin{theorem}[Endpoint obstruction with paired witnesses]\label{gsr:fm:87:thm:main}
Fix an integer $k\ge1$, put $d=k+1$, and define
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:87:eq:mainconst}
 A_j=2^{2^{j+8}},\quad K=2^{A_d},\quad R=4K,\quad
 \theta=\frac1{8R},\quad \gamma=1,\quad N_*=(2^{26}K^6)^{2K}.
\end{equation}
For every prime $N\ge N_*$, there exist $B\subseteq\F_N^d$, a function
$\phi:\F_N^d\to\F_N$, and two witnesses
$D_{\rm bad},D_{\rm good}\in\CB_{\theta,1}(B,\phi)$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $B=\F_N^k\times E$ for an interval $E$ with
$\theta\le |E|/N\le1/(4R)$, and $(B,\phi)$ satisfies the exact weighted product property and all three structured-pair conditions
\item $B_1(D_{\rm bad})=B$ and $\phi_1(D_{\rm bad})=\phi$; the required $\ML_{1,1}$ conclusion fails on the proper box $E^d$
\item $B_1(D_{\rm good})=\F_N^k\times E_c$, with $|E_c|\ge |E|/R$, and $\phi_1(D_{\rm good})$ is constant on its good domain, so the exact $\ML_{1,1}$ conclusion holds
\end{enumerate}
Consequently \filename{Section16ContextualLiftAt k} is false for every $k\ge1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{writenote}[7 October 2026; sources 82--94]
\emph{Formally refuted since, along this construction} (checked at HEAD \texttt{bf285410b}). \file{section16_contextual_lift_counterexample} (\file{Proofs16ContextualLiftCounterexample.lean}, line~80; \texttt{48efbb992}, 7~October 2026, 12:00) proves $\neg$\,\file{Section16ContextualLiftAt}~$k$ for every $k\ge1$ by instantiating the contract at $\gamma=1$, and the repository's status record names this source (``Report~299'') as its model; the contract is at line~20 of \file{Proofs16ContextualInduction.lean} at HEAD (line~17 at this source's pin). The formal witness also keeps a further unit domain of the required source mass, the analogue of the good witness here. \emph{Credit}: the earlier note of the paragraph below is this report's source~74 (Section~\ref{gsr:en:sec:endpointlift}).
\end{writenote}

\paragraph{What remains open.}
The theorem does not disprove an existential version of~\eqref{gsr:fm:87:eq:universal}; part~3 shows that the particular inputs here satisfy such a version. It does not refute the recorded Theorem~16.2, whose target allows a larger iteration parameter and an existential restriction of a relation. Nor does it invalidate source theorems conditional on the false universal premise: their implications remain implications. Section~\ref{gsr:en:87:sec:repair} states a precise existential replacement and proves only its conditional sufficiency for the existing induction route.

\paragraph{Relationship to earlier work.}
The unnumbered note \emph{Sparse defects survive the recorded product-property interfaces}, dated 7 October 2026, already constructs, for each fixed $0<\gamma<1$, a full-domain $k=1$ example satisfying the stronger recorded data and failing the unit conclusion. Its arbitrary word is localized to an interval of length $\lfloor N^{1/3}\rfloor$; the defect density tends to zero. It therefore already establishes a universal-witness obstruction. The present contribution is the exact endpoint $\gamma=1$, every $k\ge1$, positive slab density independent of $N$, and the explicit bad/good pair for the same input. The balanced-word concentration argument and finite-alphabet cover estimate are existing ingredients in the pinned source, not newly discovered lemmas. Section~\ref{gsr:en:87:sec:comparison} explains the distinction in more detail.

Its `question' environment (``Research question'', on the shared counter) is set as this report's `Research question'. Its sections carry no labels; the concordance gives their places.}
\begin{partabstract}{88}
We strengthen the configuration and cube-pair inputs in Section~14 of
Gowers' proof of Szemer\'edi's theorem. The configuration argument needs
only $3^{k-1}$ determining restrictions at the $k$th induction step,
giving the frequency exponent $8(4^k-3^k)$ in place of $2k4^k$.
A direct cube-pair construction needs only $2^{k-1}$ reference
restrictions and yields the smaller exponent $4(4^k-2^k)$.
Both results hold on products of arbitrary finite abelian groups with
arbitrary abelian targets. A two-orientation argument proves the
homogeneous weighted inequality
\[
 \mathcal C_k(w)\ge |X|^3
 \left(\E_Xw^{2^{1-k}}\right)^{4^k}
 \gamma^{4(4^k-2^k)}
 \qquad(w\ge0).
\]
We give exact integral bases for the constraint systems, prove optimal
local raw-test counts, optimize unequal coordinate parameters, and
show that the configuration density exponent and its coefficient are
optimal. Coupling the stronger cube bound with the project's existing
collision amplification gives
$a_8\ge\beta^{22\cdot4^k}\gamma^{88\cdot4^k-32\cdot2^k}$.
We carry this input through the existing degree-weighted selection
theorem with every size and characteristic hypothesis stated, obtaining
a strictly stronger extraction for $k\ge2$ when $0<\gamma<1$.
Full proofs, exact finite
diagnostics, source comparisons, and further research questions are
included. The resulting local quantitative improvements are not a
new final bound for Szemer\'edi's theorem.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small\raggedright
Repository comparison: commit \texttt{6d494222250c}\\
Proof status: mathematical proofs and exact finite checks; no new Lean certification.
\end{quote}
\label{gsr:fm:88:sec:introduction}

The product property in Section~14 of Gowers' proof turns simultaneous
one-dimensional additive information into many respected multidimensional
arrangements. Its importance is quantitative: a loss at the configuration
stage is raised to further powers when one forms higher arrangements and
then restricts to a domain on which almost every arrangement is respected.
This article improves that first loss and carries the improvement through
an explicit version of the next restriction step.

There are two different counting problems. A \emph{configuration} requires
all coordinate parallelogram identities. A \emph{parallel cube pair}
requires only equality of two top mixed differences. Gowers bounds the
second count by injecting respected configurations into respected cube
pairs. We improve the configuration argument and then prove a stronger
bound for cube pairs directly. The distinction is responsible for the two
different exponents below.

\subsection{The three quantitative changes}

Suppose that $B$ has density $\beta>0$ in a product of $k$ finite abelian
groups of total size $M$, and that $\phi:B\to V$ has the product property
with parameter $\gamma\in(0,1]$; the precise definition is given in
Section~\ref{gsr:en:88:sec:notation}. Let $\mathcal F_k$ and $\mathcal C_k$ count
respected configurations and respected ordered parallel cube pairs.
We prove
\begin{align}
 \mathcal F_k&\ge
 M^3\beta^{4^k}\gamma^{8(4^k-3^k)},
 \label{gsr:fm:88:eq:intro-configuration}\\
 \mathcal C_k&\ge
 M^3\beta^{4^k}\gamma^{4(4^k-2^k)}.
 \label{gsr:fm:88:eq:intro-cubes}
\end{align}
The earlier exponent in both places was $2k4^k$
\cite[Section~14]{gowers}. Both improvements are strict for $k\ge2$
when $0<\gamma<1$. The first bound uses exactly $3^{k-1}$ determining
vertices in an induction step, in place of $4^{k-1}$. The second uses
only the $2^{k-1}$ vertices of one reference cube. These statements are
proved in Theorems~\ref{gsr:en:88:count:configuration} and~\ref{gsr:en:88:count:cubepairs}.

For the arrangement application, write the domain as $X\times T$, where
$X$ has $k$ coordinate factors, $|X|=M$, and $|T|=n$.
Let $R_d$ be the number of respected ordered $d$-arrangements of
$k$-cubes, and normalize
\[
 a_d=\frac{R_d}{M^{2d+1}n^{2d-1}}.
\]
Combining \eqref{gsr:fm:88:eq:intro-cubes} with the collision-sensitive
amplification already established in the project \cite{srcfifteen} gives
the following new consequence for every integer $d\ge2$:
\begin{equation}
 \boxed{\quad
 a_d\ge
 \beta^{(3d-2)4^k}
 \gamma^{(12d-8)4^k-4d\,2^k}.
 \quad}
 \label{gsr:fm:88:eq:intro-arrangements}
\end{equation}
All the counting and interpolation steps needed for this combination
are proved in Section~\ref{gsr:en:88:sec:arrangements}. For $d=8$, this reads
\begin{equation}
 a_8\ge\beta^{22\cdot4^k}
              \gamma^{88\cdot4^k-32\cdot2^k}.
 \label{gsr:fm:88:eq:intro-eight}
\end{equation}
The prior project bound has the same density exponent but the larger
frequency exponent $44k4^k+56\cdot2^k$ \cite{srcfifteen}. The gain over
that bound is exactly
\begin{equation}
 \gamma^{-44((k-2)4^k+2^{k+1})}.
 \label{gsr:fm:88:eq:intro-gain}
\end{equation}
It is one at $k=1$ and greater than one at every $k\ge2$ if
$\gamma<1$.

\subsection{Weights, unequal coordinates, and exact local rank}

The cube-pair theorem has a homogeneous weighted form. If $w:X\to[0,\infty)$
is supported on $B$, and each occurrence of a vertex contributes a factor
$w$ to the pair count, then
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal C_k(w)\ge
 M^3\left(\E_{x\in X}w(x)^{2^{1-k}}\right)^{4^k}
 \gamma^{4(4^k-2^k)}.
 \label{gsr:fm:88:eq:intro-weighted}
\end{equation}
The total degree in $w$ on both sides is $2^{k+1}$. Arbitrarily large
weights are permitted; there is no hidden unit-bound hypothesis.
The proof pairs two injective constructions and uses their geometric
mean. This is the reason for the fractional moment in
\eqref{gsr:fm:88:eq:intro-weighted}.

If coordinate $j$ has its own parameter $\gamma_j$, the factor in
\eqref{gsr:fm:88:eq:intro-weighted} becomes, for any ordering $\pi$,
\begin{equation}
 \prod_{i=1}^k
 \gamma_{\pi(i)}^{8\,2^{i-1}4^{k-i}}.
 \label{gsr:fm:88:eq:intro-anisotropic}
\end{equation}
The strongest bound within these induction orders puts the largest
$\gamma_j$ first. More general product-property coefficients lead to a
finite assignment problem, with no assumption that all possible family
sizes satisfy the same estimate.

The exact rank statement behind the configuration improvement is also
useful independently. The universal abelian group of labels on the
$4^r$ vertices of a product of $r$ parallelograms, subject to all
coordinate-face identities, is free of rank $3^r$.
The $3^r$ vertices having local states $00,10,01$ form a basis.
Section~\ref{gsr:en:88:sec:rank} proves this integrally, extends it to products
of unit-pivot relations, and identifies the limitation of merely
computing rank over a field. This is an exact optimality statement for
the local determining family. It does not assert that the final
counting exponents are optimal.

\subsection{Propagation through the next extraction step}

For the finite-field restriction step, take $d=8$, put
\begin{equation}
 s=2^{k+4},\qquad
 A_k=22\cdot4^k-15,\qquad
 B_k=88\cdot4^k-32\cdot2^k,
 \label{gsr:fm:88:eq:intro-AB}
\end{equation}
and let $\F_q$ have characteristic $p$.
The degree-weighted selector in source~35 of the project
\cite{srcthirtyfive}, with bandwidth
\[
 L=\left\lceil 2^{44}(s+1)\beta^{-A_k}\gamma^{-B_k}\right\rceil,
\]
produces a subset $B'\subseteq B$ with respected proportion at least
$1-2^{-44}$ and at least
\begin{equation}
 \frac{2^{-44(s-1)-1}}{(s+2)^s}
 \beta^{sA_k+15}\gamma^{sB_k}q^{17k+15}
 \label{gsr:fm:88:eq:intro-selection}
\end{equation}
respected eight-arrangements, provided its explicit field-size
conditions and $p>2(L-1)$ hold. Section~\ref{gsr:en:88:sec:selection} states every
condition and verifies the substitution. It also compares this output
with the same selector applied to the earlier source~15 bound; thus
the comparison isolates the new counting gain.

For example, at $k=2$, the exponent on $\gamma$ after this selection
drops from $104448$ to $81920$, with the same exponent $21583$ on
$\beta$ and the same leading numerical constant. The bandwidth and
field-size requirements also become weaker. As $k\to\infty$, the
frequency exponent in the retained count is asymptotic to
$1408\cdot8^k$, compared with $704k8^k$ for the preceding
coupled input. Precise interpretations of the field-size comparison
are given in the selection section.

\subsection{Scope, provenance, and evidence}

The repository comparison is pinned to commit
\nolinkurl{6d494222250ce2d8616435cec118d74e493b95b5}, inspected on
7~October 2026 \cite{repo88}. Its merged research source has Git
blob identifier \nolinkurl{f4e5705da5d349256757ee7063c6a4480638d0d2}.
The local copy used for the audit was verified to have this exact Git
object identifier. Source~15 still uses $2k4^k$ in its configuration
and cube-pair input and explicitly asks about better product-property
amplification and its preservation through later extraction.
The present article supplies a strict improvement to that input and a
complete propagation through one adjoining selection interface.

The Fourier moment interpolation and its collision coupling are prior
results of the project; they are rederived here to make the new
consequence auditable. The degree-weighted selection theorem is also
an attributed prior input. The new contributions are the two counting
recurrences, the homogeneous weighted cube-pair inequality, their
coordinate-dependent forms, the exact determining-family treatment,
and the resulting stronger quantitative composition.

The article does not establish a new final bound for Szemer\'edi's
theorem. The subsequent multilinear modeling and density-increment
iteration remain to be propagated. Nor does a comparison with this
repository establish historical priority in the wider literature.
The proofs below are mathematical proofs, accompanied by exact finite
checks; no new Lean kernel certification is claimed.

\begin{partabstract}{89}
The phase-removal step in Gowers's proof of Szemer\'edi's theorem is particularly
transparent when a symmetric multilinear tensor can be integrated to a polynomial
phase. In small characteristic, symmetry alone ceases to suffice. We establish a
lossless localization theorem that separates this algebraic obstruction from the
analytic extraction of uniformity.

At the first obstructed degree, $d=p+1$ over $V=\F_p^n$, associate to a symmetric
$d$-linear tensor $T$ the alternating bilinear form
$\defectD_T(x,y)=T(x^p,y)-T(x,y^p)$, where superscripts indicate repeated arguments.
If $\rank\defectD_T=2r$, the largest subspace on which $T$ has a nonclassical
polynomial primitive has dimension exactly $n-r$. On every such subspace $H$,
a single primitive $P_H$ gives the inequality
\[
 \ET_T(f)\leq
 \left(\E_{c\in V/H}
 \norm{f(c+\cdot)\e(-P_H)}_{U^{p+1}(H)}^{\,2^{p+1}/(p+2)}\right)^{p+2}.
\]
Here $\ET_T$ is the normalized selected-derivative Fourier-square energy.
Consequently one coset preserves all of this energy, and a quantitatively large
set of cosets preserves a prescribed fraction. The constant and moment exponent
are sharp. The result also holds for mixed cube correlations.

We give a self-contained critical-degree integration construction, an exact normal
form modulo integrable tensors, the optimal number $2r$ of coordinates supporting
a correction, exact counts of maximal repair subspaces, and an exact rank-sensitive
repeated-variable test. A higher-degree extension uses the common isotropy of an
explicit pencil of alternating forms and the established general integration
theorem of Tidor. The new analytic proofs use finite differences,
Gowers--Cauchy--Schwarz, and Young's inequality, not an inverse theorem.
No improved global Szemer\'edi or Ramsey-number bound is asserted.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small\raggedright
\noindent\textbf{Status.} A proved research draft, with exact finite checks supplied
separately; not independently refereed and not Lean-verified. The general
nonclassical integration criterion and the characteristic-two antecedents are
credited explicitly. The principal contribution proposed for integration is the
rank-exact, lossless localization package, not a claim to have discovered
nonclassical integration.
\end{quote}
\label{gsr:fm:89:sec:introduction}

\subsection{The phase-removal interface}
In Section 17 of \cite{gowers}, a structured choice of a Fourier coefficient of
an iterated derivative is converted into a polynomial twist with large lower-order
uniformity. Proposition 17.2 is the global model of this step; Proposition 17.7
localizes it to progressions. The corrected ProveIt statement of Proposition 17.2
uses a polynomial of degree at most $k+1$, where the Fourier selector has $k$
arguments, and makes factorial invertibility explicit \cite{repo89lean}.

We study the finite-vector-space model with $d=k+1$. A homogeneous selector
$\sigma:V^{d-1}\to V^*$ determines a tensor
\[
 T(h_1,\ldots,h_d)=\sigma(h_1,\ldots,h_{d-1})(h_d).
\]
Our theorems assume that this \emph{entire} tensor, including its evaluation slot,
is symmetric. Producing that symmetry from a partly structured selector is a
separate problem. Also, the repository's predicate \texttt{IsMultilinear} allows
multiaffine lower-order terms; it must not be silently identified with the
homogeneous multiadditivity used here.

For $d<p$, polarization integrates a symmetric tensor by division by $d!$.
At $d=p$ this formula fails, but nonclassical phases still integrate every
symmetric tensor. At $d=p+1$, even nonclassical integration has an obstruction.
The distinction between ordinary symmetry and the required repeated-variable
symmetry is classical in this subject; the complete nonclassical integration criterion was established
by Tidor, building on Tao--Ziegler \cite{tidor,taozieglerlow}. Our starting question is
more quantitative:
\begin{quote}
When the global tensor is not integrable, how large a subspace can repair it,
and how much selected-derivative energy must be lost in making that repair?
\end{quote}
The critical-degree answer is: delete exactly half the rank of one explicit
alternating form, and lose no energy on at least one coset. The stronger quotient
moment inequality explains how many useful cosets remain.

\subsection{What is established here, and what is not}
The central statements are theorems~\ref{gsr:fp:89:thm:localization}, \ref{gsr:fp:89:thm:critical}, \ref{gsr:fp:89:thm:normal} and \ref{gsr:fp:89:thm:all-degree}. Their proofs yield four complementary conclusions.
First, algebraic repair is measured exactly by an ordinary matrix rank.
Second, a common primitive works on all cosets of the repair subspace.
Third, the analytic loss is controlled by a sharp moment rather than a
pigeonhole factor equal to the number of cosets. Fourth, the same argument
extends to all degrees once the appropriate mixed Frobenius defects vanish.

The critical-degree integrability criterion itself is a special case of
\cite[Proposition 3.5]{tidor}, not a new theorem of integration. The symplectic
linear algebra used to optimize the repair is standard. Repository sources
36, 43, and 46 already examine symmetry, Boolean nonclassical integration, and
Boolean energy obstructions \cite{repo89research,repo89boolean}. In particular, the
half-rank repair in characteristic two has an antecedent there. The present
extension treats every prime, proves the sharp quotient-moment localization,
and distinguishes ordinary isotropy from the mixed isotropy required at higher
degrees. Priority for the precise combined statements is not claimed on the basis
of this limited literature search.

The result does not supply a bound for the obstruction rank in terms of the
energy. That is a separate and important problem. It also does not transfer a
vector-space subspace automatically to a long progression in a cyclic group.
Accordingly, no downstream improvement of the numerical bounds in Gowers's
Theorem 18.1, Szemer\'edi's theorem, or a Ramsey-number estimate follows without
additional work.

\begin{partabstract}{90}
We prove exact local results at two interfaces of Gowers' proof of
Szemer\'edi's theorem: Fourier detection from a missing interval and
conversion of directional derivative collisions into additive graph
energy. For probability measures on the circle avoiding an open arc of
radius \(a\), we determine the complete four-frequency minimax function
\(\Phi_4(a)\), including a new algebraic branch with four support points,
all transition radii, and uniqueness without an imposed symmetry.
For every cutoff \(R\ge3\), we identify the maximal first interval on
which the cutoff-\((R-1)\) extremizer remains optimal for cutoff \(R\).
Its width is \(8\pi R^{-3}+O(R^{-4})\); its final height is an explicit
radical, also characterized as the sharp positivity ceiling for a
signed Fourier-moment prescription.

On the new four-frequency branch, a split-root polynomial gives an
exact finite-grid correction and a positive factorization of the gap
from the continuous optimum. At the semicircle radius, we obtain a
closed formula for every \(4\mid N\), \(N\ge8\), and convergent
expansions to every order on each residue class modulo twelve.
The same continuous certificate yields explicit Wasserstein stability
with the optimal square-root exponent.

For every map \(f:C_N\to W\) into an abelian group and every \(N\ge12\),
let \(d_h\) be its derivative collision defect in direction \(h\), and
let \(D=N^{-1}\sum_h d_h\). We prove the sharp inequality
\(D\le (N+1)d_1/6\). We classify every equality case: besides affine
maps, exactly the maps with one exceptional cyclic increment occur.
The proof uses an exact overlap identity for circular windows.

These results extend the explicitly audited ProveIt research corpus.
Prior first-window and last-window Fourier results are credited and
their use is isolated. Complete mathematical proofs are accompanied
by exact algebraic checks and independent finite optimizations.
We do not infer a new global quantitative Szemer\'edi bound from these
local improvements.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small\raggedright
\noindent\textbf{Mathematical status.}
This is an AI-assisted research manuscript for mathematical review.
The stated theorems have written proofs; supplementary computations
are not proof-assistant formalizations or external peer review.
Claims of extension are relative to the pinned project sources
specified in Appendix~\ref{gsr:fz:90:app:provenance}; broader priority is not
established by the source audit.
\end{quote}
\label{gsr:fm:90:sec:intro}

\subsection{Two precise problems}

The usefulness of a quantitative lemma depends on both its conclusion
and the cost of reaching its hypotheses. We focus on two points where
that cost can be isolated exactly.

The first concerns Fourier detection. Gowers' Lemma~5.2 turns the
absence of an interval into a nonzero Fourier coefficient at a
controlled frequency \cite[Lemma~5.2]{gowers}. Its proof selects a
particular convolution kernel and estimates the Fourier tail.
Once the number of frequencies is prescribed, a natural stronger
question asks for the best universal coefficient guarantee over
\emph{all} nonnegative weights with the specified missing arc.
This question is an extremal moment problem. A sharp answer requires
both a universal lower certificate and an admissible measure attaining
it.

For a probability measure \(\mu\) on
\(\T=\R/(2\pi\Z)\), write
\[
 \widehat\mu(j)=\int e^{-ij\theta}\,d\mu(\theta),\qquad
 E_R(\mu)=\max_{1\le j\le R}|\widehat\mu(j)|.
\]
For \(0<a\le\pi\), put
\[
 K_a=\{\theta:|\theta|_\circ\ge a\},\qquad
 \Phi_R(a)=\min_{\mu\in\mathcal P(K_a)}E_R(\mu).
\]
The minimum exists by compactness. The interval removed is open,
so the two boundary points are allowed. Reflection of \(\mu\)
conjugates its Fourier coefficients; averaging a measure with its
reflection cannot increase \(E_R\). Thus an even minimizer exists.
This reduction alone does not prove that every minimizer is even;
the equality analysis below establishes the stronger uniqueness
assertions.

The second problem concerns additive graph energy.
Gowers' Lemma~6.2 expresses additive quadruples of a graph through
additive relations satisfied by its defining function
\cite[Lemma~6.2]{gowers}. For a full-domain function on a cycle,
we ask how accurately a single generating direction controls the
average over all directions. This is a finite combinatorial problem:
the correct sharp coefficient depends on consistency between all
derivatives of the same function.

\subsection{Main conclusions}

Theorem~\ref{gsr:dt:90:thm:four} gives a complete seven-piece formula for
\(\Phi_4(a)\). One transition has the exact algebraic description
\[
 c_*=\frac{\sqrt{25-4\sqrt{33}}-1}{\sqrt{33}-3},
 \qquad a_*=\arccos c_*=0.4508760097\ldots\,\pi.
\]
The new algebraic phase occupies
\(a_*\le a\le3\pi/5\).
Its extremizer has two cosine coordinates, one at the boundary
\(c=\cos a\) and one interior coordinate \(v(c)\) determined by a
cubic equation. The active Fourier signs are \((-,-,+)\) at
frequencies \((1,2,4)\). The third constraint is strictly inactive
between the phase endpoints. In particular,
\[
 \boxed{\Phi_4(\pi/2)=\frac{\sqrt3-1}{2}.}
\]
This is a statement about the best weighted guarantee, together with
its unique extremizer, rather than an estimate for a selected family
of test measures.

Theorem~\ref{gsr:dt:90:thm:continuation} extends the phase analysis to every
cutoff. If
\[
 X_R(a)=-\cot(a/2)\tan(Ra/2),\qquad
 \xi_R=\frac{\sqrt{(R-1)(R+7)}-R-1}{2},
\]
then the first continuation ends exactly at
\(X_R(a_R)=\xi_R\), and
\[
 \Phi_R(a)=\Phi_{R-1}(a)=\frac1{R-1+X_R(a)}
 \quad\left(\frac{2\pi}{R+1}\le a\le a_R\right).
\]
The signed-moment ceiling in Theorem~\ref{gsr:dt:90:thm:signedmoment}
characterizes the endpoint independently of any missing arc:
the moment prescription
\[
 \widehat\mu(1)=\cdots=\widehat\mu(R-1)=-\rho,\qquad
 \widehat\mu(R)=\rho
\]
is feasible for a probability measure precisely when
\[
 0\le\rho\le
 \kappa_R=\frac2{R-3+\sqrt{(R-1)(R+7)}}.
\]
The measure at the ceiling is unique on the whole circle.

For a finite grid, Theorems~\ref{gsr:dt:90:thm:gridexact} and
\ref{gsr:dt:90:thm:gridgap} provide a finite list of algebraic feasibility tests
and an exact positive formula for the discretization gap.
These tests automatically hold for sufficiently fine cyclic grids,
uniformly on compact subintervals of the algebraic phase.
Theorems~\ref{gsr:dt:90:thm:semicircleexact} and
\ref{gsr:dt:90:thm:semicircleallorders} specialize this to a closed semicircle
formula and twelve residue-dependent analytic expansions.
Theorem~\ref{gsr:dt:90:thm:stability} controls the distance of every
near-optimal cosine distribution to the unique optimizer by
an explicit constant times the square root of its deficit.

Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:90:thm:cycle} proves, for \(N\ge12\),
\[
 \boxed{
 \frac1N\sum_{h\in C_N}
 \Pr_{x,y}[\Delta_h f(x)\ne\Delta_h f(y)]
 \le\frac{N+1}{6}
 \Pr_{x,y}[\Delta_1 f(x)\ne\Delta_1 f(y)].
 }
\]
Here \(\Delta_hf(x)=f(x+h)-f(x)\), and the target is any abelian
group. The optimal coefficient is attained by non-affine maps
whose increments are constant except at one cyclic edge.
Compared with the exact coefficient obtainable from generic
categorical cut expansion, the leading constant improves from
\(1/4\) to \(1/6\).

\subsection{What is being extended}

The baseline is the repository state specified in
Appendix~\ref{gsr:fz:90:app:provenance}, together with the relevant existing
research reports. In particular, the general first-window Fourier
formula was already established in source~37
\cite{srcthirtyseven}; the full cutoff-three profile, general last-window
formulas, and the order \(N^{-2}\) grid approximation were already
available \cite{extremallimits}. The unequal-budget first-window matrix
problem was treated separately \cite{srcsixtyseven}.
The present work develops the missing middle behavior and sharp
finite corrections. It does not relabel those earlier results as new.

\begin{center}
\small
\begin{tabular}{>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.26\textwidth}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.34\textwidth}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.29\textwidth}}
\toprule
Problem & Result here & Relationship to the baseline\\
\midrule
Fourier cutoff four
& Complete profile and all equality cases
& Resolves the algebraic middle phase and its junctions\\[4pt]
Arbitrary cutoff

& Quantifies the new branch's rigidity\\[4pt]

General expander-based homomorphism and affine testing are classical
\cite{shpilkawigderson}. The cyclic theorem concerns the particular
four-query derivative collision statistic above. Its sharp constant
and its equality classification require a separate proof; conclusions
for anchored homomorphism tests cannot be transferred by dropping
their hypotheses.

Nor does a local constant improvement, by itself, improve the best
known global progression-free-set bounds. For context, Leng, Sah,
and Sawhney prove for fixed \(k\ge5\) a bound of the form
\[
 r_k(N)\ll_k N\exp\bigl(-(\log\log N)^{c_k}\bigr)
 \qquad(c_k>0)
\]
\cite{lssbounds}, where \(r_k(N)\) is the largest size of a subset of
\(\{1,\ldots,N\}\) containing no nonconstant \(k\)-term arithmetic
progression. We make no improvement to that global bound here.
The local results below have independent extremal content; their
use in a global proof would require a complete parameter propagation.

\subsection{Guide to the proofs}

The Fourier proofs use elementary polynomial certificates.
After \(x=\cos\theta\), the Fourier modes of an even measure are
Chebyshev moments. A polynomial nonnegative on the allowed interval
supplies a lower bound; matching its contact points with a measure
supplies equality. The new quartic certificate has a double
interior root. Its root structure simultaneously explains the
algebraic phase, the finite-grid correction, and the stability exponent.
The general-cutoff transition instead follows by integrating the
known support-annihilating polynomial and imposing positivity on a
two-dimensional compression of the moment matrix.

The cyclic proof is combinatorial. Express each derivative as a
sum of consecutive increments around the cycle. If the increment
word has a majority value, all disagreement is caused by exceptional
positions. Exact probabilities for one marked position and for two
marked positions give a strengthened union bound. Every configuration
with at least two exceptional increments is strictly subextremal
when \(N\ge12\); one exceptional increment gives equality.

\begin{partabstract}{91}
Let $p$ be prime and $a\geq1$. A circle-valued polynomial on $\Fp^n$ first admits depth $a$ at degree $d_a=1+a(p-1)$. We determine exactly the loss in replacing correlation with such a phase by correlation with a polynomial of the same degree and depth at most $a-1$. The optimal factor is
\[
 c_{p,a}=\frac{\sin(\pi/p^a)}{p\sin(\pi/p^{a+1})}.
\]
The transfer is pointwise, hence valid for arbitrary nonnegative weights. It uses an explicit list of exactly $p$ lower-depth phases. No smaller fixed list can give even a positive uniform transfer factor; this follows from a cyclotomic field-degree obstruction. For uniform measure, every genuinely depth-$a$ critical-degree phase has maximum lower-depth correlation exactly $c_{p,a}$, and all maximizing phases are classified. A diagonal frame identity yields quantitative stability, exact score reconstruction, and an optimal square-root stability exponent. We also prove a simultaneous aggregate-energy version and give a one-pass selector.

At $a=1$, this sharpens the $p^{-1/2}$ conversion in the proof of Berger--Sah--Sawhney--Tidor's classical $U^{p+1}$ inverse theorem to $c_{p,1}$, strictly for odd $p$. The finite-difference algebra, transfer, optimality, and stability are proved here. The result is a small-characteristic extension of the phase-removal program around Section 17 of Gowers's proof, not a replacement for its different cyclic, factorial-invertible hypotheses and not a new end-to-end Szemer\'edi bound.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small\raggedright
\noindent\textbf{Status.} Unrefereed research draft. The attached exact and numerical checks have been run; the results have not been Lean-kernel verified. The sharp statements are proved below, but publication priority is not established by the limited literature audit.
\end{quote}

Gowers's proof of Szemer\'edi's theorem turns higher-order uniformity information into polynomial structure and then uses that structure in a density-increment argument \cite{gowers}. In the repository's corrected Section 17 interface, Proposition 17.2 removes a global frequency selector using a polynomial of degree at most $k+1$. Its ambient group is a cyclic prime field, and invertibility of $(k+1)!$ is an explicit hypothesis \cite{repo91lean}. Those assumptions are important: integration and phase removal behave differently in small characteristic.

The present paper studies a precise question on the other side of that characteristic restriction. Suppose a small-characteristic argument has already produced a polynomial phase with a denominator involving a power of $p$. How much correlation must survive when one removes its highest possible denominator layer, without increasing its additive degree? We solve that optimization problem at every degree where a new depth first appears.

There are three logically separate tasks in this part of higher-order Fourier analysis: obtaining a structured derivative selector, integrating it to a circle-valued polynomial, and converting the resulting phase to a desired value group. We address the third task. We do not assume that an arbitrary symmetric tensor is integrable, and we do not infer an inverse theorem merely from a conversion statement.

\subsection{What is known and what is sharpened}

Nonclassical polynomials and their role in the finite-field inverse theorem are established theory \cite{taononclassical,taozieglerlow}. Berger, Sah, Sawhney and Tidor proved that classical phases suffice for the $U^{p+1}$ inverse theorem; their proof converts a nonclassical degree-$p$ correlation $\varepsilon$ into a classical correlation at least $\varepsilon/\sqrt p$ \cite[Section 3]{bsst}. We replace that conversion factor by the exact constant $c_{p,1}$. The qualitative sufficiency of classical phases at this degree is not new.

The main quantitative package consists of a sharp norm comparison, a complete phase-endpoint classification, an optimally short fixed candidate list, and a stability theorem. The extension from depth one to every critical depth is not obtained by repeated application of the depth-one statement: it is a separate one-layer theorem at degree $1+a(p-1)$.

The analytic ingredient is an exact decomposition of a short arc of roots of unity into step phases. The algebraic ingredient is that, at the critical degree, the top residue of a polynomial is a single linear form. Both ingredients are elementary enough to prove fully. Their combination gives more than a generic Fourier-pigeonhole conversion: it computes the optimal constant and the optimal number of candidates.

\subsection{Repository overlap and limitations}

The inspected research index already covers phase-flat partitions, density extraction, arrangements, cube-count expansions, symmetry certification, and Boolean phase integration \cite{repo91index,repo91boolean}. We do not rederive those results. In particular, the Boolean work concerns integrability obstructions and derivative energies, whereas our main extremal problem compares an already existing phase with lower-depth phases.

The repository inspection used the explicit commit
\begin{center}\small\texttt{b9760ed931282087ee57cb1ffb66dc66e40ee47b}.\end{center}
No repository files or formalization ledger entries were modified. The proposed placement is a separate research directory beneath \reponinetyone; suggested interfaces appear in section~\ref{gsr:fz:91:sec:integration} and in \texttt{FORMALIZATION.md}.

\srcnote{92}{Section 1}

\begin{partabstract}{92}
We study the selected-derivative energy in the phase-removal step of Gowers's
proof of Szemer\'edi's theorem, with a symmetric multiadditive frequency tensor.
Every such tensor on a finite abelian group becomes the top derivative of a
circle-valued polynomial on an explicit finite abelian cover. Consequently,
the corresponding twisted cube energy is a power of a genuine norm. This
realization proves a sharp quotient-profile inequality and lossless phase
removal on cosets, without an integrability assumption on the original group.

For a symmetric $(p+1)$-linear form over $\F_p$, the first obstruction to
nonclassical integration is the alternating form
$B_T(a,b)=T(a^p,b)-T(a,b^p)$. If its rank is $2r$, we prove that the minimum
codimension of an integrable restriction is exactly $r$, while the minimum
kernel size of an integrating finite abelian cover is exactly $p^r$. We
classify all minimum covers and prove the exact joint tradeoff between
restriction and covering, also for simultaneous families through common
isotropic subspaces. The argument gives a dimension-independent
reduction of extremal energy to the canonical obstruction on $\F_p^2$.
For ternary quartic tensors, an exact enumeration gives the interval
$11/27\leq m_{3,1}\leq1099/2187$ and an all-dimensional integration certificate.
The lower endpoint is a conjectured optimum, not a proved one.

The integration criterion itself is a special case of Tidor's established
all-degree theorem; it is reproved constructively here. The principal targets
are optimal repair, the covering lower bound, and the lossless analytic
comparison. These results concern a finite-group model of Section~17; they do
not assert a new global bound for Szemer\'edi's theorem.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small\raggedright
\begin{center}
\small\textbf{Status.} Written proofs plus an exact finite computational certificate.
Unrefereed research draft; no new Lean verification is claimed.
\end{center}
\end{quote}

The final structural step in Gowers's argument passes from a selected Fourier
coefficient of a derivative of a bounded function to an untwisted uniformity
norm after multiplication by a polynomial phase
\cite[Section~17]{gowers}. In large characteristic, a symmetric multilinear
form can be integrated by division by a factorial. Two different questions
arise when that division is unavailable. Does the tensor integrate on its
original domain? When it does not, what is the exact cost of changing the
domain so that phase removal becomes possible?

The first question, for finite vector spaces and nonclassical polynomials,
has an established answer: the nonclassical symmetry identities characterize
top derivatives, as proved by Tidor \cite[Definition~3.1 and
Propositions~3.4--3.5]{tidor}, using the nonclassical polynomial framework of
Tao and Ziegler \cite{taozieglerlow}. Our purpose is not to rediscover that criterion.
Instead, we identify two optimal repairs and prove an analytic comparison
that makes them usable without further loss of selected energy.

\subsection{A precise source interface}

The relevant original statement is Proposition~17.2 of \cite{gowers}. With
$k$ derivative directions, its selected Fourier-square sum is normalized by
$N^{k+2}$. The resulting cube has dimension $d=k+1$. The printed proposition
says degree at most $k$, while the proof uses $k+1$; the inspected ProveIt
statement explicitly uses $k+1$ and records factorial-invertibility
hypotheses \cite{repo92lean}. We use $d$ throughout to avoid this shift of
index.

There is also a genuine restriction of scope. The tensors in this article
are \emph{homogeneous, multiadditive, and symmetric in all $d$ slots}, including
the slot in which the selected frequency is evaluated. The repository's
\texttt{IsMultilinear} interface allows a multiaffine expression, and its
frequency selector is not automatically a symmetric tensor in a vector-space
model. We do not silently replace that interface by ours. Symmetrization,
removal of lower-order terms, and localization to progressions remain separate
steps.

Within this stated scope, the results extend phase removal to every finite
abelian group by allowing a finite cover, and determine the exact additional
cost at the first degree where ordinary symmetry does not suffice even for
nonclassical integration.

\subsection{An optimal repair theorem}

Write $\iota:\F_p\to\T=\R/\Z$ for $\iota(t)=|t|/p\pmod1$, where
$|t|\in\{0,\ldots,p-1\}$ is the standard integer representative. For a
symmetric $(p+1)$-linear form $T:V^{p+1}\to\F_p$, put
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:92:eq:introB}
 B_T(a,b)=T(\underbrace{a,\ldots,a}_{p},b)
          -T(a,\underbrace{b,\ldots,b}_{p}).
\end{equation}
Here repeated arguments are denoted by $a^p$ when no confusion is possible.
This notation is not a tensor power in the codomain.

\begin{theorem}[Optimal restriction, covering, and their tradeoff]\label{gsr:fm:92:thm:mainrepair}
Let $p$ be any prime, let $V=\F_p^n$, and let $T:V^{p+1}\to\F_p$ be symmetric
and multilinear. The form $B_T$ is alternating. Write $\rank B_T=2r$.
Then the following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item The least codimension of a subspace $W\leq V$ for which
$\iota\circ T|_{W^{p+1}}$ is the top derivative of a circle-valued polynomial
of degree at most $p+1$ is $r$.
\item Among all surjections $\pi:A\twoheadrightarrow V$ from finite abelian
groups for which $\pi^*(\iota\circ T)$ has such a primitive, the least value
of $|\ker\pi|$ is $p^r$.
\item Every minimum cover has
\[
 A\cong(\Z/p^2\Z)^r\oplus(\Z/p\Z)^{n-r},\qquad \ker\pi=pA.
\]
The isomorphism classes of minimum covers over $V$, with the kernel
unlabelled, are in bijection with the maximal $B_T$-isotropic subspaces of
$V$. There are $\prod_{j=1}^r(p^j+1)$ such classes.
\item For every integer $0\leq c\leq n$,
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:92:eq:introPareto}
 \min_{\codim W\leq c}\log_p \cocost(T|_W)=\max\{r-c,0\},
\end{equation}
where $\cocost$ denotes the minimum kernel size of an integrating finite
abelian cover. In particular, restriction codimension plus the logarithm of
covering cost is at least $r$, and every integer point on this lower boundary
is attained.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

The lower bound in part~(ii) is not merely a count of denominators in one
chosen primitive. It applies to \emph{every finite abelian extension}, with
arbitrary invariant factors. The key is the homomorphism
$V\to\ker\pi/p\ker\pi$ induced by multiplication by $p$ on lifts.

\subsection{The analytic statement that preserves the energy}

For a finite abelian group $G$, a symmetric multiadditive
$S:G^d\to\T$, and $f:G\to\C$, define
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:92:eq:introEnergy}
 \calE_S^G(f)=\E_{x,h_1,\ldots,h_d\in G}
       \prod_{\omega\in\{0,1\}^d}
       \cC^{\,d-|\omega|}f(x+\omega\cdot h)\,\e(-S(h)),
 \qquad \e(t)=\exp(2\pi i t).
\end{equation}
Complex conjugation is denoted by $\cC$. All averages are normalized.

\begin{theorem}[Lossless quotient-profile comparison]\label{gsr:fm:92:thm:mainanalytic}
Let $d\geq2$, let $S:G^d\to\T$ be symmetric and multiadditive, and let $H\leq G$.
For $a\in G/H$, choose a representative and set $f_a(h)=f(a+h)$. Then
$\calE_S^G$ is nonnegative, and with
$u(a)=\calE_{S|_H}^H(f_a)^{1/2^d}$ one has
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:92:eq:introprofile}
 \calE_S^G(f)\leq \norm{u}_{U^d(G/H)}^{2^d}
 \leq\E_{a\in G/H}\calE_{S|_H}^H(f_a).
\end{equation}
The constants are one. If $S|_H=\Delta^d P_H$, the last expression equals
\[
 \E_{a\in G/H}\norm{f_a\e(-P_H)}_{U^d(H)}^{2^d}.
\]
No primitive for $S$ on $G$ is assumed.
\end{theorem}

Thus an optimal restriction in theorem~\ref{gsr:fm:92:thm:mainrepair} retains the full normalized
selected energy on average, and on at least one coset. The size of the
restricted domain does decrease; the word ``lossless'' refers to the energy,
not to preservation of ambient cardinality.

\subsection{The first odd-characteristic example}

The repair theorem and theorem~\ref{gsr:fm:92:thm:mainanalytic} reduce the largest possible
energy of any nonintegrable symmetric $(p+1)$-linear tensor, in every
dimension at least two, to one canonical tensor on $\F_p^2$. For $p=3$ we
obtain the following rigorous, but nonoptimal, quantitative result:
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fm:92:eq:introternary}
 \frac{11}{27}\leq m_{3,1}\leq\frac{1099}{2187}.
\end{equation}
The upper bound is certified by integer enumeration of all $9^5=59049$
quartic cubes. In particular, for a symmetric quartic tensor on any
$\F_3^n$, energy strictly larger than $1099/2187$ forces exact global
nonclassical integration. The conjecture $m_{3,1}=11/27$ remains open in this
article. Numerical maximization is reported only as evidence.

\subsection{Position relative to existing work}

The inspected ProveIt research compilation already contains Boolean
integration, alternating-form repair, and several sharp Boolean energy
results \cite{repo92research,repo89boolean}. We neither reclassify those as new
nor assert that a previously posed Boolean stabilization problem is still
open. The targets here are the arbitrary-finite-group covering realization,
the all-degree twisted quotient-profile comparison, the all-prime minimum
\emph{abelian cover} theorem, the joint repair frontier, and the odd-prime
extremal reduction.

These statements are proved below rather than imported from the repository.
The specific combined formulations were not located in the primary sources
and repository interfaces inspected for this manuscript. This is a limited
priority assessment, not a guarantee that no equivalent result exists in the
literature. The logical status of each principal ingredient is recorded in
section~\ref{gsr:fz:92:sec:audit}.

\begin{partabstract}{93}
We develop three groups of quantitative refinements in the local machinery
surrounding Gowers' proof of Szemer\'edi's theorem, with complete proofs and
an explicit comparison against the supplied ProveIt research collection.
First, we solve the four-frequency missing-arc problem at every radius.
Its new central branch is determined by a cubic contact equation and a
quartic transition polynomial. A two-frequency dual certificate also
determines an entire final band for every cutoff. On cyclic grids we obtain
an exact correction formula, an explicit oscillating second-order term,
and exact agreement on an arithmetic subsequence.

Second, for every family $\mathcal F$ of finite odd-order abelian groups,
we improve the uniform convergence of the centered norm comparison
$c_d(\mathcal F)$ to its bounded endpoint $D(\mathcal F)$ from
$O(\sqrt d\,2^{-d/4})$ to $O(d2^{-d/2})$. The constants are independent
of the group family. The proof uses a translation multiplier whose norm
is independent of the number of Fourier coefficients, together with
sign control for nearly constant cubes. For each fixed odd prime $p$,
we determine the sharper first correction
$c_d(\{\Z/p\Z\})-D_p=4D_p\log p\,d2^{-d}
+O_p(\log d\,2^{-d})$ through an exact subset-sum polynomial.

Third, we extend the sharp graph-energy recovery threshold $1/4$ to
every abelian target, including infinite targets. We classify the
quarter-endpoint obstruction, retain the sharp torsion-sensitive cubic
distance estimate, and prove that the exact non-affine energy maximum
has the optimal universal cutoff $|G|\ge13$. These results strengthen
the high-correlation application of Gowers' Proposition~6.1.

Previously established inputs are identified and reproved where needed.
Symbolic identities, exact finite computations, and directed rational
bounds accompany the proofs. The final sections give a formalization
roadmap and a prioritized programme of further questions. No stronger
global Szemer\'edi bound is inferred from these local improvements.
\end{partabstract}
\begin{quote}\small\raggedright
\noindent\textbf{Mathematical scope.} Finite abelian groups; extremal Fourier
moments; Gowers norms; graph additive energy; affine testing.
\end{quote}
\label{gsr:fm:93:sec:introduction}

Gowers' proof organizes quantitative arithmetic structure through
uniformity, detection of Fourier concentration, and extraction of
approximately affine frequency maps \cite{gowers}. Each interface
has a local extremal problem. Solving such a problem exactly can improve
a usable lemma even when the full density-increment iteration requires
additional work. This article treats three of those interfaces and
supplies complete proofs of the refinements stated here.

The comparison baseline is the ProveIt repository at revision
\texttt{6d494222250c} (full commit in the bibliography), inspected on
7~October~2026 \cite{repo88}. The merged report at that revision contains
sources~01--39; its ancillary research records also refer to later
submissions. We additionally inspected the supplied manuscripts
\emph{Sharp Extremal Thresholds and Uniform Limits in Gowers' Framework},
\emph{Exact Local Profiles and Structural Barriers in Gowers' Szemer\'edi
Framework}, \emph{Sharp Character Separation and Affine Rigidity in
Gowers' Inverse Steps}, and \emph{Sharp energy gaps and efficient
restriction} \cite{extremallimits,srcsixtyseven,srcfiftynine,srcsixtyeight}.
This extended comparison matters: several natural candidate improvements
had already been proved in those manuscripts. We do not assign the present
article an intake number or assume that later submissions have already
been merged.

\subsection{What is added}

\begin{center}
\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.19\textwidth}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.34\textwidth}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.39\textwidth}@{}}

Problem & Audited earlier result & Result proved here\\
\midrule

three; two final ranges & Complete cutoff four, including a new algebraic
branch; a larger final band at every cutoff\\[4pt]
Cyclic discretization & Quadratic error after endpoint rounding & Exact
central correction; its oscillating leading coefficient; an exact
half-circle formula\\[4pt]
Centered norm limit & Bounded endpoint $D$ and
$O(\sqrt d\,2^{-d/4})$ convergence & Family-uniform
$O(d2^{-d/2})$ convergence and a bounded approximation theorem\\[4pt]
Fixed prime groups & Bounded endpoint and fixed-group limiting question &
Exact first-order correction and an exact cube polynomial\\[4pt]
Affine graph recovery & General-target range $\eps<2/9$;
quarter range for elementary abelian $3$-targets & Sharp quarter range
for all abelian targets and a complete endpoint dichotomy\\[4pt]
Non-affine energy maximum & General cutoff $16$;
cutoff $13$ for elementary abelian $3$-targets & Optimal universal

\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

The local cubic distance profiles and the multilevel overlap inequality
are prior results \cite{srceleven,srcfiftynine,srcsixtyeight}.
Their extension to the entire sharp range for arbitrary targets is new
relative to the audited materials. Likewise, the limiting norm constant
$1/3$ is credited to \cite{extremallimits}; the contribution here is
the faster uniform rate and the fixed-prime asymptotic.

The claimed advances are proved mathematical extensions relative to this
audited project. The targeted literature check places them within moment
theory and homomorphism testing, but is not a determination of worldwide
priority. This is a research manuscript for independent review, with
reproducible checks; it is not a Lean-verified development.

\subsection{Three main statements in compact form}

For probability measures supported outside the open arc $(-a,a)$, let
\[
 \Phi_R(a)=\min_\mu\max_{1\le j\le R}
       \left|\int e^{-ij\theta}\,d\mu(\theta)\right|.
\]
Theorem~\ref{gsr:dt:93:new:Phi4} gives all seven branches of $\Phi_4$ and the
unique optimizer whenever $a\ge\pi/5$. In particular,
\[
 \Phi_4(\pi/2)=\frac{\sqrt3-1}{2},
 \qquad \Phi_3(\pi/2)=\frac13.
\]
The algebraic transition occurs at
$a_*=0.4508760097203392\ldots\,\pi$. The grid correction is given
exactly in Theorem~\ref{gsr:dt:93:grid:certificate}.

For a family $\mathcal F$ of finite odd-order abelian groups containing a nontrivial group, define
\[
 c_d(\mathcal F)=\sup_{G\in\mathcal F,\ \E f=0,\ f\ne0}
   \frac{\|f\|_{U^2}^4}{\|f\|_{U^d}^4},\qquad
 D(\mathcal F)=\sup_{G\in\mathcal F,\ \E f=0,\ |f|\le1}
   \|f\|_{U^2}^4,
\]
where functions are real. We prove
\[
 0\le c_d(\mathcal F)-D(\mathcal F)\le C d2^{-d/2}
\]
with an absolute constant. For $G=\Z/p\Z$ with $p$ a fixed odd prime,
the exact first-order term is
\[
 c_d(\{G\})=D_p+4D_p\log p\,d2^{-d}
       +O_p(\log d\,2^{-d}),\qquad
 D_p=\frac{p^3-4p+3}{3p^3}.
\]

For $f:G\to W$, with $G$ finite abelian, $|G|=N$, and $W$ any abelian
group, let $\mathcal E(f)$ count the ordered quadruples satisfying both
$x_1+x_2=x_3+x_4$ and $f(x_1)+f(x_2)=f(x_3)+f(x_4)$. Put
$\eps=1-\mathcal E(f)/N^3$. If $\eps<1/4$, there is a unique nearest
affine map, at relative distance at most $D_\kappa(\eps)$, where
\[
 \Psi_\kappa(t)=4t-(10+2\kappa)t^2+(6+2\kappa)t^3,
 \qquad D_\kappa=(\Psi_\kappa|_{[0,1/7]})^{-1}.
\]
Here $\kappa=1$ if $W$ contains a nonzero element of order two, and
$\kappa=0$ otherwise. For every non-affine $f$ and $N\ge13$,
\[
 \mathcal E(f)\le N^3-4N^2+(10+2\kappa)N-(6+2\kappa),
\]
with exactly the one-point extremizers specified below. The quarter
threshold and the cutoff thirteen are sharp universal statements.

\subsection{Normalizations and the role of the original paper}

All expectations and Gowers norms in this article are normalized.
On a group of order $N$,
$\widehat f(\chi)=N^{-1}\sum_x f(x)\overline{\chi(x)}$.
The unnormalized transform is written explicitly as a sum when needed.
The graph energy counts ordered quadruples and is not divided by
$N^3$ until the defect is formed. An affine map is a homomorphism plus
a constant. The target group need not be finite or have the same
exponent as the domain.

The original interfaces are Gowers' Lemma~5.2 for missing intervals,
the norm and Cauchy--Schwarz machinery in Section~3, and
Proposition~6.1 together with Lemma~6.2 for graphs of selected
frequencies \cite{gowers}. Our high-energy theorem does not change
the fourth power in Proposition~6.1. It improves the recovery step
after that proposition has supplied graph energy. The familiar sharp
$2/9$ threshold in the three-point homomorphism test concerns a
different statistic \cite{bclr}; the quarter threshold here is for the
four-point affine test.

The paper proceeds from exact Fourier certificates to their discrete
and set-theoretic consequences, then to uniformity norms and affine
recovery. The proofs use finite sums, elementary polynomials, normalized
Fourier expansions, and standard Gowers norm facts. Classical
arc-supported moment theory gives a broader context for the first
part \cite{yangxie}; no semidefinite solver output is used as a proof.
