\subsection{A formalization route without formal exponentials}
The implementation and proofs need not formalize analytic exponentials
inside a group algebra. A smaller route defines arrays first and proves
their tuple interpretation by finite combinatorics.

First define $N_{a,b}$ on labelled finite sets, including the empty tuple
and repeated labels. Prove that its Bernoulli expectation is a sum over
distinct supports. Next define array insertion by
\eqref{gsr:en:48:gcr:eq:init-update} and prove the inventory invariant by splitting
a tuple according to the positions occupied by the newly inserted label.
The binomial coefficients then arise from choosing those positions.

For replacement, formalize the Stirling recurrence and the truncated
identity
\[
 \bigl(1+p(e^t-1)\bigr)H_p(t)=e^t-1
 \quad\text{through degree }2s
\]
as an identity of coefficient sequences, not analytic functions.
This supplies \eqref{gsr:en:48:gcr:eq:replacement}. The rounding theorem then needs
only a finite sequence of rational inequalities.

For prescribed sizes, use an integer support-profile array and prove
\eqref{gsr:en:48:gcr:eq:hyper-identity} by counting subsets containing a fixed
support. The conditional two-branch averaging identity is a finite
binomial identity. Finally, prove that the executable array implementation
refines the abstract update. This separation keeps finite algebra,
probability, execution, and analytic filter estimates in distinct modules.

The suggested module names in \file{FORMALIZATION.md} are prospective;
no corresponding Lean files are claimed to exist or compile. In
particular, this package contains no unverified proof scripts presented
as finished formal proofs.

\section[{Further research questions\srctag{48}}]{Further research questions}\label{gsr:fz:48:sec:d12}
\srcnote{48}{Section 12}
\label{gsr:fz:48:gcr:sec:questions}

The results above settle an ambient-size algorithmic interface. The
following questions identify improvements that would change its scope,
not merely repeat the existence statement.

\begin{problem}[Eliminating exhaustive phase search]\label{gsr:fz:48:gcr:q:phase}
Can one find a translated Fej\'er parameter triple with positive surplus
in $\widetilde O_s(np^2)$ or $\widetilde O_s(p^3)$ time, while retaining
Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:48:gcr:thm:source}'s guarantee? The present total cost is
$O_s(np^5)$ because each of $p^3$ triples is evaluated separately.
A useful advance must compute a joint phase objective or a certified
conditional estimator, not assume that a random successful triple has
large probability merely because the mean surplus is positive.
\end{problem}

\begin{problem}[Subquadratic ambient storage for graph data]
For a scalar map on $\F_p$, the graph inventory uses $p^2$ locations per
coefficient. Can a representation depending on the actual graph sumsets,
Fourier support, or low-rank structure preserve exact response probes
with substantially less memory? Sparse storage alone is not enough:
lower-degree sums can become dense, and subsequent deletions introduce
cancellation. Both a running-time bound and a support-growth theorem are
needed.
\end{problem}

\begin{problem}[Sparse and high-dimensional complexity]
When $\phi$ takes values in a high-dimensional vector space, ambient
storage can be exponential in its input dimension. Find hypotheses under
which the construction is polynomial in the explicit list size and
coordinate bit length, rather than in $|G||H|$. For general systems, the
analogous target is dependence on the represented solution geometry
instead of the full group $(G\oplus H)^d$.
\end{problem}

\begin{problem}[Fixed size after nonuniform filtering]
The prescribed-size theorem starts from uniform sampling on a fixed
cardinality class. Conditioning a heterogeneous Bernoulli filter on its
total size gives a nonuniform, product-weighted distribution. Can its
conditional energy be maintained with a degree-$2s$ support state and no
cardinality-sized auxiliary state? The present one-variable
hypergeometric functional does not apply to unequal odds. A successful
answer would combine the source's strong phase filter with a hard size
constraint without an unproved independence approximation.
\end{problem}

\begin{problem}[Several genuine structural constraints]
Can respected-relation surplus be retained together with prescribed
Fourier correlations or energy on a specified spectrum? Linear
combinations are easy to evaluate, but a positive combined objective
need not make each constraint true. One needs a theorem producing a
valid separating or pessimistic certificate with explicit margin and
cost. Exact colour quotas may provide a useful intermediate model, but
are not themselves a spectral-preservation theorem.
\end{problem}

\begin{problem}[A sharp filter--precision--search frontier]
The proof retains the slack $d=\alpha+\eta-\alpha\eta$ and uses a
convenient common grid $Q$. Can exact influences, alternative positive
kernels, and a smaller phase family be jointly optimized to improve the
certified retained count at a fixed computational budget? The mathematical
objective should specify both analytic loss and evaluation cost; optimizing
only $L$ inside one sufficient bound does not solve the full problem.
\end{problem}

\begin{problem}[A faster exact array update]
The branch probe uses only $O(s^2)$ entries, but maintaining every lower
coefficient costs $O(s^4D)$ per label. Can batched translations, a
Fourier representation, or a data structure for delayed updates reduce
the total $nD$ factor without destroying exactness? The target should
include a bit-cost bound; numerical Fourier transforms with uncertified
signs would not suffice for an exact monotonicity certificate.
\end{problem}

\begin{problem}[Best possible use of a support profile]
The initial coefficients $c_j$ determine the uniform-cardinality
expectation curve exactly. Which constraints on these coefficients are
forced by graph energies, beyond nonnegativity for unsigned counts and
the obvious support bounds? Sharp constraints could produce new
threshold-free restriction theorems by locating a positive point on
\eqref{gsr:en:48:gcr:eq:fixed-profile}, rather than searching for a phase filter.
The question concerns realizable additive profiles, not arbitrary
polynomials of degree $2s$.
\end{problem}

\begin{problem}[Proof-carrying implementations]
Formalize the insertion and response invariants, and design a compact
certificate format whose verifier is materially cheaper than rerunning
the entire search. The final set and exact energy counts already certify
quality; what remains is an efficiently checkable connection to the
analytic retained-count guarantee and, where useful, to the searched
maximum. A verified search need not be implemented inside the theorem
prover if its output certificate has a small trusted checker.
\end{problem}

\begin{problem}[Propagation beyond the local restriction step]
Which later uses of Gowers's restriction machinery can consume the
constructed subset without requiring an infeasible enumeration of
higher arrangements or a loss of required spectral information?
The general-system theorem supplies a computational counting interface,
not a replacement for those later structural estimates. A complete
algorithmic version of the larger argument should track both
quantitative density losses and execution costs through every stage.
\end{problem}

\gsrnewfloats
\section[{Conclusion\srctag{48}}]{Conclusion}\label{gsr:fz:48:sec:d13}
\srcnote{48}{Section 13}
The obstruction to direct conditional-expectation extraction is not the
averaging principle. It is the interaction between repeated tuple entries
and the structured statistic being averaged. A product of label-level
exponential factors records each label exactly once, while divided powers
retain the ordered multiplicities needed for additive energies.

The resulting state is stable under probability replacement. Universal
Stirling response polynomials turn each replacement into weighted group
translations, and a small zero-coordinate probe determines its exact
slope. Recording distinct undecided support instead of total chosen size
extends the same idea to fixed-cardinality sampling. Squarefree position
variables then supply a general-system version, with repeated column
types explaining the much smaller cost of balanced energies.

These identities give a fully explicit answer to the companion's
algorithmic extraction question in the stated ambient model. Together
with certified rational filters and the retained analytic slack, they
make the polynomial-loss restriction theorem constructive without a new
loss in its retained-count bound. The more ambitious targets are now
specific: phase search, sparse dimension dependence, nonuniform
fixed-size filtering, simultaneous structural constraints, and formal
proof-carrying execution.

\gsrnewfloats
\section[{Algorithmic skeletons and invariants\srctag{48}}]{Algorithmic skeletons and invariants}\label{gsr:fz:48:sec:dA}
\srcnote{48}{Appendix A}
\label{gsr:fz:48:gcr:app:algorithms}

\subsection{Bernoulli signed rounding}
The input is a shared label list, one image list and rational weight for
each energy, an order, and rational probabilities. The following is
mathematical pseudocode; the executable version is in
\file{code/energy_inventory.py}.
\begin{verbatim}
Initialize one exact inventory for each image list.
J := the signed sum of its top, zero-group coefficients.
For each label i whose probability p_i is strictly between 0 and 1:
    Compute Delta_i from the universal response polynomials.
    Choose q_i = 1 when Delta_i >= 0, otherwise q_i = 0.
    Replace the i-th factor in every inventory, descending in degree.
    Assert J_new = J + (q_i - p_i) Delta_i.
    Record the decision and continue with J := J_new.
Return the labels with final probability one.
\end{verbatim}
The central invariant is the complete coefficient identity
\eqref{gsr:en:48:gcr:eq:identity}, not only a numerical estimate for the top entry.
Because every branch is an actual product distribution, the current
state remains an exact conditional expectation.

\subsection{Prescribed-size signed rounding}
\begin{verbatim}
Initialize integer support-profile inventories with all labels undecided.
Set N := n and r := required cardinality.
For each undecided label i:
    Compute each feasible exclude/include branch by the formal ratio.
    Evaluate exclusion using L_(N-1,r).
    Evaluate inclusion using L_(N-1,r-1).
    Choose a feasible branch of maximum signed value.
    Apply its profile update, descending in tuple degree.
    Decrease N, and decrease r exactly when inclusion was chosen.
Return the included labels.
\end{verbatim}
The invariants are the distinct-undecided-support interpretation,
$0\le r\le N$, and the exact two-branch averaging identity. The code tests
that averaging identity at every nonforced branch in its regression
instances.

\subsection{A direct verification alternative}
For small inputs, enumerate subsets and compute deterministic energy from
sum multiplicities. If
\[
 r_{s,S}(h)=\#\{(i_1,\ldots,i_s)\in S^s:
                    g_{i_1}+\cdots+g_{i_s}=h\},
\]
then $E_s(S;g)=\sum_h r_{s,S}(h)^2$.
This formula gives an independent reference for the final set and,
by weighting every subset with its exact Bernoulli probability, for the
initial expectation. For partial coefficients, the test suite also lists
ordered tuples directly and multiplies probabilities once per distinct
support. Neither reference uses the response identity being tested.

\section[{Proof-dependency map and audit boundaries\srctag{48}}]{Proof-dependency map and audit boundaries}\label{gsr:fz:48:sec:dB}
\srcnote{48}{Appendix B}
\label{gsr:fz:48:gcr:app:dependencies}
The purely finite algebraic part has the dependency chain
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{label-level sampling identity}\\
 \Downarrow\\
 \text{exact coefficient inventory}\\
 \Downarrow\\
 \text{Stirling response and translation update}\\
 \Downarrow\\
 \text{exact signed rounding and complexity}.
 \end{gathered}
\]
The prescribed-size extension adds distinct-support counting and a
hypergeometric functional; it does not use Fourier analysis. The
general-system theorem changes only the coefficient algebra and its
index set.

The source theorem adds a separate analytic chain:
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 \text{Fej\'er signal and short-relation exceptional bound}\\
 \Downarrow\\
 \text{positive mean surplus with explicit slack}\\
 \Downarrow\\
 \text{certified rational approximation and finite phase search}\\
 \Downarrow\\
 \text{exact signed rounding}\\
 \Downarrow\\
 \text{retained-count and respected-proportion bounds}.
 \end{gathered}
\]
This separation makes the boundaries explicit. A future better filter can
reuse the same exact rounding theorem. A future faster array
implementation can preserve the same analytic statement. Neither change
by itself supplies the independent structural ingredients needed to
improve a global Szemer\'edi bound.

\gsrnewfloats
\section[{Mathematical consequences and integration boundaries\srctag{49}}]{Mathematical consequences and integration boundaries}\label{gsr:fz:49:sec:d9}
\srcnote{49}{Section 9}
\label{gsr:fz:49:sec:consequences}

\subsection{What the degeneracy improvements change}

The prior two-cube argument treated every nonaffine certificate as a
possible codimension-two locus. Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:49:deg:rank-two-containment} shows
that this worst case contributes no new locus at all: its translations
are already in the affine divisor. This is why a new asymptotic
coefficient can be determined without enumerating every high-degree
ternary polynomial. The principle is useful more generally. A count of
certificates by rank alone can overestimate the union substantially;
one should ask whether the low-rank loci are geometrically contained
in components already accounted for.

The exact $k=3$ calculation adds a second principle. A prime-by-prime
search can be replaced by an integer obstruction certificate. Once
the top coefficients determine a candidate translation, a gcd of
finitely many integer residuals identifies every possible exceptional
characteristic at once. Small-prime symmetry then finishes a finite
list. The fact that the surviving cubic gcds have only primes two
and three, and the quadratic ones only three and seven, is stronger
evidence than many successful large-prime trials; it is the reason the
result is a theorem about every odd prime.

Neither principle automatically applies to the multiple-slice case.
For $d\ge2$ the shared last-coordinate equation permits more patterns
and the geometry of its vertical moments differs. A future claim about
$\delta_{k,d}$ must start from those equations. Similarly, replacing
a local degeneracy probability in a Riesz-selection argument requires
retaining the weights and threshold conditions in that argument.
The present exact two-cube identities are not silently substituted for
the eight-arrangement interface I3 or I4.

\subsection{What the norm improvement does and does not imply}

The odd-order and mean-zero hypotheses have specific roles. Odd order
makes a nonzero real Fourier coefficient pair with a distinct inverse
coefficient. Centering removes the trivial character and constant
harmonics of the dual test. If these assumptions are dropped, the
constant function or a real order-two character has all the relevant
uniformity norms equal, so a factor greater than one is impossible
without a replacement hypothesis.

The stronger non-five statement is pointwise: it is enough that one
largest Fourier coefficient has order different from five. The group
may still have five-torsion. Conversely, the weaker order-five dual
certificate does not show that five-torsion truly lowers the optimal
norm factor. It only locates the loss in the particular two-harmonic
test used here. Extra information about the remaining Fourier spectrum
could improve its tail bound.

The Fourier concentration envelope in \eqref{gsr:cc:49:ng:envelope} contains
more information than \eqref{gsr:cc:49:ng:constants}. It can be used whenever
an application independently constrains the largest Fourier pair.
The strict inequalities for individual nonzero functions do not imply
strict inequalities for the supremum constants: a sequence of groups
and functions could approach a limiting extremum. No compactness or
attainment theorem is assumed.

There is broader work on uniformity norms, including recent estimates
for their $L^p$ variants~\cite{kovacrogers}. Our target is the precise
real, centered comparison on finite odd-order groups and the explicit
constants relative to the project's baseline. A comprehensive priority
comparison or a classification of extremizers would be an additional
research task. The algebraic proof and the stated constant do not
depend on such a priority assertion.

\subsection{Why the model theorem has two dimensions and four controls}

In the cover theorem, active coordinates specify the variables on
which a model depends. Ambient coordinates specify the box in which
the partition must live. A partition in the active coordinates may
have a common difference incompatible with the untouched sides of an
ambient box. Keeping the ambient dimension in the induction resolves
this directly. It also prevents an exceptional set from being assumed
to be cylindrical when the proof has not made it so.

The four controls describe different mathematical requirements.
$N_j$ is a field-size condition needed to choose a global core.
$Q_j$ bounds the number of models on a local cell.
$c_{j,D}$ is a power in the resulting width, and $T_{j,D}$ says
when that power guarantee starts. Combining them into one number can
hide a dependency on the local error inside a supposedly global choice.
Their explicit separation is what permits the quantifier order in
theorem~\ref{gsr:en:49:ac:thm-main}.

The improvement in the local-error exponent table comes from retaining
the actual dimensions of the proper-section terms. A cube remainder
contains $\binom{k}{l-1}$ terms of active dimension $l$, rather than
$2^k-1$ terms all of dimension $k$. The resulting better exponents
are exact consequences of this recurrence. Their rapid growth also
shows that replacing successive refinements by a genuinely simultaneous
theorem remains a substantial problem.

\section[{Further research questions and a proposed program\srctag{49}}]{Further research questions and a proposed program}\label{gsr:fz:49:sec:d10}
\srcnote{49}{Section 10}
\label{gsr:fz:49:sec:questions}

The questions below are left unresolved by the present manuscript.
They are proposed research targets, not claims that each formulation
is a recognized open problem in the published literature. The first
group continues the earlier project's exactness question; the second
continues its real norm extremal problem; the third concerns the new
quantitative recurrence and its integration.

\subsection{Translation geometry and higher degeneracy coefficients}

\begin{question}[Exactness beyond dimension three]
\label{gsr:fz:49:q:exactness}
For $k\ge4$, is $T_k(p)=\Bcal_k(p)$ for all sufficiently large primes?
If not, what is the smallest dimension, characteristic, and derivative
rank admitting a translation outside the signed-coordinate arrangement?
\end{question}
The immediate milestone is dimension four. A rational off-divisor
certificate that persists modulo all sufficiently large primes would
settle the eventual exactness conjecture negatively; an isolated
exceptional-prime example would refute only exactness at every prime. A
positive proof should classify or compress the low-rank translation
loci rather than compare all pairs of $3^{16}$ patterns. A useful
certificate for a counterexample consists of the two ternary vertex
tables, the translation, and all squarefree coefficient identities.

\begin{question}[The exact cubic-order coefficient]
For fixed $k$, determine the coefficient of $p^{-3}$ in
$\delta_{k,1}(p)$. Which codimension-three translation loci actually
contribute outside $\Bcal_k$, and with what overlap multiplicities?
\end{question}
Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:49:deg:polynomiality} ensures that a fixed coefficient exists for
large primes. The first two coefficients required only containment of
rank two. The next coefficient tests rank three and intersections with
the known divisor. Counting patterns alone will not distinguish
coincident loci or loci already contained in the divisor.

\begin{question}[Derivative-rank-three classification]
Determine the optimal number of essential coordinates for a
ternary-valued multiaffine polynomial of derivative rank three, with
explicit characteristic restrictions, and classify the extremal cases.
\end{question}
The rank-two answer is four, and its exact census is a polynomial
in $k$. A comparable classification at rank three would make the
third-coefficient problem much smaller. Degree-three constraints alone
do not retain all the linear dependence among the partial derivatives;
the interaction of that dependence with three-valued Boolean images
is the relevant structural information.

\begin{question}[A sharper finite remainder]
Replace $M_k^2/2$ in \eqref{gsr:en:49:deg:finite-bound} by an explicit count of
distinct off-divisor affine loci, or by an incidence bound with a
substantially smaller dependence on $k$.
\end{question}
Common negation is only the first available symmetry. Boolean coordinate
reflections, permutations, and repeated translation orbits may identify
many more pairs. The desired statement should bound the geometric union,
not merely improve a census of certificates that may define the same
subspace.

\begin{question}[Exceptional characteristics and characteristic polynomials]
Compute $\chi_4$ or a nontrivial initial segment of its coefficients,
and obtain useful bounds on the bad-prime set $\mathcal E_k$ in
theorem~\ref{gsr:en:49:deg:polynomiality}.
\end{question}
The generic elimination algorithm is effective but too large for naive
use. A better method would keep only translation strata that can affect
the desired coefficients and use rank bounds to discard the rest.
The cubic gcd certificate suggests that arithmetic obstructions may
be much smaller than general determinant estimates predict.

\begin{question}[Human proofs of the three-dimensional certificate]
Find a short classification explaining the residual gcd histograms in
lemmas~\ref{gsr:en:49:deg:cubic-certificate} and \ref{gsr:en:49:deg:quadratic-certificate}, without a full
enumeration of all vertex patterns.
\end{question}
This is a proof-compression problem rather than a missing step in the
finite proof. An informative answer would explain the special primes
three and seven and the scarcity of rational off-divisor candidates,
and would suggest which part of the argument should extend to dimension
four.

\begin{question}[The multiple-slice second coefficient]
For $d\ge2$, determine the second coefficient of the arrangement
degeneracy probability while retaining both horizontal and vertical
moment constraints.
\end{question}
One should first classify the codimension-two loci that are not already
forced by simpler coordinate coincidences. The present two-cube result
shows why a broad union bound can miss an exact coefficient, but its
vertical collapse is special and cannot supply the answer by itself.

\subsection{Dual tests and sharp real norm comparison}

\begin{question}[The fourth-order extremal constant]
Determine $c_4^{\mathrm{odd}}$, or reduce the interval in
\eqref{gsr:fm:49:eq:c4-interval} substantially. Does the supremum arise as a limit
of functions on cyclic groups with a bounded number of Fourier pairs?
\end{question}
An optimization over finitely many harmonics produces candidates, but
a sharp result also requires a dual inequality for every spectrum.
The present proof illustrates both sides: a test inspired by a lower
example yields a universal upper certificate, but its tail estimate
still loses information.

\begin{question}[The role of five-torsion]
Is the optimal fourth-order constant on groups with no five-torsion
different from the unrestricted odd-order constant? Can the order-five
dual profile be raised to the non-five level?
\end{question}
The current gap between $29/4$ and $15/2$ is a gap between available
certificates. It does not prove different extremal constants. A useful
first step is an exact finite-dimensional optimization on the five-point
quotient that retains the phases of both nontrivial inverse pairs.

\begin{question}[A family of optimized dual functions]
For
$g=\phi_1+t_3\phi_3+t_5\phi_5+\cdots+t_{2s+1}\phi_{2s+1}$,
find rational coefficients and a tractable exact certificate that
improves the principal-to-tail ratio of $D_4g$.
\end{question}
The challenge is to improve the test's dual tail and its own norm
simultaneously. A numerical search should be followed by rational
interval certification and complete treatment of the finite set of
small character orders at which step-frequency constraints alias.
The finite formula in \eqref{gsr:cc:49:ng:finite-coefficients} provides a precise
starting point.

\begin{question}[Beyond the largest-pair parameter]
Replace the single mass $p$ by a profile involving the two or three
largest inverse pairs. Can their relative orders or additive relations
force a stronger moment--dual lower envelope?
\end{question}
The current dual tail bounds each unwanted coefficient separately by
the total remaining fourth mass. Equality in all those bounds would
usually demand incompatible concentration patterns. Keeping several
pair masses could measure that incompatibility, but modular aliases
must still be included.

\begin{question}[Higher orders and extremizing sequences]
Develop direct dual tests for $U^d$ at $d\ge5$, and determine how
$c_d^{\mathrm{odd}}$ and near-extremizing Fourier profiles behave as
$d$ grows.
\end{question}
The $U^5$ improvement here combines a fourth dual test with a higher
moment. It leaves room for a genuinely fifth-order dual certificate.
Any asymptotic conclusion should distinguish a supremum over all groups
from behavior on a fixed group and should account for the possible
nonattainment of a supremum.

\subsection{Model-theorem controls and formal integration}

\begin{question}[Simultaneous anchor refinement]
Can all anchor slices be modeled together with a width loss that grows
polynomially, rather than exponentially, in the number of anchors?
\end{question}
The factor $c_H^r$ in \eqref{gsr:en:49:ac:eq-piece-profile} is the precise
place to improve. A theorem must preserve the global core's independence
of the local tolerance and work in the same ambient common-difference
box geometry. Improving the sampling count alone does not resolve this
refinement cost.

\begin{question}[Sharper phase partition input]
Replace I7 by the strongest suitable simultaneous multilinear recurrence
theorem and recompute the exact $Q,c,T$ profiles. Which improvement in
I7 changes the final width exponent rather than only the threshold?
\end{question}
Because the induction is written as an explicit implication, a stronger
interface can be substituted without rewriting the global extraction.
The graph count is independent of the spectral phase-model count,
whereas the width and threshold are not. Tracking that distinction is
necessary to state a real quantitative gain.

\begin{question}[Propagation through the remaining density increment]
Assuming the seven interfaces have been independently certified, carry
the new Section~16 controls through the later phase-extraction and
density-increment arguments and state the resulting complete bound.
\end{question}
This is the step needed before claiming any new global Szemer\'edi
estimate. The first deliverable should be an explicit recurrence with
all positivity, minimum-width, and prime-size hypotheses, even if its
growth is weaker than a desired closed form. A successful simplification
must then be proved from that recurrence.

\begin{question}[Formal certificates and a modular theorem ledger]
Formalize the translation reduction and rank-two classification, then
verify the two finite certificates in a proof assistant and represent
the cover recurrence by a dimension-indexed expression type.
\end{question}
The natural order is structural lemmas first, finite integer reflection
second, and the deep imported interfaces as explicitly named hypotheses.
Termination of the new recurrence is a simple decrease of active
dimension. Proving it does not require hiding a failed numerical
domination inside a general automation tactic.

\section[{Reproducibility and repository integration\srctag{49}}]{Reproducibility and repository integration}\label{gsr:fz:49:sec:d11}
\srcnote{49}{Section 11}
\label{gsr:fz:49:sec:reproducibility}

\subsection{The exact verifiers}

The package contains three independent exact entry points, plus an
optional numerical cross-check. The exact programs use only Python's
standard library and reject optimized execution that would disable
assertions. They regenerate their JSON output beside the scripts.
No network access, external computer algebra system, or random seed is
required.

\begingroup\small
\begin{longtable}{>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.32\linewidth}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.60\linewidth}}
\toprule
Program & Mathematical task\\
\midrule
\endhead
\texttt{verify\_rank\_two.py} & Regenerates the square-invariant table;
checks derivative ranks and the census in small prime fields; verifies
exact two-dimensional counts, three-dimensional rank-two translations,
and the displayed first two coefficient formulas in representative
dimensions. The all-dimension theorem is proved in the text, not inferred
from these supplemental tests.\\[5pt]
\texttt{verify\_dimension\_three.py} & Performs the complete cubic and
quadratic integer obstruction enumerations; checks their formulas by
direct translated-polynomial expansion; exhausts all fourteen
signed-permutation representatives at primes eleven and thirteen.
Together with the text's reduction, this is the finite proof of
theorem~\ref{gsr:en:49:deg:exact3}.\\[5pt]
\texttt{verify\_dual\_gap.py} & Regenerates every fourth-dual coefficient
polynomial for orders $5,7,9,11,\infty$; forms all phase-dependent norm
and alias bounds; checks every rational table bound and every comparison
used in the fourth- and fifth-order conclusions; regenerates the
order-three full-cube count.\\[5pt]
\texttt{check\_dual\_numeric.py} & Optional independent direct average
of punctured-cube products at five character orders, two phases, and
three basepoints. Uses NumPy and floating point, and supplies a
cross-check only. It is not a premise of a theorem.\\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}
\endgroup

The dimension-three program examines $1\,985\,589$ ordered cubic
pairs and $12\,610$ ordered quadratic pairs with the same nonzero
quadratic part. Its small-prime part tests $14\cdot6561=91\,854$
polynomial/representative cases. The dual verifier uses five face-split
expansions, each with $4^8+4^7$ face assignments, and a separate
$2^{16}$ sign enumeration for order three. These are finite exhaustive
calculations at the reductions where the article explicitly invokes
computation. They do not establish the imported interfaces I1--I7.

\subsection{Build and file layout}

The top-level \texttt{gowers\_rank\_dual\_refinements.tex} is a single
complete source file, including its bibliography and the vector plot.
It does not depend on the earlier project manuscripts being present
on the build machine. The bibliography identifies those dependencies
mathematically. Compile with a standard TeX Live installation including
\texttt{pgfplots}; the package's \texttt{Makefile} invokes
\texttt{latexmk -pdf}. Running \texttt{make verify} regenerates the
three exact certificate files. Running \texttt{make numeric} is optional.

The proposed repository destination is a new subdirectory of the Ramsey
research directory. It should be integrated as a
research manuscript with computational certificates. Its conditional
cover theorem should retain the I1--I7 hypothesis list. A theorem ledger
should not mark the article's finite proofs as Lean-certified before an
actual formal implementation is checked. Existing source labels and
earlier manuscript numbering can remain intact; all new internal labels
here use descriptive prefixes.

\subsection{Source pin and limitations of the audit}

The repository was inspected at commit
\texttt{8c12c906e4ab5a00001a65de3c882f935a15661a}. The source-declaration
locations for the structural interfaces are recorded in
table~\ref{gsr:en:49:ac:tab-crosswalk}. They are locations in that transcription,
not proof-status assertions. The earlier project reports cited below
were also read to avoid rediscovering their sampling, interpolation,
moment, and first-order degeneracy results.

The mathematical development was independently reviewed across the
rank, duality, small-characteristic, and recurrence arguments, and the
exact programs were rerun when assembling the deliverable. These checks
support the manuscript's stated proof status. They are not a substitute
for peer review, and they do not make an unproved deep interface into a
formal theorem. No repository files were changed as part of preparing
this package.

\section[{Computational checks and reproducibility\srctag{50}}]{Computational checks and reproducibility}\label{gsr:fz:50:sec:d10}\label{gsr:fz:50:bc:sec:verification}
\srcnote{50}{Section 10}

The proof of Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:50:bc:thm:counterexample} is mathematical; no computer
can realistically enumerate its displayed field. The accompanying programs
serve two narrower purposes: exhaustive verification of the finite cover
inequalities at small moduli, and a reproducible finite illustration of the
same obstruction. They use exact integer and rational arithmetic and require
only Python's standard library.

\subsection{Exhaustive checks of the finite inequalities}
The script \filename{code/verify.py} checks all $3^5=243$ words over a three-symbol
alphabet in $\F_5$. There are $31$ distinct nonempty modular progression sets
in this field. For every such word and set it checks all affine lists of
length zero, one, or two, allowing repetitions in the two-element lists. It
also checks all single quadratic polynomials. A separate test enumerates every
two-symbol word on $\F_3$, every product of nonempty progression sets, and every
pair of bilinear polynomials. A further quadratic test uses all $2^7=128$
two-symbol words on $\F_7$ and its $99$ distinct progression sets. Finally,
all $3^9$ maps on $\F_3^2$ are tested for equivalence of separate affinity and
bilinearity. These are exhaustive finite checks, not statistical samples.

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lr}
\toprule
Test class & Exact checks passed\\
\midrule
Affine lists on $\F_5$ & 2,644,083\\
Single quadratic graphs on $\F_5$ & 941,625\\
Bilinear graph pairs on product boxes over $\F_3$ & 1,301,832\\
Single quadratic graphs on $\F_7$ & 4,346,496\\
Separate-affinity characterization on $\F_3^2$ & 19,683\\
Reduced-exponent integer budget comparisons & 54\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

Some of the root envelopes on short sets are vacuous. In the $\F_7$
quadratic test, $1,205,302$ checks have an upper bound strictly below the size
of the tested set. The endpoint test finds exactly $81$ separately affine
functions, all bilinear; it does not test every real-weight instance of the
product property.

The reduced-exponent tests do not instantiate $E=2^{1024}$. They test the
algebraic budget comparison at small exponents; the all-exponent statement is
proved in Section~\ref{gsr:en:50:bc:sec:counterexample}. Passing these tests is not
represented as a formal proof of the manuscript.

\subsection{A complete small branch-obstruction certificate}
The same script produces a specific four-symbol word on $\F_{257}$ using the
recorded pseudorandom seed $20261006$, then checks \emph{every} modular
progression parameterization of length at least $128$. The resulting exact
extrema are
\begin{equation}\label{gsr:fz:50:bc:eq:toy-extrema}
 \max_{I,j}\frac{b_j(I)}{|I|}=\frac{27}{64},
 \qquad
 \min_{I,j}\frac{b_j(I)}{|I|}=\frac{11}{138}.
\end{equation}
This involved $8,552,960$ progression parameterizations and $34,211,840$
symbol-frequency checks. The maximum occurs, for example, for symbol $0$ on
the length-$128$ progression with start $135$ and difference $19$.

Every symbol has at least four occurrences on every checked progression, as
verified directly in the script. Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:50:bc:thm:exact} therefore identifies
the best affine lists of each length $q\le4$ with the $q$ heaviest constants.
In particular, a single affine graph covers at most $27/64<1/2$ on every such
progression. By the product-box theorem, the function $F(h,y)=a(y)$ cannot be
covered on half of a union of boxes with those final-axis lengths by one
multiaffine graph per cell, even though four constant graphs cover it exactly.

The word, all parameters, the extrema, and an extremal progression are stored
in \filename{data/verification.json}. This is a concrete small analogue of the
branch-budget obstruction. It is \textbf{not} the enormous instance of the
repository's particular control functions.

\subsection{An exact deterministic construction test}
The script \filename{code/construct_word.py} implements conditional expectation
for a uniform alphabet, representing all conditional binomial tails by
integers on a common denominator. Its default run uses
\[
 p=31,\quad R=2,\quad L=20,\quad\varepsilon=2/5.
\]
It checks $4,682$ distinct progression sets. The initial expected number of
bad progression--symbol events is exactly
\[
 \frac{65,486,981}{134,217,728}<1.
\]
The final number is zero, and the maximum discrepancy of the output word is
exactly $2/5$. Here the exact initial expectation is better than the general
union-bound certificate in Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:50:bc:thm:balanced}; the algorithm needs
only that the actual expectation be less than one. Its output is recorded in
\filename{data/construction.json}.

\subsection{Commands and deliverables}
Run the checks from the package root with
\begin{lstlisting}
python3 code/verify.py
python3 code/construct_word.py
make pdf
\end{lstlisting}
The package includes the manuscript source and compiled PDF, both programs,
the exact output files, a source-audit document, a formalization plan, and a
Makefile. No unproved Lean file is included. The optional arguments of the
programs are documented by \filename{--help}. Large moduli can make the exhaustive
checks expensive; the construction algorithm's polynomial dependence is on
$p$, not on the bit length of $p$.

\gsrnewfloats
\section[{A formalization route\srctag{50}}]{A formalization route}\label{gsr:fz:50:sec:d11}\label{gsr:fz:50:bc:sec:formalization}
\srcnote{50}{Section 11}

The target is a theorem refuting the pinned catalogue entry, not a patch that
silently weakens its conclusion. The cleanest development would separate a
small finite combinatorial library from the source-specific witness assembly.

\subsection{Finite combinatorial core}
Formalize the root bound for a nonconstant polynomial agreeing with an
$R$-valued function on a finite set. Then formalize the finite list envelope
using a union bound and the maximum mass of an $s$-element subset of the
alphabet. The latter formulation avoids sorting until a separate equivalence
with order statistics is useful. Exact-optimum and deficit lemmas follow from
one inequality comparing the $s$- and $q$-branch masses.

Next prove the fibrewise product estimate by summing over the base set and the
adaptive partition estimate by summing over disjoint carriers. These steps do
not require Gowers norms, Fourier analysis, or the inverse theorem. The
counterexample uses only these finite counting statements after the word has
been constructed.

\subsection{Existence of balanced words}
A formal proof can use independent coordinates on the finite probability
space $S^{\F_p}$ with uniform measure. Only Bernoulli concentration and a union
bound over at most $Rp^3$ events are needed. Alternatively, define the exact
bad-event score used by \filename{construct_word.py}; a finite averaging argument
shows that some word has score below one once the probabilistic estimate is
established. There is no need to formalize an asymptotic random process or
uncountable probability space.

The main theorem uses a rational tolerance $1/(4R)$, a natural integer $R$,
and a finite prime field. Real logarithms occur only in a sufficient size
threshold. One can first formalize a conditional theorem taking a balanced
word as input, then add the finite existence theorem, and only afterwards
formalize the convenient explicit prime threshold.

\subsection{Source-specific assembly}
The witness assembly has four parts:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item Build the full proper two-dimensional box and show its width and
cardinality are $p$ and $p^2$.
\item Set the cube-selection family to the finite universe and prove that
\filename{section16GoodDomain} is the universe and \filename{section16PhiOne} is
$(h,y)\mapsto a(y)$.
\item Prove the identity-partition lemmas for constant and finite-range
functions, including width zero, and use them to satisfy both premises.
\item Specialize the conclusion to loss $1/2$, derive the $Q$-graph and
$p^{1/Q}$-width requirements, and contradict the retained mass by summing
cellwise covers.
\end{enumerate}

The completed statement could then be expressed as the negation of the pinned
\filename{lemma_16_10}. Until those steps are kernel checked, that is a proposed
formal theorem, not a delivered formalization. The manuscript's mathematical
proof and the finite test suite are evidence of different kinds and must not
be conflated.

\section[{Further research questions\srctag{50}}]{Further research questions}\label{gsr:fz:50:sec:d12}\label{gsr:fz:50:bc:sec:questions}
\srcnote{50}{Section 12}

The following questions are not assertions of established open status in the
wider literature. They are specific next problems arising from the proved
obstruction and the audited repository interface.

\begin{problem}[An upstream hypothesis that genuinely excludes the example]
Proposition~\ref{gsr:en:50:bc:prop:endpoint} settles the full-domain endpoint
$\gamma=1$: the product property excludes the witnesses. For
$0<\gamma<1$, identify the quantitative information retained by the relation
product property after selections and restrictions. Does it adequately control
one-coordinate summands at the branch budget needed for the induction? A useful
answer must give explicit bounds; referring generally to ``more structure'' is
insufficient. Adding both orientations of one-dimensional section control
alone does not work by Proposition~\ref{gsr:en:50:bc:prop:all-sections}.
\end{problem}

\begin{problem}[A sound replacement for the induction control]
Starting from the explicit local lift, derive a closed recurrence for graph
counts, width exponents, and iteration parameters that remains valid after
all losses and common refinements. What is the smallest additional dependence
on the input branch count forced by that recurrence? The uniform examples
require at least $(1-\eta-o(1))R$ graphs to retain $1-\eta$ of long boxes, so
any proposed compression should first pass this lower-bound test.
\end{problem}

\begin{problem}[Branch profiles instead of a single worst-case count]
Can the interface carry the whole function $q\mapsto M_q$ rather than a
single branch count? For nonuniform examples, discarding many low-mass branches
can be inexpensive, while a uniform profile cannot be compressed. Develop
composition rules for such profiles under union, interpolation, and common
partition refinement, with an explicit treatment of correlations between the
branches on different fibres.
\end{problem}

\begin{problem}[The shortest universal balance scale]
For fixed $R$ and prescribed relative error, determine sharp constants or
orders for the least length $L$ at which some word is balanced on every
modular progression of length at least $L$. Our absolute-balance construction
uses a logarithmic scale for fixed parameters, but no optimal constant is
claimed. A lower-bound analysis should distinguish modular progressions from
ordinary intervals and distinguish a fixed alphabet from a growing alphabet.
\end{problem}

\begin{problem}[Optimal scales for polynomial-list rigidity]
Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:50:bc:thm:growing} gives a sufficient scale
$O(R(d+1)\log p)$ at fixed relative error. Determine the actual transition
at which all optimal degree-$d$ lists become constant lists. The sharp implicit
nonconstant-graph threshold is smaller than our convenient $T$ when $d$ is
fixed, but relative symbol balance may dominate. Which of these two phenomena
sets the true threshold in each growth regime for $R$ and $d$?
\end{problem}

\begin{problem}[Beyond the exact-optimum regime]
For a fixed finite word, classify the list-cover optimum when
$b_{(q)}<dR$. The deterministic envelope need not be attained there. Can one
replace the root allowance by a computable incidence invariant that gives an
exact formula or a certified approximation without enumerating all lists?
Even the affine case could reveal a useful finite optimization problem.
\end{problem}

\begin{problem}[Efficient explicit constructions]
The conditional-expectation algorithm is polynomial in $p$ but not optimized.
Can the simultaneous progression constraints be certified and updated in
near-quadratic or near-linear time in $p$ for fixed alphabet? For the stronger
polynomial-avoidance construction, can the coefficient-space union bound be
implemented implicitly rather than by enumerating $p^{d+1}$ polynomials?
An explicit algebraic word with logarithmic-scale balance would be
particularly useful for formal counterexample libraries.
\end{problem}

\begin{problem}[Torsion and non-field codomains]
Over composite rings a nonconstant affine map may have large fibres, and the
root-count proof changes. Determine the exact replacement of the cover law in
terms of fibre multiplicities or annihilator sizes. Can one identify a
profile invariant that behaves well under products of cyclic groups and
reduces to $M_q$ over prime fields?
\end{problem}

\begin{problem}[Stability from incomplete observations]
The global stability theorem assumes a known alphabet and exact values of the
word. Extend it to noisy observations, partially observed fibres, or
probability-weighted point sets. The Hamming robustness corollary handles
adversarial edits after construction, but it does not yet give a reconstruction
algorithm for the underlying branch profile.
\end{problem}

\begin{problem}[A certified catalogue correction]
Formalize the negative theorem and decide how the catalogue should distinguish
the printed contextual statement, the false two-input abstraction, and a
replacement local lifting theorem. The source audit should preserve the old
statement for traceability while preventing it from being counted as an
available lemma in the main theorem's dependency graph.
\end{problem}

\gsrnewfloats
\section[{Conclusion\srctag{50}}]{Conclusion}\label{gsr:fz:50:sec:d13}\label{gsr:fz:50:bc:sec:conclusion}
\srcnote{50}{Section 13}

The exact finite cover law identifies the obstruction without relying on
numerical experimentation: a sufficiently populated constant branch cannot be
replaced, at equal coverage, by a low-degree nonconstant polynomial. Balanced
words make this true simultaneously on every long progression, so adaptive
partitions cannot eliminate the obstruction. The profile realization and
growing-alphabet theorems quantify both the mass frontier and the scales on
which it is visible.

Applied to the pinned Section 16 definitions, this yields an actual
counterexample to the two-input form of Lemma 16.10, at fixed parameters and
arbitrarily large prime moduli. Every named witness and every input budget has
been checked in the manuscript. The result demands a revision of that
abstraction, not a reinterpretation of a failed calculation as an unproved
but harmless estimate. Positive lifting remains available when its genuine
branch and width parameters are retained.

The outstanding larger task is to determine which additional structure in the
full proof can justify a suitable replacement, and at what quantitative cost.
That task is sharply separated here from the local statement that has been
resolved.

\section[{Definition-level pseudocode for the witness\srctag{50}}]{Definition-level pseudocode for the witness}\label{gsr:fz:50:sec:dB}\label{gsr:fz:50:bc:app:pseudocode}
\srcnote{50}{Appendix B}

The following is mathematical pseudocode, not a claimed Lean proof. It exposes
the finite objects and the universal input witnesses.
\begin{lstlisting}
E := 2^(2^10)
Q := 2^E
R := 4*Q
c := 1/Q
p := any prime greater than 2^(4096*Q^4)
S := {0, ..., R-1} as distinct elements of F_p
epsilon := 1/(4*R)
L := ceil(8*R^2*log(4*R*p^3))
a := an AP-balanced word supplied by conditional expectation

B := all of F_p^2
H1 := all of F_p
x0 := 0
Y(h) := every cube element with sidelength h in B
phi(h,y) := a(y)

For every fixed y and every input box:
    retain the entire box
    use its identity partition
    use the single constant graph a(y)

For every sigma, m, and proper input box P:
    qGamma := R
    qDelta := 1
    retain P
    use the identity partition P
    use final-coordinate affine maps y |-> v, for v in S

To refute the target:
    take P := F_p^2 and rho := 1/2
    every allowed cell has final-axis length at least p^c
    every allowed list has at most Q affine restrictions
    total covered fraction <= Q*(1/R + epsilon) = 5/16
    required retained fraction >= 1/2
\end{lstlisting}

The source-dependent statement has been pinned to an exact commit and blob.
The named domain $B_1$ has been realized using actual cube witnesses. The
constant-function certificates cover all proper input boxes, all allowed loss
parameters, and the zero-width edge case. The two line-cover count parameters
are kept distinct. The conclusion is tested on a full proper box, and its

\section[{The two interfaces after complete upstream extraction\srctag{51}}]{The two interfaces after complete upstream extraction}\label{gsr:fz:51:sec:d11}\label{gsr:fz:51:sec:next}
\srcnote{51}{Section 11}
The two results have different quantifiers. Theorem~\ref{gsr:fm:51:thm:main} proves that even the full budgets and all retained predicates do not force a grid for arbitrary selected outputs. Corollary~\ref{gsr:en:51:cor:actualrepair} constructs suitable outputs by preserving information in the actual selection, then localizing before the final square extraction. In the zero-phase counterexample other bilinear squares were already easy to choose; the constructive result works with the original phase and domain of a general admissible context, using the stated analytic source theorem.

The latest source already proves complete square extraction with a density-uniform threshold as described in Section~\ref{gsr:en:51:sec:uniformcurrent}. The following items describe a formal interface for the particular direct route proved here, not missing prerequisites for every current upstream square construction:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Export the actual fact $\lenfiftyone R=m$ or $m+1$, or just $\lenfiftyone R\le m+1$, through the existing Stage 13.6 wrappers. It belongs to their selected witness, not to every object satisfying the old conclusion.
\item Record short-carrier rectification with optional reversal and unchanged carrier, and the balanced aligned-parent partition with lengths $\lceil L/2\rceil$ through $L$.
\item Reuse the existing all-scale coefficient localization at unchanged density, rectify its selected $U$ inside the short parent, and feed the recovered stride and side $\lenfiftyone U-1$ into the common-step cover.
\item State the direct Stage 13.8-to-square result with its effective width \eqref{gsr:en:51:eq:effectivewidth}, rather than claiming the old Stage 13.9 lower length or the arbitrary-witness catalogue Corollary 13.10.
\end{enumerate}
This report establishes the mathematical geometry and source-interface assembly; it does not claim those strengthened wrappers or the direct theorem have been newly implemented or Lean-checked. The existing context-to-extraction, covering, parent-localization, complete fixed-density square, and uniform actual-density square results are credited at their pins. Reconciliation with the unchanged catalogue or printed target statements, optimization beyond the stated effective bounds, and a new global quantitative Szemer\'edi bound remain outside the result.

\gsrnewfloats
\section[{Proof and computation have different roles\srctag{51}}]{Proof and computation have different roles}\label{gsr:fz:51:sec:d12}\label{gsr:fz:51:sec:verification}
\srcnote{51}{Section 12}
The proof of Theorem~\ref{gsr:fm:51:thm:main} is symbolic; the constructive geometry is also proved for arbitrary admissible parameters, with its analytic input explicitly imported in Section~\ref{gsr:en:51:sec:constructive}. Existence of one sufficiently large prime follows from the finite list of fixed positive-exponent inequalities; no prime at that scale has been computed. In particular, the package must not be interpreted as a numerical witness satisfying the six full budgets.

The Python companion uses bounded exact integer arithmetic to check finite exponent identities, small difference-set obstructions, endpoint and residue-chain covers, density averaging on bounded cases, convolution counts and fixed-height normalizations for small arrangement examples, and exact Fourier normalizations. Further bounded checks cover short-carrier rectification, balanced aligned-parent partitions, weighted density preservation, the side-$M-1$ fit, and original-coordinate phase reversal. It also verifies the frozen source inventory against byte lengths, SHA-256 hashes, and Git blob identities. It does not approximate the astronomical exponents by floating point, expand $2^{9437184}$, build a denominator $2^T$, search for the huge modulus, or enumerate the enormous graph family.

Finite checks are useful for catching an indexing error or a missing factor of $N$; they do not prove the universal statements. Conversely, a successful source hash check verifies the identity of inspected bytes, not the logical correctness of a Lean theorem or the health of a whole project. No repository file was edited, no new Lean proof was produced, and no build or axiom audit of the upstream project is claimed.

The deliverable includes the editable \LaTeX\ source, PDF, bounded companion, tests, frozen relevant Lean source snapshots and curated hash records, and an offline reproducible packaging command. The README describes the exact command-line limits, provenance scope, and output checks. A checksum inventory detects accidental changes; it is not an independent trust anchor for an archive whose bytes an adversary controls. The article supplies the mathematical proof at full scale, while the companion supplies deliberately bounded diagnostics.

\section[{Repairs and questions left open\srctag{52}}]{Repairs and questions left open}\label{gsr:fz:52:sec:d10}\label{gsr:fz:52:sec:repairs}
\srcnote{52}{Section 10}
The examples determine several necessary distinctions, but do not supply a complete replacement theorem over composite moduli.

\paragraph{Retain the prime hypothesis.}
This is already the corrected source statement and the scope of the pinned theorem \codefiftyone{lemma\_13\_7\_holds}. No new result is needed to see why our examples do not apply there: the moduli in every construction are nonprime. A fresh formal audit of the corrected theorem is outside this report.

\paragraph{A unit common input step is insufficient.}
Section~\ref{gsr:en:52:sec:unit} disproves this proposed repair, even with genuine initial-stage predicates if no upper bound on $R$ is added. The dense row domain occupies one residue class inside a unit-step interval. Making the containing progression parameter invertible does not by itself force an ambient affine extension of a Freiman map on its sparse row subset.

\paragraph{The simultaneous geometric strengthening remains a separate question.}
Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:52:thm:budgets} rules out repairing the all-moduli implication merely by adding genuine initial stages, the exact cutoff, $\len R\le\len Q$, or all six numerical budgets together. Its common step is a nonunit. The combined interface that adds a unit common step to that full package remains a separate question: the unit-step examples in Section~\ref{gsr:en:52:sec:unit} do not supply it. No positive theorem or counterexample for that simultaneous package is claimed here.

\paragraph{Coordinate-affine conclusions change the problem.}
The map on $T$ is exactly $j\mapsto j$ in the progression coordinate $2j$. A conclusion phrased in such coordinates avoids this particular nonextendability demand. But its compatibility with later stages, ambient coefficient extraction, translations, and bilinear conclusions must then be proved. The current predicates cannot simply be read as if they already used this weaker meaning.

\paragraph{Torsion compatibility offers a concrete test.}
Lemma~\ref{gsr:en:52:lem:gcd} supplies a necessary two-point test for every proposed row slope. For an entire row, pairwise congruence solvability alone is not asserted to be sufficient for one common slope; compatibility of all congruences must also be checked. A useful replacement theorem might retain a slope in a module or a compatible homomorphism on a difference subgroup, together with explicit extension information. This is a proposed direction, not a theorem established here.

\paragraph{Formalize the negative statement separately.}
A Lean development could construct the context and records and prove negations of the two old \codefiftyone{Prop} definitions without touching the corrected theorem. The modular unit lemma, Freiman no-wrap argument, arrangement bijection, and real-power strict inequality are natural components. This report supplies written proofs and finite exact diagnostics, not such a formal certificate. In particular passing the companion does not establish the universal real inequalities or compile any Lean file.

\section[{Reproducibility and verification limits\srctag{52}}]{Reproducibility and verification limits}\label{gsr:fz:52:sec:d11}\label{gsr:fz:52:sec:repro}
\srcnote{52}{Section 11}
The accompanying archive contains this editable TeX source, the PDF, a standard-library Python companion, tests, a deterministic builder, and five curated Lean source snapshots with JSON provenance. It does not contain full third-party papers, raw service receipts, private review notes, or a repository checkout. No repository files were changed or uploaded.

\subsection{What the exact companion checks}
The bounded checks cover:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the integer exponents in~\eqref{gsr:en:52:eq:constants}, the two explicit length thresholds, and the symbolic parameter identities in~\eqref{gsr:en:52:eq:largeparams};
\item the full-budget cutoff, spectrum and radius exponents, strict symbolic margin $\beta<\sigma$, and finite toy floor inequalities;
\item the rational brackets $5<56/11$ and $16/3<6$, which combine with the stated elementary bounds on $\pi$ to verify the floor;
\item exact small-model Freiman relations using an eightfold convolution indexed jointly by domain sum and image sum, with repeated entries allowed;
\item the one-point and residue-class agreement obstructions on bounded prime-power examples;
\item exact spectral alias sets, arrangement-energy normalization, and the two-point $\Z/18\Z$ model including its failure at order nine;
\item bounded examples of the congruence-solvability criterion and the symbolic unit-step mass ratios;
\item byte lengths, SHA-256 hashes and Git blob SHA-1 hashes of the five fixed source snapshots.
\end{enumerate}
These finite checks help expose indexing, sign-independent spectral, exponent, and normalization mistakes. They do not numerically inspect the enormous witnesses, prove the analytic Fourier bound by floating point, or replace the written arbitrary-parameter proof. Large constants are represented by literal formulas and small exponents; the companion does not construct $U,k,N$ from the genuine initial-stage example or evaluate the full exponent towers.

\subsection{Build and packaging contract}
From a fresh extracted \codefiftyone{Report280} directory, run
\begin{quote}\ttfamily\small
python3 -I -B build.py verify\\
python3 -I -B build.py reproduce --output /tmp/report280-rebuild
\end{quote}
The output path must be fresh or empty, absolute, outside the source directory, and outside protected system locations. The Linux builder checks a closed file inventory and rejects symlinks, hard-link aliases and nonregular files. It snapshots source bytes; stages checks in a separate directory; runs all tests and the companion normally and under \codefiftyone{-O}; checks identical standard output; uses bounded subprocess logs and timeouts; and verifies that original and staged source inventories remain unchanged.

The PDF is compiled twice with shell escape disabled and deterministic metadata. Undefined references, missing citations, overfull boxes, and unresolved rerun requirements are build failures. Archive members, permissions, ordering, timestamps and compression settings are fixed. An internal SHA-256 manifest covers every public payload file, while an external SHA-256 sidecar identifies the actual ZIP bytes. Neither a hash nor deterministic packaging proves the mathematics or authenticates its author.

A successful replay from the distributed package also requires the rebuilt PDF to match its distributed bytes. This is a toolchain-sensitive requirement, not a promise of byte identity across every TeX distribution. The README records the reference tools and alternatives for interpreting a mismatch. Rendering and visual inspection are separate quality checks performed before release; the builder's text-level TeX gates are not a replacement for them.

\section[{A concise reconstruction guide\srctag{52}}]{A concise reconstruction guide}\label{gsr:fz:52:sec:dB}\label{gsr:fz:52:app:guide}
\srcnote{52}{Appendix B}
For a manual check of the counterexample, the following order avoids both giant-integer computation and dependence on the optional finite tests.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Read \codefiftyone{LinearOn} and the two target quantifiers, then the complete Stage 13.6 and weak Stage 13.7 predicates.
\item Verify the strip context by the strict bound $8(m-1)<N/2$ and the exact identity $C(h)=N^{16}E_8(T)$.
\item Check the two Stage 13.6 masses against the number of critical heights. For step two their ratios are $\delta,\lambda$; for the unit-step enlargement they are $2\delta,2\lambda$.
\item Prove the odd multiplier $2a-1$ is a unit. This forces at most one agreement on each parity class.
\item Cancel the positive number of rows in the first output mass inequality. Compare the resulting upper bound $2^{939}$ or $2^{940}$ with the exact output length lower bound.
\item For genuine initial data, check both spectral aliases, the exact floor $\lfloor16/\pi\rfloor=5$, and the Stage 13.5 coefficient estimate appropriate to the chosen step.
\item For the full numerical package, check $\beta<\sigma<uw$, all nine scale conditions, and the separate lower-target width budget. Retain the distinction between its nonunit step and the unit-step examples with fewer simultaneous extra conditions.
\end{enumerate}
This order isolates the obstruction from the large constants: the algebra is elementary, while the giant scale is used only to make a positive-power length lower bound exceed a fixed row-density cap.

\section[{Scope and further questions\srctag{53}}]{Scope and further questions}\label{gsr:fz:53:sec:d9}\label{gsr:fz:53:sec:scope}
\srcnote{53}{Section 9}
The result is a quantitative consequence of the source constructions on the full density interval. It preserves actual-density quantities uniformly and exhibits an explicit closed threshold. The seventh-term dominance is exact for the displayed seven-term budget; no claim is made that this is the smallest possible threshold for square extraction.

The basic uniform source theorem remains fully credited. The geometric route here strengthens selected outputs by preserving $\len R\in\{m,m+1\}$ and using a new localized height progression. It does not repair a proposition that asks for a grid from every arbitrary witness satisfying a weaker retained interface, and does not compare the new square with the length of an independently chosen old Stage 13.9 progression.

The following questions delimit useful further work:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Can the existing Stage 13.6 wrappers formally export $\len R\le m+1$, and can the short-carrier and balanced-parent arguments be implemented with unchanged carriers under reversal? The proof-level construction above identifies precisely the extra information to retain.
\item Can the threshold be reduced by deriving only the width and short-parent budgets needed for the sharper route? We retained the stronger sixth budget that also pays all scales of the existing square API; its economy is not asserted.
\item For a chosen constant $\lambda<4$, what is the best explicit threshold for $k\ge N^{\lambda\gamma(a)}$ uniformly? The coefficient-bearing result \eqref{gsr:en:53:eq:exactsharp} is a suitable starting point, but this report only proves the stated clean value three at \eqref{gsr:fm:53:eq:N0}.
\item How should this actual-density refinement be composed with subsequent Fourier and global iteration interfaces while preserving their hypotheses and printed target exponents? No such global conclusion is derived here.
\end{enumerate}
These are questions about further quantitative or formal developments, not assertions that every current upstream extraction route requires them.

\section[{What the reproducible companion verifies\srctag{53}}]{What the reproducible companion verifies}\label{gsr:fz:53:sec:d10}\label{gsr:fz:53:sec:reproduction}
\srcnote{53}{Section 10}
The proof is symbolic at the full scale. No natural number near $N_0(a_0)$ is constructed, no enormous prime is searched for, and no denominator of astronomical bit length is allocated.

The standard-library Python companion checks bounded exact exponent identities and coefficient inequalities underlying the scalar estimates, the natural floor/half and ceiling budgets, short rectification on finite models, balanced aligned-parent partitions, common-step cover capacity and side-fit arithmetic. It uses integers and rational numbers, not floating-point surrogates for the thresholds. These finite checks detect transcription and indexing mistakes; they do not prove the universally quantified analytic inputs or replace the proofs in the article.

The companion also verifies the curated source files against their byte counts, SHA-256 digests and Git blob identities. The latter use
\[
 \operatorname{SHA1}(\texttt{blob }\Vert\text{decimal byte length}
 \Vert\texttt{NUL}\Vert\text{file bytes}).
\]
Matching hashes identify the inspected source bytes, not their logical correctness or the health of a whole dependency build. No Lean source was edited, no new Lean proof was produced, and no kernel replay or axiom-dependency audit is claimed.

The ZIP contains the editable \LaTeX\ source, PDF, bounded companion, tests, offline builder, and twenty-three relevant raw Lean source snapshots with a curated JSON inventory. Private reviews, raw connector receipts, unrelated source inventories and full third-party papers are excluded. The builder runs diagnostics and tests normally and with Python optimization, rejects source mutation, uses a fixed PDF build epoch and deterministic archive metadata, and supports replay from an extracted delivered archive. The README states its platform, toolchain and output restrictions. A manifest detects byte changes; it is not an independent trust anchor for an archive controlled by an adversary.

\subsection{Dependency ledger}
The dependency structure is small enough to state without a diagram.
Lemma~\ref{gsr:en:54:lem:factor} depends only on finite Fourier inversion.
Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:54:thm:factor} adds the triangle inequality and Parseval.
Theorem~\ref{gsr:fm:54:thm:main} adds one quadratic identity and the exact
amplitude of a balanced indicator. The all-group extension adds
Proposition~\ref{gsr:en:54:prop:refine}.

For the extremal theory, Lemma~\ref{gsr:en:54:lem:power} and the elementary
certificate of Lemma~\ref{gsr:en:54:lem:TF} give all single-offset ceilings
and equality cases. Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:54:thm:cycle-stability} retains the
deficit in that certificate; Lemma~\ref{gsr:en:54:lem:lifting} converts it to
function distance. The simultaneous-intercept result is the one
place where a named classical graph theorem is invoked, and its
extremal-value proof is included.

No large inverse theorem, Freiman theorem, asymptotic input,
probabilistic existence theorem, or unproved repository statement
is needed for these proofs. Conversely, the present results do not
construct the affine selector supplied to Section 8. The quantitative
cost of obtaining that selector, and the costs of subsequent phase
flattening and iteration, remain part of any global application.

\subsection{Status of verification}
The accompanying checks are reproducible but are not a substitute
for the proofs. The exact graph tests enumerate \textbf{31,030}
rational probability distributions, using integer arithmetic for
the triangle-free certificate and testing \textbf{227} equality
instances against the cycle classification. The exact four-frequency
obstruction is checked at five rational values of $t$.

Independent floating-point calculations check \textbf{2,016} mixed
weighted factorization cases, \textbf{2,540} offset-power and ceiling
cases, \textbf{402} weighted balanced-function cases, and
\textbf{1,440} constructive stability cases. The largest recorded
factorization or global power-identity discrepancy is below
$1.9\cdot10^{-15}$, with an acceptance tolerance of $10^{-10}$.
The backward/forward chirp-sign identity is checked separately,
and even cyclic refinements and Example~\ref{gsr:en:54:ex:even} are tested.
In addition, \textbf{1,440} short-orbit repairs and
\textbf{7,704} exact rational polarization identities on product groups
are checked, together with coordinate periodicity.
The random seed is \texttt{20261006}. Full counts and environment
versions are recorded in \texttt{data/verification.json}.

No Lean proof is bundled or claimed checked. The companion
formalization plan specifies candidate statements and proof
boundaries, rather than presenting uncompiled Lean syntax as a
verified artifact. The mathematical proofs and source comparisons
have been self-audited, not independently peer-reviewed.

\section[{Further research questions\srctag{54}}]{Further research questions}\label{gsr:fz:54:sec:d11}
\srcnote{54}{Section 11}
\label{gsr:fz:54:sec:questions}
The following problems distinguish missing improvements in the
present theorems from harder changes to the global inverse argument.
None is being asserted to be a previously published open problem.

\begin{question}[The best balanced-indicator coefficient]
For fixed odd $N$ and density $\delta$, determine the largest
coefficient replacing $1/(B\sigma)$ in
Theorem~\ref{gsr:fm:54:thm:main}, uniformly in $P,\lambda,\mu$ after normalizing
by the actual input energy. Does the balanced constraint yield a
strict improvement over the amplitude-only bound, uniformly as
$N\to\infty$? A solution must respect that the elementary
coefficient-one extremizer need not be a balanced indicator.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[The exact stability modulus]
For cycles of order $m\geq5$, determine the optimal function
$\Phi_m(\varepsilon)$ bounding distance to the extremal star family.
Is there a common asymptotic leading coefficient for all $m\geq5$?
The four-frequency family gives a lower bound, while
\eqref{gsr:en:54:eq:l1-star} supplies a dimension-free upper bound of the
correct exponent but not a matching coefficient.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Pointwise-constrained repair]
Suppose $|g|\leq1$ and the offset energy is almost extremal at a
prescribed value of $\norm g_2$. Can one repair $g$ to an extremizer
while preserving the pointwise cap, or quantify the unavoidable
increase in the cap? The phase-preserving Fourier repair in
Lemma~\ref{gsr:en:54:lem:lifting} does not answer this. Balanced indicators
are an even more restrictive version.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Sharp localized ceilings]
For a prescribed interval or Bohr set $P$, compute the maximum
of $\E_{h\in P}|A_\eta(g)(h)|^2/\norm g_2^4$ under specified
amplitude constraints. The coverage estimate
\eqref{gsr:en:54:eq:local-ceiling} is deliberately coarse. The phases of
Fourier coefficients, absent from the full-group identity, now
matter through the Fourier transform of $\one_P$.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Uniform extraction from a family of windows]
Find useful conditions on a family of nonnegative windows $w_j$
under which one common frequency attains a fixed fraction of each
window's individual optimal score. Theorem~\ref{gsr:en:54:thm:factor} selects
a common phase across translates of one window, not simultaneously
across unrelated windows. Aggregate extraction is easy; per-window
control is the substantive problem.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Higher-degree common-phase extraction]
When a higher-order derivative selector has an exact polynomial
primitive, which local hypotheses force one global polynomial
phase to replace the translate-dependent phases in a higher-order
analogue of Proposition 8.1? The obstruction to simply repeating
the present argument is that the relevant lower-order Fourier
coefficient becomes a higher-order correlation, rather than an
ordinary Fourier product with controlled $\ell^1$ norm.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Non-symmetric selectors on a restricted shift set]
For a nonsymmetric bilinear selector, can local extraction be
organized using its alternating radical and projective Fourier
blocks while retaining a useful common structured object? Global
symmetry thresholds are already treated in other repository
research; the distinct issue is a weighted shift set and a local
window conclusion without silently assuming integrability.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Several intercepts and graph stability]
Which Cayley graphs $\Gamma_S$ admit dimension-free power-spectrum
stability near the clique ceiling, and with what exponents? The
transition between four-cycles and longer cycles shows that the
extremizer space, not just the clique number, is relevant. A
classification should avoid assuming that every maximizer is
supported on a single clique.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[A faster certified selector]
Can the $O(N^2\log N)$ all-frequency scan be reduced when the
overlap spectrum is sparse, or when the window is an interval,
while keeping an a posteriori certificate for the retained score?
Randomized sampling from the overlap spectrum is natural, but a
useful running-time theorem needs an explicit lower bound for
success probability or a suitable stopping certificate.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Quantitative propagation through Section 8]
Combine the common-phase theorem with the strongest compatible
selector construction and phase-flat partition in the repository.
Track every normalization and exceptional-set loss to determine
which downstream constants improve. An improved local coefficient
alone does not establish a better exponent in a final bound for
$r_4(N)$ or $r_k(N)$.
\end{question}

\begin{question}[Formal generality of quadratic refinements]
Develop a reusable finite-abelian-group quadratic-refinement API,
with classical cyclic refinements as a special case and doubled
roots for even moduli. The conceptual theorem is elementary, but
formalizing the coordinate-independence calculation once would
avoid repeated incorrect divisions by two in local inverse steps.
\end{question}
